jobs.title: Research Assistant Professor - Electromagnetics  - (496280 )
jobs.description:
Job Details
Department: Electrical & Computer Engineering
EngineeringSalary: Commensurate with experience
Description:
The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) at
the University of Houston invites applications for a
non-tenure-track position at the rank of Research Assistant
Professor in the area of Electromagnetics. The successful candidate
will have the opportunity to lead and contribute to multiple
research projects supported by the U.S. Department of Energy and
industrial partners. We are seeking individuals prepared to assume
leadership roles across several dimensions of these efforts.
This is a 12-month appointment, renewable contingent on funding,
performance, and programmatic need. The anticipated start date is
July 1, 2026.
Qualifications:
Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in Electrical or Computer Engineering,
or a closely related field. Candidates should have a strong
experimental background in the area of Magnetic Resonance (MR)
Safety for medical implantable devices. Candidate should be able to
perform electromagnetic simulations via software packages, such as
Sim4Life and High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS), and carry
out experiment studies along with a proven record of preparing
technical reports, scientific publications, and research grant
proposals. Demonstrated experience supervising Ph.D. students
and/or postdoctoral researchers, as well as excellent oral and
written communication skills, is required.
The successful applicant will be expected to contribute to the
Department’s research activities, collaborate across the College
and University, and participate in securing externally funded
research grants as part of a dynamic team of faculty and research
scientists. Review of applications will begin immediately and
continue until the position is filled.
University, College, and Department:
The University of Houston is a Carnegie Tier One public research
university that is located on a park-like campus a few minutes from
the Houston city center. The university has embarked on an exciting
period of research growth, a rising reputation, a committed
leadership. The ECE Department stretches across two campuses, one
in Houston (central), and one in Katy, TX. Our central campus is
home to 36 tenure-track faculty, 4 full-time research faculty, and
4 instructional faculty, with 3 NAE members, 3 NAI Fellows, 8 IEEE
Fellows, 3 AIMBE Fellows, 2 SAE Fellows, 2 FRSC (UK), and Fellows
of OSA, APS, AAAS, ECS, and SPIE, among other distinctions. The
department is home to multiple NSF Centers, Industry/University
Consortia, and NanoFabrication Facility. The university has a
well-developed faculty-centered ecosystem for translational
research and commercialization of technologies.
UH central campus has over 39,000 undergraduate students and 8,000
graduate students. The Department has 30 tenured and tenure-track
faculty, modern research facilities, annual research expenditures
exceeding $10 million, and a vibrant graduate program with more
than 100 Ph.D. students. The successful candidate will join a
collegial group of research-oriented faculty working in a highly
collaborative environment.
The Cullen College of Engineering is ranked #44 in the 2025 U.S.
News & World Report list of top public engineering programs
across the nation. Houston is the fourth-largest city in the U.S.,
with a population of over 6.8 million in the greater Houston area.
It is the “energy capital of the world” and houses the largest
medical center in the world. The greater Houston area offers
state-of-the-art recreational facilities, world-class arts and
activities, excellent schools, and affordable housing.
How to Apply:
Applications should include a cover letter, curriculum vitae, a
description of research interests (not exceeding three pages). The
application and associated documentation should be submitted to the
following site for consideration: https://www.uh.edu/human-resources/careers/
Official transcripts are required for a faculty appointment and
will be requested upon selection of the final candidate.
All positions at the University of Houston-System are security
sensitive and will require a criminal history check. Individuals
conducting research in critical infrastructure areas (i.e.,
communication infrastructure systems, cybersecurity systems,
electric grid, hazardous waste treatment systems, and/or water
treatment facilities) are subject to regular review to ensure the
security and integrity of the research is maintained.
The University of Houston System and its universities are Equal
Opportunity Institutions. Everyone is encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: Tenure-Track Faculty Positions in Genome Analysis
jobs.description:
Job Details
1. Open Positions:
Assistant Professor or Lecturer (Senior Assistant Professor), 3 open positions
2. Location:
Tohoku University Tohoku Medical Megabank Organization, Genome Analysis Division
Tohoku University Tohoku Medical Megabank Organization is a world-leading research center for large-scale genomic analysis, operating one of the world's largest and most comprehensive general-population biobanks. To pioneer next-generation personalized healthcare and prevention, ToMMo has built an "Integrated Biobank" based on a prospective cohort study of over 150,000 participants, including a highly unique three-generation cohort. Furthermore, ToMMo drives cutting-edge genomic research, having completed Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) for over 120,000 individuals.
3. Job Responsibilities:
Successful applicants will establish and lead independent research groups as Principal Investigators (PIs) in one of the three fields below.
I. AI-driven Genomic and Information Science
Advance data-driven life science research that leverages AI and machine learning, underpinned by large-scale genomic and omics data as well as supercomputing infrastructure.
Demonstrate outstanding leadership in spearheading next-generation genomic informatics through collaboration with domestic and international partners.
II. Life-Course Omics Science
Lead research to extend human healthspan through cutting-edge multi-omics analysis, capitalizing on the unique strengths of ToMMo’s cohort samples and data.
Conduct original research that delves into the fundamental principles of human biology by integrating longitudinal life-course health and disease data with large-scale omics information.
III. Disease Cell Biology
Leverage core biobank resources, including cells and biospecimens linked to genotypic, longitudinal health information, and environmental factors, to drive original research using iPS cells for elucidating disease mechanisms, drug discovery, and regenerative medicine.
4. Qualifications:
Candidates must hold a Ph.D. upon taking up the post and have outstanding achievements in the above-mentioned fields of expertise.
5. Start Date:
April 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter
6. Compensation:
(1) Salary: To be determined in accordance with university regulations, based on experience.
Annual salary system. Approx. starting from 9,000,000 JPY
Commuting allowance may also be provided.
(2) Employment type: Full-time
(3) Term: Tenure-Track Appointment of 5 years (No reappointments)
This is a tenure-track position. Candidates who successfully pass the tenure review before the end of the appointment term will be promoted to a tenured Associate Professor. The result of the tenure review will be communicated at least one year before the end of the appointment term.
(4) Working Hours: Discretionary Labor System for Professional Work. In general, the hours are from 8:30 to 17:15, but individuals have the discretion to manage their own hours.
(5) Days off: Saturdays, Sundays, public holidays, and New Year’s holiday (from December 29 to January 3)
(6) Insurance Benefits: Enrollment in the MEXT Mutual Aid Association for health and pension insurance, employment insurance, and Worker’s Accident Compensation Insurance
(7) Research Funding: Basic research funding of 1,000,000 JPY will be provided annually, along with funding to hire one postdoctoral researcher. Successful candidates will be expected to proactively secure external funding as well.
7. Submission Materials:
a) Resume (Designated format)
b) List of Research Achievements (free format: research papers, patents, books, review articles, awards)
c) List of research funding grants, academic activities, and international conference presentations (free format)
d) Reprints of 10 major papers
e) Summary of research activities to date (free format: up to 2 pages)
8. Deadline:
November 13, 2026 (Fri.) 17:00 JST
*Late submissions not accepted
9. Submission Instructions:
Please access the application form to complete the required form fields below and upload the required documents listed in the Submission Materials section:
https://jotform.com/262107634175051
a) Desired research field chosen from the three fields listed in the Job Responsibilities section and statement of reason (maximum 120 words)
b) Contact information for two references (researchers who can evaluate the applicant's research achievements and character), including their names, titles, email addresses, and telephone numbers
10. Contact Info:
For research-related inquiries:
Professor Nobuo Fuse
Genome Analysis Division, Tohoku Medical Megabank Organization
E-mail: nobuo.fuse.b6@tohoku.ac.jp
For inquiries regarding compensation:
General Affairs Office, Administrative Department, Tohoku Medical Megabank Organization
E-mail: tommo-som@grp.tohoku.ac.jp
11. Remarks:
Candidates may be asked to give a presentation as part of the selection process.
Research and daily academic operations can be conducted in English. Japanese language proficiency is not required for this role.
Tohoku University provides comprehensive support for international researchers relocating to Japan through the International Support Center (ISC), including assistance with visa procedures, housing arrangements, and life in Sendai.
Please see the Tohoku University International Support Center (ISC) website.
Tohoku University promotes activities to increase Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) and encourages people of varied talents from all backgrounds to apply for positions at the university.
Tohoku University’s website about the DEI Declaration can be found here.
Pursuant to Article 8 of the Act on Securing, Etc. of Equal Opportunity and Treatment between Men and Women in Employment, Tohoku University shall, as a measure for increasing the presence of women among the academic staff, prioritize the hiring of women deemed qualified for each job opening, based on impartial evaluation.
Tohoku University has published ‘Tohoku University-Live as Who You Are-Guidelines for Gender and Sexual Diversity' to provide explanations and details of how those at the university should respond with respect to diverse sexuality. The purpose of the guidelines is to create an environment in which all students, faculty, and staff respect diverse sexuality in their academic, research, and professional activities.
Tohoku University has the largest on-campus childcare system of all Japanese national universities. This network comprises three nurseries: Kawauchi Keyaki Nursery school (capacity: 22) and Aobayama Midori Nursery school (116), both open to all university employees, as well as Hoshinoko Nursery school (120), which is open to employees working at Tohoku University Hospital. In addition, Tohoku University Hospital runs a childcare room for mildly ill and convalescent children, which is available to all university employees. See the following websites for information on these and other programs that Tohoku University runs to assist work-life balance, to support researchers, and to advance gender equality, including measures to promote childcare leave among male employees.
Center for Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) Website
Human Resources and Planning Department Website (Japanese text only)
Tohoku University offers a Dual Career Program to assist the spouses or partners of qualified faculty members in seeking employment opportunities for academic and non-academic jobs within the university. For more information, please contact the recruiting department.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor, LGBTQIA+ History, Brown University
jobs.description:
Job Details
The Pembroke Center for Teaching and Research on Women and the Department of History at Brown University invite applicants for a full-time, tenure-track position, at the Assistant Professor level, in LGBTQIA+ History. All geographic and temporal specialties will be considered, and particular interest will be given to candidates whose research centers locations in the Global South.
While the successful candidate will have defended the Ph.D. thesis by the time of appointment, we are seeking early-career candidates who will develop their first major monograph supported by the Pembroke community and the History Department’s robust mentorship program, including a manuscript workshop that generally takes place in the third or fourth year in rank. The Brown University History Department and the Pembroke Center place a high priority on research excellence, high-quality teaching, and a commitment to fostering a diverse and inclusive academic community. Interested candidates should describe their ability to contribute to each of these three areas in a letter of application, and they should describe their ability to design and teach courses both for History and for the Gender and Sexuality Studies program housed at the Pembroke Center. Please also send a curriculum vitae, an article or chapter-length writing sample, and the contact information (name, phone and email) of three references via Interfolio. Review of applications will begin October 15, 2026. To assure full consideration, applicants should submit their materials by that date. Brown University is committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive academic global community; as an EEO/AA employer, Brown considers applicants for employment without regard to, and does not discriminate on the basis of, gender, race, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Earth and Environmental Sciences
jobs.description:
Assistant Professor of Earth and Environmental Sciences, LEHIGH UNIVERSITY.
The Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences invites applications for a tenure-track assistant professor with a specialization in solid Earth geosciences with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027. We seek a broadly trained geoscientist who uses field-based approaches to examine fundamental processes in the lithosphere, with links to current and emerging scientific challenges and societal needs, the latter including, but not limited to, critical resources, hazards, and energy. Candidates must have an earned Ph.D. in Earth and Environmental Sciences or a closely related field by the date of employment and a publication record in the solid Earth geosciences.
Candidates working across disciplinary boundaries or in emerging areas of the solid Earth geosciences are encouraged to apply. The successful candidate will have research expertise that contributes to a vibrant department research ecosystem and will show the capability of developing a robust research program that integrates field-based observations with analytical, computational, or experimental approaches. We encourage applications from candidates who would integrate their novel research approaches with an interest in leading and developing experiential learning opportunities for our students, potentially contributing to our nationally recognized field camp. The individual hired will be expected to teach graduate and undergraduate courses in the geosciences within the context of a broad curriculum in Earth and Environmental Sciences, demonstrate a commitment to inclusive teaching and broadening participation in fieldwork, establish an internationally recognized and externally funded research program, participate in departmental, college, and university service, and contribute to inclusion efforts towards A Lehigh for Everyone.
Lehigh’s Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences examines how the solid earth, oceans, atmosphere, and life interact to shape the world in which we live. Our research spans observational, experimental, theoretical, and numerical approaches, which we incorporate into field-based, experiential, multidisciplinary education. We seek to instill in our undergraduate and graduate students the skills needed to succeed in life, and this includes engagement with diverse perspectives and people. We also work to enhance earth-science literacy so that individuals and communities can make informed decisions about environmental and resource issues. More information about people and programs can be found at the EES department web pages at https://ees.cas.lehigh.edu/.
Founded in 1865, Lehigh University has combined outstanding academic and learning opportunities with leadership in fostering innovative research. Recognized among the nation's highly ranked research universities, Lehigh offers a rigorous academic community for over 7,500 students. Lehigh University has some 5,800 undergraduates, 1,800 graduate students, and nearly 600 full-time faculty members. Lehigh University is located in Bethlehem, PA, a vibrant and historic area. Over 840,000 people live in the Lehigh Valley, which is in close proximity to New York City and Philadelphia.
For full consideration, applications should be received by October 19, 2026. Applicants should submit their materials at https://apply.interfolio.com/192530. Candidates should submit a cover letter of no more than 2 pages indicating interest in the position and how your research expertise contributes to our vibrant research ecosystem; a curriculum vitae; a statement of research that describes past scholarly contributions and future research directions; a statement about teaching that describes prior experience, teaching philosophy, and courses that you would want to teach or develop; and a statement on past experience enhancing the success of students of all backgrounds and future plans for Contributions to Lehigh’s Principles of Our Equitable Community (the Lehigh ADVANCE Center’s guide for understanding and preparing such statements is available here). We will request letters of recommendation from qualifying candidates at a later stage of the search. Any inquiries regarding this search should be directed to Prof. Joan Ramage, chair of the search committee, at ramage@lehigh.edu.
Lehigh University is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital or familial status, national origin (including shared ancestry), pregnancy or related conditions, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, or veteran status. Lehigh University is committed to a culturally and intellectually diverse academic community and is especially interested in candidates who can contribute, through their research, teaching and/or service, to this mission. Lehigh University provides competitive salaries and comprehensive benefits, including domestic partner benefits, and supports faculty members’ work/life balance.

jobs.title: Assistant Teaching Professor, Associate Teaching Professor, or Teaching Professor of Chemistry
jobs.institution: Emory University, Emory College of Arts and Sciences, Department of Chemistry
jobs.description:
The Department of Chemistry at Emory University invites applications for a teaching track professor (open rank) position in Organic or Biochemical/Biophysical Chemistry to teaching both lecture and/or laboratory courses. The candidate will be appointed as Assistant Teaching Professor, Associate Teaching Professor, or Teaching Professor depending on qualifications and years of experience in a similar role. This is a career-track position with full faculty governance rights and responsibilities, competitive salary and benefits, with potential for regular term renewal and promotion through the teaching track ranks. The expected start date is in the fall of 2027.
The candidate will join a cohesive group of tenure- (28) and teaching-track (7) faculty who teach in our innovative undergraduate curriculum, Chemistry Unbound (https://pubs.acs.org/doi/pdf/10.1021/acs.jchemed.8b00585). The candidate will be committed to excelling professionally in a department of supportive colleagues who believe that excellence is achieved both individually and collectively. Our faculty, staff, and students contribute to a thriving community of educators and scholars and seek colleagues who are dedicated to joining us in this mission.
Qualifications
Minimum qualifications: Completion of a Ph.D. degree in organic chemistry, biochemistry, or biophysical chemistry is required at the start of the appointment.
Preferred Qualifications
Demonstrated excellence in teaching undergraduate chemistry lecture and/or laboratory courses Demonstrated commitment to working towards collective goals in a team setting Experience in evidence-based pedagogy and instructional creativity Supervising and collaborating with graduate teaching assistants and undergraduate learning assistants
Application Instructions
Applicants must apply online at: apply.interfolio.com/192677 . Review of applications will begin on October 15. To ensure full consideration, all materials should be received by November 15.
A complete application will include:
A cover letter outlining your interest in the position and highlighting relevant teaching experience A curriculum vitae Contact information for three referees A statement (up to 3 pages) of teaching experience, educational methods, mentoring experience, and future professional goals For technical assistance with Interfolio, contact help@interfolio.com or call (877) 977-8807. For questions about the position, contact chemsearch@emory.edu.
Emory is an equal opportunity employer, and qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by state or federal law.

jobs.title: Professor of Chemistry
jobs.institution: Emory University, Emory College of Arts and Sciences, Department of Chemistry
jobs.description:
The Department of Chemistry at Emory University invites applications for full-time, tenured faculty positions at the rank of Full Professor starting in the Fall 2027 semester. We seek faculty candidates with research interests that lie in translational biomedical sciences as part of the Game Changers Initiative at Emory University. Focus research areas for this search include but are not limited to the following topics: chemical biology and proteomics, biophysical chemistry, synthetic chemistry and drug discovery, and ML/AI for biomedical discovery. We seek candidates that have demonstrated the ability to establish and maintain a vibrant, externally funded independent research program having high national and international visibility. In addition, candidates should have a strong commitment to teaching and mentoring undergraduate and graduate students in the classroom and research laboratory. Successful candidates must hold a PhD in Chemistry or related discipline. Salary is competitive and commensurate with rank and experience.
The appointee will join a cohesive group of tenure- (26) and teaching-track (6) faculty in the Chemistry Department during an exciting period as we grow into new and renovated space in the Atwood Chemistry Center, refine our Chemistry Unbound undergraduate curriculum, and further enhance our strong record of fundamental discovery, translational impact, and cross-disciplinary collaboration.
Please submit the following through Interfolio: apply.interfolio.com/192717
1) cover letter; 2) curriculum vitae; 3) contact information for three referees that can provide letters of recommendation; 4) a three-page summary of independent research accomplishments and future research plans; 5) a one-page statement of teaching experience, interests, and philosophy; 6) any additional information that provides a demonstration of excellence in research, pedagogy, and mentoring.
Application review will begin on October 15. To ensure full consideration, all applicant materials should be received on or before November 15. For technical assistance with Interfolio, contact help@interfolio.com or call (877) 977-8807. For questions about the position and further information on the Game Changers Initiative, please contact chemsearch@emory.edu.
Emory is an equal opportunity employer, and qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by state or federal law.

jobs.title: Teaching Professor with Assistant Rank: Media Studies
jobs.description:
This position focuses heavily on undergraduate teaching in a program that integrates comprehensive technical training with a rigorous critical approach. jobs.title: Clinical Assistant/Associate Professor in Actuarial Science
jobs.institution: School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences
jobs.description:
Clinical Assistant/Associate Professor of Actuarial Science (Job # 190960)
Arizona State University
School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences
The School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences (SoMSS) at Arizona State University invites applications for a full-time position in Actuarial Science at the rank of Clinical Assistant or Clinical Associate Professor. The anticipated start date is August 16, 2027. The Actuarial Science programs at Arizona State University, established in 2014 and 2018 for the Bachelor's and Master's degrees, respectively, have a total enrollment of approximately 100 students. Our Actuarial Science program obtained the Center of Actuarial Excellence (CAE) designation by the Society of Actuaries (SOA) in June 2024, which complements the program’s recognition at the gold level by the Casualty Actuarial Society (CAS). The program also has an active chapter of the Gamma lota Sigma, Kappa.
About the School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences (SoMSS)
The School offers Bachelor’s, Master’s, and Ph.D. programs in Applied Mathematics, Theoretical Mathematics, Mathematics Education, and Statistics, as well as undergraduate and Master’s programs in Actuarial Science. In addition, the School offers an interdisciplinary Bachelor’s degree program in Data Science and participates in a cross-college Ph.D. program in Data Science.
The School has a strong interdisciplinary research profile that includes numerous opportunities for collaboration on the campus with, for example, the Fulton Schools of Engineering, the School of Earth and Space Exploration, the School of Geographical Sciences and Urban Planning, and with interdisciplinary centers and institutes, such as the Institute for Social Science Research, the College of Health Solutions, the Global Institute of Sustainability, as well as off-campus with the thriving medical and technical industries in the Phoenix region.
The School has excellent computing resources that include individual faculty workstations, several high-performance servers, and a small cluster, as well as access to the University's central computing facilities and the High-Performance Computing Initiative. More details can be found at https://math.asu.edu.
About The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences is the academic heart of Arizona State University, committed to improving communities on a local, national and global scale. We support the professional development and growth of our faculty and staff in their cutting-edge research to advance these aims. Within The College, our faculty engage with a large and curious student body, guiding them as they grow into socially aware, critical thinkers and writers able to succeed in a wide range of careers and to address the challenges of the twenty-first century. Advancing the success of our students remains our top priority. To learn more about The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences, please visit https://thecollege.asu.edu.
About Arizona State University
ASU exemplifies a new prototype for the American public research university. As articulated in the ASU Charter, ASU is a comprehensive public research university, measured not by whom it excludes, but by whom it includes and how they succeed; advancing research and discovery of public value; and assuming fundamental responsibility for the economic, social, cultural and overall health of the communities it serves.
Essential Functions:
Deliver high-quality teaching in courses relevant to our undergraduate and Master’s Actuarial Science programs
Mentoring students
Engage in professional service
Required Qualifications:
A Ph.D. degree in actuarial science, mathematics, statistics, computer science, or a closely related field by the time of appointment.
Demonstrated potential for excellence in teaching and mentoring students in actuarial science.
No more than two outstanding credentialing requirements, including no more than two remaining examinations, toward Associateship or Fellowship with the Society of Actuaries (SOA), Casualty Actuarial Society (CAS), or a society mutually recognized by SOA or CAS. Candidates must also have completed one credentialing requirement within the previous three years.
Desired Qualifications:
Experience in curriculum development in actuarial science or related disciplines, such as statistics, risk management, or mathematics.
Demonstrated success working with a broad range of students and colleagues.
Demonstrated active engagement with the actuarial profession within the previous five years through actuarial employment, internships, industry projects, participation in professional societies, research, publications, presentations, or other comparable professional activities.
Demonstrated service to the actuarial profession through volunteer activities with the Society of Actuaries (SOA), the Casualty Actuarial Society (CAS), or another mutually recognized professional organization.
Demonstrated ability to develop and maintain collaborative relationships with the actuarial industry.
Presentations at or participation in national and/or international actuarial science conferences.
Demonstrated commitment to working with faculty, staff, students, and communities to advance the principles of the of the ASU Charter.
Application Instructions:
The application deadline is October 14, 2026. Applications will continue to be accepted on a rolling basis for a reserve pool. Applications in the reserve pool may then be reviewed in the order received until the position is filled. Candidates will be asked to create or use an existing Interfolio Dossier to submit the following application materials to https://apply.interfolio.com/192702:
A cover letter that briefly explains the candidate’s interest in the position and addresses the candidate’s commitment to ASU’s Charter.
A curriculum vitae.
A statement of teaching experience and philosophy.
Four (4) letters of recommendation; at least one of these letters should address the candidate’s teaching qualifications.
Applications submitted outside of Interfolio will not be considered.
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
A background check is required for employment. Arizona State University is a VEVRAA Federal Contractor and an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. All qualified applicants will be considered without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other basis protected by law. ASU’s full nondiscrimination statement (ACD 401) is located on the ASU website at https://www.asu.edu/aad/manuals/acd/acd401.html and https://www.asu.edu/titleIX.
Clery Act Statement
In compliance with federal law, ASU prepares an annual report on campus security and fire safety programs and resources. ASU’s Annual Security and Fire Safety Report is available online at https://www.asu.edu/police/PDFs/ASU-Clery-Report.pdf. You may request a hard copy of the report by contacting the ASU Police Department at 480-965-3456
For additional information regarding position specifics, please contact Tammy Palmer via email at tammy.palmer@asu.edu

jobs.title: Assistant Professor (tenure track directly to Professor Ordinaire) in Modern English Literature
jobs.description:
Introduction
UNIL is a leading international teaching and research institution, with over 5,000 employees and 17,000 students split between its Dorigny campus, CHUV and Epalinges. As an employer, UNIL encourages excellence, individual recognition and responsibility.
Presentation
The English Department of the Faculty of Arts, University of Lausanne, invites applications for the post of Assistant Professor (tenure track directly to Professor Ordinaire [Full Professor]) in Modern English Literature. We welcome applications from candidates with specialisations in Victorian literature, Modernism, and/or modern poetry.
Job information
Expected start date in position : 1 August 2027
Contract length* : 2 years, renewable 2 x 2 years, maximum 6 years
Activity rate : 100%
Workplace : Lausanne-Dorigny
* The person appointed as tenure-track Assistant Professor will be hired for a term of two years, renewable twice on the proposal of the Dean's Office. In principle, an evaluation procedure will be initiated at the end of the 8th semester, i.e. at the start of the third two-year term. At the end of this procedure, the Faculty may propose the promotion of the candidate to the rank of Professor Ordinaire (Full Professor).
Your activities
Teaching
The succesful candidate will be expected to teach 4 hours per week at the Bachelor's and Master's levels during the pre-tenure period (6 hours per week after tenure). They will also contribute to the coordination and supervision of examinations, as well as to the mentoring and supervision of students research work.
Research
The successful candidate will develop an independant research agenda while contributing to collaborative research projects. They will actively engage in scholarly activities and participate in national and international research collaborations, including initiatives such as CUSO doctoral programme in English Studies.
Institutional engagement
The successful candidate will collaborate with other sections, programmes, and research centres within the Faculty. They will contribute to inter-institutional collaborations and participate in the administrative duties associated with the life of the Section, the Faculty and the University. They should be able to work effectively in a bilingual English-French environment, as French is the official language used for Faculty - and University - level meetings and correspondance.
Your qualifications
A PhD in one of the areas of modern literature specified above.
Two published monographs, or one monograph and at least five substantial peer-reviewed (Scholarly critical editions will also be taken into account)
Experience in university teaching at all levels (at least 2-3 years)
Ability to obtain grant funding and coordinate team projects
What the position offers you
A friendly and dynamic working environment with many opportunities for collaboration and intellectual entrepreneurship.
For further information
Please contact : Professor Kevin Curran (kevin.curran@unil.ch)
Your application
Deadline : 15 November 2026
Applications should include the following:
A cover letter that includes a description your current research project(s)
A cv that includes a clearly presented list of publications
Names and contact details of 2 referees
Copies of university degrees
Please upload your full application as a single PDF here:
Only applications submitted through the following platform will be taken into account: https://unil-selectus.frentix.com/positiondetails/13434883
Remarks
UNIL is commited to:
Promoting equality, diversity, and inclusion within its community;
Fostering an open, respectful, and supportive environment in which all members can thrive;
Providing working conditions that support a healthy work-life balance;
Supporting early-career researchers and the next generation of scholars.
To increase the representation of women in academic positions, applications from women are particularly encouraged.

jobs.title: Clinical Assistant Professor in Human Development
jobs.institution: University of Rochester Warner School of Education and Human Development
jobs.description:
Job Details
The Warner Graduate School of Education and Human Development at the University of Rochester invites applications for a full-time Clinical Assistant Professor in Human Development. This position combines teaching, student mentorship, program development and improvement, and community-engaged partnership development. The term of employment will begin on July 1, 2027.
The successful candidate will play a central role in advancing the Warner School's mission of leveraging the power of education to transform lives and make the world more just and humane. The Warner School’s Human Development program prepares graduates to understand and address complex issues affecting human development across educational, healthcare, organizational, and community contexts. The program emphasizes interdisciplinary inquiry, applied learning, and community engagement to foster healthy development across the lifespan. The program offers PhD, EdD, and master’s degrees. The person occupying this position would have primary responsibility for the master’s degree and field experiences. The position is designed for an innovative educator and community-engaged professional who can connect graduate education in human development with meaningful experiences and partnerships across the Greater Rochester region and beyond.
We welcome applicants with doctorates in Human Development or related fields, including psychology, sociology, social work, or family studies. The applicant must have an educational and practical background that prepares them to teach graduate-level courses in human development and work with students and community organizations to design and facilitate varied opportunities for graduate students outside of the classroom.
The principal duties are associated with this position are to:
Teach the equivalent of six graduate courses annually in the Human Development program.
Contribute to curriculum development and continuous program improvement.
Design and oversee community-based learning opportunities that integrate academic coursework with practice-based experiences aligned with students' professional interests and career aspirations.
Collaborate with other faculty in creating community-based research experiences for students
Support students in identifying professional goals, navigating career pathways, and connecting academic learning to community-based practice.
Supervise independent studies, capstone projects, internships, and other applied learning experiences as appropriate.
Ideal candidates for this position will have qualifications and experiences that include:
Doctorate in Human Development or related fields, earned prior to the position’s starting date.
Experience and a demonstrated commitment to teaching and mentoring graduate students
Evidence of successful community-engaged work, partnership development, or applied professional practice.
A demonstrated commitment to preparing effective, justice-oriented professionals and researchers. Strong interpersonal, organizational, and collaborative skills.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience developing and sustaining partnerships within the Greater Rochester region, the Finger Lakes region, or comparable community ecosystems, with demonstrated understanding of local educational, health, human service, nonprofit, and community organizations.
Established professional networks within Rochester-area community agencies, school systems, healthcare organizations, foundations, or civic institutions.
Experience coordinating internships, practica, community-engaged learning, or workforce development initiatives.
Expertise in one or more areas aligned with Human Development program strengths, including youth development, family studies, developmental differences, community development, or community-engaged scholarship.
Experience working across university-community boundaries to develop mutually beneficial partnerships.
The review of applications will begin on October 1, 2026 and will continue until the position is filled. For more information about this position, please contact the search chair, Martin Lynch at mlynch@warner.rochester.edu.
As part of the application, the following documentation will be required:
A cover letter that addresses your interests in and qualifications for the position, including your research interests and priorities as well as your teaching philosophy and evidence of teaching effectiveness CV Writing sample Contact information for three references
To apply, access the University of Rochester Interfolio via the following link: https://apply.interfolio.com/193251
About the Warner School: The Warner Graduate School of Education and Human Development is part of the University of Rochester, one of the world’s leading research-intensive universities. At the Warner School, we believe that education can transform lives and make the world more just and humane. This vision informs our teaching, research, and service as a research school of education, as we strive to: PREPARE practitioners and researchers who are knowledgeable, reflective, skilled, and caring educators, who can make a difference in individual lives as well as their fields, and who are leaders and agents of change; GENERATE and disseminate knowledge leading to new understandings of education and human development, on which more effective educational policies and practices can be grounded; and COLLABORATE across disciplines, professions, and constituencies to promote change that can significantly improve education and support positive human development.
Our diverse work in each of these domains is informed by the following underlying beliefs: the improvement of education is in pursuit of social justice; development and learning shape and are shaped by the contexts in which they occur; the complexity of educational problems requires an interdisciplinary and collaborative approach; and wise practices are grounded in research and theory, just as useful theory and research are informed by practice. The Warner School fosters a learning community that represents and builds on the rich diversity of human experiences, backgrounds, cultures, histories, ideas, and ways of living. Learn more about equity, diversity, and inclusion at the Warner School here: https://www.warner.rochester.edu/about/diversity

jobs.title: Tenured or Tenure-Track Faculty Position – Open Rank
jobs.description:
The Molinaroli College of Engineering and Computing at the University of South Carolina is continuing to expand its tenured and tenure-track ranks significantly. As part of this growth, the Department of Chemical Engineering seeks to add a tenured or tenure-track faculty member to begin in Fall 2027. This position will be located in Columbia, SC. Applicants at all ranks are encouraged to apply. Applicants for the rank of Assistant Professor must possess a Ph.D. degree in chemical engineering or a related field by the time of appointment and demonstrate potential for excellence in teaching and research; applicants for the rank of Associate Professor and Full Professor must also have years of relevant academic experience commensurate with academic policy by the time of appointment, with a strong, sustained record of excellence in teaching and research. Successful candidates will be expected to develop and sustain an internationally recognized research program.
The focus of this search is in the area of advanced battery science and engineering. The state of SC has seen a large amount of private investment (>$10B) in battery development and manufacturing, which is expected to create 10,000+ jobs over the next decade. USC is building from our already strong team in this area (19 faculty) and supporting this industry through activities within the newly formed Carolina Institute for Battery Innovation (CIBI). Specific research areas of interest for this search include: i) electrochemical modeling, preferably including advanced machine learning and AI; ii) battery safety and reliability; iii) novel approaches to recycling; and iv) new chemistries and active materials.

jobs.title: Clinical Assistant Professor in Mental Health Counseling
jobs.institution: University of Rochester Warner School of Education and Human Development
jobs.description:
Job Details
The Warner Graduate School of Education and Human Development at the University of Rochester invites applications for a full-time Clinical Assistant Professor in Mental Health Counseling. We are seeking a candidate who excels at teaching, both in-person and online, and clinical supervision, in ways that promote culturally sustaining practices. The term of employment will begin on July 1, 2027.
The Clinical Mental Health Counseling program, which is part of the Department of Counseling and Human Development, is a 60-credit hour CACREP-accredited program. The program faculty seek to train ethical and competent professional counselors to diagnose and treat a variety of mental and emotional concerns and disorders. Our students can work with diverse clients, providing individual, couple, family, and group counseling in various settings. The program is designed to prepare graduates to work effectively as counselors offering services to people challenged by emotional, behavioral, and relationship issues. Well-grounded in counseling theory, research, and practice, our program prepares qualified, diversity-sensitive, license-eligible mental health counselors for practice.
The program faculty are productive, nationally and internationally recognized counselors, teachers, and scholars who are also committed to improving the quality of mental health counseling and the development of the counseling field. The department prepares scientific practitioners with diverse career and research interests and backgrounds. We have developed several online programs and courses at Warner as part of our commitment to enhancing learning opportunities for students and ensuring equitable access. The program, as well as the Warner School, is dedicated to producing and using research to enhance the effectiveness of mental health counseling processes and practices.
The Bridge program is an advanced certification pathway that allows Professional School Counselors to obtain LMHC licensure or Licensed Professional Counselors to obtain certification as a Professional School Counselor in New York State. This program offers hybrid and distance courses and is not CACREP-accredited.
The principal duties associated with this position are to:
Teach the equivalent of six graduate-level counseling courses using rigorous pedagogy that adheres to CACREP standards. Lead program recruitment efforts and interview program applicants. Provide program and career advising for master’s and doctoral candidates. Seek external funding to support program development, student success, and scholarship. Provide service/leadership to the department, Warner School, and Counseling profession. Collaborate with departmental and University partners to help build and sustain a thriving Counseling Center, help establish clinical operations, supervision structures, and community partnerships to support the Center's long-term success.
Ideal candidates for this position will have qualifications and experiences that include:
A Doctorate in Counselor Education & Supervision from a CACREP-accredited program with a specialization in REBT/CBT, Systems Theories, and/or Trauma-informed care (e.g., EMDR, TF-CBT, etc.). The doctoral degree must be earned before the position’s starting date. A master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from a CACREP-accredited program. A commitment to the preparation of strong mental health counselors, leaders, and scholars at both the master’s and doctoral levels. Demonstrated ability to utilize competency-driven pedagogy (e.g., experiential learning, case-based interventions, simulated learning environments, etc.) to facilitate students’ clinical and cultural competencies. A commitment to Meliora by collaborating with the department faculty and CACREP liaison to design and assess coursework using measurable learning outcomes, contributing to ongoing program evaluation and continuous improvement efforts. The potential to complement the expertise of our current faculty in counseling and human development. Eligible to be licensed as an LMHC-D counselor with New York State, with a clear professional identity as a Professional Counselor. Demonstrated commitment to strengthening educational resources, opportunities, and trajectories for diverse, historically marginalized students, families, and communities. An ability to use technology tools flexibly and inventively to create powerful synchronous and asynchronous learning experiences, both in-person and online. Experience providing clinical supervision and overseeing clinical practice or agency setting.
The mission of the Counseling Program at the Warner School of Education and Human Development is to educate counselors who will empower their clients and students to create more rewarding and meaningful lives and relationships; become more self-reflective, caring, and compassionate people; and contribute to reform of the systems in which their lives are embedded and to prepare counselor educators, researchers, practitioners, and leaders in the counseling profession who will educate the next generation of counselors to do all of the above; will contribute new knowledge in the fields of counseling, counselor education, and human development; and will be leaders in reforming educational and social systems to promote social justice, healthy human development, and quality relationships.
This mission is based on an ecological perspective of professional counseling that acknowledges the importance of personal development but also recognizes that individual lives are embedded in a variety of personal, extended relationships, and social systems.

jobs.title: Open Rank Faculty Position of Architecture - Architectural History and Theory
jobs.institution: Christopher C. Gibbs College of Architecture
jobs.description:
The University of Oklahoma’s Christopher C. Gibbs College of Architecture (GCA) is expanding to match the scale of its ambitions. Based in Norman, a lively college town within the Oklahoma City metropolitan area, which was recently ranked the “No. 1 Best Big City to Live In” by U.S. News & World Report, the Division of Architecture (DivA) seeks new faculty members to help shape the future of architectural education and practice. These positions reinforce OU’s university-wide commitment as an R-1 public research institution, fueled by growth in faculty excellence, research innovation, and cross-sector partnerships.
We invite applications for a 9-month, full-time, open-rank (Assistant, Associate, and/or Full Professor) tenure-track or tenured position beginning in August 2027. Review of applications will begin on October 12, 2026, and continue until the position is filled.
Who We’re Looking For
We seek an educator and historian whose teaching and research drives architectural ideas forward. Applicants should demonstrate a clear research trajectory that contributes to contemporary architectural discourse within and through a historical context. Candidates will join a faculty known for its experimental spirit and its legacy of the American School of Architecture. They will play an active role in seminars, lecture courses, and curriculum discussions across our Ph.D. and NAAB-accredited B.Arch and M.Arch programs.
Possible areas of investigation may include but are not limited to history of 20th Century architecture; architectural and urban design history since 1880, or similar. The successful applicant shall have access to wide-ranging resources including the incredible body of work produced by the architects of the American School now housed in the OU Libraries American School Archive.
Our Community
Faculty in the Division of Architecture foster a culture that connects design education with discovery and impact. They create new knowledge in the areas of placemaking and belonging, health and well-being, entrepreneurship and applied practice, and resilience and sustainability (https://ou.edu/gibbs/explore/research). The Institute for Quality Communities, host of the biennial national Placemaking Conference, connects faculty and students with communities across Oklahoma to shape civic life through design. Annual travel study in Rome, complemented with domestic travel programs, broaden students’ perspectives and deepen their design education through experiential learning. An award-winning Design+Build program and strong results in national student competitions, often in partnership with OU Construction Science, underscore our commitment to hands-on learning. The nationally recognized student journal Telesis reflects a tradition of intellectual creativity and rigor that extends beyond the classroom.
How Faculty Contribute
Faculty in the Division of Architecture play an active role in shaping a culture of creativity and impact. This includes:
Infusing energy and innovation through studio, seminar and lecture course teaching
Advancing scholarly and creative work through recognized venues
Contributing to the life of the division, college, and university through shared governance
Engaging with the profession and the public through meaningful service and outreach
What We Offer
The Division of Architecture and Gibbs College provide robust faculty support through:
Mentorship programs,
Research and travel funds, and
Teaching and research assistants, supported by the Gibbs Endowment and other resources.
About the Division of Architecture and the Christopher C. Gibbs College of Architecture
The Division of Architecture (DivA), which first began accepting students in 1926, and has a legacy of experimentation that began with Bruce Goff’s leadership in the mid-20th century, continues today in a culture of creativity and purposeful impact. The Christopher C. Gibbs College of Architecture brings together through in-person and online programs more than 1,300 students across seven disciplines: Architecture, Construction Science, Environmental Design, Interior Design, Landscape Architecture, Regional and City Planning, and Urban Design. The College serves as a hub for interdisciplinary collaboration and community engagement. Learn more at architecture.ou.edu/architecture.
About the University of Oklahoma
Founded in 1890, the University of Oklahoma (OU) is a Carnegie R1 Institution with over $500M in annual research expenditures and more than 34,000 students across online and three in-person campuses in Norman, Oklahoma City, and Tulsa. OU is advancing an ambitious vision to shape the future through discovery, creativity, and innovation as outlined in the Lead On, University Strategic Plan (https://ou.edu/leadon/strategic-plan).
Norman offers the atmosphere of a vibrant college town within the Oklahoma City metropolitan area. The region combines affordability with cultural vitality, strong K–12 schools, and nationally recognized works of architecture and landscape architecture. Home to the 2025 NBA champions and a host site for events during the 2028 Olympics, Oklahoma City reflects a growing international profile. Oklahoma’s 39 Native Nations shape a context where faculty and students engage in collaborative work that links design to place, culture, and community.
Visit https://ou.edu/facultyrecruitmentfor more information about what OU and the local communities have to offer.
Salary Range
Salary will be commensurate with qualifications and experience.
Search Committee Chairperson
Inquiries shall be directed to Dr. Wanda Liebermann RA, at wkliebermann@ou.edu
Qualifications
A PhD (or equivalent) in architectural history and theory, or similar field
Evidence of ability to successfully teach architectural history and theory seminars or lecture courses
Evidence or emerging research record of peer-reviewed scholarly productivity
Demonstrated ability to contribute to a collegial and collaborative working environment, in addition to possessing effective communication and interpersonal skills
Application Instructions
Applicants shall submit the following materials as PDF documents at https://apply.interfolio.com/192969.
Cover letter
Statement of interest outlining in two to three pages the applicant’s experience and research agenda
Current Curriculum Vitae
Full contact information for minimum three academic/professional references
Digital portfolio that provides evidence of 1) scholarly activity and 2) efficacy in teaching with examples of student work if applicable. Digital submission size should not exceed 100MB.
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
The University, in compliance with all applicable federal and state laws and regulations, does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, marital status, genetic information, gender identity/expression (consistent with applicable law), age (40 or older), religion, disability, political beliefs, or status as a veteran in any of its policies, practices, or procedures. This includes but is not limited to admissions, employment, housing, financial aid, and educational services.
Why You Belong at the University of Oklahoma
The University of Oklahoma values our community's unique talents, perspectives, and experiences. At OU, we aspire to harness our innovation, creativity, and collaboration for the advancement of people everywhere. You Belong Here!
Mission of the University of Oklahoma
The Mission of the University of Oklahoma is to provide the best possible educational experience for our students through excellence in teaching, research and creative activity, and service to the state and society.

Classification Title: Assistant Professor
Working Title: Assistant Professor of Management

To teach undergraduate and graduate classes in Management (face-to-face and online), specifically Management Fundamentals, Organizational Behavior, E-Bus Systems Fundamentals, Intro to Business Analytics and other management related courses to adequately provide a good foundation in Management, and to prepare students for many other classes within the department and the Lewis Bear Jr. College of Business. This position will teach three classes each fall and spring with a possible teaching assignment in the summer. This position will also serve on departmental, college, and university committees. This faculty member will maintain professional affiliations and contribute to professional activities. The person in this position must retain their scholarly academic qualifications. This position will mentor students and provide advice on professional endeavors.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:
Doctoral degree from an AACSB-accredited institution, in Management, or a closely related field (i.e., Organizational Behavior), with a strong commitment to teaching, academic research, and service. Pertinent work experience, continuing professional development and an active research agenda to maintain qualifications for performing teaching assignment are required. This faculty member will have relevant teaching experience which includes proven effectiveness in online course development and teaching. Must meet the Lewis Bear Jr. College of Business Policies on Faculty Qualification for an Assistant Professor position.
POSITION QUALIFICATIONS:
Doctoral degree from an AACSB-accredited institution, in Management, or a closely related field (i.e., Organizational Behavior), with a strong commitment to teaching, academic research, and service. Pertinent work experience, continuing professional development and an active research agenda to maintain qualifications for performing teaching assignment are required. This faculty member will have relevant teaching experience which includes proven effectiveness in online course development and teaching. Must meet the Lewis Bear Jr. College of Business Policies on Faculty Qualification for an Assistant Professor position.

A PhD from an AACSB-accredited institution, in Management, or a closely related field (i.e., Organizational Behavior). This position requires a criminal background screening.

Applicants are required to attach a cv, letter of interest and contact information for three references. References will be contacted upon submission of this application. An opportunity to upload these documents will be provided during the application process. For assistance, please contact Human Resources at 850.474.2694 or email jobs@uwf.edu.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Biochemistry - Neuroscience
jobs.description:
The Department of Biochemistry & Molecular Biology at the University of Massachusetts, Amherst invites applications for a full-time tenure-track position in Molecular and Cellular Neuroscience. We are seeking talented applicants qualified for an assistant professor position. Under exceptional circumstances, highly qualified candidates at other ranks may receive consideration. The successful candidate will also be a part of the Institute for Applied Life Sciences (IALS), which has a primary goal of developing translational research programs, fostering interactions with industry, and training of an applied life sciences workforce.
Essential Functions
We seek candidates with expertise in the molecular and cellular mechanisms of brain development, aging, and neurological disorders. We are especially interested in candidates who use molecular, biochemical, genetic, and cellular approaches applied to specific models and/or systems to investigate the nervous system and its translation to human health and disease. The successful candidate will complement and extend existing departmental strengths in synapse biology, learning and memory, and neurodegeneration. New faculty members will be able to take full advantage of the IALS substantial investments in campus infrastructure and core facilities (http://www.umass.edu/ials/core-facilities).
This is a full-time (9-month academic year) tenure-track position. The successful candidate must have outstanding potential to build a vibrant, externally funded, active research program, effectively teach and mentor undergraduate and graduate students, and contribute to service in support of the department and college.
Other Functions
Work collaboratively and effectively to promote teamwork, equality and inclusiveness.
Work in partnership with colleagues within the CNS community and across the campus to support the Dean’s strategic priorities.
Perform other duties as assigned in support of the mission and goals of the College of Natural Sciences.
Minimum Qualifications
We are seeking talented applicants qualified for an assistant professor position. Under exceptional circumstances, highly qualified candidates at other ranks may receive consideration. Candidates must have a Ph.D. or equivalent in Life Sciences or a related field with relevant post-doctoral experience.
Additional Details
At UMass Amherst and in CNS, we strive to be a community where every individual feels a sense of belonging, where every individual is included, and where every individual is valued. These values and goals are reflected in the College of Natural Sciences’ Inclusive Excellence framework and in the UMass Amherst’s For the Common Good: 2024–2034 Strategic Plan.
This position is subject to final budgetary and administrative approval.
Working Conditions
Work is performed in a standard office or indoor university environment and involves minimal physical exertion.
Work Schedule and Work Arrangement
Anticipated start date of September 1, 2027
Monday - Friday, 40 hours per week.
Salary Information
The University expects to pay within an approximate range between $79,350 and $125,349 for this position.
Please note:
The low end of this range is based on the minimum salary for the rank included in the collective bargaining agreement between the University and the Massachusetts Society of Professors, UMass Amherst/MTA/NEA. The high-end of the pay range reflects an increase above the median salaries at this rank within the department for faculty who may have multiple years of faculty experience. The specific pay for this position will be determined by the University based on consideration of all relevant factors, including faculty rank and required relevant certifications, when and if it decides to extend an offer of employment.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Agribusiness Management
jobs.description:
Assistant Professor of Agribusiness Management
POSITION SPECIFICS
The Department of Agricultural Economics, Sociology, and Education (AESE) in the College of Agricultural Sciences at The Pennsylvania State University (University Park campus) invites candidates to apply for an Assistant Professor of Agribusiness Management position. This is a full-time, 36-week, tenure-track appointment with a 60% teaching and 40% Extension appointment.
The successful candidate will be expected to teach five 3-credit courses per year in the Agribusiness Management (AGBM) undergraduate program. Most of these courses will be taught online via Penn State's World Campus program, though some may be taught in person at Penn State's University Park campus. Potential course topics include agricultural market and price analysis, agribusiness finance, managing the food system, food product marketing, and economic principles applied to agriculture and the food system. The successful candidate will be expected to advise and mentor undergraduate students, including professional development for future employment in industry.
The successful candidate will also be expected to develop a nationally and internationally recognized Extension program on agribusiness management that enhances the university's engagement with the agricultural industry in Pennsylvania. Pertinent Extension topics may include price and income risk management, agricultural products and markets, smart ag technologies, and related areas. The successful candidate will be expected to secure external funding to support their Extension program.
Qualifications: Doctorate in agricultural economics, agribusiness, or a related economics or business field. The successful candidate must have completed all degree requirements by the appointment date. Experience in agriculture, agribusiness, or the food industry is preferred. Applicants should demonstrate excellent communication skills and the ability to work in multi-disciplinary teams. The ability to engage professionally with an inclusive population of faculty, staff, students, and Extension audiences is required, and the successful candidate will actively strive to provide an inclusive learning environment for all.
Application Requirements: Review of applications will begin on December 1, 2026, with a start date of July 1, 2027, or as negotiated. Candidates should provide a cover letter, curriculum vitae, names and contact information for three references, a writing sample, a statement of teaching/pedagogy related to the position description, and a statement of Extension vision and philosophy related to the position description. System limitations allow for a total of 5 documents (5mb per document) as part of your application. Please combine materials to meet the 5-document limit.
Questions can be directed to the Search Committee chair: Ted Jaenicke (ecj3@psu.edu).
AESE is a welcoming community with our scholarship focusing on people, society, and economic systems grounded in theory and methods from the social, economic, and behavioral sciences. Faculty and students develop and employ rigorous approaches to discover fundamental and applied principles that advance science in their core disciplines. AESE strives to improve the health, prosperity, and welfare of people in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania and beyond. Our core areas for teaching and research are (1) Agricultural and Food Systems, (2) Community Development and Engagement, (3) Environment and Natural Resources, and (4) Population Processes in Global Perspective. The Department offers three resident and one online graduate programs and oversees four undergraduate majors. For more information visit our site at https://aese.psu.edu/.

jobs.description:
Assistant Professor of Technology Ethics and Global Security
Location: University of Notre Dame campus
Open Date:
Deadline:
Description: The Keough School of Global Affairs at the University of Notre Dame invites applications for a tenure-track position at the rank of Assistant Professor in Technology Ethics and Global Security, to begin in Fall 2027. This position will be affiliated with the McKenna Center for Human Development and Global Business, one of the Keough School's constituent institutes and centers. The successful candidate will also be appointed as an affiliated faculty member of Notre Dame's Institute for Ethics and the Common Good, which convenes a multidisciplinary community to advance moral understanding and develop compelling responses to the most pressing ethical issues of our era.
We seek candidates focusing on the ethical issues related to technology and conflict. Duties include research, teaching and service. We seek a scholar whose research examines the intersection of emerging technology and national security - including but not limited to nuclear weapons, artificial intelligence, autonomous and drone systems, biotechnology and bioweapons, and cybersecurity - through a lens that is both policy relevant and ethically grounded. The successful candidate will produce scholarship that speaks to policymakers, military and intelligence practitioners, and the broader public, while rigorously examining how these technologies bear on human welfare, human dignity, and the norms that govern the use of force.
About the Keough School and the McKenna Center
The Keough School of Global Affairs is Notre Dame's home for the interdisciplinary study of global affairs, with a mission to advance integral human development - the promotion of every person and the whole person - through research, teaching, and policy engagement. The school unites scholars across international relations, ethics, human rights, and development, and maintains a Washington, D.C. office to connect research with policy practice.
The McKenna Center for Human Development and Global Business examines the role of business, technology, and innovation in reducing poverty and inequality and in advancing integral human development worldwide. The center supports faculty and student research that bridges rigorous scholarship with practical, real-world application.
Qualifications:
Competitive candidates for this professorship will have a scholarly track record with evidence of, or potential for, high-quality research and, ideally, policy engagement in global and national discussions on ethical issues related to the use of technology in warfare and conflict. A PhD from any discipline is acceptable with a preference for business, computer science, economics, philosophy, political science, public policy, science and technology studies, or sociology. Regardless of discipline the candidate's research should include deep expertise on the intersection between ethics and technology. ABD candidates will be considered for an entry level position.
The University of Notre Dame seeks to recruit and retain a diverse workforce as a reflection of our commitment to our Catholic tradition, to maintain the excellence of the University, and to offer our students richly varied disciplines, perspectives and ways of knowing and learning. The Keough School is committed to fostering a culture of diverse views and approaches to Global Affairs. We welcome candidates whose experience in teaching, research, or service has prepared them to contribute to our mission and commitment to diversity and excellence. All applicants whose scholarly pursuits will enhance our ability to fulfill that commitment are encouraged to apply.
To apply, visit https://apply.interfolio.com/192061
This appointment is contingent upon the successful completion of a background check. Applicants will be asked to identify all felony convictions and/or pending felony charges. Felony convictions do not automatically bar an individual from employment. Each case will be examined separately to determine the appropriateness of employment in the particular position. Failure to be forthcoming or dishonesty with respect to felony disclosures can result in the disqualification of a candidate. The full procedure can be viewed at https://facultyhandbook.nd.edu/?id=link-73597.

The University of Notre Dame seeks to attract, develop, and retain the highest quality faculty, staff and administration. The University is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national or ethnic origin, sex, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or age in employment. Moreover, Notre Dame prohibits discrimination against veterans or disabled qualified individuals, and complies with 41 CFR 60-741.5(a) and 41 CFR 60-300.5(a). We strongly encourage applications from candidates attracted to a university with a Catholic identity.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Precision Agriculture
jobs.description:
Assistant Professor of Precision Agriculture
Kaskaskia College, Centralia, Illinois
Build a program from the ground up. Kaskaskia College is launching a new Precision Agriculture major and looking for a founding faculty member to shape it. This is a rare opportunity to design the curriculum, choose the technology stack, set the program's direction, and establish partnerships with regional agribusiness and school districts, rather than stepping into an existing framework.
Centralia sits in the heart of Southern Illinois farm country, surrounded by row-crop, livestock, and specialty-crop operations, making it an ideal region to build a precision agriculture program with real industry demand and real student outcomes.
The Assistant Professor of Precision Agriculture will teach precision agriculture and related courses, develop pathways and curriculum, and work directly with industry to ensure the program reflects where the field is headed, not where it's been. This is a full-time, nine-month academic year faculty position in the Career and Technical Education division.
What you'll shape:
Curriculum design and course development for a new program, including short-term certificates and competency-based education options
Selection and integration of instructional technology, UAS operations, yield monitors, field mapping, remote sensing, and data platforms
Partnerships with regional agriculture employers, K-12 districts, and community organizations
Program identity and growth strategy from day one
Required qualifications:
Certification and/or credential in precision agriculture
Minimum of 2,000 hours of non-teaching, relevant work experience in precision agriculture
FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate, or ability to obtain one by June 30, 2027
Hands-on experience with precision agriculture technologies, including UAS, yield monitors, field mapping, remote sensing, and data collection
Commitment to student-centered, technology-enabled instruction across face-to-face, online, hybrid, and blended formats
Strong communication, organization, and presentation skills
Ability to work independently and build collaborative relationships across the college
Commitment to the community college mission
Preferred qualifications:
Bachelor's degree or higher in precision agriculture or a closely related field
Prior teaching experience
Compensation and benefits:
Salary range $51,818 to $117,210 annually.
Benefits include 10 days of sick leave and 3 days of personal leave per fiscal year, health insurance effective the first of the month after hire (medical, vision, and dental through Blue Cross Blue Shield of Illinois, employee-only rate $303/month), employer-provided life insurance equal to annual salary, flexible spending accounts, 403(b) plans, State Universities Retirement System participation, tuition waivers for staff and family, and a childcare discount.
Location: Centralia is about an hour from St. Louis, giving faculty easy access to a major metro area while living in a rural, affordable community.
Kaskaskia College is an AA/EEO employer and welcomes applications from individuals who would enhance the diversity of the college.
