jobs.title: Assistant Professor - Tenure Track, Coastal Ecology
jobs.institution: UNC Department of Earth, Marine and Environmental Sciences
jobs.description:
The Department of Earth, Marine and Environmental Sciences (EMES) at UNC Chapel Hill is seeking a tenure-track faculty member at the Assistant Professor level in Coastal Marine Ecology who will be based at the Institute of Marine Sciences (IMS) in Morehead City, NC.
We seek candidates to develop an innovative and collaborative research program in estuarine and coastal ecology with a strong emphasis on field research and experiential learning. Potential areas of research focus include, but are not limited to community ecology, integrative conservation ecology, plankton ecology, fisheries ecology and marine apex predators. We welcome candidates who use molecular techniques, novel sensors and/or quantitative analysis to address fundamental questions in coastal marine ecology. The successful candidate will develop a world-class research program, teach undergraduate and graduate courses that support EMES and Environment, Ecology & Energy Program (E3P) majors and minors, including the Morehead City IE Field site, and pursue external funding. The position will be based at the Institute of Marine Sciences, located in Morehead City, NC, an essential facility and integral part of the Earth Marine and Environmental Sciences (https://emes.unc.edu/) department and many other departments at UNC-Chapel Hill. IMS offers immediate access to local ecosystems and is embedded within a collaborative network of nearby universities (i.e., North Carolina State University’s Center for Marine Sciences and Technology, Duke University Marine Lab), state (NC Division of Marine Fisheries) and federal (NOAA Beaufort Lab) research and management institutions. Infrastructure includes a 50,000-sqft office and laboratory complex, 5,500-sqft wet lab, 6,000-sqft machine shop, 25,000-sqft outdoor mesocosm farm, and 2,250-sqft dormitory. IMS maintains a fleet of trucks/vans and research vessels (17-48’), an AAUS-certified dive program as well as the US’s longest longline shark survey. Research, teaching, outreach and service to the state are important components of the mission of IMS “to conduct cutting-edge research, train young scientists, provide expertise to governmental agencies and industry, and to promote new knowledge to inform public policy.” For more information about IMS, please visit http://ims.unc.edu/.
Complete applications should include a cover letter, curriculum vitae (CV), the names and contact information of four references, and teaching and research statements. Submit application online using https://unc.peopleadmin.com/postings/325187. Applicants who are also interested in the Biological Oceanography position on the main campus of UNC at Chapel Hill should submit separate applications for each position. Applications for both positions will be accepted through November 16, 2026.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor - Tenure Track, Biological Oceanography
jobs.institution: UNC Department of Earth, Marine and Environmental Sciences
jobs.description:
The Department of Earth, Marine and Environmental Sciences (EMES) at UNC-Chapel Hill is seeking a tenure-track faculty member at the Assistant Professor level in Biological Oceanography who will be on our main campus in Chapel Hill.
We seek innovative candidates who investigate the distribution, abundance, diversity, and interactions of marine organisms across spatial and temporal scales, and who examine how these dynamics influence marine ecosystem function, resilience, and global biogeochemical cycles. We welcome candidates whose research addresses fundamental questions in marine ecology and oceanography using field-based, experimental, observational, computational, and/or integrative approaches.
Potential areas of research include, but are not limited to, marine food web dynamics, plankton ecology, biodiversity and community structure, coastal and ocean ecosystem processes, organism-environment interactions, fisheries, and biological responses to environmental change. We especially encourage candidates who employ innovative interdisciplinary approaches that bridge biological oceanography with related fields, including marine biogeochemistry, physical oceanography, environmental genomics, remote sensing, ecological modeling, and/or data science (AI and machine learning). We are particularly interested in candidates whose research programs will foster strong collaborations within EMES and leverage the department’s existing strengths to advance understanding of marine ecosystems in a changing world.
The successful candidate is expected to develop and maintain a vibrant, externally funded research program and contribute to the department’s mission of training the next generation of marine and environmental scientists. The candidate will teach undergraduate and graduate courses that support our EMES (https://emes.unc.edu/) and Environment, Ecology & Energy Program (https://e3p.unc.edu) majors and minors, incorporating experiential and research-based learning opportunities that build practical skills in field sampling, experimental design, quantitative analysis, data management, and scientific communication. The successful candidate is also expected to mentor graduate students conducting Biological Oceanography research and is encouraged to connect teaching and research to North Carolina systems.
In addition to excellent campus-based resources, EMES offers field, laboratory, and experimental infrastructure through its Institute of Marine Sciences (https://emes.unc.edu/ims/) located in Morehead City, providing campus-based faculty with direct access to diverse coastal habitats, long-term environmental monitoring resources, and an AAUS scientific diving program.
Complete applications should include a cover letter, curriculum vitae (CV), the names and contact information of four references, and teaching and research statements. Submit application online using https://unc.peopleadmin.com/postings/325186.
Applicants who are also interested in the Coastal Ecology position at IMS should submit separate applications for each position. Applications for both positions will be accepted through November 16, 2026.

jobs.description:
Description
The NYU Wagner Graduate School of Public Service is seeking highly qualified candidates for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Management and Public Service position with an expected start date of August 2027. The school seeks candidates who have completed their doctoral program or post-doctoral appointment by the start date or are two years or less into an Assistant Professor position. We will consider candidates from a wide range of fields but are especially interested in candidates with a PhD or DBA in Management / Organizational Behavior, Strategy, Healthcare Management, Organizational Sociology, Personnel Economics, and Public Administration. Applications should demonstrate a strong record, or evidence of strong potential, for publishing innovative, rigorous research that is relevant to public service organizations and fields in top-rated academic journals.
In compliance with NYC's Pay Transparency Act, the annual base salary range for this position is $125, 000 - $145,000.
NYU Wagner
NYU Wagner's mission is to educate and support the next generation of public service leaders and pursue interdisciplinary and impactful research on complex public interest challenges. We seek candidates with demonstrated excellence in research and teaching, and a commitment to institutional service.
The candidate would be joining Wagner’s 30+ full-time faculty members who are trained in a wide variety of disciplines including: management, healthcare management, sociology, economics, public policy, social entrepreneurship, financial management and public finance, political science, and urban planning. NYU Wagner confers the following degrees: MPA in Public & Nonprofit Management & Policy, MPA in Health Policy & Management, Master of Urban Planning, Online Master of Health Administration, Master of Science in Health Law and Strategy, Master of Science in Public Policy, Executive MPA, PhD in Public Administration, and a variety of dual degrees for NYU graduates and undergraduates.
The candidate will specifically join the current management faculty at Wagner, including tenure-track faculty (Thomas D’Aunno, Patricia Satterstrom), clinical faculty (Martha Stark, Judy Pryor Ramirez, Carla Jackie Sampson, Jacob Victory) and highly regarded adjunct faculty.
Our faculty share a commitment to addressing issues of public importance in their teaching and research and to supporting and mentoring colleagues and students. They collaborate with other schools and departments across the university, including the Leonard N. Stern School of Business, School of Global Public Health, Rory Meyers College of Nursing, School of Law, Tandon School of Engineering, and Departments of Sociology, History, Economics, and Politics, among others.
Research & Teaching Areas
We seek scholars whose work addresses how organizations function today and how they will function in the years ahead; how new technologies and systems are reshaping the way work gets done and how people relate to one another inside and across organizations; how people lead with particular grounding in public and cross-sector settings — especially the sectors where many of our students build careers, including healthcare, education, government, advocacy, urban policy, consulting, and impact investing, domestically and internationally. We welcome scholars who do qualitative, quantitative, experimental, and simulation work. Content areas that are particularly important for our school include:
Innovation and technology: Research on how to lead, manage, and support innovation and organizational learning amidst accelerated technological changes and new collaboration structures
Leading and negotiating wisely and ethically: Research on how people – particularly in sectors of interest to us – make decisions, negotiate, and create ethical frameworks in complex, real-world settings. Ideally with an eye toward overcoming systemic and interpersonal biases.
Social movements and power: Research on the strategy, management, and power at the heart of organizing and social movements, and community-based organizations — how organizers build and structure coalitions, mobilize resources and people, exercise power and influence within and across institutions, and translate sustained effort into durable social change.
Cross-organization, cross-sector, and cross-national leadership: Research on how people lead, manage, and work between organizations, across sectors, and across countries. Ideally with an eye on how to cultivate sustainable collaborations.
Policy implementation and organizational performance: Research on what happens after a policy is passed — the processes, structures, networks, and jobs that are created or reshaped. This area could also look at how changes and performance are managed, evaluated, and measured.
Organizational and human resources: Research on organizational change, organizational structures, understanding difference and creating conditions for inclusive and thriving cultures; career development and talent management are also of interest.
We seek candidates who bring a demonstrated commitment to excellence in the classroom. We are particularly interested in candidates who create active-learning classroom cultures that foster student agency and personal investment in the material. We seek candidates who have a commitment to, and experience or evidence of the potential for success in teaching a diverse population of students in one of the most diverse cities in the U.S. A new hire would carry a share of our core management and leadership courses (e.g., Management & Leadership, Strategy, Human Resources and Job Design, Performance Management & Measurement) and electives across our Master’s, mid-career, and executive formats, bringing actual organizational problems into the classroom in support of Wagner's effort to prepare students to lead in real-world settings.
Benefits
NYU offers a competitive benefits package for full-time employees. This includes comprehensive medical, dental, vision, and life insurance coverage, robust retirement plans, and flexible spending accounts. NYU provides all full-time employees with access to wellness and assistance programs, including free access to health care advocacy. NYU also provides subsidies for back-up child and elder care and commuter benefits. For full-time faculty with eligible dependent children, 90% of NYU tuition is waived for undergraduate degree programs. Portable tuition benefits for eligible children attending other institutions are also available.
Qualifications
PhD or DBA in Management / Organizational Behavior, Strategy, Healthcare Management, Organizational Sociology, Personnel Economics, Public Administration, or a related field.
Application Instructions
Candidates should submit the following information by October 5, 2026 for full consideration on Interfolio:
Curriculum Vitae (CV)
Cover letter

Research Statement
Teaching Statement, including all teaching evaluations
Three letters of recommendation
(Optional) Additional Research Papers
Note: Placeholder documents are not acceptable and will make your application incomplete. Please do not submit or update material via email.
Initial interviews will be conducted over Zoom. Finalists will be invited to visit in the fall semester.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor - Music
jobs.description:
Job Details
The Hamline University Division of Arts seeks a collaborative musician-educator to join our faculty as a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor of Music in an innovative curriculum that blends music production and performance. This position is designed for a versatile performer and technologist who is comfortable crossing stylistic borders and blending and bridging genres and traditions.
The successful candidate will join a dedicated cohort of faculty focused on a holistic approach to modern music-making. This position requires classroom and studio teaching in areas of history/culture, performance, digital music technologies, and directing an ensemble in their area of expertise. The successful candidate will have a performance specialty - vocal, strings, wood/brass/wind, or piano - and experience with both live performance and making music in the box and in the studio.
Primary Responsibilities
Classroom Teaching: The successful candidate will contribute their individual strengths and interests to teaching in the core curriculum of the Music Production Major. This may include teaching subjects in contemporary and traditional music history and theory, composition/song-writing, digital technology, and performance courses.
Ensemble Direction: Direct/conduct one or more of the following ensembles: choir, orchestra, band, jazz band, modern or hybrid pop/acoustic/electronic orchestra.
Software and Technology Instruction: Teach courses that integrate assignments using digital music technology (preferably Logic Pro) with practical instruction in gain staging, foundational audio engineering, and basic audio and MIDI editing and programming.
Program Support: Participate in curricular development, assessment, recruitment and departmental service as an engaged member of the music faculty team.
OPTIONAL Performance Instruction: Provide studio instruction in primary area (vocal, instrumental or composition), focusing on technical development, inclusive repertoire, and applications in traditional and contemporary performance settings.
Required Qualifications:
Terminal Degree: A PhD, DMA or MFA in Music (Performance, Composition, Music Production, or other relevant specialty) from an accredited college or university or completed ABD by July 31, 2027 (Required at time of appointment)
Performance: Active performer at the professional level
Music Technology: Competent skills in DAWs (strong preference for Logic Pro) and a foundation in audio hardware (signal flow, interfaces, experience with microphone use as part of live performance and music recording.).
Classroom Teaching Experience: A proven record of successful classroom teaching at the high school or collegiate level, minimum 5 years.
Collaboration: A demonstrated ability to work effectively with a team, academic or professional, and contribute to a shared vision and mission.
Community-oriented: Professional or pedagogical work connecting with diverse communities outside of academia.
Ensemble Leadership: Experience building, maintaining and directing traditional or contemporary ensembles.
Professional Portfolio: Evidence of commitment to ongoing creative activity as a performer, sound designer/composer, and/or producer.
Interdisciplinary Interest: Experience working across genres, collaborations across disciplines, theater, digital media, creative writing, as well as subjects outside of the arts.
Application Materials
Cover Letter: Please highlight your experience working within a faculty or professional team, teaching students with a wide range of interests, and connecting your work with the greater community.
Curriculum Vitae
Digital Portfolio: Links to recordings or videos that demonstrate:
Professional performance (Vocal or Instrumental).
Representative production work (recordings, Logic Pro projects or mixed tracks).
Optional but encouraged: Video of ensemble conducting, rehearsal leadership, or teaching demo.
Statement of Teaching Philosophy.
List of Three Professional References. Optional Student Reference
Our Program's Guiding Principles: We believe that successful careers in music will increasingly require our students to graduate with a panoply of skills and experiences. Hamline's Major in Music Production develops individual and collaborative skills in live performance, digital sound production, and music composition/design, as well as strong foundations in music history/culture and theory. The music curriculum is greatly enhanced by Hamline's nationally recognized liberal arts program with abundant opportunities for interdisciplinary experience. We are looking for a colleague who is able and eager to contribute their specific expertise to this growing, multi-faceted program.

Tenure Track Assistant Professor Positions
University of Southern California
Suzanne Dworak-Peck School of Social Work
Start Date: August 2027
About the USC Suzanne Dworak-Peck School of Social Work
The Suzanne Dworak-Peck School of Social Work at the University of Southern California (USC) invites applicants to apply for a tenure-track faculty position at the assistant professor level to join a community of scholars dedicated to social work research, education, and community partnerships.
Our School and University are located in the heart of Los Angeles, one of the largest, most diverse, and culturally rich cities in the United States. Our faculty pursues research and scholarship to catalyze positive social impact and enhance the well-being of individuals, families, and communities. Research opportunities and collaborations are enhanced through seven research centers and institutes, two clinical centers, and transdisciplinary collaborations with the schools of medicine, gerontology, pharmacy, policy, engineering, education, and liberal arts, among others. Partnerships with community-based stakeholders including health care providers, programs serving justice-involved youth, public child welfare and mental health providers are also central to our work as a School. In fall 2026, the school welcomed incoming Dean Laura Abrams and launched our BSW program. We seek to grow our tenure-track faculty to enhance our local, national, and global scholarly impact.
About the Positions
To complement our existing strengths and further advance social work scholarship, we seek candidates with substantive focus and research and teaching experience in at least one of three areas: 1) social welfare policy and analysis; particularly focusing on poverty, the welfare state, and children and families; 2) child welfare policy or practice; and/or 3) technology, AI, and the future of social work. Across all areas, we welcome scholarship focused on the experiences of Black communities in the US and/or other racial and ethnic minority groups. Methodologically, we encourage applications from scholars with training in causal inference, experimental designs, and big data analytic approaches.
We also welcome candidates who are interested in forging interdisciplinary collaborations with allied disciplines across the USC campus, such as the health sciences, public policy, and others. All candidates must demonstrate exceptional promise or evidence of impactful scientific research and publications.
Assistant professor positions require on-campus presence as candidates will teach in our range of educational programs, including MSW, BSW, PhD, Doctor of Social Work (DSW), and Doctor of Social Innovation (DSI). Applicants should describe their portfolio of experience and excellence in teaching in social work. Candidates are required to have an MSW degree from a CSWE-accredited university and a PhD in social work/welfare or a related field. Two-years of post-MSW practice experience is preferred.
Application Procedure
To be considered for this position, candidates must submit application materials online at https://usccareers.usc.edu/job/los-angeles/tenure-track-assistant-professor-positions/1209/100143263472. A complete application will include: 1) a cover letter describing their interest in the position and an overview of their research and teaching experiences, 2) a curriculum vitae, and 3) contact information for three professional references who can provide letters of recommendation. Review of applications will begin in fall 2026. Applications will be considered until position(s) are filled.
The annual base salary range for this position is $110,000-$130,000 based on a nine-month contract. When extending an offer of employment, USC considers factors such as (but not limited to) the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate’s work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, federal, state and local laws, contractual stipulations, grant funding, as well as external market and organizational considerations.
USC is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law or USC policy. USC observes affirmative action obligations consistent with state and federal law.
USC will consider for employment all qualified applicants with criminal records in a manner consistent with applicable laws and regulations, including the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for employers and the Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, and with due consideration for patient and student safety.
We provide reasonable accommodations to applicants and employees with disabilities. Applicants with questions about access or requiring a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application or hiring process should contact USC Human Resources by phone at (213) 821-8100, or by email at uschr@usc.edu. Inquiries will be treated as confidential to the extent permitted by law.
All other questions and information requests should be directed to the Office of Faculty Affairs in the USC Suzanne Dworak-Peck School of Social Work at ssw.facultyaffairs@usc.edu. The search committee chair is Dr. Ben Henwood, the Frances L. and Albert G. Feldman Professor of Social Policy and Health.

University of California, Davis Assistant Professor of Philosophy and Linguistics
The Departments of Philosophy and Linguistics at the University of California, Davis invite applications for a joint tenure-track position at the rank of Assistant Professor, specializing in research questions at the intersection of philosophy of language and theoretical/computational linguistics. A successful candidate is expected to be active in both departments. The anticipated start date is July 1, 2027.
We seek a scholar whose research and teaching bridge philosophy, linguistics, and modern computational methods, including formal (symbolic) models, neural language models, and other formal or computational systems. We welcome candidates working on areas such as: semantics and pragmatics, morphology and syntax of natural languages, philosophy of linguistics, language evolution and change, AI interpretability or alignment, and computational models of communication. We are especially interested in candidates whose work addresses how meaning, reasoning, linguistic structure, or grammar is represented and processed in generative AI systems.
The successful candidate will hold a joint appointment in the Department of Philosophy and the Department of Linguistics and will be expected to develop a robust, externally fundable research program alongside a strong record of teaching and mentorship at both the undergraduate and graduate levels. The successful candidate will contribute to core curricula in both departments, and the Cognitive Science program. Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in Philosophy, Linguistics, Cognitive Science, Computer Science, or a closely related field by the start of the appointment. Candidates should demonstrate strong potential for excellence in research and teaching at the intersection of philosophy, linguistics, and computational/AI methods.
Applicants should submit: curriculum vitae, a cover letter that clearly states reasons for the candidate’s interest in the position, qualifications, and a summary of academic trajectory; statements of research and teaching interests, official graduate transcripts, one writing sample (publication, submitted manuscript, or dissertation chapter), and three letters of recommendation through the online application system found at: https://recruit.ucdavis.edu/JPF07874.
This recruitment is conducted at the Assistant rank. The resulting hire will be at the Assistant rank, regardless of the proposed appointee’s qualifications. Appointment level and salary are commensurate with experience. A reasonable estimate for this position is $117,000 to $143,700. The position will remain open until filled. Applications received by November 15, 2026 will receive full initial consideration. The Department of Management and Entrepreneurship houses a diverse, multi-disciplinary and research-active faculty who support undergraduate and graduate programs in business analytics, human resource management, entrepreneurship, general management, supply chain management, and sustainability management. Faculty publish in leading journals including Academy of Management Journal, Academy of Management Review, Strategic Management Journal, Journal of Management, Leadership Quarterly, Journal of Business Venturing, and Entrepreneurship Theory and Practice, among others. Many of the department's faculty also support the college's rigorous Doctorate in Business Administration program. The department is also home to the Coleman Center for Entrepreneurship. A number of active student groups are affiliated with the department.
Located in the center of Chicago's downtown, DePaul's Driehaus College of Business immerses students in one of the world's great business centers to provide transformative, hands-on educational experiences. Enrolling over 5,400 students, Driehaus's undergraduate and graduate programs are highly ranked and nationally recognized. Founded in 1912, Driehaus was among the first 10 business colleges in the United States and the first at an American Catholic university. The Driehaus mission is to empower students to become socially responsible leaders who make an impact in their communities. Guided by our Catholic and Vincentian values and aided by our deep roots in the City of Chicago, we deliver a cutting-edge business education, generate pathbreaking research, and collaborate closely with our community and industry partners to drive positive social outcomes. Visit https://business. depaul.edu/Pages/default.aspx
Applicants will be asked to submit a CV, cover letter, teaching statement, research statement, sample publications, teaching evaluations, and contact information for references. The position will remain open until filled and review of applications will begin immediately. Applications received by September 30th will receive full consideration.
Questions about the position should be emailed to Dr. Rich Devine (Search Committee Chair) at rdevine2@depaul.edu.
Qualifications
The required qualifications are a Doctoral degree in Strategic Management or related field. ABD candidates will be considered. Prior university teaching experience in areas of strategic management, business policy, or corporate strategy is preferred. Candidates with industry experience are welcome.
Application Instructions
Candidates will need to submit the following materials as a part of their application:
A cover letter stating interest and qualification A curriculum vitae Research Statement Teaching Statement Teaching evaluations, if applicable Sample publications, if applicable Contact information for three professional references. Confidential letters of recommendation may be requested from those individuals. General Compensation/Benefits Statement
DePaul University has provided a compensation range that represents its good faith estimate of what the University may pay for the position at the time of posting. The salary offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on factors such as (but not limited to) the qualifications, education, experience, and training of the selected candidate, the scope and responsibilities of the position, departmental budget availability, internal salary equity considerations, and available market information.
DePaul University offers excellent benefits, including medical, dental, retirement, paid time off, and tuition benefit. Further information regarding benefits can be found here: https://offices.depaul.edu/human-resources/benefits/Pages/default.aspx.
About DePaul University's Academic Calendar
Except for the College of Law, DePaul University operates on a quarter system. Classes in Autumn, Winter, and Spring quarters are 11 weeks in length (including finals week) and Summer courses, in two sessions, are typically 5 weeks in length. The College of Law operates on the semester system. Classes in the Fall and Spring semesters are 16 weeks in length (including finals week) and it offers a Summer Session of 7 weeks (including final exams).
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
DePaul University is an Equal Opportunity employer with a strong commitment to hiring for our mission and diversifying our faculty and staff. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion (except where religion is a bona fide occupational qualification for the job), national origin, sex, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, protected veteran status or any other factor protected by law.
DePaul University and Our Mission
As an innovative Catholic, Vincentian university anchored in the global city of Chicago, DePaul supports the integral human development of its students. The university does so through its commitment to outstanding teaching, academic excellence, real-world experience, and community engagement. DePaul prepares its graduates to be successful in their chosen fields and agents of transformation throughout their lives.
Guided by an ethic of Vincentian personalism and professionalism, DePaul passionately upholds the dignity of all members of its diverse, multi-faith, and inclusive community. Through education, creative endeavors, and research, the university addresses the great questions of our day, promoting peaceful, just, and equitable solutions to social and environmental challenges. Since its founding in 1898, DePaul University has remained dedicated to making education accessible to all, with special attention to including underserved and underrepresented communities.
Comprised of ten colleges and schools, offering 130+ undergraduate majors and 170+ graduate programs, DePaul’s faculty challenges its students to analyze and solve real-world problems with rigor and innovation.
As an urban faith-based institution with a diverse student body, DePaul is committed to growing and maintaining a faculty dedicated to advancing the Vincentian mission through research, teaching, and service. DePaul upholds a fair and equitable recruitment, interview, and hiring process where supporting diverse populations and academic excellence are compatible goals. Our vibrant and diverse faculty is supported through academic and professional development resources. Successful candidates thrive and are at home in an environment where diverse cultures and identities, ideas, backgrounds, and experiences are welcomed and supported.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Computing - Tenure Track
jobs.description:
Job Details
Franklin College invites applications for a tenure-track position in Computing at the Assistant Professor level to begin August 2027. Located about 20 miles from downtown Indianapolis, Franklin College offers a strong, tailored liberal arts education through small class sizes and intentional faculty-student mentoring. The computer science and software engineering curricula emphasize career-connected learning through a variety of hands-on projects. The senior-year software development project, in which students develop full software solutions for real-world clients, is a hallmark of the computer science and software engineering majors. The department’s recent initiatives include the creation of new majors in data science and cybersecurity, as well as a game development track for its software engineering major.
The successful candidate will demonstrate a strong commitment to engaged, student-centered teaching and learning as well as a sincere interest in working with undergraduates in a supportive liberal arts environment. jobs.title: Professor(s) of Digital and Computational Studies
jobs.description:
Job Details
The Program in Digital and Computational Studies at Bates College invites applications for two full-time, open-rank, tenure-line positions in Computer Science, beginning July, 2027. We seek outstanding scholars with a strong commitment to excellent undergraduate teaching and mentorship in a liberal arts environment, and who will help to deepen the discipline of computer science in an interdisciplinary computing program. Candidates should have a Ph.D. in Computer Science, completed no later than 01 July 2027.
While areas of expertise are open, the successful candidates will have a demonstrated commitment to interdisciplinary computing in the liberal arts, in research areas which may include, but are not limited to: human computer interaction (HCI), artificial intelligence / machine learning (AI/ML), natural language processing (NLP), and disciplinary-based computer science education. We are especially interested in candidates who will add to the existing breadth of the DCS faculty. Successful candidates will have a demonstrated interest in teaching undergraduate students and supporting a diversity of students in computing with a range of prior programming experience (including none). Successful candidates will also have a demonstrated commitment to collaboration and collegiality. They will also demonstrate interest in collaboratively building an interdisciplinary and inclusive computing program for the liberal arts.
The anticipated salary range for this position is $87,000–$135,000, commensurate with rank, experience, qualifications, and other relevant factors. As an open-rank tenure-line search, the appointment may be made at the assistant professor, associate professor, or full professor level. The final salary offer will reflect the candidate’s academic experience, record of professional achievement, and the rank at which the appointment is made.
Digital & Computational Studies (DCS) is an interdisciplinary program that seeks to build bridges between core elements of computer science, data science, and digital studies, connecting to the arts, humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, and other existing interdisciplinary programs on campus. DCS teaches students to design, build, and analyze digital & computational tools and algorithms, while also developing the ability to critique those same tools and algorithms. Bates DCS faculty are prepared to support candidates as they develop courses designed for an interdisciplinary program.
The position carries a standard five-course teaching load either as a 2-3 or 3-2 across two semesters, or as a 2-2-1 across two semesters and the Bates Short Term. Faculty responsibilities include teaching, professional achievement, and governance and engagement, as described in Article II of the Bates College Faculty Handbook. Successful candidates will contribute to inclusive and evidence-based teaching, maintain an active program of scholarship or creative work, and participate in the life and governance of the College.
The successful candidates will teach introductory computer science sequences in Python (e.g. DCS 109X, DCS 229 Data Structures, and DCS 211 Computing for Insight), and other upper level computing courses based on their area(s) of expertise. They will also regularly teach the DCS senior capstone course; contribute to the general education curriculum, including teaching our college-wide First Year Seminar program; advise senior theses, and serve as an academic advisor.
Review of applications will begin on October 15, 2026 and continue until the position is filled.
Required application materials should include:
A Cover letter which addresses how candidates envision their research and teaching Digital and Computational Studies at Bates; A Curriculum vitae A Teaching statement describing an approach to teaching the introductory computer science sequence, and identifying courses currently offered as well as new courses that candidates would be interested in developing. This statement should also describe how the candidates will meet Bates’ standards in terms of inclusive and evidence-based pedagogy. A Research statement describing a five-year plan for research at a small liberal arts college, and mentoring undergraduate research.
We seek candidates who are committed to supporting the success of all students. Applicants are encouraged to describe relevant preparation, experience or plans for creating an inclusive learning environment.
Letters of recommendation will be requested only for candidates selected to move forward after the initial review. Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check and verification of degree.
Faculty scholarship and creative work at Bates are robustly supported by start-up packages, a paid pre-tenure leave, support for post-tenure sabbaticals, internal grants, professional travel funding, and a well-staffed external grants office. Community-engaged learning—with community partnerships facilitated by the Harward Center for Community Partnerships—and study abroad are both broadly encouraged and institutionally supported. Pedagogical development and innovation is further buttressed by our highly engaged Center for Inclusive Teaching and Learning. Educational access and racial justice are central to Bates’ history and mission and our faculty-led initiatives reflect this commitment.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor - American Studies and Global Studies
jobs.description:
The Department of American Studies (AMST) and the Institute for Global Studies (IGS) at the University of Minnesota-Twin Cities invite applications for a joint tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor, with an anticipated start date of August 31, 2027. We seek a transnational American Studies scholar of comparative and multi-sited Global Souths (especially Latin America, and/or Southeast Asia, and/or the U.S. South) whose interdisciplinary research draws on settler colonial studies and relational race/ethnic studies in order to consider the legacies of the U.S.’s political role in the global flows and functions of race, empire, war, colonialism, and capital in the twentieth century and twenty-first centuries . We are particularly interested in a scholar with expertise in environmental humanities, critical refugee studies (with an emphasis on Southeast Asia), and/or transoceanic studies who looks at how agribusiness (principally, farming and fisheries), technology, and/or cultural objects and materials inform (and are informed by) those and other processes (like diaspora, nation-state formation, and refugee lifeworlds/deathworlds). Thus, we seek a scholar whose work explores histories of wartime counterinsurgency networks in the Global South and the ways that they shape contemporary (broadly construed) landscapes and discourses of structures like the nation, policing, surveillance, border enforcement, displacement, dispossession, and forced migration in the United States.
Preferred candidates will be scholars whose research substantively engages with studies of race, gender, class, sexuality, and/or disability; who have a background in interdisciplinary studies (i.e., American Studies); who have evidence of interest in digital humanities; and whose work holds promise to resonate with Twin Cities metro histories and communities.
Faculty are expected to maintain an active research program that includes publication, teach courses in area(s) of specialty as well as core American Studies curriculum, advise undergraduate and graduate students, and contribute service to the department, college, university, profession, and broader communities as appropriate.
This is a full-time position; 9-month academic year appointment. Ph.D. in American Studies is required by the start date of the appointment, as well as evidence of potential for excellence in teaching, and productive, innovative scholarship. Salary is competitive.
The Standards for Promotion and Tenure in the Department of American Studies are available here or at: https://faculty.umn.edu/sites/faculty.umn.edu/files/2020-09/american_studies_7.12_dept_approved_20091104.pdf
The Workload Principles and Guidelines for Regular Faculty in the College of Liberal Arts are available here or at: https://neighborhood.cla.umn.edu/college-knowledge/workload-principles-and-guidelines

jobs.title: Tenure-Track Professor in Life Science and AI
jobs.description:
The Life Sciences Departments in Harvard Faculty of Arts and Sciences seek to recruit a tenure-track professor whose research is at the interface of AI and life sciences, from methodological developments to AI-enabled discovery. The successful candidate will be appointed in one of the participating FAS departments, including Earth and Planetary Science, Human Evolutionary Biology, Molecular and Cellular Biology, Organismic and Evolutionary Biology, and Stem Cell and Regenerative Biology, consistent with the best-matching research focus. Candidates conducting AI-integrated research in any subfield covered by these departments are encouraged to apply. We seek an outstanding individual who will establish an innovative research program and teach both undergraduate and graduate students.
The successful candidate will benefit from state-of-the-art research facilities, strong institutional commitment to career development, and a vibrant, collaborative research enterprise that brings together many disciplines in the biological sciences to create unique scientific and educational opportunities. Appointments will be made at the pre-tenure academic ranks of Assistant or Associate Professor, in accordance with the candidate’s experience and accomplishments. The appointment is expected to begin on July 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.
Basic Qualifications: Doctorate or terminal degree in any life sciences, computer science, mathematical sciences, engineering or machine learning, or related discipline required by the time the appointment begins.
Additional Qualifications: Demonstrated strong commitment to teaching and advising is desired.
Special Instructions:
Please submit the following materials through the ARIeS portal (https://academicpositions.harvard.edu/postings/16773). Complete applications must be submitted no later than October 15, 2026 Selected candidates will be invited to participate in an on-campus symposium-style visit in January 2027.

7. Publications or copies of creative works, if applicable
If visa sponsorship is needed, Harvard retains the discretion to determine which visa status is appropriate and whether a visa sponsorship application will ultimately be submitted, including payment of any applicable fees. jobs.title: Assistant Clinical Professor
jobs.description:
Assistant Clinical Professor in Biostatistics
The Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics, School of Public Health, University of Maryland, College Park (http://www.sph.umd.edu/EPIB) invites applications for an Assistant Clinical Professor in biostatistics. The position primarily involves teaching courses along with departmental related duties/service.
The Department’s mission is to improve health and reduce health disparities in local communities, the state of Maryland, and the nation. The Department offers an MPH degree in biostatistics, a PhD degree in biostatistics and MS in biostatistics, an MPH
degree in epidemiology, and a PhD degree in epidemiology.
The School of Public Health is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health and is located on the flagship campus of the University of Maryland. The School’s vision is “to be a leader in the discovery, application and dissemination of public health knowledge in the State of Maryland, the nation and the world.” The successful candidate will contribute to fulfilling this vision.
QUALIFICATIONS. Qualified candidates should possess a doctoral degree in biostatistics or a closely related public health field. Qualified candidates will have demonstrated the ability to teach undergraduate and graduate level biostatistics courses and mentor students.
RESPONSIBILITIES. Successful candidates for the position are expected to teach biostatistics courses to undergraduate and graduate students at fundamental and intermediate levels, mentor students, and engage in university and professional service.
Effective interpersonal, communication, and collaborative skills are essential.
SALARY and APPOINTMENT DATE. This is a full-time, nine-month, non-tenure-track position with benefits; salary is competitive and commensurate with qualifications and experience. Funding is guaranteed for 9 months annually, with the potential to extend salary support with teaching summer courses. The initial contract length is 1 year with possible future renewable multi-year contracts. Appointments may begin January 2027 or a mutually agreed-upon date.
APPLICATION. Applicants must apply electronically to https://umd.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/en-US/UMCP/details/AssistantClinical-Professor_JR104869, the faculty section, position P-103605. For best consideration, candidates should submit materials by October 2, 2026. Applications will be accepted until the position is filled. Applications should include the following: 1) cover letter clearly indicating how the candidate meets the qualifications listed above, 2) curriculum vitae, 3) teaching statements, and 4) contact information for three references (to be contacted only with the candidate’s approval). The Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics is committed to increasing the diversity of the campus community. Candidates who have experience working with a diverse range of faculty, staff, and students, and who can contribute to the climate of inclusivity are encouraged to state their experiences in these areas. Contact: Dr. Charles Ma, Search Committee Chair (tma0929@umd.edu) for questions about the position, and Ms. Bernadette Gormally (bgormall@umd.edu) for questions about application submission.
A wide range of collaborative opportunities exist at the University with nearby federal, state and local government agencies, non-profit organizations, and other academic institutions. Our faculty members also interact with faculty in the Joint Program in Survey Methodology (JPSM), the Maryland Population Research Center (MPRC), the Maryland Institute of Applied Environmental Health (MIAEH), the Biostatistics and Risk Assessment Center (BRAC), the Center for Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (CBCB), University of Maryland School of Medicine at Baltimore, as well as with researchers in other applied fields. The position represents a unique opportunity to join a growing department and contribute to an exciting research agenda and graduate student training program.
The University of Maryland is a Research Intensive University. College Park is the flagship campus of the University of Maryland System with over 2,500 faculty and 30,000 undergraduate and 11,000 graduate students. The University is located 8 miles from Washington D.C. For further information on the University of Maryland, please visit the University Web Site: http://www.umd.edu.
The University of Maryland, College Park, actively subscribes to a policy of equal employment opportunity, and will not discriminate against any employee or applicant because of race, age, sex, color, sexual orientation, physical or mental disability, religion, ancestry or national origin, marital status, genetic information, political affiliation, and gender identity or expression. Position overview
Position title: Assistant Professor of Human-Computer Interaction (HCI)
Salary range: The current salary range for this position is $84,100 - $132,900 (9-month academic year salary), however, off-scale salary and other components of pay, which would yield compensation that is higher than this range, are offered to meet competitive conditions.
Anticipated start: July 1, 2027

Apply by this date to ensure full consideration by the committee.
Final date: Monday, Nov 2, 2026 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time)
Applications will continue to be accepted until this date.
Position description
The School of Information at the University of California, Berkeley, invites applications for appointment to the faculty at the Assistant Professor rank.
Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) is a field of expertise focused on the evolving relationship between people and computing systems. HCI researchers design and study new ways for people to interact, collaborate, create, work, and make decisions with technology, and investigate how emerging computing systems shape human capabilities, practices, organizations, and society. Methods include the design and development of novel systems, experimentation, qualitative and ethnographic research, participatory design, computational methods, field studies, and mixed-methods research.
We seek applicants who are defining the next generation of human-computer interaction: developing new ways for people to interact, collaborate, create, work, and make decisions with increasingly intelligent computing systems. We are particularly interested in scholars who both imagine and build new forms of human-computer interaction and rigorously investigate how these technologies shape people, organizations, and society.
We welcome research across HCI and related fields, including, but not limited to, human-AI interaction and collaboration, intelligent and adaptive interfaces, social and collaborative computing, the future of work, accessibility, values such as sustainability, privacy, and justice in and through design, ubiquitous and embodied computing, information visualization, human-robot interaction, and emerging interaction modalities. We welcome a broad range of methodological approaches, including the design and development of novel systems, experimental and computational methods, qualitative and ethnographic research, field studies, participatory and critical design methods, and mixed-methods approaches.
Successful candidates will demonstrate the potential to establish an internationally recognized research program, contribute to undergraduate and graduate teaching in HCI, and engage with the School of Information's interdisciplinary community.
The School of Information is a graduate research and education community committed to expanding access to information and to improving its usability, reliability, and credibility while preserving security and privacy. This requires the insights of scholars from diverse fields — information and computer science, design, social sciences, management, law, and policy.
We are committed to addressing the family needs of faculty, including dual-career couples and single parents. We are also interested in candidates who have had non- traditional career paths or who have taken time off for family reasons, or who have achieved excellence in careers outside academia. For information about potential relocation to Berkeley, or career needs of accompanying partners and spouses, please visit New Senate Faculty | Office for Faculty Equity & Welfare.

jobs.description:
Tenure-Track Faculty Position in Product Design (Assistant Professor)
Hite Institute of Art + Design, University of Louisville
Target start date: August 2027
Application deadline: November 24, 2026 11:59PM
Rank/Salary: Tenure-track, open rank; salary and start-up support are competitive and commensurate with experience and qualifications
Position Description:
The University of Louisville invites applications for a tenure-track Professor of Product Design, Open Rank. We seek a practitioner-scholar whose work bridges human-centered design, three-dimensional form development, and hands-on fabrication.
The successful candidate will guide students through the full design process, from ideation, research, and prototyping to finished form, while emphasizing sustainable and materially responsible practices. We welcome candidates whose work engages physical products, systems, emerging technologies, sustainable design, social innovation, or related areas of contemporary product design practice. The successful candidate will prepare students to contribute to interdisciplinary teams and contemporary design practice.
Program and Institutional Context
The University of Louisville is a Carnegie R1 research university located in a dynamic metropolitan region with strong connections to manufacturing, healthcare, logistics, and civic innovation.
The Hite Institute of Art + Design is the most comprehensive art and design program in Kentucky, offering BA, BFA, MA, and MFA degrees across multiple disciplines. The Design program is grounded in a shared first-year foundation and includes coordinated tracks in Graphic Design, Interaction Design, Product Design, and Interior Design.
Students benefit from robust campus partnerships, community-engaged initiatives, and an active internship network throughout Louisville's cultural and innovation ecosystem.
Facilities & Resources
Product Design faculty and students benefit from facilities that connect traditional craft, contemporary design practice, and advanced engineering innovation. Resources include Hite's glass, sculpture, printmaking, photography, and ceramics studios; the Cressman Center for Visual Arts; Rowan, the graduate studio building; and the J.B. Speed School of Engineering's new 114,000-square-foot Student Success and Research Building, which houses advanced makerspaces, fabrication labs, research facilities, and collaborative studios.
Additional opportunities are available through the Additive Manufacturing Institute of Science and Technology (AMIST), a world-class center for metal, polymer, and ceramic additive manufacturing. Together, these resources support interdisciplinary teaching, research, and industry-engaged projects. Faculty are provided with individual studio space as well as access to shared instructional and fabrication facilities.
Teaching Responsibilities
Teach undergraduate and graduate courses that include drawing, form-giving, fabrication, prototyping, and human-centered research methods.
Contribute to curriculum development and interdisciplinary initiatives.
Mentor students through portfolio development, internships, independent study, and capstone projects.
Research / Creative Practice
Maintain an active and visible program of creative practice, scholarship, and/or professional design activity appropriate for a tenure-track appointment.
Disseminate work through appropriate venues (e.g., peer-reviewed publications, exhibitions, conferences, patents, juried shows, industry partnerships).
Pursue external funding or sponsored collaborations when appropriate.
Collaborate with the J.B. Speed School of Engineering on shared programs, facilities, and interdisciplinary initiatives.
Participate in departmental, college, and university service, including curriculum development, committee work, and student mentorship.
Engage with professional organizations and regional, national, or international design communities.
Required Qualifications
Terminal degree in Product Design, Industrial Design, or a closely related field (MFA, MID, or equivalent) completed by the start date; ABD considered.
Expertise in product design processes, form development, fabrication, and prototype-driven making.
Evidence of effective university-level teaching or equivalent instructional experience.
Strong portfolio demonstrating conceptual rigor, formal sophistication, and material exploration.
Commitment to inclusive pedagogy and student mentorship.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience integrating human-centered design and user research into studio teaching.
Experience with makerspaces, digital fabrication, additive manufacturing, or related technical facilities.
Interest in interdisciplinary collaborations involving design, engineering, or other STEM fields.
Record of industry collaboration, sponsored projects, community-engaged work, or externally funded research.
Application Instructions

jobs.title: Part Time Doctoral Faculty - Artificial Intelligence
jobs.description:
Anderson University’s International Graduate School invites applications for part-time doctoral faculty in Artificial Intelligence to teach in the University’s Doctor of Education (Ed.D.) in Leadership and Artificial Intelligence.
The Ed.D. in Leadership and Artificial Intelligence is a professional doctorate designed for experienced professionals who will lead organizations through the opportunities, challenges, and transformations created by artificial intelligence. The program integrates advanced leadership study with artificial intelligence, digital transformation, cybersecurity, ethics, organizational innovation, and applied doctoral research.
Anderson University is particularly interested in scholar-practitioners and accomplished AI professionals who combine appropriate doctoral credentials with significant real-world experience in artificial intelligence and related technologies.
Because artificial intelligence is a rapidly developing field, Anderson University values both academic preparation and substantive professional experience. Candidates are not required to hold a doctorate specifically titled “Artificial Intelligence”. However, candidates must possess an earned terminal degree and demonstrate significant academic and/or professional expertise appropriate to the doctoral course or courses they would teach.
Areas of Teaching Need
Anderson University is recruiting faculty qualified to teach one or more of the following courses:
LEAI 701 – Foundations of AI: History and Development
LEAI 740 – Machine Learning and Generative AI
LEAI 750 – AI Ethics and Responsible Use
LEAI 760 – Cybersecurity, Privacy, and AI Risk Management
LEAI 770 – Leading Change through Digital Transformation and AI Innovation
LEAI 780 – Applied Doctoral Research Seminar in Leadership and AI
LEAI 790 – Capstone Project
Minimum Qualifications
Candidates must possess:
An earned terminal degree (Ph.D., Ed.D., D.Sc., D.B.A., D.Eng., D.C.S., or other appropriate doctorate) from an appropriately accredited institution.
Graduate education, scholarship, research, and/or significant professional expertise related to the course or courses to be taught.
Demonstrated knowledge of contemporary artificial intelligence and its application within organizations.
The ability to teach and mentor students at the doctoral level in an academically rigorous and professionally relevant environment.
The ability to teach effectively in online, hybrid, and intensive-residency formats.
A commitment to supporting the mission and values of Anderson University.
Preferred Qualifications
Preference will be given to candidates demonstrating one or more of the following:
Significant professional experience implementing or leading artificial intelligence initiatives in business, government, healthcare, education, technology, cybersecurity, consulting, nonprofit organizations, or other sectors.
Expertise in generative AI, large language models, machine learning, AI-enabled analytics, AI agents and workflows, predictive systems, or emerging AI technologies.
Experience with enterprise AI implementation, digital transformation, technology strategy, organizational innovation, or AI-enabled decision-making.
Expertise in AI governance, ethics, privacy, cybersecurity, regulatory compliance, responsible AI, or AI risk management.
Graduate or doctoral-level teaching experience.
Experience supervising dissertations, doctoral research, applied research, or executive-level capstone projects.
Evidence of continuing engagement with the rapidly evolving AI field through scholarship, applied projects, consulting, industry leadership, professional certifications, professional development, or other substantive activities.
The Scholar-Practitioner We Seek
The Ed.D. in Leadership and Artificial Intelligence is a professional doctorate. Anderson University therefore seeks faculty who can connect doctoral scholarship with contemporary organizational practice. Ideal candidates may include senior technology executives, artificial intelligence and data science leaders, cybersecurity professionals, consultants, researchers, entrepreneurs, government technology leaders, or experienced academics who possess both an appropriate terminal degree and demonstrated expertise in artificial intelligence.
Of particular interest are professionals who have participated directly in the development, implementation, management, governance, or strategic use of artificial intelligence within organizations. Our faculty should help doctoral students understand not simply what artificial intelligence can do, but how leaders can evaluate, implement, govern, secure, and responsibly use AI to improve and transform organizations.
Teaching in the Ed.D. Program
Faculty members will work with experienced professionals pursuing a practice-oriented doctoral degree. Depending upon course assignment, responsibilities may include:
Teaching doctoral courses in online and hybrid formats.
Connecting current AI developments with leadership and organizational practice.
Using case studies, applied projects, simulations, and contemporary organizational challenges.
Mentoring doctoral students in applied research.
Advising students as they translate research into organizational solutions.
Participating, when appropriate, in the Responsible AI Leadership Capstone, through which students address significant workplace, organizational, industry, or societal challenges using responsible applications of artificial intelligence.
Faculty teaching research and capstone courses may also guide students in research design, organizational analysis, implementation strategies, evaluation, and professional presentation of doctoral-level work.
About our Commitment to Fairness in Employment
Anderson University does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, national or ethnic origin, sex, disability, age, religion, genetic information, veteran or military status, or any other basis on which the University is prohibited from discrimination under the local, state, or federal law, in its employment or in the provision of its services, including but not limited to its programs and activities, admissions, educational policies, scholarship and loan programs, and athletic and other University-administered programs. As a Christian institution of higher education, Anderson University is entitled to certain religious accommodations under federal and state law, including Title IX of the Education Amendments Act and Title VII of the Civil Rights Act. For questions or concerns contact the Office of Human Resources at hr@andersonuniversity.edu.

FACULTY VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT
ABOUT THE COLLEGE
John Jay College of Criminal Justice is a senior college of the City University of New York (CUNY) and an internationally recognized leader in educating for justice. Led by President Karol V. Mason, John Jay is a federally designated Hispanic-serving institution, ranked third in the nation in Black student success, and a top-ten institution for promoting student social mobility. John Jay is proud to serve a diverse and dynamic student body of 15,000 students, including nearly 50% who are first in their family to attend college, as well as students who are immigrants, from low-income families, or from other historically underrepresented groups in higher education.
The College participates in the doctoral programs of the Graduate Center of CUNY and offers bachelor’s and master’s degrees both in traditional criminal justice-related fields of study as well as in a robust portfolio of liberal arts and sciences programs that highlight themes of justice across the arts, sciences, humanities, and social sciences.
POSITION OVERVIEW
The Department of Sciences at John Jay College of Criminal Justice invites applications for a tenure-track position at the rank of Assistant Professor in Molecular Biology, with expertise relevant to forensic biology, to begin Fall 2027.
We seek an enthusiastic and collaborative scholar-educator who will contribute to our nationally recognized forensic science programs and help prepare the next generation of forensic scientists. The successful candidate will teach undergraduate and graduate courses in molecular biology, genetics, forensic biology, and related areas within the Forensic Science Program, while developing an active research agenda that complements the mission of the Department and the College.
The ideal candidate will demonstrate a strong commitment to excellence in teaching, mentoring, and research. We are especially interested in candidates with the potential to engage students in meaningful research experiences and to develop externally funded projects in molecular biology, forensic biology, forensic genetics, or closely related areas. Candidates should have a record of scholarly productivity or demonstrate strong potential for publishing in peer-reviewed scientific journals.
Responsibilities include teaching courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels, mentoring students in research, contributing to curriculum development in forensic biology, participating in departmental and college service, and developing a sustainable research program. The candidate should demonstrate a commitment to working collaboratively with faculty, students, and external partners, be enthusiastic and well-prepared to work with students from a wide range of backgrounds, and demonstrate a commitment to fostering an inclusive and supportive learning environment. As demonstrated in John Jay College’s Seven Principles for a Culturally Responsive, Inclusive, and Anti-Racist Curriculum (https://www.jjay.cuny.edu/john-jays-seven-principles), the College seeks a faculty member who thrives in a multicultural, collaborative academic environment and is committed to both access and excellence in higher education.
John Jay College offers a unique opportunity to work in a dynamic academic environment dedicated to justice, science, and public service. The Department of Sciences is home to rigorous forensic science programs that combine strong scientific training with real-world applications, preparing students for careers in forensic laboratories, research institutions, graduate and professional programs, and public service.
QUALIFICATIONS
A Ph.D. in Molecular Biology, Forensic Biology, Genetics, Biochemistry, Cell Biology, or a closely related field is required.
Professional experience in forensic science, forensic biology, DNA analysis, forensic genetics, or related laboratory practice is strongly preferred.
Experience teaching or mentoring undergraduate or graduate students, a strong publication record or evidence of scholarly potential, and the ability to develop an externally funded research program are strongly valued.
COMPENSATION
$59,256 - $114,091. Salary commensurate with education and credentials
CUNY offers faculty a competitive compensation and benefits package covering health insurance, pension and retirement benefits, paid parental leave, and savings programs. We also provide mentoring and support for research, scholarship, and publication as part of our commitment to ongoing faculty professional development.

jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
The Department of Kinesiology, Nutrition, and Health seeks a teacher-scholar in Exercise Science who will contribute to the department’s undergraduate and graduate programs through high-quality teaching, an active program of research, and student mentorship. The successful candidate will bring expertise in exercise physiology and related areas that complements existing departmental strengths and supports the preparation of students for clinical, professional, and graduate careers. The faculty member will be expected to contribute to a collaborative academic environment and participate actively in the teaching, research, and service missions of the department.
Responsibilities include teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in Exercise Physiology, Clinical Exercise Testing and Prescription, Research Methods, Experiential Learning/Capstone, and related kinesiology courses; establishing and maintaining an active research program; pursuing external funding; advising and mentoring students; and engaging in service at the departmental, college, University, and professional discipline levels. This is a full-time, tenure-track, on-campus position that requires regular campus presence and active engagement with students. The appointment is expected to begin in August
2027.
Job Description
The Department of Kinesiology, Nutrition, and Health seeks a teacher- scholar in Exercise Science who will contribute to the department’s undergraduate and graduate programs through high-quality teaching, an active program of research, and student mentorship. The successful candidate will bring expertise in exercise physiology and related areas that complements existing departmental strengths and supports the preparation of students for clinical, professional, and graduate careers. The faculty member will be expected to contribute to a collaborative academic environment and participate actively in the teaching, research, and service missions of the department.
Responsibilities include teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in Exercise Physiology, Clinical Exercise Testing and Prescription, Research Methods, Experiential Learning/Capstone, and related kinesiology courses; establishing and maintaining an active research program; pursuing
external funding; advising and mentoring students; and engaging in service at the departmental, college, University, and professional discipline levels. This is a full-time, tenure-track, on-campus position that requires regular campus presence and active engagement with students. The appointment is expected to begin in August 2027.
Minimum Qualifications
Ph.D. in Exercise Physiology, Exercise Science, Kinesiology, or a related discipline by the date of appointment.
Consideration may be given to candidates with:
Experience teaching undergraduate and/or graduate courses in Exercise Physiology, Clinical Exercise Testing and Prescription, research Methods, and Experiential Learning/Capstone.
Postdoctoral research experience.
Professional certification through the American College of Sports Medicine (e.g., ACSM-EP, ACSM-CEP), the National Strength and Conditioning Association (e.g., CSCS), or another nationally recognized exercise science organization.
Evidence of collaborative scholarship or interdisciplinary research.
Experience working with students from diverse backgrounds and fostering an inclusive learning environment.
Department of Kinesiology, Nutrition, and Health
The Department of Kinesiology, Nutrition, and Health is one of the largest in the College of Education, Health, and Society, with sustained enrollment growth and strong student demand. The department is committed to excellence in teaching, research, and student mentorship while preparing graduates for clinical, professional, and graduate careers. We value the breadth of the kinesiology discipline and seek a faculty member whose expertise in Motor Behavior will strengthen our curriculum, expand collaborative scholarship, and contribute to the continued growth of the department.
Faculty in the department maintain active research programs across motor behavior, biomechanics, exercise physiology, nutrition, athletic training, health behavior, and related disciplines. The successful candidate will have access to well-equipped research facilities supporting human movement and performance research, including motion capture and biomechanical analysis systems, force platforms, body composition assessment, ultrasound imaging, exercise physiology laboratories, and other human performance testing resources.
Research Environment
The Department of Kinesiology, Nutrition, and Health (KNH) offers a sophisticated, translational research infrastructure specifically designed to support high-impact Exercise Physiology. Our shared laboratory network facilitates seamless investigation across the physiological spectrum—from molecular pathways to systemic cardiometabolic and performance outcomes—providing an ideal environment for mechanistic, clinical, and applied research.
Core Research Infrastructure:
Human Integrative Physiology & Metabolism: Advanced capabilities for cardiometabolic phenotyping, including gold-standard indirect calorimetry (ParvoMedics TrueOne 2400), comprehensive body composition analysis (DEXA, InBody 770, ultrasound), and resting/exercise metabolic testing.
Vascular Physiology: Specialized infrastructure for hemodynamic assessment, featuring flow-mediated dilation, arterial stiffness analysis, microneurography, and continuous glucose monitoring to characterize vascular health.
Applied Exercise Testing: A large-capacity, adaptable space for clinical and physiological trials equipped with multiple treadmill and cycle ergometers, ECG systems, and on-site clinical chemistry diagnostics.
Molecular & Tissue Bioscience: A collaborative facility that integrates whole-body physiological data with cellular-level analysis, utilizing gene expression profiling (RT-PCR), histology, protein detection, and skeletal muscle tissue processing.
Pre-Clinical Opportunities: Use of the Laboratory Animal Resource (LAR) to conduct experimental physical activity and inactivity studies with rodents utilizing metabolic, behavioral, and functional phenotyping.
This integrated environment fosters a highly collaborative culture, providing faculty the flexibility to execute translational research and offer meaningful, hands-on training to undergraduate and graduate students.
The College of Education, Health and Society:
The vision of the College of Education, Health, and Society is to foster critically engaged leaders prepared to take on complex and interdisciplinary challenges through transdisciplinary problem-solving that seeks equity and justice in our changing global society. The College embraces the rich opportunities available for cross-disciplinary collaboration across its six departments (Educational Leadership; Educational Psychology; Family Science and Social Work; Kinesiology, Nutrition, and Health; Sport Leadership and Management; and Teaching, Curriculum, and Educational Inquiry).
Miami University
Established in 1809, Miami University consistently ranks among the top national public universities for providing students with a superior education and exceptional value. Miami is located in the quintessential college town of Oxford, Ohio, with polytechnic campuses in Hamilton and Middletown, a learning center in West Chester, a European study center in Luxembourg, and a 100% virtual option in Miami Online. A comprehensive research university, Miami empowers students to engage with premiere teacher-scholars and benefit from a well-rounded liberal arts foundation and vibrant campus experience to develop lifelong skills for any career. With more than 240,000 high-achieving alumni, students gain access to an extensive and supportive community that opens doors globally and leads to amazing outcomes. With an ambition to effect meaningful change, Miami delivers the resources and experiences that prepare graduates to learn with purpose and lead with courage.
