FTE: 1.0
Scope of Job:
The UTRGV SOM is seeking a Board Certified or Board Eligible
physician in Radiation Oncology to provide both clinical
(non-teaching) and academic radiation services. The successful
candidate will serve as Founding Director of Radiation Oncology and
Cancer Therapeutics and Cancer Service Line Director for UT Health
RGV. The successful candidate will provide leadership across the
academic, clinical, research, and strategic dimensions of the
growing UTRGV cancer enterprise.
This role will be charged with establishing and leading the UTRGV
academic Radiation Oncology program while helping shape the broader
development of the UTRGV Cancer Center and providing strategic
leadership for cancer services across UT Health RGV. The position
will provide an opportunity to build and develop programs, recruit
and mentor faculty, establish multidisciplinary clinical and
research programs, advance innovative cancer technologies and
therapeutics, strengthen the integration of cancer services across
UT Health RGV, and develop regional partnerships to advance cancer
care throughout South Texas. Leadership responsibilities will
include:
Establishing and leading the UTRGV academic Radiation Oncology
program, including faculty recruitment, clinical quality and
safety, education, research, innovation, and long-term programmatic
growth.
Serving as Cancer Service Line Director for UT Health RGV,
developing a strategic plan alongside UT Health RGV leadership and
providing strategic clinical leadership for the continued
development, integration, quality, and growth of cancer services
across the health system, while working collaboratively with
medical, surgical, radiation, and other oncology leaders.
Establishing and leading the UTRGV Comprehensive Breast Cancer
Program, integrating medical oncology, radiation oncology, breast
surgery, imaging, pathology, genetics, survivorship, prevention,
and clinical research into a coordinated multidisciplinary
program.
Serving as Co-Director of the UTRGV Cancer Clinical Trials
Program, working collaboratively with leadership and other Cancer
Center leaders to expand investigator-initiated, cooperative-group,
industry-sponsored, and translational cancer trials throughout
South Texas.
Developing a Molecular Imaging, Theranostics, and
Radiopharmaceutical Oncology Program, including expansion of
diagnostic and therapeutic isotope capabilities and leadership in
planning for future radiopharmaceutical production and potential
cyclotron development.
Advancing cancer therapeutics and technology at UTRGV,
including innovative radiation techniques, image-guided therapies,
precision oncology approaches, theranostics, radiopharmaceutical
therapies, and other emerging cancer treatments.
Recruiting, mentoring, and developing academic cancer
specialists and investigators, helping create the faculty and
leadership infrastructure necessary for the continued growth and
maturation of the UTRGV Cancer Center.
Developing a Rio Grande Valley Cancer Consortium, bringing
together UTRGV and community oncologists, health systems, and
cancer programs throughout the region to expand clinical trials,
collaborative research, education, advanced therapeutics, and
access to high-quality cancer care.
Providing broader institutional and regional cancer leadership,
working with the School of Medicine, UT Health RGV, Cancer Center
leadership, university leadership, and community partners to
advance UTRGV's cancer treatment, research, education, and
innovation efforts.
The successful candidate will also provide clinical Radiation
Oncology services. Clinical responsibilities will include
outpatient radiation services and may include in-patient
consultation. Academic responsibilities may include teaching
residents/medical students in the outpatient clinical setting and
in the classroom. Participation in scholarly activity, faculty
development, patient safety and quality improvement initiatives,
and other administrative and program committees are expected. Also,
preparation and presentation of program didactics, grand rounds,
and assisting with undergraduate medical education will be assigned
at the Chair's discretion. The successful candidate will develop a
robust clinical/translational research program that advances the
therapeutic paradigm.
Academic rank will be awarded commensurate with academic experience
and credentials.
Minimum Qualifications:
MD or DO from an accredited institution, Board Certified or Board
Eligible in Radiation Oncology and licensed in the State of Texas.
5-10 years of academic, clinical and administrative experience
experience.
Discipline Specific Required Qualifications:
Successful completion of ACGME accredited residency training
program in Radiation Oncology.
Preferred Qualification:
Experience in teaching medical students, residents, and
fellows.Bilingual in English and SpanishRegional or emerging
reputation for the rank of associate professor or higher.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Asst Professor - Psychology
Join Our Campus Community!
Thank you for your interest in joining the University of Wyoming.
Our community thrives on the contributions of talented and driven
individuals who share in our mission, vision, and values. If your
expertise and experience align with the goals of our institution,
we would be thrilled to hear from you. We encourage you to apply
and become a valued member of our vibrant campus community
today!
Why Choose Us?
At the University of Wyoming, we value our employees and invest in
their success. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to
support your health, financial security, and work-life balance.
Benefits include:
Generous Retirement Contributions: The State contributes
over 15% of your gross salary. With your mandatory employee
contribution, the total contribution toward your retirement plan
exceeds 19%.
Exceptional Health & Prescription Coverage: Enjoy
access to medical, dental, and vision insurance with competitive
employer contributions, that include 4 deductible options to suit your
needs.
Paid Time Off: Benefit from ample vacation, sick leave,
paid holidays, and paid winter closure.
Tuition Waiver: Employees and eligible dependents can
take advantage of tuition waivers, supporting continuous education
and professional growth.
Wellness and Employee Assistance Programs: Stay healthy
with wellness initiatives, counseling services, and mental health
resources.
At the University of Wyoming, we are committed to creating a
supportive and enriching workplace. To learn more about what we
offer, please refer to UW's Benefits Summary.
JOB TITLE:
Assistant Professor
JOB PURPOSE:
Contribute to the Department of Psychology's mission in teaching
undergraduate and graduate students, conducting research, and
providing service to the department, field, and community.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
The Department of Psychology at the University of Wyoming (UW), a
Carnegie R1 research institution, invites applications for two
tenure-track Assistant Professor positions in Clinical Psychology,
to begin August 2027. Research area is open. We encourage
applicants with adult and/or child/developmental backgrounds
interested in research that complements the work of existing
faculty (e.g., suicide and non-suicidal self-injury, sexual
violence prevention, trauma-related psychopathology, emotion
regulation, severe and persistent mental illness, transdiagnostic
assessment, ADHD, substance use, eating disorders) as well as
interests that extend existing areas of expertise.

engagement and public service, and with an intentional focus on

appointment. Primary duties will include teaching specialty
didactic and clinical courses in PMHNP; supervising and assessing
student clinical competencies and theoretical knowledge while
supporting comprehensive learning experiences; evaluating students'
progress in course work and clinical experience; planning,
developing, implementing, and evaluating the curriculum, as
appropriate; completing all administrative aspects of courses
taught; and advising/mentoring the next generation of PMHNP's.
Duties also include serving on and participating in college and
university committees; and providing service to the community and
profession. This position requires face-to-face interactions
through a regular schedule of attendance on campus and in the
workplace.

the Accreditation Commission for Nursing Education (ACEN) and is
approved by the Texas Board of Nursing (TBON). For more
information, please visit our website at https://www.tamiu.edu/conhs.
Required Qualifications
The successful candidate must hold an earned doctorate in nursing
from an accredited university. ABDs will be considered but must
have earned a doctorate before the appointment. PMHNP master's
degree or post-graduate certificate in PMHNP from an accredited
program; board certification as a PMHNP; a current
unrestricted/unencumbered license to practice registered nursing
within the State of Texas; and two or more years' experience
treating patients as a PMHNP are required. We strongly encourage
candidates with have one or more years of teaching experience in
higher education.
We offer competitive salaries and a benefits package including
health insurance, retirement benefits, and life insurance.
Additional pay is available for summer teaching. Financial support
for professional development opportunities, such as attending
academic conferences, is also provided. Moving expenses are covered
in whole or in part by the university.

Letter of interest or cover letter that addresses

Names and contact information of three current professional
references

JOB TITLE:

JOB PURPOSE:
The mission of the Division of Communication Disorders is to
advance the science behind practice, develop practice ready
speech-language pathologists to serve the communication needs of
individuals from all backgrounds. The successful candidate will
contribute to these efforts.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
The Division of Communication Disorders at the University of
Wyoming is seeking an Associate or Assistant Professor in
speech-language pathology with a strong preference for candidates
with commensurate experience at the Associate level in alignment
with division tenure and promotion standards. This is a full-time,
9-month, tenure-track position. Primary responsibilities include
sustaining a research program in areas of interest, teaching, and
service. On campus presence is required for teaching and other
duties. Salary and benefits are competitive, and start-up package
is excellent.

Assistant Professor Minimum Qualifications:

discipline and evidence of potential for independent research
productivity and publications by time of appointment. Experience:
Evidence of promise for scholarly achievement, potential to develop
an independent research program, and potential for high-quality
teaching. Valid driver's license with a motor vehicle record (MVR)
compliant with the Driving for University Business
SAP.
Associate Professor Minimum Qualifications:
Education: Earned doctorate in speech-language pathology or related
discipline and evidence of independent research productivity and
publications. Experience: Evidence of scholarly achievement,
development of an independent research program and evidence of
high-quality teaching. Valid driver's license with a motor vehicle
record (MVR) compliant with the Driving for University Business
SAP.

based on qualifications.

and Dick Scarlett Chair in Speech-Language Pathology.

dysphagia, cognitive communication disorders, voice disorders,

The Department of Marketing at the David Eccles School of Business,
University of Utah, is seeking candidates for a tenured position
beginning in Fall 2027 at the Associate Professor or Professor
level. Successful candidates will be Marketing scholars who excel
in research, teaching, service, and mentorship. The position should
serve as a model of collaboration within the Department and School
and reflect an appreciation for all areas traditionally represented
in Marketing. These roles require a strong record of research,
effective teaching, and collegial engagement.

· PhD in Marketing.
· Record of high-quality scholarship focused on A-level Marketing
journals as evidenced by productivity and impact on the
field.

environment of the Department and School.

appointments at one or more A-level Marketing journals.

undergraduate and Master level.
· Record of supporting PhD student development.

university level.
· Proven ability to engage with the business community to support
students and research.

goals.
The Marketing Department has expanded over the last 12 years from
just over 60 students to approximately 250 undergraduate majors
with interests in both marketing and professional sales. The
Department was among the first handful of schools to launch a
successful Master of Business Analytics Program focused on machine
learning and artificial intelligence, which is a top-10 TFE Times

The Department of English at Texas A&M University-Corpus
Christi invites applications for a 9-month, tenure-track position

in Applied Linguistics, beginning in Fall 2027. The position
entails a 3/3 teaching load and has commensurate research and
service expectations. Summer and online teaching opportunities may

The Department of English allows English majors to pursue
undergraduate coursework with either a Writing or Literary Studies
emphasis. The department additionally offers curricula for
secondary English certification; certificates in Writing for
Non-Profits, social media, and TESOL; and minors in Technical and
Professional Writing, Creative Writing, and Literary Studies. The
graduate program provides an interdisciplinary educational
experience by requiring coursework in Literary Studies, Writing
Studies, and Applied Linguistics.

for two undergraduate TESOL certificates. In addition, they teach
courses in the ENGL BA, ENGL BA with secondary English teaching
certification, ENGL MA, Elementary Education BS, and BIEM ESL
Minor. The TESOL certificates are pursued by students from across
the university with an enrollment of 50+ students.

rated degree programs since 1947. The University has a heritage of

palm tree-lined pathways throughout the campus, nearby natural
wetlands, a scenic hike-and-bike trail, and a university beach,
Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi is the only university in
the nation located on its own island, at the heart of the Texas
Gulf Coast.

A PhD in Applied Linguistics or related field. Advanced ABD
will be considered; degree must be conferred at the time of
appointment.
Demonstrated a successful research agenda specializing in at
least two of the following areas: TESOL methods,
technology-assisted language learning/teaching, corpus linguistics,
or an area of sociolinguistics.
Preferred qualifications:
Demonstrated commitment to teaching a broad range of applied
linguistics courses at the undergraduate level.

historically underserved communities.

Job Description
The Department of English at Texas A&M University-Corpus
Christi invites applications for a 9-month, tenure-track faculty
position in Rhetoric and Composition, beginning Fall 2027. The
appointment may be made at the rank of Assistant or Associate
Professor, commensurate with the candidate's qualifications, level
of expertise, and professional experience. The department is
seeking an experienced writing program administrator to support the
First-Year Writing Program. Applicants should demonstrate a record
of excellent teaching and have an active, current scholarly agenda
in writing program administration.
Teaching expectations will include a 3/3 course load (not including
course release time for program administration) comprising
first-year writing courses and upper-division undergraduate courses
in writing studies. Candidates will also have the opportunity to
offer graduate courses and mentor students in the department's
English MA program. Administrative duties, when part of the
faculty's appointment, will include development and assessment of
writing curricula and outcomes and initiating faculty development
opportunities to support writing pedagogy in the program.
The Department of English offers undergraduate English majors a
choice in either a Writing or Literary Studies emphasis, curricula
for secondary English certification, certificates in Writing for
Non-Profits, social media, and TESOL, and minors in Technical and
Professional Writing, Creative Writing, and Literary Studies. The
graduate program provides an interdisciplinary educational
experience in a generalist MA in English by requiring advanced
study in Writing Studies, Literary Studies, and Applied
Linguistics.
At TAMU-CC, our first-year writing program is informed by research
on how people write, how they learn, and what they need to be
flexible, adept writers ready to take on new challenges. Our
program works to teach writing in ways that connect students to
their majors and coordinate with the demands of other first-year
classes. As a program, we want to help students understand that
writing, language, and rhetoric are all multifaceted and evolving;
we want students to be able to use writing and language in ways
that will help them achieve their goals.

jobs.description:
Job Details
The Biology Department at Lycoming College invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor, starting August 2027.
This is a unique opportunity for an energetic educator and scholar to help shape a new academic major. Beyond teaching, the successful candidate will guide the acquisition of laboratory teaching and research equipment and assist in designing facilities for the new Exercise Science major, established in 2026.
Teaching & Mentorship Responsibilities include Introduction to Exercise Science, Exercise Physiology (300-level), departmental/general education offerings (e.g., courses for non-science majors, First-Year Seminars), and mentoring a diverse student population through coursework, undergraduate research, and capstone experiences.
Qualified candidates will have a Ph.D. in Exercise Physiology, Exercise Science, Kinesiology, or a closely related field by the start date. Previous undergraduate teaching experience is strongly preferred.
Who We Are
Founded in 1812, Lycoming College is one of the nation’s oldest and most respected liberal arts colleges. Today, our community of 1,100 active learners from 22 states/territories and 17 countries comprises a student body that is 32 percent domestic students of the global majority or international. All students work with renowned scholars to craft customized combinations of market-driven majors, minors, and concentrations across our 48+ academic programs. Students compete in 20 NCAA Division III sports, participate in faculty-driven research, thrive in a robust internship program, and study abroad in more than two dozen countries. Lycoming College has one of the highest endowment-per-student ratios in the country, is a member of the Annapolis Group of Liberal Arts Colleges and is recognized by U.S. News & World Report as a top 100 National Liberal Arts College and No. 21 Best Value School. Learn more at www.lycoming.edu.
The College proudly celebrates and values the principle of inclusive excellence. In support of its commitment to establishing an inclusive and equitable campus, Lycoming College seeks to recruit faculty and staff of diverse perspectives and experiences.
Lycoming College is an equal opportunity employer.
To Apply
Application files should include:
Cover Letter & CV highlighting prior leadership/achievements and vision for growing this new Exercise Science major.
Teaching Statement: A description of your teaching philosophy and how it aligns with the mission of Lycoming College, specifically highlighting inclusive excellence.
Research Statement: A summary of your research interests and goals for the next five years, explicitly addressing how undergraduates will be meaningfully involved in research.
Transcripts: Unofficial graduate and undergraduate transcripts.
References: Names and contact information for three professional references (at least one must address teaching abilities). Letters may be requested at a later date.
Application Review: Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Full consideration will be given to applications received by October 23, 2026.
Inquiries may be directed to the Chair of the Search Committee, Dr. Jeff Newman, at newman@lycoming.edu.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Department: Computer
ScienceSalary: Commensurate with experience
Description:
The Department of Computer Science at the University of Houston
(www.cs.uh.edu)
invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the
Assistant Professor level in Quantum Information Science, as part
of the university's Presidential Frontier Faculty (PFF) program.
Candidates working on theoretical or practical aspects of quantum
information science are encouraged to apply, including algorithms
for quantum computing and communication, quantum networking,
quantum distributed computing, quantum cryptography, the
integration of quantum computing and HPC systems, and software for
heterogeneous quantum systems.
The Presidential Frontier Faculty program is a university-wide
strategic initiative to recruit outstanding early-career scholars
in frontier research areas. This position is anchored in the
Department of Computer Science (tenure home) and involves
collaboration with the Department of Mathematics and the Department
of Electrical and Computer Engineering (Cullen College of
Engineering). The hire will join a growing campus-wide quantum
effort, including concurrent quantum-themed searches in Physics and
Earth and Atmospheric Sciences, the university's partnership with
IonQ, and alignment with the National Quantum Initiative and the
State of Texas quantum initiatives. The position carries a
competitive salary and a substantial start-up package.
The department is seeking exceptional candidates with the potential
for exceptional research, excellence in teaching, and mentoring of
graduate and undergraduate students. Candidates must demonstrate an
outstanding scholarly record of research, exhibited by high-impact
peer-reviewed publications and a forward-looking, vigorous research
agenda that will secure competitive, external funding as Principal
Investigator (PI). The anticipated start date for this position is

science, computer engineering, mathematics, physics, or a closely
related scientific field before September 1, 2027.
Located in Houston, the fourth largest city in the United States,
UH is a Carnegie Tier One public research university located on a
park-like campus a few minutes from the Houston city center. The
university has embarked on an exciting period of research growth, a
rising reputation, and committed leadership. The Department of
Computer Science is home to a dynamic and interdisciplinary group
of 30+ full-time faculty members and over 2000+ students across its

machine learning, computer vision, graphics and visualization,
systems, distributed algorithms, high-performance computing, and

and has been funded by numerous agencies, including the National
Science Foundation, National Institutes of Health, National
Institute of Standards and Technology, and the U.S. Departments of
Defense, Homeland Security, Justice, Energy, and
Transportation.
Houston is a large city, with world-class theaters, museums,

housing and enjoys a low cost of living. The university is close to
the Texas Medical Center, the largest medical center in the world,
a large industrial base, and NASA.

prospective applicants are encouraged to contact the search

jobs.title: Assistant Professor - AI-enabled Drug Discovery & Translation  - (496910 )
jobs.description:
Job Details
Department: Chemical
EngineeringSalary: Commensurate with experience
Description:
The William A. Brookshire Department of Chemical and
Biomolecular Engineering at the University of Houston (UH) seeks to
hire a tenure-track faculty member at the rank of Assistant
Professor under the Presidential Frontier Faculty Program with
research interests in AI-enabled drug discovery.
The Presidential Frontier Faculty Program is a university-wide,
integrated interdisciplinary hiring campaign overseen by central
University leadership and designed to recruit a large cohort of
convergence research faculty working in health, energy,
sustainability, and security. Competitive candidates are expected
to hold a Ph.D. or equivalent degree by the start of the
appointment and demonstrate the potential for exceptional research
and excellence in teaching and service. The successful candidate
will be appointed at the rank of Assistant Professor.
Description of the position: We seek candidates who will establish
nationally recognized, externally funded research programs in
biomolecular engineering addressing grand challenges in AI-enabled
drug discovery. The convergence of artificial intelligence and
machine learning, computational chemistry, molecular modeling,
structural biology, robotics, and laboratory automation is
fundamentally transforming the pharmaceutical discovery and
development process. These advances have the potential to
dramatically reduce the time, cost, and risk associated with
identifying and optimizing new therapeutic candidates.
AI-driven molecular design, predictive modeling, virtual screening,
digital twins of biological systems, and autonomous laboratories
are creating an integrated discovery paradigm in which promising
drug candidates can be rapidly designed, synthesized,
characterized, tested, and iteratively optimized. By tightly
coupling computational prediction with automated experimentation
and high-throughput validation, these technologies enable the
exploration of chemical and biological design spaces at a scale and
speed that were previously unattainable. AI-enabled drug discovery
therefore represents one of the most rapidly advancing and
potentially transformative frontiers in modern biomolecular
engineering, with profound opportunities to accelerate the
development of next-generation therapeutics and improve human
health.
We welcome applications from candidates working across a broad
spectrum of AI-assisted drug discovery methodologies. Key areas of
interest include, but are not limited to:
• Therapeutic Discovery & Screening: Novel AI frameworks for
the discovery and optimization of small-molecule therapeutics,
biologics, and peptide-based drugs.
• Multi-Omic Integration: Advanced machine learning architectures
for integrating genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic data to
identify actionable therapeutic targets.
• Next-Generation Modalities: Computational design of RNA- and
gene-based therapeutics.
• Precision & Personalized Medicine: AI-driven platforms
targeting cancer, infectious diseases, neurological disorders,
cardiovascular disease, and rare genetic conditions.
Expertise in cancer-related research would be particularly
desirable because it would maximize opportunities for collaboration
with researchers working at the forefront of the field at UH and
the nearby Texas Medical Center, the largest medical complex in the
world. The Department has 26 tenured and tenure-track faculty,
modern research facilities, annual research expenditures exceeding
$12 million, and a vibrant graduate program with more than 100
Ph.D. students. The successful candidate will join a collegial
group of research-oriented faculty working in a highly
collaborative environment and will become a member of the
prestigious Presidential Frontier Faculty network of scholars at
UH.
UH is a Carnegie Tier 1 public research university and is home to
several research centers and institutes that provide opportunities
for collaborative research, including the UH Drug Discovery
Institute, the UH Hewlett Packard Enterprise Data Science
Institute, the Center for Nuclear Receptors and Cell Signaling, and
the recently awarded $44.2 million Consortium for Translational and
Precision Health between UH and Baylor College of Medicine, among
others. The successful candidate will also have access to
state-of-the-art shared core facilities at UH and the Texas Medical
Center.
The Houston metropolitan area offers an excellent quality of life
and a vibrant arts and entertainment scene supported by a growing
economy. Houston is home to the Texas Medical Center and has a
broad industrial base in energy, chemicals, materials, aeronautics,
and medical technologies, offering additional opportunities for
collaborative research. Houston has recently attracted
multibillion-dollar investments in drug manufacturing facilities
from two major pharmaceutical companies.
A complete application consists of: (1) a cover letter; (2) a
curriculum vitae; (3) a detailed description of research interests
(not to exceed 5 pages); (4) a statement of education discussing
teaching interests, teaching experience, and mentoring experience
(not to exceed 2 pages); (5) three representative publications; and
(6) the names and contact information (email addresses and phone
numbers) of three professional references whom we may
contact.
Review of applications will begin on November 15, 2026, and will
continue until the position is filled. The position is available
effective Fall 2027.
For more information please contact the appropriate Search
Committee Chair:
Professor Navin Varadarajan
William A. Brookshire Department of Chemical & Biomolecular
Engineering
http://www.chee.uh.edu/
E-mail: chbefacultysearch@egr.uh.edu
Employees are expected to have a home address in the state of
Texas for the duration of their appointments.
Official transcripts are required for a faculty appointment and
will be requested upon selection of the final candidates.
All positions at the University of Houston-System are security
sensitive and will require a criminal history check. Individuals
conducting research in critical infrastructure areas (i.e.,
communication infrastructure systems, cybersecurity systems,
electric grid, hazardous waste treatment systems, and/or water
treatment facilities) are subject to regular review to ensure the
security and integrity of the research is maintained.
The University of Houston System and its universities are Equal
Opportunity Institutions. Everyone is encouraged to apply.

the salary range for this position is $104,00 to $124,000.

health, dental and retirement benefits, extensive accrued time
off/paid holidays, and tuition reimbursement for employee, spouse,
and dependents attending Rowan University, Glassboro. (Tuition
reimbursement will apply to undergraduate degrees only for spouse
and dependents).
For more detailed information, please visit: https://sites.rowan.edu/hr/benefits/
NOTE: Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the
US, and the University will not sponsor an applicant for a work
visa for this position.
NOTE: This faculty appointment is Tenure eligible and
may be granted upon successful completion of criteria listed in the
Rowan-Virtua SOM Faculty Bylaws.
NOTE: Faculty Rank of Assistant Professor is pending review
and recommendation made by the Faculty Affairs Committee.

jobs.title: Professor of Digital and Computational Studies
jobs.description:
Job Details
Located in Lewiston, Maine, Bates is internationally recognized as
a leading liberal arts college. We are proud to offer a highly
personalized education that centers on deep and sustained
interactions among students, faculty, and community. We are
engaging the forces — intellectual trends, demographic changes, and
technology — that are transforming higher education and the world
into which our students graduate.
The
Program in Digital and Computational Studies at Bates College
invites applications for two full-time, open-rank, tenure-line
positions in Computer Science, beginning July, 2027. We seek
outstanding scholars with a strong commitment to excellent
undergraduate teaching and mentorship in a liberal arts
environment, and who will help to deepen the discipline of computer
science in an interdisciplinary computing program.
While areas of expertise are open, the successful candidates will
have a demonstrated commitment to interdisciplinary computing in
the liberal arts, in research areas which may include, but are not
limited to: human computer interaction (HCI), artificial
intelligence / machine learning (AI/ML), natural language
processing (NLP), and disciplinary-based computer science
education. We are especially interested in candidates who will add
to the existing breadth of the DCS faculty. Successful candidates
will have a demonstrated interest in teaching undergraduate
students and supporting a diversity of students in computing with a
range of prior programming experience (including none). Successful
candidates will also have a demonstrated commitment to
collaboration and collegiality. They will also demonstrate interest
in collaboratively building an interdisciplinary and inclusive
computing program for the liberal arts.
The anticipated salary range for this position is $87,000–$135,000,
commensurate with rank, experience, qualifications, and other
relevant factors. As an open-rank tenure-line search, the
appointment may be made at the assistant professor, associate
professor, or full professor level. The final salary offer will
reflect the candidate’s academic experience, record of professional
achievement, and the rank at which the appointment is made.
Digital & Computational Studies (DCS) is an interdisciplinary
program that seeks to build bridges between core elements of
computer science, data science, and digital studies, connecting to
the arts, humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, and other
existing interdisciplinary programs on campus. DCS teaches students
to design, build, and analyze digital & computational tools and
algorithms, while also developing the ability to critique those
same tools and algorithms. Bates DCS faculty are prepared to
support candidates as they develop courses designed for an
interdisciplinary program.
The position carries a standard five-course teaching load either as
a 2-3 or 3-2 across two semesters, or as a 2-2-1 across two
semesters and the Bates
Short Term . Faculty responsibilities include teaching,
professional achievement, and governance and engagement, as
described in Article II of the Bates
College Faculty Handbook . Successful candidates will
contribute to inclusive and evidence-based teaching, maintain an
active program of scholarship or creative work, and participate in
the life and governance of the College.
The successful candidates will teach introductory computer science
sequences in Python (e.g. DCS 109X, DCS 229 Data Structures, and
DCS 211 Computing for Insight), and other upper level computing
courses based on their area(s) of expertise. They will also
regularly teach the DCS senior capstone course; contribute to the
general education curriculum, including teaching our college-wide
First Year Seminar program; advise senior theses, and serve as an
academic advisor.
Faculty scholarship and creative work at Bates are robustly
supported by start-up packages, a paid pre-tenure leave, support
for post-tenure sabbaticals, internal grants, professional travel
funding, and a well-staffed external
grants office .
Community-engaged learning —with community partnerships
facilitated by the
Harward Center for
Community Partnerships —and study abroad are both
broadly encouraged and institutionally supported. Pedagogical
development and innovation is further buttressed by our highly
engaged
Center
for Inclusive Teaching and Learning . Educational access and
racial justice are central to Bates’ history and mission and
our
faculty-led initiatives reflect this commitment .
Candidates should have a Ph.D. in Computer Science, completed no
later than 01 July 2027.
Review of applications will begin on October 15, 2026 and continue
until the position is filled.
Required application materials should include:
● A Cover letter which addresses how candidates envision their
research and teaching Digital and Computational Studies at
Bates;
● A Curriculum vitae
● A Teaching statement describing an approach to teaching the
introductory computer science sequence, and identifying courses
currently offered as well as new courses that candidates would be
interested in developing. This statement should also describe how
the candidates will meet Bates’ standards in terms of inclusive and
evidence-based pedagogy.
● A Research statement describing a five-year plan for research at
a small liberal arts college, and mentoring undergraduate
research.
We seek candidates who are committed to supporting the success of
all students. Applicants are encouraged to describe relevant
preparation, experience or plans for creating an inclusive learning
environment.
Letters of recommendation will be requested only for candidates
selected to move forward after the initial review. Employment is
contingent upon successful completion of a background check and
verification of degree.
Bates College is committed to equal opportunity and to providing an
educational and work environment free from discrimination. The
college prohibits discrimination on the basis of race, color,
national or ethnic origin, religion, sex, sexual orientation,
gender identity or gender expression, age, disability, genetic
information, veteran status, and other legally protected statuses
in the recruitment and admission of its students, in the
administration of its education policies and programs, or in the
recruitment of its faculty and staff. Bates College adheres to all
applicable state and federal equal opportunity laws and
regulations. All college faculty, staff, students, contractors,
visitors, and volunteers are responsible for understanding and
complying with the Non-Discrimination Policy.
Inquiries concerning the college’s policies, compliance with
applicable laws, statutes, and regulations (such as Title VII,
Title IX, and ADA/Section 504), and complaints may be directed to
the Title IX Officer, Gwen Lexow at 207-786-6445 or
titleix@bates.edu.

Job Details
About University at Albany:
The University at
Albany is a Carnegie-classified Research 1 institution driven
by academic excellence, pioneering research and scientific
discovery, and service to community. UAlbany's world-class faculty experts and approximately 17,500 students are
creating new knowledge in fields such as artificial intelligence,
semiconductor engineering, atmospheric and environmental sciences,
cybersecurity, public health, public administration and social
welfare while deepening our understanding of our world through
scholarship and creative activity in the social sciences and
humanities. As one of the most diverse public research institutions
in the nation, the University is a national leader in public
engagement, educational equity and social mobility. For over 180
years, UAlbany has molded bright, curious and engaged students and
launched them toward success.
Located in Albany, New York, New York State's capital, the
University is convenient to Boston, New York City and the
Adirondacks.
Job Description:
The School of Education at the University at Albany, State
University of New York is seeking a full-time tenure track
Assistant Professor in Mathematics Education with an interest in
joining a newly launched and growing undergraduate teacher
preparation program. Applicants with expertise in PreK-6
mathematics teacher preparation are strongly encouraged to apply.
We seek candidates with a strong commitment to teaching
undergraduate and graduate students enrolled in teacher preparation
programs as well as doctoral students. The successful applicant
will engage with colleagues whose research interests and
scholarship span pre-K to post-graduate education and who prepare
students to be innovative scholar-leaders. The School of Education
is a vibrant and inclusive community of students and faculty. In
this community, students and faculty innovate and challenge via
research, teaching and service to focus on education that meets the
contemporary learning needs of society.
Primary Responsibilities:
The candidate should be prepared to teach both introductory
courses and advanced courses in their area of expertise. Duties
will include teaching courses across undergraduate and graduate
programs as needed based on candidate's expertise; publishing and
obtaining funding to support research in their area of educational
expertise; mentoring students; attending departmental and program
meetings; and serving on department, school, and university
committees.
Functional and Supervisory Relationships:
Reports to Department Chair
Supervises the following positions: Graduate Assistants
Job Requirements:
Candidates must be sensitive to the needs of and possess an
interest in working in an academic community that is diverse with
regard to gender, race, ethnicity, religion, nationality, sexual
orientation or identity, disability status, and protected veteran
status.
Applicants must demonstrate an ability to develop inclusive and
equitable relationships within our diverse campus community.
Applicants must demonstrate an ability to support diversity,
equity, access, inclusion, and belonging relative to their
role.
Requirements:
Minimum Qualifications:
A Ph.D. or Ed.D in mathematics education, teaching and
learning, curriculum and instruction, teacher education, learning
sciences, and/or related education area from a college or
university accredited by a U.S. Department of Education or
internationally recognized accrediting organization by August 21,
2027. Candidates who will not hold the degree by this date will not
be considered.
Active research program addressing mathematics teaching and/or
learning as evidenced by scholarly and professional publications
and/or presenting at regional and/or national professional
conferences.
Three or more years experience in full-time classroom teaching
mathematics in PK-12 settings.
Experience in teaching undergraduate and/or graduate
mathematics education courses (content and/or methods
courses).
Preferred Qualifications:
Demonstrated interest in personal ongoing professional
development, incorporation of research to practice, and/or
community engagement activities.
Teaching certification in early-childhood or childhood
(elementary) education or related area.
Full-time classroom teaching experience specifically in U.S.
PK-12 public school contexts.
Experience seeking and/or securing research funding, or the
potential to do so.
Ability to teach courses across the School's teacher education
majors (adolescent education, childhood and special education, or
early-childhood/childhood education).
At least 18 hours of graduate mathematics or statistics content
coursework, or equivalent.
Working Environment:
Typical office/instructional environment
In-person and online instruction
Additional Information:
Professional Rank and Salary Range: Assistant Professor
(Academic-year appointment), Salary commensurate with
experience.
The Jeanne Clery Disclosure of Campus Security Policy and Campus
Crime Statistics Act, or Clery Act, mandates that all Title IV
institutions, without exception, prepare, publish and distribute an
Annual Security Report. This report consists of two basic parts:
disclosure of the University's crime statistics for the past three
years; and disclosures regarding the University's current campus
security policies. The University at Albany's Annual Security
Report is available in portable document format [PDF] by clicking
this link http://police.albany.edu/ASR.shtml
Pursuant to New York Labor Law 194-a, the University will not seek,
request, or rely upon an applicant's wage or salary history in
determining whether to interview, hire, or establish compensation
for an applicant. Applicants are not required to provide wage or
salary history information as a condition of employment
consideration. Salary history may only be verified in the limited
circumstances permitted by law.
THE UNIVERSITY AT ALBANY IS AN EO/AA/IRCA/ADA EMPLOYER
Please apply online via http://albany.interviewexchange.com/candapply.jsp?JOBID=204828
Application Instructions:
Applicants MUST submit the following documents:
CV
A cover letter (no more than 3 single-spaced pages) explaining
your scholarship, teaching philosophy and practice, and any
service
Two to three scholarly publications or unpublished papers
Contact information for three references
Transcripts for all degrees earned and in progress (unofficial
transcripts accepted initially).
Note: After submitting your CV, the subsequent pages give
you instructions for uploading additional documents (i.e. cover
letter etc.).
See the FAQ for using our online system. Please contact us if you need assistance
applying through this website.
Returning Applicants - Login to your
UAlbany Careers Account to check your completed application.
Preference will be given to applications received by October
14.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor (Tenure-Track) - Occupational and Environmental Safety and Health
jobs.description:
Job Details
Current Employees: If you are currently employed at any of
the Universities of Wisconsin, log in to Workday to apply through
the internal application process.
Position Title:Assistant Professor (Tenure-Track) -
Occupational and Environmental Safety and Health
Job Category:Faculty
Employment Type:Regular
Job Profile:Assistant Professor
Job Duties:
Attention:
The Department of Occupational and Environmental Safety and Health
in the College of Business and Economics seeks an Assistant
Professor.
Job Summary:
The Department of Occupational & Environmental Safety &
Health (OESH) in the College of Business and Economics (CoBE) at
the University of Wisconsin-Whitewater seeks a dedicated educator,
scholar, and colleague to join our faculty as a tenure-track
Assistant Professor in Environmental/Occupational Safety &
Health, beginning August 2027. This position carries a
24-credit annual teaching load* with an emphasis on
high-impact instructional practices, student success, research, and
professional service. The successful candidate will teach
face-to-face and online undergraduate courses for the
Occupational Safety B.S. and graduate courses for the
M.S. in Environmental Safety & Health (online) and will
pursue an active research agenda that complements existing faculty
expertise. Areas of research interest may include one or more of
the following:
Construction safety and health
Risk management and loss control
ISO auditing/management systems and international safety and
health
Ergonomics and human factors engineering
Environmental management
The approved standards for promotion and tenure at the time of
initial contract are the standards that will be used for promotion
and tenure. If there are revisions to department or college
standards, a faculty member can request (in writing to the
department chair) to have the revised standards applied.
Teaching & Instructional Expectations
Course Load: Deliver 24 credits of instruction per
academic year in Occupational and Environmental Safety &
Health. *Faculty who maintain Scholarly Academic (SA) status
under AACSB standards receive up to three credits per semester of
release time to support scholarly productivity and AACSB
accreditation expectations. ( UW-Whitewater Teaching Responsibilities and
Workload Policy )
Office Hours for Students: Maintain at least eight
office hours for students each week during the academic year. These
office hours should be consistent to provide accessible student
support and academic advising/mentoring. For faculty who teach a
portion or all courses online, the modality of the office hours
should be proportionate to the modality of the courses taught
unless the department or college has additional requirements.
Advising/Mentoring: Use the systems, “Navigate” and
“Stellic” for all advising/mentoring notes.
Communication: Maintain professional and timely
responsiveness to student, colleague, and administrator inquiries
via Navigate, Canvas, email, and telephone, generally within 24–48
business hours while on contract. When off contract, use the “out
of office” feature in Outlook to let individuals know who to
contact in your absence.
Administrative Compliance: Ensure the punctual
submission of course syllabi at the start of each term, ensuring
they meet all University and system-wide requirements ( UWW Syllabi Requirements ).
Contribute to curriculum development and review, including
efforts supporting ABET-ANSAC accreditation and BCSP Qualified
Academic Program (QAP) status.
Accessibility: Select and develop instructional
materials that are Title II (ADA) compliant. All digital course
content, textbooks, and media must be accessible to students with
disabilities to ensure an equitable learning environment.
Representative Teaching Areas
Full-time teaching responsibilities may include, but are not
limited to:
Introduction to Occupational Safety and Health
Occupational Safety and Health Standards and Applications
Occupational Safety Management
Graduate and undergraduate courses in Ergonomics
Graduate and undergraduate courses in Construction Safety
Principles of Environmental Management, along with courses
focusing on hazardous materials, air pollution, and facility water
management
Additional teaching responsibilities potentially
include:
Teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in face-to-face,
hybrid, and online formats
Curriculum development and review for improvement and
re-accreditation
Internship supervision
Faculty at UW-Whitewater may be required to teach online or in
a hybrid format, or courses in the evenings or on weekends, if
applicable
Faculty may also elect to teach New Student Seminar or
University Learning Communities, or participate in other programs
geared toward improving student success
Research, Scholarship & Creative Activity
Maintain an active scholarly agenda that contributes to the
field of environmental and occupational safety and health,
including applying for grants and collaborating with other faculty
or members of the OESH community.
Disseminate research through peer-reviewed publications,
conference presentations, or professional exhibitions per
department and college standards.
Seek opportunities to involve undergraduate and graduate
students in research initiatives and other scholarly and creative
activities.
Service & Engagement
Participate in departmental, college, and university-level
meetings and committee work.
Participate in professional and public service, and in
community organizations relevant to the candidate's expertise and
interests.
Contribute to program assessment and development.
Engage in professional outreach and service that aligns with
the University Mission Statement and the Wisconsin Idea .
Participate in at least one graduation ceremony each academic
year.
Workplace Expectations
Please see the link below regarding workplace expectations at
UW-Whitewater. We believe that by adhering to these expectations,
we develop a university community in which all students, staff, and
faculty feel valued and supported.
UWW Workplace Expectations
Key Job Responsibilities:
Department:
Department of Occupational & Environmental Safety & Health
- College of Businesses and Economics
The Department of Occupational & Environmental Safety
& Health prepares students for rewarding careers protecting
America's workforce, the public, and the natural environment. Our
faculty are nationally recognized, and our graduates are highly
sought after.
Coursework covers a wide range of subjects, including approaches to
accident prevention, environmental protection, ergonomics, fire
prevention, and legal aspects, among others. Students are provided
with essential skills to recognize and evaluate risks and devise
and implement effective control methods. In addition, students gain
several practical work-site experiences, culminating in a
full-semester internship with a practicing EHS professional. Our
B.S. in Occupational Safety degree is ABET-ANSAC accredited, and
both the B.S. and M.S. degrees are BCSP Qualified Academic Programs
(QAP), enabling graduates to obtain the Graduate Safety
Practitioner designation.
The UW-Whitewater College of Business and Economics is Wisconsin's
largest AACSB-accredited business school, enrolling approximately
4,000 undergraduate business students and offering 15 majors and 26
emphases. Nearly 1,000 graduate students are enrolled across a
breadth of online and on-campus programs, including the Master of
Business Administration, Master of Science in Cybersecurity, Master
of Science in Data Analytics, Master of Science in Environmental
Safety & Health, Master of Science in Finance, Master of
Science in Education in School Business Management, Master of
Science in Marketing, and the Doctor of Business
Administration.
Compensation:
Well-qualified candidates can expect a salary commensurate with the
candidate's academic preparation, related experience, and
professional certifications.
UW System employees receive an excellent benefit package. To learn
more about the UW System's comprehensive benefit package, review
the UW System Employee Benefits Brochure .
Required Qualifications:
Doctoral degree (Ph.D., ScD, EdD, or equivalent) in
environmental safety and health or a closely related field,
including but not limited to: Environmental Health, Engineering,
Public Health, Public Policy, or Risk Management and Loss Control,
by the time of appointment.
ABD candidates may apply but must have their degree completed
by the contract start date in August 2027; if not, they will be
hired on a one-year contract with the understanding that their
degree will be completed before January 2028, in advance of their
first scheduled review.
Demonstrated commitment to teaching with an emphasis on
promoting the success of undergraduate and graduate students, clear
evidence of scholarly potential, commitment to working with
inclusive populations, and serving as an active member of the
university community.
A research record in environmental safety and health, or the
ability to develop and carry out a research agenda, is
required.
Good oral and written communication and interpersonal skills
are essential.
Demonstrated application of artificial intelligence (AI) in the
generation and presentation of instructional and assessment
documents.
Preferred Qualifications:
Demonstrated excellence in university-level teaching,
experience with Canvas, and a record of scholarly
achievement.
Professional experience in OESH and certification are desirable
(e.g., CSP, CIH, REHS, CPE, ARM, CRM, PE, CHMM, REM).
Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:
Ability to interact respectfully with people with diverse
socioeconomic, cultural and ethnic backgrounds
Willingness and ability to be an active participant in
following applicable safety rules and regulations including
necessary training and drills.
How to Apply:
Only complete application packages will be considered. This
includes online submission of the following documents. If
submitting more than five application materials, you'll need to
combine files prior to uploading and label with an appropriate
name.
Cover letter/letter of interest
Statement of teaching philosophy
Curriculum Vita
Names and contact information for three professional references
(letters of recommendation may be solicited at a later time)
Copies of unofficial graduate transcripts (official transcripts
will be required if offered the position)
Contact Information:
If you have questions regarding this recruitment, or if you are
unable to complete the application online due to a disability or
system problem, please contact us at (262) 472-1024 or hr@uww.edu .
For questions regarding this position, please contact:
Dr. Todd Loushine, Department Chair and Associate
Professor
262-472-1208
loushint@uww.edu
To Ensure Consideration
Applications received by October 18th, 2026, are ensured
full consideration. Applications received after that date may be
given consideration at the discretion of the search committee. The
most qualified applicants will be invited to participate in the
next step of the selection process.
CAMPUS INFORMATION:
UW-Whitewater is a thriving public university located in
southeastern Wisconsin. It leads the way in providing world-class,
affordable higher education programs to more students than
neighboring regional comprehensives in the University of Wisconsin
System. A collaborative team of 1,300 faculty and staff are devoted
to the success of the university’s 11,500 students at its main and
Rock County campuses. The team provides high-impact practices and
academic programs — online and in person — from associate to
doctoral levels. Recognized nationally for affordability,
inclusion, and career development, UWW serves approximately
one-third first-generation students and boasts strength in many
areas, especially business and education. The campus and community
embrace the Warhawk Family spirit, supporting the university’s arts
and nationally recognized NCAA Division-III level championship
athletics. As a proud institution of access, more than 10 percent
of undergraduate students use the acclaimed Center for Students
with Disabilities — a priority mission since the 1970s.
UW-Whitewater's campuses are located centrally near Milwaukee,
Madison, and Chicago, offering easy access to the cultural and
commercial opportunities of major metropolitan areas. Near both
Lake Geneva and the Wisconsin Dells, the area attracts numerous
visitors from across the country. Whitewater is a vibrant college
community near the Kettle Moraine State Forest offering area
residents seasonal outdoor enjoyment. The nearby Rock County campus
is located in Janesville, a town of 60,000 located on the Rock
River and known as Wisconsin’s Park Place.
ORGANIZATION INFORMATION:
The University of Wisconsin-Whitewater is part of the 13-campus
Universities of Wisconsin ( https://www.wisconsin.edu ).
Wisconsin Statute 19.36(7)(b) provides that applicants may indicate
in writing that their identity should be kept confidential. In
response to a public records request, the University will not
reveal the identities of applicants who request confidentiality in
writing, except that the identity of the successful final candidate
will be released. See Wisconsin Statute 19.36(7)(a).
Per Regent Policy Document 20-19, University of Wisconsin System
Criminal Background Check Policy and Universities of Wisconsin

Florida Southern College invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor of Communication position with specialization in multimedia journalism. The position start date is August 2027. Florida Southern College is nationally recognized for its commitment to engaged learning. jobs.title: Tenured/Tenure-Track Assistant, Associate or Full Professor Faculty Positions in Measurement
jobs.description:
Job Details
Posting Details
Position Details
Title
Tenured/Tenure-Track Assistant, Associate or Full Professor Faculty
Positions in Measurement Science in Chemistry
Appointment Status
Tenure
Department
IU Bloomington Vice Provost For Faculty Affairs
Location
Bloomington
Position Summary
Indiana University Bloomington ( IUB ) invites applications
for multiple, tenured/tenure-track positions at all ranks
(assistant, associate or full professor) in the Department of
Chemistry within the College of Arts and Sciences as a part of
the Faculty 100 strategic hiring initiative. Successful candidates
are expected to develop visible, externally funded research
programs to address research priorities in measurement
science . The department seeks scientists who develop new
quantitative tools, instrumentation, and measurement approaches
that answer previously inaccessible chemical, physical, and/or
biological questions in any area related to chemistry. In addition
to ensemble approaches, research directions may include
measurements that resolve chemical and biological heterogeneity
across individual molecules, particles, cells, and beyond. This
initiative is intended to grow a nationally distinctive community
around interdisciplinary quantitative measurement to these system
-from single molecules and nanoparticles to living systems, enabled
by advances in instrumentation, spectroscopy, mass spectrometry,
microscopy, and machine learning.
Appointments would begin August 1, 2027, although an
earlier or later start date is negotiable. Applications received by
October 16, 2026, will receive full consideration, and applications
will be accepted until the positions are filled.
Responsibilities: Tenured/tenure-track faculty at Indiana
University Bloomington are expected to substantially contribute to
the overall academic excellence of the department by developing and
maintaining a record of scholarly accomplishment, research
leadership, and success or strong potential in securing competitive
external research support, commensurate with rank; teaching and
mentoring undergraduate and/or graduate students as designated by
the department chair; and actively providing service within the
department, school, and university alongside active engagement with
the profession and community.
These positions are located on the campus of Indiana University,
Bloomington ( IUB ) in Bloomington, Indiana, and successful
candidates are expected to work on the IUB campus to allow full
engagement with the department, school, campus, and community.
Indiana University bases its tenure and promotion recommendations
upon performance in three areas: research, teaching, and service.
All individuals hired through this initiative are expected to excel
in research and demonstrate strong performance in teaching and
service.
Minimum Qualifications: All applicants should have a PhD in
Chemistry (or a related field) and postdoctoral experience
and be committed to excellence in scholarship and teaching at the
undergraduate and graduate levels.
Application Procedures: Review of applications will begin
October 16, 2026, and continue until all positions are
filled. The following materials are required for all applicants:
Cover letter
In 1-2 pages, identify your application for a position with
tenure (associate or full professor) or a tenure-track position
(assistant professor) and summarizing your qualifications and
interest in the position.
Current Curriculum Vitae
Research Statement
In no more than 4 pages, describe your current research and
future aspirations in research.
Teaching Statement
In no more than 2 pages, describe your teaching philosophy,
experience(s) teaching at the undergraduate and/or graduate level,
and/or your experience serving as a mentor.
Contact information for three professional references
Professional references for applicants for tenure-track
positions will only be solicited for those selected for
screening interviews.
Professional references for applicants for positions with
tenure will only be solicited for those selected for a finalist
interview and/or job offer.
Application materials for all positions should be submitted at:

jobs.title: Assistant Professor in Media, Behavior, and Health
jobs.description:
Job Details
Posting Details
Position Details
Title
Assistant Professor in Media, Behavior, and Health
Appointment Status
Tenure Track
Department
IU Bloomington Media School
Location
Bloomington
Position Summary
The Media School at Indiana University’s flagship Bloomington
campus is pleased to announce a faculty search for an outstanding
tenure-track colleague whose research and teaching examine the
relationships among media, behavior, and health, to start August 1,
2027.
We welcome applications from scholars working across a broad range
of topics at the intersection of media, health, and well-being.
Areas of interest may include, but are not limited to, media
influences on mental and physical health; health communication and
health behavior; social media and well-being; media representations
of health, illness, and disability; stigma and stereotyping;
cognitive, emotional, and behavioral responses to health-related
media; health misinformation; and the development and evaluation of
media-based interventions designed to improve health and
well-being. We are particularly interested in scholars whose work
helps explain how media environments, messages, and technologies
shape health-related attitudes, psychological processes,
decision-making, and behavioral outcomes.
We welcome a range of theoretical perspectives and methodological
approaches, including experimental, survey, longitudinal,
computational, neuroscientific, qualitative, and mixed-method
approaches. Candidates may study children, adolescents, adults, or
populations across the lifespan.
This position offers substantial opportunities for
interdisciplinary collaboration across Indiana University,
including with faculty in the Media School, the School of Public
Health, the Department of Psychological and Brain Sciences, the
Irsay Institute, and other units engaged in health and behavioral
research. The successful candidate will join a growing community of
scholars examining media, behavior, health, and well-being across
the campus.
The chosen applicant will be expected to maintain a productive and
theoretically significant research program, effectively teach and
mentor undergraduate and graduate students on a standard 2-2
teaching load, and serve the university, profession, and wider
community. Teaching opportunities may include courses in media
psychology, strategic communications, health communication, social
media, research methods, and other areas related to the candidate’s
expertise.
The primary criteria for this search are excellence in research and
teaching related to media, behavior, and health. Evidence of
potential to secure external funding is viewed
favorably. External funding is conceived broadly to include
government, industry, foundation, and other private sources.
About the School
The Media School combines a long-standing tradition of excellence
in journalism, film, gaming, and communications with a commitment
to digital and interactive media. It fosters a multidisciplinary
approach to education and research, equipping students with the
theoretical and practical tools necessary to lead and innovate in
the media landscape of tomorrow. Faculty members are distinguished
for their scholarly contributions and their dedication to teaching,
offering a dynamic environment for engaging with media theory,
production, and design.
The Media School is home to the Center for Documentary Research and
Practice, the Center for International Media Law and Policy
Studies, the Institute for Communication Research, the Michael I.
Arnolt Center for Investigative Journalism, the National Sports
Journalism Center, the Observatory on Social Media, Indiana Public
Media, Cream and Crimson Studios, the KIX Lab, and the Black Film
Center & Archive. The school serves more than 2,300
undergraduate majors in eight degree programs (Journalism, Media,
Game Design, Cinematic Arts, Global Media, Media Advertising,
Public Relations, and Sports Media). It also offers graduate
degrees (M.S. and Ph.D.) to approximately 75 graduate students, of
whom two-thirds are in a doctoral program. Our state-of-the-art
facilities include equipment for television, film and audio
production, game design, and communication research.
University and Community Setting
Nestled in the lively community of Bloomington, our university
campus is renowned for its stunning limestone architecture and
scenic natural landscapes. This setting fosters a culture that
values both the arts and sciences and provides substantial
opportunities for interdisciplinary research and
collaboration.
Bloomington is a vibrant midsize city located within driving
distance of Indianapolis, Chicago, Cincinnati, Columbus, and
Louisville. Our community is small yet welcoming, a home to people
from all over the world. Bloomington features an active arts
community, with several independent music and performance venues
and one of the best university cinemas in the country. Southern
Indiana is also home to beautiful scenery, and residents enjoy
year-round outdoor activities.
Basic Qualifications
ABD applications considered, but Ph.D. in communication, media,
psychology, public health, or a related field must be completed by
the date of appointment.
Demonstrated potential for research productivity in areas
related to media, behavior, and health.
Effective teaching skills adaptable to undergraduate and
graduate learning environments.
Department Contact for Questions
Questions regarding this position or the application process should
be directed to the chair of the search committee, Dr. Nicole
Martins, The Media School, Indiana University, at
nicomart@iu.edu.
Additional Qualifications
Preferred Qualifications
Demonstrated potential for interdisciplinary
collaboration.
Demonstrated potential to secure external funding.
Demonstrated success working with faculty and student
populations from a wide variety of backgrounds and
experiences.

As part of a major, multi-year effort to expand research activities
in Quantum Information Science through the Faculty
100 initiative , the College of Arts and
Sciences at IU Bloomington invites applications for a
tenured position at the Associate or Full Professor rank to begin
in the Fall of 2027. Appointment will be in the Department of
Physics .
We are particularly interested in applicants working in the areas
of quantum sensing and quantum detection experiments, especially
those who intend to establish a tabletop or benchtop research lab
at IU Bloomington. Candidates who conduct experimental research
complementing our activities in atomic/molecular/optical physics,
quantum information science and technology, quantum photonics,
precision measurement, nuclear and particle physics, or quantum
sensing for biophysics/biomedical sciences will be given
preference. We encourage applications from scholars who apply
interdisciplinary perspectives across a variety of these domains,
who may collaborate with colleagues across the IU Quantum Science & Engineering
Center , the Center for Exploration of
Energy and Matter , or the multi-institutional Center for Quantum
Technologies .

applicants should be committed to excellence in scholarship and
teaching at the undergraduate and graduate levels.

Position Summary
Indiana University Bloomington ( IUB ) invites applications for a
tenure-track Assistant in the College of Arts and Sciences,
Department of Biology in the field of Virology . We
seek candidates to join IU’s outstanding Microbiology research
program to lead research in the areas of Cellular Responses to
Virus Infection, Cell Biology of Virus Infection, and Evolution of
Emerging Viruses but other areas of virology will be
considered.
We encourage applications from scholars who apply interdisciplinary
perspectives and share important research overlap with current IUB
scholars, while also offering new dimensions that will expand and
strengthen
virology research at IUB . Researchers have access to
state-of-the-art facilities for genomics and bioinformatics,
light and electron microscopy, flow cytometry, proteomic analysis,
physical biochemistry analytical instrumentation, and
crystallography.
This 10‐month appointment would ideally start August 1,
2027, but start date is negotiable.
Responsibilities: Tenure-track faculty in the Biology
department at Indiana University Bloomington are expected to
substantially contribute to the overall academic excellence of the
department by developing and/or maintaining a robust research
portfolio including pursuing and obtaining major extramural
research funding to conduct cutting-edge research as a principal
investigator, teaching undergraduate and graduate in the classroom,
mentoring graduate students in our graduate programs, participating
in service at the University and actively engaging with their
professional community. Indiana University bases its tenure and
promotion recommendations on performance in research, teaching, and
service.

degree and demonstrate a strong record of scholarly achievement
appropriate to the level of appointment.

should provide evidence of past and current research productivity

presentations of research at relevant scientific or professional
conferences, and other indicators of scholarly impact. Candidates
should also demonstrate strong potential to secure external
research funding.

colleges and schools, offering more than 300 undergraduate majors,
300 master’s programs, and 150 doctoral and professional degree
opportunities. IUB’s mission is to create, disseminate, preserve,
and apply knowledge through cutting-edge research, scholarship,
arts, and creative activity; challenging undergraduate, graduate,
professional, and lifelong educational programs; meaningful
experiences beyond the classroom; and expansive global educational
opportunities. The University is also home to first-rate library
and museum collections and contributes significantly to economic
development and impact throughout Indiana and the region. Known for
its Indiana limestone architecture and expansive green spaces, IUB
is widely regarded as one of the country’s most beautiful college
campuses.
The College of Arts and
Sciences is at the academic heart of Indiana University
Bloomington. The College offers more than 225 academic programs
spanning three broad areas: Arts and Humanities, Natural and
Mathematical Sciences, and Social and Historical Studies. It is
home to more than 70 departments and programs and three schools:
the Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design; the Hamilton
Lugar School of Global and International Studies; and The Media
School. More than 900 faculty members contribute to the College’s
teaching, research, and creative mission. College faculty are
regularly recognized with some of the nation’s and world’s highest
academic and professional honors, including election to the
American Academy of Arts and Sciences, the National Academies, and
the American Association for the Advancement of Science, as well as
MacArthur and Guggenheim Fellowships, Fulbright Awards, Pulitzer
Prizes, Oscars, and Emmys.
The position is based in the Department of
Biology , a large, unified department within the College of
Arts and Sciences. Biology offers strong undergraduate programs,
nationally ranked graduate programs, and a broad, collaborative
research environment. Research in the department spans biological
questions and experimental systems across scales, from ecosystems,
evolution, and organismal biology to microbiology, developmental
and cell biology, molecular and systems biology, bioinformatics,
and genomics. This breadth provides opportunities for
interdisciplinary research and collaboration across the department
and the broader IUB research community.
Located in the rolling hills of south-central Indiana,
Bloomington is a vibrant community of approximately 85,000
residents that combines the character of a college town with many
of the cultural and recreational amenities of a larger city. The
community offers theater, music, and arts events—including the
LOTUS World Music & Arts Festival—as well as quick access to
approximately 250,000 acres of public recreation lands. With strong
public schools and a reasonable cost of living, Bloomington offers
an attractive environment in which to live and work.
Basic Qualifications
Minimum Qualifications: Applicants should possess a doctoral
degree and demonstrate a strong record of scholarly achievement
appropriate to the level of appointment.
Candidates seeking appointment at the Associate Professor
level must demonstrate a sustained record of scholarly
achievement commensurate with a tenured appointment. This should
include a record of extramurally funded research as principal
investigator, an established body of corresponding-author
publications, evidence of visibility and engagement within the
broader scholarly community, and experience leading substantial
research initiatives.
