jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Computational Biology
jobs.description:
Job Details
Position Announcement
The Department of Biological Sciences at Utah Tech University
invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track Assistant
Professor position in Computational Biology, with a primary focus
on Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) algorithms and their
pedagogical application at both the undergraduate and graduate
levels. This position is part of a two-position hire supporting the
department's expanding programs in bioinformatics and
genomics.
The successful candidate will be an expert in NGS algorithms and
pipeline development, capable of translating complex computational
concepts for students at varying levels of experience. The position
will provide instruction for an existing Bachelor of Science in
Bioinformatics and Master of Science in Genomics with a
Bioinformatics emphasis.
The Biological Sciences department houses degree programs in
Bioinformatics, Biological Sciences, Biomedical Sciences, Natural
Sciences, and Biology Secondary Education. Additional program
information is available at https://biology.utahtech.edu/
.
Responsibilities
Teaching and Curriculum
Teach 24 credit hours of lower and/or upper-division courses
per academic year across undergraduate and graduate levels.
Deliver upper-division and master's-level courses in NGS
algorithms, bioinformatics pipeline design, computational genomics,
and related topics, with the ability to adapt instruction to
students from both computational and life science backgrounds.
Teach core NGS topics including short- and long-read sequencing
platforms, read alignment algorithms (e.g., BWA, STAR, minimap2),
variant calling, de novo assembly, transcriptomics, and epigenomics
analysis.
Develop and teach additional courses as needed, which may
include Principles of Genetics, Introduction to Programming for
Biologists, or Statistical Genomics, depending on departmental need
and applicant expertise.
Create innovative upper-level elective courses that reflect
emerging areas of NGS technology and computational biology,
complementing and diversifying the department's current
offerings.
Design and deliver instruction in multiple modalities including
face-to-face, flipped classroom, hybrid, and fully online formats;
willingness to teach evening and summer courses when needed.
Research and Mentorship
Mentor master's students in functional genomics and NGS-focused
research projects, guiding them from data generation through
computational analysis and interpretation.
Supervise undergraduate research in computational biology,
providing hands-on experience with NGS datasets and bioinformatics
workflows.
Maintain an active scholarly profile consistent with the
teacher-scholar model, including publications, presentations, or
collaborative research appropriate to a primarily undergraduate and
master's serving institution.
Assist in mentoring and supervising part-time instructors
teaching in the bioinformatics program.
Service and Institutional Contribution
Collaborate with the Department Chair, Dean, and faculty
colleagues on curriculum development, program assessment, and
strategic planning for both the Bioinformatics B.S. and Genomics
M.S. programs.
Perform campus-wide service duties including holding regular
office hours, attending department and division meetings, serving
on university and college committees, and participating in outreach
and recruitment activities.
Contribute to interdisciplinary curricular and scholarly
activities within the Department, the College of Science,
Engineering & Technology, and the University.
Perform other duties as assigned.
Qualifications
Required
PhD in Computational Biology, Bioinformatics, Genomics,
Computer Science with a biological application focus, or a closely
related field.
Demonstrated expertise in NGS algorithms and the analysis of
high-throughput sequencing data, with proficiency in at least one
scripting/programming language (Python, R, Bash, or equivalent) and
familiarity with bioinformatics tools and workflow management
systems (e.g., Snakemake, Nextflow).
Successful teaching experience at the college or university
level, with evidence of effective instruction of NGS and
computational biology topics to students from diverse disciplinary
backgrounds.
Demonstrated ability to design and deliver innovative
curriculum using a variety of instructional approaches, including
active learning, project-based learning, and computational lab
environments.
Commitment to inclusive excellence: ability to work
respectfully and collaboratively with students and colleagues from
all backgrounds, and demonstrated advocacy for women, people of
color, first-generation students, and other groups underrepresented
in computational sciences.
Strong written and oral communication skills, including the
ability to explain complex algorithmic concepts clearly to
non-expert audiences.
Demonstrated capacity for continuous professional development,
including staying current with rapidly evolving NGS technologies,
tools, and best practices.
Preferred
Postdoctoral or industry experience applying NGS methods in a
research context.
Experience teaching or mentoring in a bioinformatics, genomics,
or data science program at the graduate level.
Familiarity with cloud computing environments (AWS, Google
Cloud, or equivalent) and high-performance computing clusters for
large-scale genomics analyses and workflow management tools
(Nextflow, Snakemake).
Experience developing online or hybrid bioinformatics courses,
including the design of computational lab modules and auto-graded
assessments.
Track record of interdisciplinary collaboration bridging
computational and experimental biology.
Strong commitment to the teacher-scholar model at a primarily
undergraduate institution (PUI).

jobs.title: TT ASSISTANT PROFESSOR of VOICE / UMKC CONSERVATORY / Music Div
jobs.description:
Job Details
Hiring Department
UNIVERSITY of MISSOURI-KANSAS CITY
CONSERVATORY
Music Division
At the University of Missouri-Kansas City Conservatory, we take
pride in collaboration across the divisions of music, dance, and
theatre, and in advancing the integration of art forms through
performance, teaching, and creative work. Our integrated arts
approach intentionally brings together multiple disciplines to
deepen learning, expand artistic practice, and enrich audience
experiences. Conservatory
| UMKC
Building on the Conservatory's strengths in classical voice, opera,
and art song, and its integrated programs in theatre, dance, and
emerging media, this position strengthens a distinct need in the
Voice area: a teacher and performer whose work is grounded in sound
vocal technique and pedagogy, with demonstrated ability to extend
that technical foundation into musical theatre and
contemporary-commercial styles. The successful candidate will value
foundational voice building as the basis for stylistic flexibility
while preparing singers to perform successfully across multiple
genres.
The position is intended to enhance existing degree programs rather
than establish a new one. It does not create a musical theatre
major or degree. Instead, it broadens students' access to
contemporary vocal skills and styles within the Conservatory's
established voice and music curricula, supports the new
undergraduate certificate in Musical Theatre, and complements
existing strengths in classical voice, opera, choral, and
cross-genre performance. The goal is to prepare singers as
versatile artists with broad, modern skills for a range of
21st-century careers. Music - Areas
of Study - Conservatory | UMKC
Job Description
Musical Theatre & Contemporary-Commercial Emphasis
Full-time, Tenure-Track | Assistant Professor of Voice
The UMKC Conservatory invites applications for a full-time,
tenure-track Assistant Professor of Voice with an emphasis in
musical theatre and contemporary-commercial styles, beginning Fall
2027.
We seek a versatile teacher and performer with expertise in sound
vocal technique and pedagogy who can also lead students into
musical theatre and contemporary-commercial practice, including
belt, mix, and a range of contemporary styles. The successful
candidate will understand foundational voice building and vocal
pedagogy as the basis for stylistic versatility, preparing singers
to move fluidly among classical, musical theatre, and
contemporary-commercial genres. The ideal candidate may also
demonstrate: Excellence as a teacher and performer grounded in
sound vocal technique and pedagogy, with demonstrated experience
applying that technical foundation to musical theatre and/or
contemporary-commercial styles.
Areas of practice may include musical theatre voice and styles,
contemporary-commercial music, song interpretation and acting
through song, and related contemporary vocal work grounded in
healthy vocal technique and sound technical craft.
Primary Responsibilities
Teach undergraduate and graduate applied voice across
classical, musical theatre, and contemporary-commercial styles,
grounded in foundational voice building and vocal pedagogy.
Teach studio and classroom coursework in areas of specialty,
which may include musical theatre voice and styles, song
interpretation and acting through song, and contemporary vocal
pedagogy.
Support the new undergraduate certificate in Musical Theatre
through instruction and curriculum, without establishing a separate
degree program.
Collaborate with faculty in Theatre and Dance to provide
integrated training in singing, acting, and movement.
Contribute to the Voice area's strategic vision for versatile,
career-ready artists, including new initiatives and
interdisciplinary performance.
Maintain an active agenda of creative and/or scholarly activity
at the regional, national, and international levels.
Recruit and mentor undergraduate and graduate students,
including outreach and possible summer programming.
Engage in service through committees, community partnerships,
and professional organizations.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications
A terminal degree in vocal performance, vocal pedagogy, or a
related field, or equivalent professional experience.
Pedagogical command of foundational voice building together
with contemporary vocal technique (including belt, mix, and healthy
contemporary vocal production), demonstrating the ability to teach
singers successfully across classical and contemporary styles.
A record of professional performance in musical theatre and/or
contemporary-commercial music.
Ability to recruit and retain talented undergraduate and
graduate students.
Creative and/or scholarly achievement and the interpersonal
skills necessary for success in higher education.
Preferred Qualifications
Collegiate teaching experience in voice, musical theatre, or
contemporary-commercial styles.
Demonstrated experience teaching singers across both classical
and contemporary vocal traditions, including opera, art song,
musical theatre, and contemporary-commercial repertoire.
Experience teaching or developing curriculum for non-major and
interdisciplinary students.
Skills in music direction and/or collaborative piano, including
the ability to coach and lead from the keyboard to assist Musical
Theatre productions when needed.
Experience collaborating with Theatre and Dance faculty to
integrate acting and movement into vocal instruction and/or the
curriculum in support of expressive, stylistically versatile
performance.
Familiarity with vocal health and pedagogy across multiple
styles.
Experience with recording, media, or immersive and
interdisciplinary performance.
Connections to professional musical theatre and the broader
performing arts industry.
Active involvement in professional organizations, with
long-term potential for leadership.
Anticipated Hiring Range
This is a 9-month, tenure-track, benefit-eligible ranked faculty
position to begin with the Fall 2027 semester. Salary is
commensurate with experience and credentials. Our academic
workloads and schedules provide for a positive work/life
balance.
Your total compensation goes beyond the number on your paycheck.
The University of Missouri provides generous leave, health plans,
discounted tuition at all four UM System campuses for employees and
qualifying dependents, and retirement contributions that add to
your bottom line.
Application Materials
For consideration, you must apply online at Careers - Human Resources |
University of Missouri-Kansas City / Academic Positions /
Prospective employees: Job Opening ID 61022 .
Please complete the online application form with questions, and
submit the following materials:
A one-page cover letter that explains how your work, past or
future, aligns with the Conservatory Vision Statement:
https://conservatory.umkc.edu/about-us/vision-mission-principles.html
Curriculum Vitae
Current contact information for at least three professional
references
Links to representative performances demonstrating musical
theatre and/or contemporary-commercial styles, as well as classical
repertoire that reflects the candidate's technical and artistic
foundation.

Microsoft Word document and upload as your resume attachment
. Additionally, please limit the document name to 50
characters and do not include any special characters (e.g., /,
&, %, etc.). Maximum size limit is 11MB .
If you are experiencing technical problems during application,
please email umpshrsupport@umsystem.edu
.
For questions about the position, please contact umkcfacultysearch@umkc.edu
including the Job Identification number 61022 and name of
the position.
Reasonable accommodation may be requested during the
application and recruitment process. If you need an accommodation,
please contact the Office of Equity and Title IX at (816)
235-1323.
We will request higher education transcripts for applicants who
progress to the finalist stage. A Criminal Background Check is

Application Deadline
Review of applications will begin November 1, 2026, and continue
until a qualified candidate is hired.
Sponsorship Information

currently in the United States in H-1B status or other

Other Information
The UMKC Conservatory is a vibrant community of artists, educators,
and scholars located in the heart of Kansas City's thriving arts
corridor. Committed to excellence, innovation, and equity, the
Conservatory prepares students to become leading performers,
educators, conductors, and scholar-artists. As part of an
R-1 public research university, the Conservatory offers
exceptional opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration,
community engagement, and global impact.
We seek colleagues who:
help build the future of performance, education, and research
in the performing arts;
demonstrate a growth mindset, with an understanding that
learning is an ongoing process;
believe that art has the power to help us understand ourselves,
each other, and our culture while empowering us to move that
culture forward;
engage in work that appeals to, and positively impacts, the
global population;
contribute to a collaborative, respectful, and supportive
culture by building positive relationships with colleagues and
fostering an environment that encourages creativity, innovation,
and student success; and
adapt to the opportunities in their regions and work within

Community Information
A City on the Rise: Big City Life and Midwest Charm, Kansas

with midwestern appeal and an affordable cost of living. Our UMKC
campuses are centered in the hubs of cultural arts, business

Our beautiful state has rolling hills, rivers, lakes, and long

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of History/Coordinator of History Education
jobs.description:
The successful candidate will serve as both an Early World History professor and the Program Coordinator for the nationally accredited History Education program, which includes supervising the student teaching field experiences, teaching the required Methods course for Social Studies secondary education, and maintaining documentation and data for the purposes of preserving the program’s accreditation. The candidate will also advise History Education majors, ensuring that teacher candidates have fulfilled the minimum hours required for field experiences. Finally, the successful candidate will teach General Education courses both online and in-person in subjects such as Early World History and World Cultural Geography, in addition to upper-division courses in their area of expertise.
The successful candidate will be responsible for:
Completing systematic program reviews to ensure content alignment with the Council for Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP) and national or state approved standards.
Evaluate assessments to ensure content aligns with teacher competencies and state and national standards, review and adjust processes for assessment redevelopment, and track passing rates on subject-area tests to analyze and target potential obstacles to teacher certification.
Serve on the Teacher Education Council (TEC) and coordinate History Education program accreditation processes, which includes attending TEC meetings.
Attending NCSS annual training sessions and overseeing the implementation of any SPA standard changes to the History Education program.
Maintaining weekly office hours appropriate to course load
Participating in early grade alert systems and assessing student outcomes
Advising students and supporting student activities
Continuing professional development
Work Setting & Expectations
Reports to the Chair of the Social Sciences Department.
Completion of safety and job-related training as required.
Salary determined according to SWOSU’s wage structure.
Responsible for following safety procedures and maintaining a safe work environment.
Full-time, 9-month, exempt position.
Employment at will.
Education and Experience
Ph.D. in History preferred.
Must be legally authorized to work in the United States.
Familiarity with InTASC Core Teaching Standards, CAEP accreditation standards, and C3 Framework is preferred.
Prior teaching experience at the secondary and collegiate level is preferred.
Technological competence and experience in the LMS Canvas is preferred. Expectations are to maintain a Canvas site for each course and gain a working knowledge of the Colleague system.
Candidates must include a statement on teaching philosophy.
Application submission deadline: November 6, 2026

jobs.title: Assistant Professor (Teaching) - Psychology
jobs.description:
Job Details
Assistant Professor (Teaching) - Psychology
Wayne State University is searching for an experienced Assistant
Professor (Teaching) - Psychology at its Detroit campus
location.
Wayne State is a premier, public, urban research university located
in the heart of Detroit, Michigan where students from all
backgrounds are offered a rich, high-quality education. Our
deep-rooted commitment to excellence, collaboration, integrity,
diversity and inclusion creates exceptional educational
opportunities which prepare students for success in a global
society.
Essential functions (job duties):
The Department of Psychology invites applications for a full-time
(9 months) Assistant Professor (Teaching) position
(non-tenure-track). We seek an active and engaged colleague with
demonstrated professional and teaching interests within Psychology.
Preferred candidates should be able to teach several of our
undergraduate core major courses, which include Introduction to
Psychology, Statistics, Research Methods, Learning and Memory,
Perception, Cognition, Developmental Psychology, and Health
Psychology. Course format is primarily in-person, but may also
include hybrid, or online delivery. Teaching load is 3:3 (fall and
winter semesters) Candidates are also expected to participate in
department committees and activities.
The successful candidate will join a vibrant and engaged academic
unit. Our faculty have achieved national and international
reputations for excellence in their respective fields of research.
We offer a collegial environment, state-of-the art facilities,
excellent programming, and extensive training opportunities for
teaching-related careers, such as those offered by the University’s
Office of Teaching and Learning.
Teach in-person, hybrid and/or online courses in the Psychology
undergraduate program. Courses could include Introduction to
Psychology, Statistics, Research Methods, Learning and Memory,
Perception, Developmental Psychology, Cognitive Psychology or
Health Psychology.
Assist program faculty and staff with student recruitment and
retention initiatives, program assessment and other duties required
to meet organizational needs.
Serve on departmental committees.
Qualifications:
Candidates with a Ph.D. in Psychology or a related field are
preferred. However, those who are ABD or hold a Master's degree and
have considerable professional experience may be considered.
Evidence of effective university teaching experience, including in
person instruction using best practices in course design.
Candidates should apply at jobs.wayne.edu. Include a cover letter
that addresses: (1) teaching experiences and interests; (2)
teaching philosophy, particularly regarding undergraduate
instruction; and (3) commitment and readiness to work with a
diverse population of students. Applicants should also provide a
curriculum vitae (CV) with the names, titles, and contact
information for three professional references, and a teaching
portfolio that includes course evaluations and example
syllabi.
Questions about this search may be directed to Emily Grekin, Search
Committee Chair, at grekine@wayne.edu.

jobs.title: Associate/Full Professor Tenured Faculty Appointment
jobs.description:
Job Details
Associate/Full Professor Tenured Faculty Appointment
Wayne State University is searching for an experienced
Associate/Full Professor Tenured Faculty Appointment at its
Detroit campus location.
Wayne State is a premier, public, urban research university located
in the heart of Detroit, Michigan where students from all
backgrounds are offered a rich, high-quality education. Our
deep-rooted commitment to excellence, collaboration, integrity,
diversity and inclusion creates exceptional educational
opportunities which prepare students for success in a global
society.
Position Purpose:
The College of Education (COE) at Wayne State University (WSU) is
pleased to invite applications for a tenured faculty position at
the rank of Associate Professor or Full Professor.
Salary and rank for position are commensurate with qualifications
and experience.
Application Deadline: October 16, 2026. Start Date: Fall
2027
The Wayne State University College of Education invites
applications for a full-time, 9-month, tenured faculty position in
the History of Education and/or Cultural Studies in Education, with
a research agenda centered on the study of Black education broadly
defined. This innovative role will include graduate teaching and
advising responsibilities in the COE Educational Leadership and
Policy Studies (ELPS) program, inform and assist in the development
and oversight of curriculum, youth and professional development,
and school-community engagement programs in coordination with the
newly established WSU Detroit Center for Black Studies.
The College of Education:
Since beginning as the Detroit Normal Training School in 1881, the
College of Education at Wayne State University has grown to offer
award-winning, nationally recognized bachelor’s, master’s,
education specialist, and doctoral degree programs in 29 programs
with 39 degree and certificate options, which are accredited
through their national professional organizations and by the
Michigan Department of Education. The College of Education educates
approximately 2,000 students annually.
The College’s diverse academic programs benefit greatly from its
history of engagement with urban communities and the comprehensive
range of programs spanning teaching and research opportunities
afforded by its location in metropolitan Detroit. The College of
Education’s faculty and staff are dedicated to preparing
professionals who can contribute in meaningful ways to a global,
technology-oriented society by helping them acquire the knowledge,
skills and attitudes necessary to succeed in their chosen careers
in education, health, wellness, sports, counseling, government, and
more.
The Wayne State University Community:
Wayne State University is classified as a “doctoral university:
very high research activity” by the Carnegie Classification of
Institutions of Higher Education. We are located in Midtown
Detroit, the city center and one of the country’s fastest growing
neighborhoods, which welcomes more than 2.5 million visitors
annually. Here, you’ll find 200 acres of green space, walking
paths, and state-of-the-art facilities surrounded by renowned
cultural institutions and industry-leading employers.
Candidates should possess scholarship that demonstrates a sustained
commitment to advancing the study of Black education while
contributing to broader conversations in the history of education,
cultural studies, educational foundations, curriculum studies, and
related interdisciplinary fields.
Essential Functions:
Exceptional candidates are humanities-oriented scholars whose
research examines the historical, cultural, political,
intellectual, and institutional dimensions of Black educational
experiences in the United States and/or across the African
Diaspora. Areas of specialization may include, but are not limited
to:
Histories of Black education and educational thought.
Curriculum, pedagogy, and the politics of knowledge
production.
Black cultural studies and education.
Black educational politics, policy, and social movements.
Arts, humanities, and cultural production as sites of Black
teaching and learning.
Black independent schools and institution-building
traditions.
Informal, community-based, and out-of-school educational
practices.
Homeschooling, home education, and alternative educational
formations within Black communities.
Black abolitionist, and liberatory educational traditions.
Afro-Pessimist, Black feminist, Africana, and other critical
theoretical approaches to education.
Rehumanizing, culturally sustaining, and community-centered
methodologies in Black educational research.
Interdisciplinary approaches that expand conventional
understandings of schooling, education, knowledge, and Black
intellectual life.
Minimum Qualifications:
A Record of Community-Engaged Research and Curriculum : We
seek a scholar who has established a community-engaged and Black
Studies-focused research agenda, preferably through works
supporting the work of urban schools and cultural institutions,
including museums and youth & community organizations. Scholars
who have engaged in humanities-focused educational and curriculum
initiatives and with a track record of ongoing engagement with
educators, youth, community leaders and organizers, and/or cultural
workers will be prioritized.
Scholarly Productivity: Compelling candidates will have
publications in reputable academic journals in education,
humanities, and/or cultural studies, monographs, edited volumes,
and and/or journal special issues who are engaged in multi- and
trans-disciplinary research and collaborations both within and
beyond education. They will also be engaged in dissemination
practices that raise the visibility of Black Studies in Education
(e.g., publications in influential journals and/or media outlets,
state- or national-level speaking engagements, community-based
programming with notable impact, etc.).
Doctoral Advising: As the College of Education moves to
establish a new Ph.D. program, applicants must have experience and
an interest in and capacity to advise doctoral students early in
their appointment, especially to guide and support Ph.D. and Ed.D.
students already enrolled in the ELPS program.
Embody College Values: Important review criteria include
evidence of a commitment to working with communities and
organizations that reflect Detroit’s demographics and address their
socio-cultural, economic, and political realities; commitment to
excellence in research, teaching, and graduate student advising;
and eagerness to embody the College’s vivid vision of radical
neighborliness (i.e., supporting all members of the College and
local communities by taking bold and provocative actions to foster
compassion, inclusivity, social connection, and a sense of the
common good).
Applicants must have an earned doctorate in Education, Black or
African/African American Studies, a disciplinary or
interdisciplinary field in the humanities, or a related
field.
Application Process :
All applicants must use the WSU Online Hiring System at www.
https://hr.wayne.edu/jobs ,
referring to position req # 3604 . Electronic
applications must include a cover letter; curriculum vita (CV);
names and contact information for at least 3 references, and 2 to 3
representative publications. The search committee will begin
reviewing applications on October 16, 2026, and continue
until the position is filled.
Inquiries about the position may be directed to the chair of the
search committee:
Dr. Rema Vassar
Professor, Educational Leadership and Policy Studies
College of Education
DrRema@wayne.edu
Preferred Qualifications:
Educational Experience : We are especially interested in
applicants who have served as educators in K-20 schools,
community-based organizations, or cultural institutions,
particularly in urban and diverse settings.
Externally Funded Research : We are excited about applicants
who have demonstrated the ability to raise external funds to
support their research and other collaborative projects.

jobs.title: DIRECTOR, CLINICAL EDUCATION AND CLINICAL ASSISTANT PROFESSOR
jobs.description:
Job Details
Full-time, 12-month, multi-year renewable notice (non-tenure)
position to begin on or about October 1, 2026, the Director of
Clinical Education (DCE) provides administrative, educational, and
clinical leadership for the clinical phase of the Physician
Assistant Studies program. The DCE oversees development,
implementation, evaluation, and continuous improvement of clinical
education; supports clinical site and preceptor development;
monitors learner performance and progression; and collaborates with
faculty and staff to promote student success and compliance with
applicable accreditation standards. The DCE also contributes to the
didactic and clinical curriculum through teaching, assessment,
advising, and clinical learning activities.
Primary Responsibilities
Provide administrative leadership, coordination, and guidance
to faculty and staff involved in the clinical phase of the
Physician Assistant Studies program.
Provide clinical education oversight, including clinical
curriculum, site development, learner performance monitoring, and
accreditation compliance.
Create, update, and evaluate syllabi, instructional objectives,
and learning activities for clinical rotations and ensure alignment
with program competencies, current clinical practice, and
applicable ARC-PA standards.
Manage clinical-phase learner assignments, assessments,
progression, and remediation in collaboration with faculty, the
clinical year team (CYT), and program leadership.
Establish, maintain, and evaluate review clinical sites and
preceptors in collaboration with clinical and didactic education
team members.
Develop and implement clinical rotation scheduling in
collaboration with the Clinical Coordinator and clinical/didactic
team.
Collaborate with the Clinical Coordinator regarding clinical
placement, affiliation agreements, clinical documentation,
scheduling, learner records, and clinical education
operations.
Ensure clinical faculty and preceptors are oriented to learner
assessment, program expectations, and evaluation of student
achievement of clinical competencies.
Schedule, organize, and conduct clinical site visits to
evaluate clinical learning environments, learner experiences,
preceptor support, and access to appropriate supervision.
Schedule, organize, plan, and implement clinical orientation
activities, learner evaluations, End-of-Rotation activities, and
other clinical-year educational programming.
Lead, organize, and facilitate clinical callback sessions to
support integration of didactic and clinical learning, strengthen
clinical reasoning and decision-making, address identified learner
needs, and promote preparation for clinical practice and the
PANCE.
Lead and facilitate Clinical Year Team meetings, establish
priorities, coordinate discussion of student performance and
clinical operations, document action items, and monitor
follow-through.
Provide effective advising and mentoring to learners regarding
clinical rotations, clinical performance, professional development,
and preparation for clinical practice.
Teach within the didactic and clinical curricula, including
clinical cases, clinical reasoning, patient care, skills, and other
content consistent with professional expertise and program
needs.
Collaborate with faculty, staff, the Medical Director, and
other program stakeholders to integrate didactic and clinical
education and address learner needs.
Monitor clinical learner performance, including clinical
evaluations, EOR examination performance, clinical competencies,
remediation, and progression.
Conduct and/or coordinate data collection and analysis related
to the clinical phase and use findings to support continuous
quality improvement.
Facilitate clinical contract completion and coordinate with
appropriate College personnel, contract specialists, and legal
counsel as needed.
Ensure that accurate clinical education records, including
schedules, evaluations, learner documentation, immunizations,
certifications, site information, and preceptor qualifications are
maintained
Maintain and update clinical site and rotation information to
ensure accuracy in designated clinical education management and
accreditation portal.
Work with Clinical Coordinator to monitor that required
documentation demonstrating preceptor qualifications and other
clinical education requirements is accurate and up to date.
Collaborate with appropriate College personnel and Clinical
Coordinator regarding preceptor compensation and related
documentation.
Participate in learner academic and professional progression
processes, including the Academic Progress, Promotion, and
Remediation Committee (APPRC), as assigned.
Serve as a member of the Admissions Committee and participate
in applicant review and interviews.
Serve as a member of the Curriculum Review Committee and
contribute to curriculum review, mapping, assessment, and
continuous improvement.
Serve as a member of the Executive Committee and contribute to
program planning, strategic priorities, operational decisions, and
continuous quality improvement.
Participate in faculty meetings, program assessment,
accreditation activities, and other committees or initiatives as
assigned by the Program Director.
Collaborate with program faculty and staff to strengthen
clinical education processes, policies, procedures, and
performance.
Perform other duties consistent with the responsibilities of
the position and needs of the Physician Assistant Program.
Required Qualifications
Master’s degree in Physician Assistant Studies, Health
Professions Education, Medical Education, Health Sciences
Education, Curriculum and Instruction, Educational
Leadership/Administration or another closely related health
professions or education discipline.
If a PA, current NCCPA certification and licensure in the State
of New York within six months of start date. If not a PA, current
professional license/certification in the State of New York within
six months of start date appropriate to the professional
discipline, when applicable.
Three years of professional preparation and experience
appropriate to assigned clinical and instructional
responsibilities.
Demonstrated clinical expertise sufficient to provide clinical
education and instruction.
Demonstrated ability to provide clinical instruction,
supervision, assessment, and learner feedback.
Preferred Qualifications
Doctoral degree
Previous clinical precepting or teaching experience in an
accredited Physician Assistant program, medical school, or other
health professions program.
Prior experience in clinical education leadership or
administration.
Experience developing, evaluating, or coordinating clinical
education programs.
Experience with clinical site and preceptor recruitment,
development, evaluation, and compliance.
Experience with student remediation, academic advising, and
learner assessment.
Experience with accreditation, continuous quality improvement,
curriculum development, and assessment.
Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
Strong interpersonal, organizational, and communication
skills.
Effective leadership and collaborative skills.
Competent analytical and problem-solving skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, due dates, and clinical
education operations.
Commitment to learner-centered education and student
success.
Commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and a culture of
care.
Passion for Physician Assistant education and development of
future healthcare professionals.
Ability to work collaboratively with students, faculty, staff,
clinical partners, preceptors, and healthcare professionals.
PA Program Equity, Belonging, and Inclusion Statement
The Ithaca College PA Program uses an equity framework to guide our
work that seeks to be representative of all people including those
impacted by systematic disadvantages and marginalization. Program
activities and topics will enhance the capacity of our faculty,
staff, and learners to communicate across differences in productive
ways. The activities and topics in our program can be applied in
the workplace, classroom and clinic, interpersonal relationships,
and community engagement. The Ithaca College PA Program will
provide a brave place for healthy discussions while respecting and
caring for each other.
Salary Range
$116,000-$123,000, commensurate with experience. Associate
Professor level considered, depending on experience.
Application Instructions
Interested applicants must apply online and submit a cover letter,
resume, and the names and contact information for three
professional references. Questions regarding the application
process should be directed to the Office of Human Resources at
(607) 274-8000 or humanresources@ithaca.edu
.
Ithaca College is committed to building a diverse academic
community and encourages applications from individuals whose
experiences contribute to the diversity and excellence of the
College.
Visa sponsorship may be provided for this position.
We pride ourselves on providing our benefit-eligible employees
with comprehensive benefits, including:
• Healthcare including vision and dental
• Generous Paid Time Off Policies
• 403B Retirement Savings Plan with Matching Employer
Contribution
• EAP
• Flexible Work Plans
• Educational Benefits
• Career-Enhancing Trainings
• For an overview of our benefit offerings, please visit https://www.ithaca.edu/human-resources/employee-benefits-wellness.
In an effort to promote campus safety and the security of College
resources, Ithaca College will, consistent with the requirements of
the law and prudent practices, conduct criminal background
investigations per College policy. This position is subject to a
criminal background check. All offers of employment are contingent
upon review of the criminal background check.
About Us
At Ithaca College, a comprehensive residential campus community of
approximately 5,000 students, we strive to be at the forefront of
the higher education landscape. We offer a distinct integrative
learning experience that makes students ready for the personal,
professional, and global challenges of our age.
We seek candidates who embrace integrative learning and want to be
a part of this exciting time in Ithaca College history. We
encourage creative collaboration and innovation in our faculty and
staff, providing support and resources for them to grow in their
fields and lead students to their own innovative ideas and
achievements.
We welcome different ways of thinking and look for candidates with
unique points of view and life experiences. We are inclusive of
individuals with a wide range of cultural, personal, and
professional backgrounds, talents, and skills. Our campus is a
vibrant and rewarding community where diverse minds can learn,
succeed, and excel.
When reviewing candidates, we are looking for indicators of a
number of core competencies. Prospective candidates must be
adaptable, collaborative, inclusive, respectful, responsive,
results driven, and sustainable. They must communicate effectively,
demonstrate leadership, exhibit professional integrity and ethics,
take initiative, value personal and professional development, and
show that they will engage in the college.
Nestled in the heart of New York State’s scenic Finger Lakes
region, Ithaca College sits atop South Hill overlooking picturesque
Cayuga Lake and is just minutes away from the city center.
Combining small town warmth and charm with the vibrancy of a
college community, the thriving and culturally diverse city of
Ithaca has been rated by Kiplinger’s as one of the top 10 places to
live in the United States.
In an effort to promote campus safety and the security of College
resources, Ithaca College will, consistent with the requirements of
the law and prudent practices, conduct criminal background
investigations per College policy. This position is subject to a
criminal background check. All offers of employment are contingent

jobs.title: Instructional Faculty FT - Biotechnology
jobs.description:
Job Description
Montgomery College invites applications for one full-time faculty
position based at the Biotechnology Department at their Germantown
Campus. We seek an enthusiastic and dedicated educator who exhibits
a strong commitment to our students, a high degree of
professionalism, and the ability to create a positive and an
engaging learning space . The ideal candidate should have
experience working in biotechnology or biopharmaceutical industry
with current technical knowledge, regulated-workplace experience,
and real-world perspective, and/or experience teaching those skills
at a post-secondary level (two-year or four-year institutions) . We
are looking for a candidate with strong commitment to student
success, the community college mission, and preparing a diverse
student population for biotechnology careers. This position is part
of a collective bargaining unit.
The successful candidate will appreciate teaching in a
multi-cultural environment and will welcome the opportunity to work
with students with diverse learning abilities.
Montgomery College is strategically located in the BioHealth
Capital Region near federal agencies, biotechnology companies,
research institutions and healthcare organizations. Montgomery
College has state-of-the art science facilities and equipment with
all of our science buildings being less than 15 years old.
Biotechnology instruction is supported by specialized teaching
laboratories and a simulated cGMP training facility at the
Bioscience Education Center.
Teaching assignments may include various delivery modes, such as
face-to-face, on-line, hybrid and/or blended formats during days,
evenings, and weekends. Montgomery College has multiple campuses,
and faculty may be assigned to teach in-person at any of these
campuses and teach online .
The successful candidate will teach lecture and laboratory courses
across the biotechnology curriculum, with particular emphasis on
cell culture and aseptic technique, biomanufacturing and current
Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP), and cell and gene therapy
techniques. The faculty member will translate industry practices
into accessible, hands-on learning and help students understand the
expectations, workflows, documentation, quality systems, and
problem-solving approaches used in biotechnology workplaces.
Candidates must have a demonstrated history of teaching scientific
content and training others in scientific techniques, methods,
equipment, or procedures. This experience may have been gained in
industry, academic, or other professional settings.
About the Biotechnology Program
The Biotechnology Department offers an Associate of Applied Science
in Biotechnology and certificates in Biotechnology,
Biomanufacturing, and Cell and Gene Therapy. The program emphasizes
applied laboratory skills, scientific problem-solving,
documentation, and workforce preparation while also supporting
transfer to four-year institutions.
Courses include Introduction to Biotechnology, Cell Culture,
Aseptic Technique, Protein Biotechnology, Applied Immunology,
Nucleic Acid Methods, Biomanufacturing, and Cell and Gene Therapy.
Students may also participate in internships, apprenticeships, and
other experiential learning opportunities.
Duties include but are not limited to:
Teach lecture and laboratory sections of biotechnology courses
using student-centered and evidence -based instructional
practices.
Teach across the biotechnology curriculum, with primary
emphasis on mammalian cell culture and aseptic processing,
biomanufacturing and cGMP, and cell and gene therapy concepts and
laboratory methods.
Teaches 30 semester hours per academic year. Prepares course
materials such as syllabi, homework assignments and handouts;
evaluates and grades students' exams, assignments, and papers.
Holds office hours for student help.
Teaches a varied schedule of courses that may include day,
night, early morning, weekend and/or accelerated sections,
compressed and online. Opportunities may exist for teaching summer
classes.
Translate current industry workflows, standards, case examples,
and workplace expectations into practical learning experiences
appropriate for community college students.
Develop students' ability to follow standard operating
procedures, apply good documentation practices, work safely and
aseptically, analyze data, troubleshoot technical problems, and
communicate scientific information.
Design, assess, and continuously improve curricula to reflect
current biotechnology practices, workforce needs, transfer
expectations, and emerging technologies.
Use current laboratory instrumentation, digital tools,
instructional technology, and the College learning management
system to support student learning.
Advise and mentor students regarding academic planning,
transfer, internships, and biotechnology career pathways.
Participate in student recruitment, retention, outreach, and
experiential-learning initiatives, including partnerships with
employers, schools, government agencies, and four-year
institutions.
Collaborate with faculty, staff, advisory committees, and
external partners; participate in departmental, campus, College,
and participatory-governance activities.
Maintain professional currency through continuing education,
industry engagement, scholarship, and participation in relevant
professional organizations.
Contribute to grant-funded projects and, as opportunities
arise, supervise undergraduate research, honors projects,
internships, or other applied learning experiences.
Required Qualifications:
Master's degree or higher in biotechnology, biological
sciences, biochemistry, chemistry, biomedical sciences, or a
closely related field.
At least three years of full-time professional experience in
the biotechnology, biopharmaceutical, cell and gene therapy, or
closely related industry. A combination of industry experience and
teaching experience in Biotechnology or a closely related field
will be considered.
Hands-on industry experience in cell culture and aseptic
technique and in at least one of the following areas:
biomanufacturing, bioprocessing, cell and gene therapy, process
development, quality control, quality assurance, manufacturing
sciences and technology, or technical operations.
Demonstrated history of teaching scientific content and
training others in laboratory techniques, technical methods,
equipment, or procedures in an industry, academic,
workforce-training, or other professional setting.
Current knowledge of biotechnology laboratory and manufacturing
practices, instrumentation, documentation, and workplace
expectations.
Experience writing, interpreting, and following standard
operating procedures and working within a regulated or
quality-focused environment such as cGMP, GLP, or an equivalent
quality system.
Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively and collaborate
with colleagues, students, and external partners.
Demonstrated ability to engage and facilitate learning for
students with varied academic preparation, backgrounds, cultures,
and experiences.
Experience using instructional technology and a learning
management system, or the ability to develop these skills
promptly.
Eligible applicants must currently be authorized to work in the
United States and not require employer visa sponsorship
Preferred Qualifications:
Ph.D. in biotechnology, a life-science discipline, chemistry,
biomedical engineering, or a closely related field.
Five or more years of biotechnology or biopharmaceutical
industry experience, particularly in manufacturing, process
development, quality control, quality assurance, manufacturing
sciences and technology, or technical operations.
Hands-on experience with mammalian cell culture, aseptic
processing, contamination control, cell banking, and upstream
bioprocessing.
Experience teaching or working in biomanufacturing environments
involving cGMP, good documentation practices, deviations, change
control, CAPA, data integrity, or other elements of a
pharmaceutical quality system.
Knowledge of cell and gene therapy platforms and manufacturing
workflows, such as viral or nonviral gene delivery, transfection or
transduction, cell expansion, harvest, purification, or relevant
analytical and release testing.
Experience with bioprocessing and analytical equipment such as
benchtop bioreactors, single-use systems, AKTA/FPLC systems,
chromatography, plate readers, flow cytometers, PCR/qPCR
instruments, or related platforms.
Experience with protein, immunological, nucleic-acid, or

manufacturing, or clinical and quality laboratories.
Experience developing technical training, competency
assessments, standard work, or job aids; coaching individuals with

Experience collaborating with employers, advisory boards,

jobs.description:
Job Description
Montgomery College, Rockville Campus, seeks a full-time Biology
faculty member in the Natural Sciences and Engineering (NSE) area
to fill a position starting January 2027. This position will
primarily teach Human Anatomy and Physiology I and II, with
additional teaching responsibilities in introductory biology
courses for biology majors and non- majors students. We are seeking
an enthusiastic and dedicated educator who exhibits a high degree
of professionalism, a strong commitment to our students, and the
ability to motivate and educate in an engaging manner. This
position is part of a collective bargaining unit.
Anatomy and Physiology I and II serve as a foundational course
sequence for students preparing to enter nursing and other health
sciences programs at Montgomery College and at other regional
institutions. The successful candidate will play a key role in
preparing these students for competitive admission and for success
in their coursework. All of Montgomery College's science buildings
were constructed within the last 15 years and feature
state-of-the-art facilities and equipment, including dedicated
anatomy and physiology laboratories.
The successful candidate will appreciate teaching in a
multi-cultural environment and will welcome the opportunity to work
with students with diverse learning abilities. Faculty duties
include classroom and laboratory instruction, assessment,
curriculum development, advising, professional inquiry, committee
work, and instructional technology. The opportunity to engage in
research with students is also supported and encouraged.
Teaching assignments may include various delivery modes, such as
face-to-face, online, remote, hybrid and/or blended formats during
days, evenings, and weekends. Montgomery College has four campuses
and instructs courses at area high schools, as part of the growing
dual enrollment program. Faculty may be assigned to any of these
campuses and/or teaching different modalities.
Duties include but are not limited to:
Teaching and Curriculum
Teaches anatomy and physiology and introductory biology courses
with a minimum of 30 semester hours per academic year. This
teaching position is expected to include Human Anatomy and
Physiology I and II (BIOL 212 and BIOL 213), Introductory Biology
(BIOL 101 and/or BIOL 150), and other courses in the discipline as
needed.
Teaches a varied schedule that may include day, evening, early
morning, weekend, and accelerated sections. Opportunities may exist
for teaching summer classes.
Designs, implements, manages, and assesses courses taught in a
variety of modes, incorporating the use of a learning management

instruction.
Engages students in learning through active, collaborative, and
experiential learning approaches, and accommodates students with
varying backgrounds and learning styles.
Contributes to curriculum development and revision, including

materials.
Delivers assigned courses in accordance with College catalog
descriptions and the teaching standards of the College and the NSE
area.
Participates in General Education assessment, course
recertification, and program review with the goal of increasing
student success.
Laboratory Instruction
Designs and prepares laboratory activities for anatomy and
physiology courses, collaborating with lab staff on necessary

Uses anatomical models, prepared specimens, histological

learning of structure and function.
Implements and enforces laboratory safety protocols, including
the safe handling and disposal of biological materials and
chemicals, in accordance with College policy.

Holds regular office hours and maintains availability to
students. Mentors and tutors students outside of class to assist
them with being successful in college.
Advises students about program curricula, health sciences
career pathways, and transfer options to four-year
institutions.
Arranges and promotes scholarship, research, and internship
opportunities for students.
Advises and supports student clubs and related student
activities.

Participates in college and community activities that
contribute to the growth and development of students, the College,

Serves on and leads department, discipline, campus, and college
committees.
Stays current in the discipline and pursues continuous
professional development, including participation in professional
organizations and activities.

Master’s degree or higher in a Biological Science or closely

physiology, or a related area.
One year of demonstrated college-level teaching experience,

jobs.title: Tenure-Track Faculty in Chemical and Biological Engineering
jobs.description:
Job Summary
The Department of Chemical and Biological Engineering at the
University of Colorado Boulder is currently seeking applications
for a tenure-track faculty position. The department and college are
particularly interested in qualified candidates who can contribute
through their research, teaching, and service to the diversity and
excellence of our academic community. This position will be hired
at the Assistant Professor rank.
CU is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all
applicable federal, state, and local laws governing
nondiscrimination in employment. We are committed to creating a
workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and
dignity, and we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to
apply, including protected veterans and individuals with
disabilities.
Who We Are
The University of Colorado Boulder (CU Boulder) is one of
Colorado’s flagship public institutions and among the most
research-active public universities in the country. The College of
Engineering and Applied Science is the second largest school or
college on the CU Boulder campus and boasts top-tier rankings for
both its graduate and undergraduate engineering programs, earning
the 11th spot among public graduate programs and 17th nationwide
for undergraduate engineering. Multiple specialty areas are also
ranked within the top 20. Equally importantly, we are committed to
fostering a diverse, inclusive, and academically excellent
community. Our approximately 250 tenure-track, 120
instructional-track, and 30 research-track faculty serve more than
6,000 undergraduate students, 1,300 master’s students, and 850 PhD
students. Our college has three core foci: (i) Research &
Innovation, (ii) Education, and (iii) Inclusion. We believe that
our college’s success requires faculty who actively work to create
an inclusive culture within the college and are committed to the
campus plan of creating and
sustaining supportive campus environments .
To learn more about the College of Engineering and Applied Science
please visit our website .
Ranked 11th among public universities for its graduate program and
11th for its undergraduate program by US News, the Department of
Chemical and Biological Engineering is a world-class department
with 38 faculty members, approximately 42 postdoctoral and other
research associates, 137 graduate students, and 401 undergraduate
students. The department has a proud tradition of academic
excellence. We have two robust ABET-accredited undergraduate degree
programs, where the emphasis is on interactive learning, computer
applications, a wide variety of interdisciplinary options, and
undergraduate research. We have created thousands of screencasts
and interactive simulations – available on LearnChemE.com – that
are accessed millions of times annually.
To learn more about the Department of Chemical and Biological
Engineering, please visit our website .
What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be
Successful candidates will be expected to engage in
undergraduate and graduate teaching and mentoring; develop an
externally funded research program in their technical area that
synergizes with others in the University of Colorado system (the
search is open with respect to area); contribute professional
leadership and service to the department, the college, and their
professional community; and cultivate and contribute to the
inclusive excellence of our academic community.
The typical distribution of work for this role is 40% teaching,
40% scholarly and creative work (research), and 20% leadership and
service.
What You Should Know
The anticipated start date for this position is Fall 2027;
however, a later start date may be negotiated.
Candidates whose expertise cuts across engineering and related
disciplines are especially encouraged to apply.
The University of Colorado Boulder has implemented a reference check
program with respect to final candidates for tenured faculty
appointments. The reference check program is intended to allow CU
Boulder to collect and review information about a candidate's
conduct at their current and previous institutions, specifically
conduct related to sexual misconduct, harassment, and/or
discrimination, before making hiring decisions. All final
candidates for tenured faculty appointments are required to
complete an Authorization to Release Information.
What We Can Offer
The anticipated academic year salary range for this position at
the Assistant Professor rank is $120,000-$130,000.
A relocation stipend may be available within CEAS
guidelines.
CU offers a competitive 401(a) retirement plan, with employees
contributing 5% of their annual eligible compensation and CU
contributing 10% of their eligible compensation. This plan is
standard for most faculty hires. For more information on CU's
retirement benefits visit our website here .
In addition to a competitive salary, the University of Colorado
Boulder offers a wide variety of other benefits and perks. Links to
these are below. To forecast the value of your total compensation,
check out our total compensation
calculator . More information on some of our benefits and perks
is available here: gender-neutral paid
parental leave ; housing down-payment
assistance programs ; dual-career &
relocation resources ; and teaching , research , and
professional development
.
Benefits
At the University of Colorado Boulder , we are
committed to supporting the holistic health and well-being of our
employees. Our comprehensive benefits package includes medical,
dental, and retirement plans; generous paid time off; tuition
assistance for you and your dependents; and an ECO Pass for local
transit. As one of Boulder County’s largest employers, CU Boulder
offers an inspiring academic community and access to world-class
outdoor recreation. In fact, CU Boulder has been named one of
Forbes' America's Best
Large Employers , ranking #4 among large employers in Colorado
and #28 among universities nationwide. Explore additional perks and
programs through the CU Advantage program.
Be Statements
Be authentic. Be pioneering. Be Boulder.
What We Require
Applicants must have earned a research doctorate or equivalent
degree in chemical engineering, biological engineering,
bioengineering, or a related field, and have their degree conferred
before starting a tenure-track faculty appointment.
Special Instructions
To apply, please submit the following materials as individual PDF
files:
Cover Letter: A one-page cover letter describing your
interest in the position and summarizing your personal academic
goals. Please indicate in the cover letter if you plan to attend
the fall national meetings for the American Institute of Chemical
Engineers (AIChE), Biomedical Engineering Society (BMES), or
Materials Research Society (MRS) and provide the details of the
sessions and presentations scheduled (if any).

jobs.title: Tenure-Track Faculty in Computer Architecture and Systems
jobs.description:
Job Summary
The Department of Computer Science at the University of Colorado
(CU) Boulder seeks applications for a tenure-track Assistant
Professor position in the broad areas of Computer Architecture and
Systems. The specific focus of this position is interdisciplinary,
spanning the broad areas of computer architecture, networking,
operating systems, distributed systems, database systems, and
mobile systems.
CU is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all
applicable federal, state, and local laws governing
nondiscrimination in employment. We are committed to creating a
workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and
dignity, and we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to
apply, including protected veterans and individuals with
disabilities.
Who We Are
The University of Colorado Boulder (CU Boulder) is one of
Colorado’s flagship public institutions and among the most
research-active public universities in the country. The College of
Engineering and Applied Science is the second largest school or
college on the CU Boulder campus and boasts top-tier rankings for
both its graduate and undergraduate engineering programs. Earning
the 11th spot among public graduate programs and 17th nationwide
for undergraduate engineering. Multiple specialty areas are also
ranked within the top 20. Equally importantly, we are committed to
fostering a diverse, inclusive, and academically excellent
community. Our approximately 250 tenure-track, 120
instructional-track, and 30 research-track faculty serve more than
6,000 undergraduate students, 1,300 master’s students, and 850 PhD
students. Our college has three core foci: (i) Research &
Innovation, (ii) Education, and (iii) Inclusion. We believe that
our college’s success requires faculty who actively work to create
an inclusive culture within the college and are committed to the
campus plan of creating and
sustaining supportive campus environments .
To learn more about the College of Engineering and Applied Science
please visit our website .
The Department of Computer Science is one of the largest
departments within the College of Engineering and Applied Science.
The department is home to over 50 tenured and tenure-track faculty
and 20 instructional faculty, and includes about 2000 undergraduate
and 500 graduate students. The Computer Systems Lab consists of
over ten faculty members whose expertise lies in building practical
computer systems. As members of one of the premier research
universities in the country, Computer Science faculty, staff, and
students are engaged in cutting-edge research projects that address
some of the most important challenges facing society today.
The Department's research and education efforts interact broadly
with many interdisciplinary programs and collaborators in Boulder
and the Denver Metropolitan area, including the national labs at
National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration
(NOAA), National Laboratory of the
Rockies (NRL) , and National Center for
Atmospheric Research ( NCAR ) , and CU Boulder research centers
and institutes, including the Center for National Security Initiatives , the
ATLAS Institute , the BioFrontiers Institute , and the Institute for Cognitive Science . More than 20 faculty
members have joint affiliations with one of these labs. The
Department also has a long-standing partnership with National Center for Women and IT and has faculty
active in increasing the broadening of participation in computer
science via their research, teaching, and service. In addition, the
Department has extensive ties with the thriving local tech
community and inhabits a picturesque location in the foothills of
the Rocky Mountains. The Department fosters and supports
entrepreneurial activities – CU Boulder is ranked No.
1 for launching startups based on university discoveries.
Our department is committed to creating a community in which every
individual matters and all can thrive. We embrace inclusive
excellence as a guiding principle, actively fostering a culture of
belonging, equity, and respect. Through intentional practices and
shared responsibility, we celebrate the diversity of our students,
faculty, and staff, and work collaboratively to ensure that all
members of our community have the opportunity to succeed and
contribute fully.
For more about the Department of Computer Science, please visit our
website .
What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be
Successful candidates will be expected to engage in
undergraduate and graduate teaching and mentoring; develop an
externally funded research program in their technical area;
contribute professional leadership and service to their unit, the
college, and their professional community; and cultivate and
contribute to the inclusive excellence of our academic
community.
The typical distribution of work for this role is 40% teaching,
40% scholarly and creative work (research), and 20% leadership and
service.
What You Should Know
The anticipated start date for this position is Fall 2027;
however, a later start date may be negotiated.
The University of Colorado Boulder has implemented a reference check
program with respect to final candidates for tenured faculty
appointments. The reference check program is intended to allow CU
Boulder to collect and review information about a candidate's
conduct at their current and previous institutions, specifically
conduct related to sexual misconduct, harassment, and/or
discrimination, before making hiring decisions. All final
candidates for tenured faculty appointments are required to
complete an Authorization to Release Information.
What We Can Offer
The anticipated academic year salary range for this position at
the Assistant Professor rank is $130,000 - $145,000.
A relocation stipend may be available within CEAS
guidelines.
A recruitment incentive is available within Department
guidelines.
CU offers a competitive 401(a) retirement plan, with employees
contributing 5% of their annual eligible compensation and CU
contributing 10% of their eligible compensation. This plan is
standard for most faculty hires. For more information on CU's
retirement benefits visit our website here .
In addition to a competitive salary, the University of Colorado
Boulder offers a wide variety of other benefits and perks. Links to
some of these are below. To forecast the value of your total
compensation, check out our total compensation
calculator . More information on some of our benefits and perks
is available here: gender-neutral paid
parental leave ; housing down-payment
assistance programs ; dual-career &
relocation resources ; and teaching , research , and
professional
development .
Benefits
At the University of Colorado Boulder , we are
committed to supporting the holistic health and well-being of our
employees. Our comprehensive benefits package includes medical,
dental, and retirement plans; generous paid time off; tuition
assistance for you and your dependents; and an ECO Pass for local
transit. As one of Boulder County’s largest employers, CU Boulder
offers an inspiring academic community and access to world-class
outdoor recreation. In fact, CU Boulder has been named one of
Forbes' America's Best
Large Employers , ranking #4 among large employers in Colorado
and #28 among universities nationwide. Explore additional perks and
programs through the CU Advantage program.
Be Statements
Be engaged. Be pioneering. Be Boulder.
What We Require
Applicants must have earned a research doctorate in Computer
Science or a related discipline, or have their degree conferred
before starting a tenure-track faculty appointment.
What You Will Need
Preferred candidates are those that demonstrate the potential for
excellence in research and teaching through a strong publication
track record and a history of working with undergraduate and
graduate students of varied backgrounds.
Special Instructions
To apply, please submit the following materials as individual PDF
files:

interest in the position and summarizing your personal academic
goals.

experience and plans for research and/or creative work that
contributes to the body of knowledge in your field and provides
broader benefits to education and society (3-4 pages).
A Statement of Teaching Philosophy: A statement of your
experience and plans for teaching and mentoring a diverse student
body (2-3 pages).
Leadership, Service and Community Contributions
Statement: In this statement, describe your leadership and
service experience, and demonstrated ability to contribute to a
supportive campus community. Please provide details on your track
record, calibrated to your career stage, that describe the specific
role you played in these efforts. These could include, but are not
limited to service on committees, outreach activities to broaden
engagement in or with engineering, or serving on advisory boards or
task forces contributing to policies or regulations. In addition,
describe your plans to contribute to our campus plan to Create Supportive
Environments , and the College of Engineering and
Applied Science Strategic Vision (1-2 pages).
Names and contact information for three or more
references: Contact information for at least three references
who may be contacted as the search progresses. Please include
names, job titles, phone numbers, and email addresses. Separately
during the application process, you will be asked to provide the
name and contact information for at least three references to

individuals.

jobs.title: Open Rank Assistant, Associate, Professor: English Education/ Secondary Literacy
jobs.description:
Job Summary
The School of Education invites applications for an open-rank
faculty position in English Education and Secondary Literacy. This
position responds to a critical need in the field as schools
navigate evolving standards, emerging digital literacies, and
persistent disparities in literacy learning and achievement. Hiring
at an open rank will allow the School to recruit either an emerging
or established scholar whose expertise will strengthen our teacher
preparation programs, graduate offerings, and historically strong
Literacy Studies program.
The successful candidate will contribute to scholarship that
advances knowledge of English and literacy toward equitable,
inclusive, and culturally responsive literacy practices. They will
teach undergraduate and graduate courses in English education,
secondary literacy, and related areas of teacher learning and
practice and will play a key role in preparing future educators to
support diverse learners, including multilingual students. This
position will also support continued program growth, partnerships
with schools and communities, and sustainable teaching and
mentoring capacity across undergraduate and graduate
programs.
CU is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all
applicable federal, state, and local laws governing
nondiscrimination in employment. We are committed to creating a
workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and
dignity, and we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to
apply, including protected veterans and individuals with
disabilities.
Who We Are
The University of Colorado Boulder’s School of Education is a
collaborative, research-driven community dedicated to transforming
education through scholarship, innovation, and partnership. We
prepare educators, researchers, and leaders to address complex
challenges in learning and educational systems through rigorous
research, engaged teaching, and meaningful collaboration with
schools, communities, and organizations. Our faculty generate
impactful scholarship that informs practice and policy, and our
work is grounded in a deep commitment to equity, inclusive
excellence, and expanding opportunity for learners across diverse
contexts. We are driven by our shared commitments to diversity,
democracy, equity, and justice, and evidence-based policy and
practice.
For more information about the School of Education, please visit:
https://www.colorado.edu/education/.
What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be
Maintaining an active research agenda and corresponding
publication record that demonstrates a compelling progression of
scholarship.
Engaging in strong teaching and mentoring and contributing to
the School’s teacher education, master’s, and doctoral programs;
advising undergraduate students; mentoring graduate students; and
providing outreach and leadership to schools, districts, campus
partners, professional organizations, and broader communities.
Teaching undergraduate courses in English education and
secondary literacy, as well as undergraduate and graduate courses
in literacy studies, teacher learning and practice, and related
areas of teacher education.
Supporting the development of equitable, inclusive, culturally
responsive, and evidence-based English education and literacy
curricula that prepare educators to support diverse learners.
Building and sustaining meaningful partnerships with local
schools, districts, educators, and communities.
Contributing service to the program, School, university,
profession, and broader community, consistent with expectations for
rank.
What You Should Know
This role is located in Boulder, CO.
The workload for this role is 40% research, scholarly, and
creative work, 40% teaching, advising & mentoring, and 20%
service.
Tenure track faculty are expected to teach four courses per
academic year, and all courses are typically taught in person on
campus.
What We Can Offer
The salary range for this nine-month faculty role is $87,500 -
$97,500 for Assistant Professor, $106,000 - $128,500 for Associate
Professor, $131,500 - $165,000 for Professor, plus an $8,000
relocation allowance as applicable.
Benefits
At the University of Colorado Boulder , we are
committed to supporting the holistic health and well-being of our
employees. Our comprehensive benefits package includes medical,
dental, and retirement plans; generous paid time off; tuition
assistance for you and your dependents; and an ECO Pass for local
transit. As one of Boulder County’s largest employers, CU Boulder
offers an inspiring academic community and access to world-class
outdoor recreation. In fact, CU Boulder has been named one of
Forbes' America's Best
Large Employers , ranking #4 among large employers in Colorado
and #28 among universities nationwide. Explore additional perks and
programs through the CU Advantage program.
Be Statements
Be creative. Be impactful. Be Boulder.
What We Require
Doctorate (Ph.D. or Ed.D.) in English education, literacy
education, curriculum and instruction, teacher education, or a
closely related field by the time of appointment.
A record of scholarly productivity—or demonstrated promise of
such—in English education, secondary literacy, or a closely related
field.
Expertise in one or more areas of secondary literacy or English
Education, for instance: adolescent literacies; digital and
multimodal literacies; English and secondary literacy teacher
learning; classroom literacy teaching and learning; culturally
responsive and sustaining literacy practices; young adult
literature; youth identities and literacies; and/or social and
cultural contexts of literacy education.
PK–12 teaching experience in U.S. schools, preferably in
secondary English language arts or literacy.
Evidence of effective teaching at the university level, at
either the undergraduate or graduate level.
A record of working successfully with people from a wide range
of backgrounds and fostering a strong sense of community and
belonging.
Candidates seeking appointment at the associate or full
professor level must demonstrate a record of teaching, scholarship,
and service appropriate for appointment with tenure at the proposed
rank.
What We Would Like You to Have
A research agenda focused on educational equity, justice, and
access to high-quality literacy learning opportunities.
Three or more years of PK–12 teaching experience in U.S.
schools, preferably at the secondary level.
Experience working with culturally, linguistically,
socioeconomically diverse, and/or LGBTQ+ student populations in
K-12 public schools in the U.S.
Experience advancing inclusive, culturally responsive literacy
practices.
Experience developing partnerships with schools, districts,
educators, or community-based organizations.
Experience supporting teacher licensure programs.
Experience mentoring graduate students as emerging researchers
and teacher educators.
Evidence of, or potential for, contributing to the growth and
intellectual community of a graduate program in Literacy
Studies.
Special Instructions
To apply, please submit the following materials:
A 3-page cover letter addressing how you meet the required and
preferred qualifications with an emphasis on your
scholarly/research agenda
CV
1–2-page teaching statement
Additional materials may be requested of candidates who advance
to the second phase of the search (sample syllabi and letters of
reference)
During the application process you will need to enter contact
information for three references who will be contacted to provide
letters of recommendation as the search progresses.
Review of applications will begin October 19, 2026 (full
consideration will be given to applicants who submit by this
deadline) and will continue until the position is filled.
Note: Application materials will not be accepted via email. For
consideration, please apply through CU Boulder Jobs.
In compliance with the Colorado Job Application Fairness Act, in
any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying
information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school
attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting
or removing this information.

complexity theory, quantum information theory, and quantum error
