jobs.title: Associate and Full Professor
jobs.location: Washington, District of Columbia, United States
jobs.description:
Job Details
Johns Hopkins, founded in 1876, is America's first research
university and home to nine world-class academic divisions working
together as one university.
Salary : $175,000 - $425,000
Johns Hopkins University: School of Government and Policy
Description
Johns Hopkins University’s School of
Government and Policy seeks to recruit multiple tenured faculty
in multiple disciplines and fields of study, including (but not
limited to) political science, law, sociology, history, philosophy,
computer science, and economics.
While searching broadly, we have a particular interest in faculty
conducting research on the following topics of inquiry:
Cities and Communities: State and local policymaking and
implementation. Applications are encouraged from candidates in
civil engineering, economics, history, law, sociology, political
science, public administration, or urban planning, with research
interests including local governance, state capacity, urban
innovation, housing and real estate, public education and school
choice, transportation and land use, or local finance and
budgeting.
Frontier AI: The implications of highly advanced AI for
government and society. Applications are encouraged from candidates
from a wide range of disciplines including computer science,
economics, philosophy, law, political science cognitive science,
and sociology. Research interests might include: AI alignment and
governance; the government, societal, and labor market impacts of
and adaptation to AI; the use of AI to simulate and design policy
interventions; regulatory theory and innovation; institutional
design and innovation; and AI evaluation, auditing and
verification.
Political Philosophy and Theory: Ambitious, foundational,
big-picture political philosophy and/or political theory with
direct relevance to government and policy, advancing the school's
mission of shoring up and renewing the core institutions of liberal
democracy. Applications are encouraged from candidates who are
problem-focused and syncretistic, drawing on different conceptual,
methodological, and empirical approaches and orienting themselves
outward from philosophy/theory toward the world, with particular
interest in candidates whose work intersects with or complements
other parts of the School's research strengths.
Public-Sector Innovation and Management: How governments
and other public-sector organizations function, why they succeed or
fail, and how to change them to more effectively solve public
problems. Applications are encouraged from candidates in the social
sciences, management, history, organizational behavior, psychology,
urban planning, operations research, industrial and systems
engineering, management science, public management, or public
policy. Research interests might include: institutional reform and
organizational change; public innovation and problem solving;
public-sector management, budgeting, procurement, contracting, and
operations; state capacity and bureaucratic performance;
organizational structure, behavior, learning, and culture; the
adoption and management of technology in government, including the
organizational challenges of effective implementation and how
technologies affect public-sector organizations, policy, and
governance.
Regulation, Bureaucracy, and Public Administration: Why
governments so often fail to deliver what policies promise, and
what institutional redesigns would enable them to do so.
Applications are encouraged from candidates in political science,
law, public administration, history, sociology, or other fields
whose work is changing the terms of academic and public debate.
Research interests might include: the politics of civil service and
personnel systems; federalism and the implementation of large
public programs; intergovernmental relations; regulation,
enforcement, and capture; administrative procedure and policy
analysis; or state capacity more broadly.
Across all these searches, we seek candidates who can work and
learn across disciplines and take seriously the need to improve
government effectiveness. We welcome candidates who have worked
within public-sector and policymaking institutions and alongside
government reformers from across the political spectrum. We are
also interested in candidates who wish to investigate the
challenges and opportunities of governing and deploying artificial
intelligence.
About the School of Government and Policy
Anchored at the Hopkins Bloomberg Center in the heart of
Washington, D.C., the School of Government and Policy will be a hub
of discovery, collaboration, and impact. At a time of political,
social, and technological upheaval, this new school will support
and inform scholarly and practical efforts to build a more
effective government and solve complex policy challenges. The
school will scrutinize institutional reforms that have the
potential to improve government operations, examine the potential
for advancing technologies to transform government workforces and
operations, develop novel approaches to multidisciplinary education
and experiential learning, and foster vital dialogue and engagement
across a wide range of worldviews, backgrounds, and
epistemologies.
Similar to JHU’s other academic divisions, the School of Government
and Policy will be grounded in a commitment to both world-class
research and exceptional education. It will prepare the next
generation of policy and public sector leaders to advance
evidence-based solutions to society’s greatest challenges through
innovative approaches that: 1) embed science, data, and technology
in curricula; 2) give students the tools required to think
strategically and creatively about government and policy
innovations; and 3) emphasize the critical need for
cross-functional skills and capabilities at all levels of
government and in bridging public, non-profit, and industry
sectors.
We are building a community of scholars, experts, and leaders from
a wide range of disciplines who embrace intellectual pluralism—with
the intention not merely of representing different perspectives and
ways of understanding, but of putting these differences to good
use. We welcome applications from scholars who challenge
conventional thinking through rigorous inquiry.
Over the course of its founding years, the school will grow to
encompass 35 full-time faculty members with expertise that spans
both theoretical and applied approaches to public policy and
government. During this founding period, additional hires will be
made with other units across the University, yielding an even
larger and more integrated tenured and tenure-track faculty.

record of excellence in teaching, mentoring, and public
engagement.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor
jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Description
The Department of Mathematics at Virginia Tech ( http://www.math.vt.edu/) invites
applications for an Assistant Professor, tenure-track faculty
position in the research area of mathematics education with a start
date of August 10, 2027, at its Blacksburg, VA, campus. The
successful candidate will conduct research in undergraduate
mathematics education, with particular interest in research
specialties that complement and add to the department's existing
research strengths. Possible specialties include but are not
limited to the following: the teaching and learning of
undergraduate mathematics and/or graduate mathematics, the
mathematical preparation of prospective teachers, and the teaching
and learning of applied or computational mathematics.
Job requirements include a Ph.D. in mathematics, mathematics
education, or a closely related field, including the equivalent of
18 semester credit hours of graduate level mathematics, at the time
of appointment; and an active research program in undergraduate
mathematics education. The successful candidate will be expected to
establish and maintain a distinguished research program, including
seeking and securing funding needed to support their research
agenda, and to provide effective instruction and advising to a
diverse population of undergraduate and graduate students.
Successful candidates will be able to teach courses in graduate
mathematics education research and undergraduate mathematics
content or mathematics for prospective teachers. Additional
responsibilities include continuing development of professional
capabilities and scholarly activities, including travel to attend
conferences and meetings, and participation in department, college,
university, and professional service.
This position builds on the Mathematics Department’s existing
strengths and efforts to expand its national prominence in
mathematics education research. The successful candidate will join
a thriving mathematics education research group, housed in the
Mathematics Department, which currently has three tenured faculty,
a postdoc, and several graduate students enrolled in a Mathematics
PhD program with a dissertation and coursework focus in educational
research. Additionally, the mathematics education community at
Virginia Tech includes two tenure-track faculty in the School of
Education with a PhD program in Curriculum and Instruction. The two
groups are highly collaborative, with joint research projects and a
weekly seminar. Additionally, the College of Science has a Center
for Advancing Undergraduate Science Education, which supports
broader DBER efforts beyond mathematics. The successful candidate
will have the opportunity to engage in interdisciplinary research,
curriculum development, or outreach initiatives with other members
of the Virginia Tech faculty.
The Mathematics Department is committed to building a welcoming and
supportive community of mathematical scientists through programs
and activities woven into the department’s research, teaching, and
outreach efforts. This commitment is illustrated by programs such
as the following: Mathematics: Opportunities in Research and
Education; activities organized by the Virginia Tech Chapter of the
Association for Women in Mathematics (winner of the 2021 AWM
Student Chapter Award for Scientific Excellence); and the
Blacksburg Math Circle. Additionally, Virginia Tech is committed to
supporting the success of its faculty members through policies that
include the modification of duties, the extension of tenure clocks,
mentoring, proposal-writing guidance, and dual-career
accommodations, depending on individual circumstances. Interviewed
candidates will meet with a work-life liaison for a confidential
conversation about the details of these policies.
The person appointed will have the following
responsibilities:
- Develop and maintain a distinguished research program in
mathematics education research, including seeking and securing
funding needed to support your research agenda;
- Continually develop their own scholarly activities, professional
capabilities, and service to the profession;
- Provide effective instruction and advising to a diverse
population of undergraduate and graduate students;
- Teach courses in graduate mathematics education research and
undergraduate mathematics content or mathematics for prospective
teachers;
- Participate actively and effectively in department and university
administrative governance; and
- Adhere to the responsibilities of the faculty as described by the
faculty handbook
( https://faculty.vt.edu/faculty-handbook.html ).
Required Qualifications
To receive consideration, applicants must have:
- a Ph.D. in mathematics, mathematics education, or a closely
related field at the time of appointment with the equivalent of 18
semester credits of graduate level mathematics; and
- an active research program in research in undergraduate
mathematics education.
Preferred Qualifications
It is desired that candidates have:
- a comprehensive record of achievement, commensurate with career
stage;
- a research program in mathematics education that compliments and
adds to the department’s existing strengths;
- vision, creativity, and initiative relevant to research and
instruction;
- evidence of viable research funding; and
- demonstrated effectiveness or interest and potential in
undergraduate and graduate teaching and mentoring.
Overtime Status
Exempt: Not eligible for overtime
Appointment Type
Regular
Salary Information
Commensurate with experience
Hours per week
40 hours - exempt position
Review Date
October 23, 2026
Additional Information
An online application is required. Please visit www.jobs.vt.edu , select “,” and
search by posting number 537656. Please include a cover letter, a
CV, a research statement, a teaching statement, an (un)official
transcript documenting the equivalent of 18 semester credits of
graduate level mathematics, and a list of 3 references that will be
contacted for those candidates that are being considered for a
screening interview.
Additional information about position requirements and
responsibilities can be found at the following URLs: http://www.hr.vt.edu or https://www.math.vt.edu . The
faculty handbook ( https://faculty.vt.edu/faculty-handbook.html
) gives a complete description of faculty responsibilities.
Questions about the search may be addressed to:
mathed2026@vt.edu.
Applications received by 11:59 pm EST on October 23, 2026 will
receive full consideration.
The successful candidate will be required to have a criminal
conviction check.
Some travel to meetings and conferences is required.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Description
The Department of Fish and Wildlife Conservation in the College of
Natural Resources and Environment at Virginia Tech invites
applications for a tenure-track Assistant or Associate Professor of
Mammalian Conservation Ecology. We seek a collaborative scholar and
educator whose work advances understanding and conservation of
mammals and strengthens the department’s core missions in
biodiversity conservation and experiential education.
The successful candidate will develop an internationally visible
research program in mammalian conservation ecology. The candidate
should have a strong track record studying the conservation and
ecology of wild mammal populations, with research addressing
contemporary socio-environmental challenges such as climate change,
emerging infectious diseases, invasive species, and habitat loss.
The Department and the University are highly collaborative
environments, creating the opportunity for diverse collaborations
across Virginia Tech and with state and federal natural resource
agencies, conservation organizations, and other partners. The
position is envisioned as approximately 25% teaching, 65% research,
and 10% service.
Teaching and Mentoring Expectations
The department boasts a high-quality teaching environment that
emphasizes modern pedagogical techniques and ample experiential
learning opportunities. Teaching will include a 1:1 teaching
expectation, including FIW 4334 Mammalogy, a high-enrollment,
field-oriented course central to the Wildlife Conservation
curriculum. During the first two years, the faculty member is also
expected to develop or contribute to a graduate course in their
area of expertise and, as the appointment matures, contribute
(e.g., team teach) to general education or other high-demand
undergraduate courses. The faculty member will mentor undergraduate
researchers and M.S. and Ph.D. students and provide field-based,
experiential learning opportunities.
Research, Scholarship, Extension, and Engagement Expectations
The successful candidate will establish a highly productive,
externally funded research program that supports graduate students
and produces high-quality, peer-reviewed scholarship. Expectations
include publishing impactful research in respected peer reviewed
journals. The candidate will be expected to apply for
McIntire-Stennis (USDA NIFA capacity grant) funding in the first
year. The candidate should pursue annual external funding from
appropriate federal and state agencies and foundations, including
opportunities through NSF, U.S. Geological Survey, U.S. Fish and
Wildlife Service, National Park Service, U.S. Forest Service,
Natural Resources Conservation Service, Animal and Plant Health
Inspection Service, Department of Defense, the Virginia Department
of Wildlife Resources as well as state wildlife agencies in
surrounding states or beyond. Externally-funded research should
contribute to science-based wildlife conservation and management
and strengthen interdisciplinary collaborations across the
department and Virginia Tech.
Required Qualifications
-Ph.D. in wildlife science, ecology, biology, zoology, natural
resources, forestry, range management, or a closely related field
by appointment start date.
-Demonstrated expertise in mammalogy and mammalian conservation
ecology.
-Evidence of potential for excellence in university teaching,
field-based instruction, and student mentoring.
-Evidence of strong potential to develop a productive, externally
funded research program and peer-reviewed scholarship.
Preferred Qualifications
-Postdoctoral or comparable professional research experience.
-Experience with modern quantitative, geospatial, field,
laboratory, technological, and/or experimental techniques relevant
to mammalian conservation ecology.
-Demonstrated ability to collaborate with natural resource
agencies, conservation organizations, and/or interdisciplinary
research teams.
-Experience mentoring graduate and undergraduate students.

interest in the position

Names and contact information for three professional
references

jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Description
The Department of Fish and Wildlife Conservation in the College of
Natural Resources and Environment at Virginia Tech invites
applications for a tenure-track Assistant or Associate Professor of
Wildlife Extension. This position will provide statewide leadership
at the intersection of wildlife science, applied research,
extension education, and public engagement. The faculty member will
connect Virginia Tech research with Virginia Cooperative Extension,
wildlife management agencies, landowners, local governments,
agricultural producers, natural resource professionals, and
communities across the Commonwealth.
Priority program areas could include wildlife health and
wildlife-vectored diseases, human-wildlife conflict/coexistence,
deer and bear management, invasive and exotic wildlife, habitat
conservation in rapidly changing landscapes, and public
understanding of wildlife conservation and sustainable use.
Position Expectations
The anticipated allocation is 50% extension, 35% research, 10%
teaching, and 5% service.
The extension program is expected to include an assessment of
stakeholder needs and the development of programming and materials
to address these needs such as, statewide workshops, webinars,
field days, landowner trainings, agent professional development,
publications, decision-support tools, and digital resources, and
ultimately documenting the impact of programming. The faculty
member will work closely with Virginia Cooperative Extension
specialists, Agriculture and Natural Resource agents and partners
such as the Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources, United
States Department of Agriculture (USDA) - Wildlife Services,
Virginia Department of Forestry, non-governmental organizations
(NGOs), and local governments.
The successful candidate will establish a competitive, externally
funded, applied research program that supports graduate students.
The faculty member will submit competitive proposals beginning in
the first year, pursue appropriate capacity and external funds,
develop collaborations across the university, and produce
peer-reviewed publications, extension scholarship, conference
presentations, and impact reports.
The faculty member will teach a 0:1 course load with teaching
focused on FIW 4454 Human-Wildlife Conflicts and Coexistence,
anticipated annually in the spring, and will contribute to graduate
education and mentoring through applied research and extension
scholarship.
Required Qualifications
• Ph.D. in wildlife science, human dimensions of wildlife, natural
resources, ecology, extension education, or a closely related field
by appointment start date.
• Demonstrated expertise relevant to wildlife management,
human-wildlife conflict and coexistence, wildlife health, habitat
management, or human dimensions.
• Evidence of ability to develop and deliver research-based
educational programs for professional and public audiences.
• Evidence of strong potential for externally funded applied
research.
• Demonstrated effectiveness in verbal and written communication,
including a peer-reviewed publication record.
Preferred Qualifications
• Experience working with Cooperative Extension, state or federal
wildlife agencies, landowners, local governments, or stakeholder
organizations.
• Graduate student mentoring experience.
• For appointment at Associate Professor, a record of sustained
scholarly productivity, strong record of external funding, and
extension or engagement leadership commensurate with rank.

Regular

40

10/15/2026

be authorized to work in the United States without the need for

1) Cover letter describing their interest in the position
2) Curriculum vitae
3) A 1-2 page statement describing their extension or professional
program as appropriate to the position

5) A 1-2 page statement describing their teaching and mentoring

together as a programmatic theme
6) Names and contact information for three professional
references

progresses.

Virginia Tech

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor of Environmental Security and Global Change
jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Description
The Department of Geography at Virginia Tech invites applications
for a tenure-track Assistant or Associate Professor with expertise
in environmental security in the context of global climate and
environmental change. We define environmental security broadly to
encompass interactions among environmental processes, human
populations, resources, infrastructure, and societal vulnerability
and resilience. We are particularly interested in candidates who
bridge environmental or climate science with human–environment
perspectives and employ advanced geospatial, computational, or
data-intensive approaches, such as spatial and spatiotemporal
modeling, machine learning and artificial intelligence, sensor or
mobility data, and high-performance computing, as well as
qualitative, participatory, or integrated methods that complement
these approaches. The position is intended to strengthen research
productivity while expanding high-demand undergraduate and graduate
instruction in environmental security, geospatial analysis, and
climate-societal interactions.
Teaching and Mentoring Expectations - The responsibility profile
for the position is envisioned as approximately 40% teaching, 50%
research, and 10% service. An Assistant Professor is expected to
teach a two-course load in year one and a three-course load in
years two through six; an Associate Professor is expected to teach
a three-course load during year one with a longer-term teaching
load informed by research productivity.
Teaching will include a high-enrollment introductory geography,
environmental geography, or climate course, an introductory
geospatial course, and a course focused on environmental security
and/or climate change. The possibility of teaching a specialty
course or graduate seminar around expertise is envisioned, along
with the opportunity to contribute to existing study abroad
courses.
Graduate student mentoring is expected in support of the M.S.
Geography (department) and Ph.D. Geospatial and Environmental
Analysis (college) degree programs.
Research, Scholarship, Extension, and Engagement Expectations - The
successful candidate is expected to establish or continue a
competitive externally funded research program and pursue proposals
annually as principal investigator (PI) or co-PI. Relevant federal
sponsors include NASA, NSF, NOAA, DoD, NGA, and related agencies.
The position offers strong opportunities for collaboration with the
Center for Geospatial Information Technology, the Virginia Tech
National Security Institute, and faculty across the College of
Natural Resources and Environment. Research funding is expected to
support graduate students in the Geography M.S. program and the
Geospatial and Environmental Analysis Ph.D. program. Candidates
should demonstrate capacity to continue or develop a strong
trajectory of external funding, high-quality peer-reviewed
scholarship, and research of national or international
impact.
Required Qualifications
• Ph.D. in geography or a closely related discipline by appointment
start date.
• Research expertise in environmental or climate science with
human-environment perspectives using advanced geospatial,
computational, or data-intensive approaches, such as spatial and
spatiotemporal modeling, machine learning and artificial
intelligence, sensor or mobility data, and high-performance
computing, as well as qualitative, participatory, or integrated
methods that complement these approaches.
• Evidence of excellence or strong potential in university
teaching, including a large introductory course, and graduate
mentoring.
• Evidence of excellence or strong potential for competitive
external funding and high-quality peer-reviewed scholarship.
Preferred Qualifications
• For Associate Professor, a strong record of externally funded
research, graduate student support, and scholarly impact
commensurate with rank.
• Experience leading or contributing to large interdisciplinary
proposals and research teams.
• Expertise that connects environmental security or climate
challenges with advanced geospatial modeling.
• Ability to contribute to high-enrollment undergraduate
instruction and experiential or international education.

Regular

Commensurate with experience.
Hours per week
40

October 15, 2026

mentoring approach; a statement describing research, scholarship,

and names and contact information for three professional
references. Additional materials may be requested as the search
progresses.
This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Applicants must
be authorized to work in the United States without the need for

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor of Distribution Packaging
jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Description
The Department of Sustainable Biomaterials invites applications for
a tenure-track Assistant / Associate Professor (open rank) of
Distribution Packaging. The successful candidate will strengthen a
nationally distinctive program in protective and industrial
packaging and contribute to the long-term growth of the Packaging
Systems and Design (PSD) program. We seek a scholar whose work
advances packaging performance across distribution systems,
including protective packaging, pallets and unit loads, packaging
dynamics, testing, optimization, and resilient supply chains.
Teaching and Mentoring Expectations
The position carries a 50% teaching, 40% research, and 10% service
appointment, with a standard 2:2 teaching load expected by the end
of the second year. Core teaching will include SBIO 4024 Packaging
Design for Global Distribution and SBIO 4224 Industrial Packaging,
with SBIO 5664 Advanced Packaging Dynamics offered on a rotating
basis. The faculty member may also develop a Protective Packaging
for Engineers course serving students beyond the department.
Research and Service Expectations
The successful candidate will build a nationally recognized,
externally funded research program in protective and distribution
packaging. Expectations include submitting external proposals
annually by year two, actively participating in the
McIntire-Stennis program and pursuing other appropriate federal,
industry, and capacity funding, producing high-quality
publications, and contributing research findings to national and
international standards. The faculty member is expected to
collaborate across Virginia Tech, including with Food Science,
engineering programs, the Virginia Tech Transportation Institute,
and the newly established Packaging HUB.
Center for Packaging and Unit Load Design (CPULD) Engagement
The successful candidate will be actively involved in the operation
of the Center for Packaging and Unit Load Design (CPULD), which
provides testing, research, and design services to the packaging
and unit load industries. It also encompasses active engagement in
the Packaging Innovation Hub, an interdisciplinary initiative that
CPULD is leading for promoting collaborative packaging research and
industry partnerships across Virginia Tech, bringing together
faculty, researchers, and external stakeholders to address emerging
challenges in packaging science and engineering. The candidate will
be expected to build and maintain productive relationships with
packaging companies, work directly with Center clients on testing,
design, and applied research projects, and contribute to the
Center's continued growth by developing new industry partnerships
and expanding its portfolio of services. The candidate should
demonstrate the interest and ability to assume, over time, a
leadership role in the Center's operations and strategic
direction.
Service Expectations:
The successful candidate will be expected to collaborate
effectively with colleagues within the department, across Virginia
Tech, and with government agencies, industry partners,
non-governmental organizations (ISO, ISTA, ASTM), and other
academic institutions. The candidate will also contribute to
departmental, college, and university service activities and engage
with external stakeholders on packaging engineering
challenges.
The rank considered for this position will be either assistant
professor or associate professor. Rank is determined based on the
selected candidate’s commensurate experience and impact.
Required Qualifications
• Ph.D. in packaging science/engineering, industrial engineering,
mechanical engineering, wood science, sustainable biomaterials, or
a closely related field by appointment start date.
• Evidence of potential for excellence in university teaching and
graduate student mentoring.
• Evidence of strong potential to establish a competitive
externally funded research program and publish high-quality
scholarship.
Preferred Qualifications
• Expertise in packaging dynamics, distribution packaging,
protective packaging, or pallet and unit-load design.
• Experience with package testing, modeling, optimization,
standards development, or industry-sponsored research.
• Experience working with packaging, pallet, logistics, or
transportation industries.
• Experience building collaborative research across engineering,
food science, transportation, agriculture, or natural
resources.
• Experience with professional standards organizations.
Overtime Status
Exempt: Not eligible for overtime
Appointment Type
Regular
Salary Information
$85-$95,000 for Assistant; $100-$124,000 for Associate
Hours per week
40

October 15, 2026

1. Cover letter describing their interest in the position (up to
one page)
2. Curriculum vitae
3. Names and contact information for three professional
references.
4. Teaching and Mentoring Approach Statement (up to two
pages)
Details to include:
Your approach to effective teaching and mentoring at the
undergraduate and graduate levels.
Courses that you would offer to enhance the Packaging Systems

How your expertise, interests, and goals would contribute to

community.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Description
The Department of Sustainable Biomaterials invites applications for
a tenure-track Assistant or Associate Professor in Sustainable
Systems. We seek a systems-oriented scholar working at the
intersection of industrial ecology, sustainable biomaterials,
energy systems, circular economy, and industrial decarbonization.
Rank will be determined based on the selected candidate’s
commensurate experience and impact.
The successful candidate will strengthen the growing Sustainable
Systems Science major by integrating material and energy flows
across supply chains, infrastructure, manufacturing, packaging, and
bio-based systems. Relevant approaches may include life-cycle
assessment, carbon accounting, sustainability analytics, renewable
and bioenergy systems, and modeling of energy-material
interactions.
Teaching and Mentoring Expectations
The position is a 50% teaching, 40% research, and 10% service, with
a standard 2:2 teaching load expected by the end of the second
year. Core instructional responsibilities include SBIO 2514 Applied
Industrial Ecology, SBIO 3545 Society, Sustainability,
Biomaterials, and Energy, SBIO 4724 Sustainable Systems Science
Capstone, and development of a new SBIO 2XXX Materials-Energy
Systems and Analytics course. During the transition period, the
faculty member may provide temporary coverage for SBIO 4164/5164G
Sustainability Performance and Assessment. The faculty member will
play a central role in the Sustainable Systems Science Bridge
Experience program, supervise capstone and undergraduate research,
and contribute to curriculum development in energy systems,
decarbonization, and sustainability analytics. Study abroad courses
with students are also possible.
Research, Scholarship, Extension, and Engagement
Expectations
The successful candidate will establish a nationally recognized
externally funded research program addressing sustainability and
energy-transition challenges. Expected areas include industrial
ecology, energy-material systems, industrial decarbonization,
circular systems, renewable or bioenergy systems, carbon
accounting, and life-cycle assessment. The candidate is expected to
pursue funding from agencies such as NSF, DOE, EPA, USDA, as well
as industry and foundations, and to support graduate training and
interdisciplinary initiatives; this includes submitted external
proposals annually by year two, and active participation in the
USDA’s McIntire-Stennis program. Research should be integrated with
teaching and experiential learning.
Service Expectations
The successful candidate will be expected to collaborate
effectively with colleagues within the department, across Virginia
Tech, and with government agencies, industry partners,
non-governmental organizations (ISO, ISTA, ASTM), and other
academic institutions. The candidate will also contribute to
departmental, college, and university service activities and engage
with external stakeholders on sustainability-related industrial
systems and energy challenges.
Required Qualifications
Appointment at the rank of Assistant Professor:
• Ph.D. in industrial ecology, sustainability science, energy
systems, environmental engineering/science, sustainable
biomaterials, systems engineering, or a closely related field by
appointment start date.
• Expertise in one or more of the following: life-cycle assessment,
energy-material flow modeling, carbon accounting, industrial
decarbonization, circular economy, renewable/bioenergy systems, or
sustainability analytics.
• Evidence of excellence or strong potential in university teaching
and student mentoring.
• Evidence of strong potential for externally funded research and
high-quality peer-reviewed scholarship.
Appointment at the rank of Associate Professor:
• Evidence of a sustained externally funded research program and
scholarly record commensurate with rank.
• Evidence of an established and productive scholarly research
program with a strong publication record.
• Demonstrated leadership and recognized contributions through
professional service, outreach, engagement, or other academic
service activities.
Preferred Qualifications
• Experience integrating research with capstone, experiential, or
project-based learning.
• Ability to collaborate across natural resources, engineering,
infrastructure, manufacturing, packaging, and industry.
• Experience with LCA software, energy auditing, sustainability
performance analytics, or related computational tools.

jobs.title: Tenure-Track Assistant Professor in Exercise Medicine Research
jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Description
Virginia Tech seeks to recruit an innovative researcher in the area
of exercise medicine with a focus on the impact of
exercise/physical activity on health, including but not limited
exercise immunology related to cancer prevention, cardiometabolic,
skeletomuscular and neurocognitive health for a tenure track
faculty position at the assistant professor level. The successful
candidate should address issues of the health effects of regular
exercise during development in childhood and/or throughout the
adult lifespan with a focus on the cellular, molecular and organ
systems’ effects of exercise. Investigators who focus on
mechanistic understanding of the effects of exercise in human
subjects and/or laboratory animal models with innovative genetic,
biochemical, and/or physiological approaches in addition to strong
computational/data analytic skills are encouraged to apply. The
person hired for this position will join 44 other faculty led teams
at the research institute that currently have an active portfolio
of over $240 million in extramural research and training grants and
contracts and will join the new FBRI Center for Exercise Medicine
Research (CEMR). The position will be located at the FBRI at VTC
(https://research.vtc.vt.edu) on the university’s health sciences
campus in Roanoke, Virginia. In addition to the original 100,000
square foot research institute that opened in 2010, an adjacent
139,000 square foot additional research building
(http://fralinbiomed.info/buildingtour) recently opened in which
the new faculty member will have their research program. The new
CEMR is immediately adjacent to the research laboratories of the
FBRI Center for Vascular and Heart Research, Cancer Research,
Addiction Recovery Research Center, Center for Health Behaviors
Research, Center for Neurobiology Research as well as Center for
Human Neuroscience Research, offering additional opportunities for
collaborations that span metabolism, cardiovascular science, cancer
and neuroscience research. Facilities at the research institute
include multiple research MRIs for human and animal research,
including high field MR guided PET and MR guided focused
ultrasound, multiple cellular/molecular imaging facilities,
including spinning disc confocal microscopy, standard laser
scanning confocal microscopy, scanning block face electron
microscopy, super resolution microscopy, biochemical and molecular
biology cores, including Mass Spec and proteomics as well as
behavioral testing suites for animals and humans, as well as two
human whole room calorimeters, metabolic kitchen and dining areas
for the study of human nutrition and eating behaviors.
Applications will be reviewed continuously until the position is
filled. It is expected that initial interviews will begin in
October 15, 2026. To apply, please submit your application,
including curriculum vitae, detailed statement of research
accomplishments and plans, and teaching/mentoring philosophy at
www.jobs.vt.edu, posting #537596. To complete the application, the
applicant should also have at least three references post their
letters of support when requested.
Inquiries about the position should be directed to the Executive
Director of the Fralin Biomedical Research Institute (FBRI), Dr.
Michael J. Friedlander at friedlan@vtc.vt.edu or to the Director of
the FBRI Center for Exercise Medicine Research, Dr. Zhen Yan at
zhenyan1@vtc.vt.edu
Required Qualifications
Applicants should have an earned doctorate in physiology,
immunology, molecular biology, biochemistry, cell biology exercise
science or a related field, postdoctoral experience and a
demonstrated record of accomplishment of research productivity. The
successful applicant will be expected to establish and maintain a
high-quality, extramurally-funded research program and participate
in research mentoring of undergraduate, graduate, and medical
students with some teaching in graduate programs.

jobs.title: Collegiate Assistant Professor of Forestry
jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Description
The Department of Forest Resources and Environmental Conservation
invites applications for Collegiate Assistant Professor of
Forestry. At Virginia Tech, Collegiate professors are full members
of the faculty whose responsibilities are focused on teaching. The
successful candidate will join Virginia’s only four-year Society of
American Foresters-accredited forestry program and will play a
highly visible, student-facing role in sustaining core forestry
instruction, field-based education, professional preparation, and
workforce connections.
We seek an educator with broad forestry expertise, a strong
background in forest operations, and the ability to connect
classroom and field laboratory instruction with contemporary
forestry practices and employer expectations.
Teaching and Mentoring Expectations
The position is expected to carry approximately a 3:3 teaching
load, with appropriate consideration of the additional time demands
of field laboratory courses. Specific teaching assignments may
include some of the following courses, depending on program needs
and the professional experience and expertise of the successful
candidate:
• FREC 2214 Introduction to Land and Field Measurements
• FREC 3714 Forest Harvesting
• FREC 3724 Forest Boundaries and Roads
• FREC 3734 Forest Fiber Supply
• FREC 4004 Professional Skills in Natural Resources
• FREC 4714 Harvesting Systems Evaluation.
The successful candidate may also contribute to a first-year
experience course, forestry courses for non-majors, a forestry
capstone course, or study-abroad experiences, as appropriate,
within the approximately 3:3 teaching workload expectation.
Research, Scholarship, Extension, and Engagement
Expectations
For a Collegiate faculty appointment, approximately 5–10% of effort
may support pedagogical or disciplinary scholarship and
collaborative research. The successful candidate will be expected
to contribute to curriculum development and revision, student
mentoring, experiential learning, and engagement with forestry
employers and stakeholders. Participation in Forestry Extension
activities is possible but not required.
About the Department of Forest Resources and Environmental
Conservation
The Department of Forest Resources and Environmental Conservation
at Virginia Tech is one of the top forestry, natural resource
management, and conservation programs in the United States. Our
vision, mission, and values statements can be found here: https://frec.vt.edu/vision_mission_values.html.
We are an inclusive and collaborative department that values
knowledge and innovation; ethics and integrity; diversity and
inclusivity; opportunity and affordability; and sustainability. Our
exceptional education, research, and outreach programs are diverse
and approach critical natural resource issues from many
perspectives. The department offers master's and doctoral programs,
as well as five undergraduate majors: environmental conservation
and society, environmental data science, environmental resource
management, forestry, and water resources policy and management.
Faculty research areas of focus include forest biometrics,
modeling, and remote sensing; forest biology, physiology, and
genomics; ecology, silviculture, and wildland fire; hydrology,
soils, and watershed management; forest management, operations, and
business; resource economics and policy; human dimensions of
natural resources and sustainability; environmental education,
interpretation, and communication; and urban forestry. Department
faculty also are engaged with industrial cooperatives, as well as
extension and outreach efforts such as landowner education, SHARP
logger, Master Naturalist, learning networks focused on
environmental education and interpretation, and geospatial
education programs.
Required Qualifications
• Doctorate by time of appointment in forestry, natural resources,
or a closely related field.
• Demonstrated professional or academic expertise sufficient to
teach the above-listed courses, with emphasis on forest operations
courses.
• Demonstrated commitment to deliver high-quality, field-based and
experiential undergraduate education.
• Strong communication, organizational, and interpersonal
skills.

jobs.description:
Department of Radiology UT Health San Antonio
The Department of Radiology in the Joe R and Teresa Lozano long School of Medicine at UT Health San Antonio is seeking a Neuroradiologist for a faculty position at the Assistant Professor rank and will include teaching duties. Our hospitals are regional referral centers for trauma, oncology, surgery, general medicine, and organ transplantation.
Duties include the clinical care of adult patients. Diagnosing and treating conditions of the brain, spine, head, neck, and nervous system using advanced imaging. Interpretation of complex scans, guide treatment choices, and performance of minimally invasive procedures. Read and analyze CT scans, MRIs, X-rays, and angiograms of the central nervous system. Identify strokes, brain and spinal tumors, aneurysms, vascular malformations, trauma, and degenerative brain diseases like Alzheimer's. Teaching and instruction within the clinical setting includes clinical supervision, case-based conferences, and formal lectures, focusing on training medical students, radiology residents, and subspecialty fellows. Provide instruction related to patient diagnosis and using tools like MRI and CT with hands-on instruction. Reviewing brain and spine scans side-by-side with trainees at workstations to teach pattern recognition and diagnostic accuracy. Correcting interpretations of complex neuroimaging modalities like CT, MRI, and angiography as active cases flow through the clinical setting.
Candidates will be providing clinical services at University Health System, UT Health Medical Arts and Research Center, UT Health Hill Country and other affiliated facilities. Candidates must have graduated from an approved medical university and possess a Medical Degree or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO), completed an ACGME accredited radiology residency or an equivalent international program and be fellowship trained in Neuroradiology, be board-certified or board-eligible by the American Board of Radiology and have or be able to obtain a Texas medical license. Candidates who qualify for the ABR Alternate Pathway may be considered based on documented eligibility for departmental sponsorship. Applicants should be competent in all aspects of diagnostic neuroradiology. Academic rank and salary commensurate with qualifications. Hospitals are regional referral centers for trauma, oncology surgery, general medicine, and organ transplantation.
Candidates meeting all requirements may apply at http://uthscsa.edu/hr/employment.asp
UT Health San Antonio is an Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer including protected veterans and persons with disabilities. All faculty appointments are designated as security sensitive positions.

Job Description
The Department of Forest Resources and Environmental Conservation
at Virginia Tech invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant

scientist whose work addresses the human dimensions of
sustainability with an emphasis on natural resource management,
environmental conservation, and/or environmental governance. The

contribute to our department’s ongoing efforts to integrate
rigorous social science into our interdisciplinary curriculum and
research portfolio. The successful candidate must develop a
productive externally funded research program and teach
undergraduate and graduate courses in areas such as leadership for
sustainability and other topics aligned with their expertise.
Individuals must have a PhD in a social science field relevant to
sustainability.
Job responsibilities will include:
Research (50%)
• Develop and maintain a robust, externally funded research program
focused on the human dimensions of sustainability.
• Engage in interdisciplinary collaboration across campus and with
external stakeholders, such as natural resource agencies, NGOs, and
community organizations.
• Advise and mentor graduate students.
Teaching (50%)

Conservation & Society major, with a specific expectation to
teach “FREC 2554 Leadership for Global Sustainability”
• Contribute to curriculum development and departmental
service.

Conservation
The Department of Forest Resources and Environmental Conservation
at Virginia Tech is one of the top forestry, natural resource
management, and conservation programs in the United States. Our
vision, mission, and values statements can be found here: https://frec.vt.edu/vision_mission_values.html.

knowledge and innovation; ethics and integrity; diversity and
inclusivity; opportunity and affordability; and sustainability. Our

perspectives. The department offers master's and doctoral programs,

and society, environmental data science, environmental resource

environmental education and interpretation, and geospatial
education programs.

We seek an outstanding scholar with a strong commitment to excellent undergraduate teaching and mentorship in a liberal arts environment.
The position carries a standard five-course annual teaching load, and entails teaching introductory and intermediate-level courses in early modern literature, including Shakespeare and non-dramatic poetry and prose, as well as upper division courses in the areas of the candidate’s field(s) of specialization, advising students, mentoring senior theses, and contributing to the general education curriculum. Faculty responsibilities additionally include professional achievement and governance and engagement, as described in Article II of the Bates College Faculty Handbook. Successful candidates will contribute to inclusive and evidence-based teaching, maintain an active program of scholarship, and participate in the life and governance of the College. A Ph.D. is required by the start of the contract.
The anticipated salary range for this position is $87,000–$91,000, commensurate with experience and qualifications. This position begins July 2027.
Required application materials include:
Cover letter Curriculum vitae Statement of teaching philosophy A list of three recommenders Review of applications will begin on October 20, 2026, and continue until the position is filled.
We seek candidates who are committed to supporting the success of all students. Applicants are encouraged to describe relevant preparation, experience, or plans for creating an inclusive learning environment. Letters of recommendation and writing samples will be requested only for candidates selected to move forward after the initial review. Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check and verification of degree.
Bates College is a residential liberal arts college located in Lewiston, Maine.Faculty scholarship and creative work at Bates are robustly supported by start-up packages, a paid pre-tenure leave, support for post-tenure sabbaticals, internal grants, professional travel funding, and a well-staffed external grants office. Community-engaged learning—with community partnerships facilitated by the Harward Center for Community Partnerships—and study abroad are both broadly encouraged and institutionally supported. Pedagogical development and innovation is further buttressed by our Center for Inclusive Teaching and Learning. Educational access and racial justice are central to Bates’ history and mission and our faculty-led initiatives reflect this commitment.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor, Dairy Foods Microbiology
jobs.institution: Cornell University Department of Food Science
jobs.description:
The Department of Food Science in the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences (CALS) at Cornell University invites candidates for a full-time, tenure-track assistant professor position to develop a research and extension program related to Dairy Foods Microbiology.
The successful candidate will establish an innovative, nationally and internationally recognized program addressing microbiological challenges and opportunities across the dairy foods system. Research may take a farm-to-table systems approach and advance the safety, microbial quality, functionality, and sustainability of dairy foods. Research addressing farm-level practices that influence the microbiological quality, safety, or suitability of milk for processing is within scope; however, research focused primarily on farm-level microbiology without a clear connection to milk or dairy product outcomes is not a primary focus of this position.
Appropriate research areas may include, but are not limited to: physiology, genetics, and ecology of microorganisms important to dairy food safety and quality; microbial interactions and their effects on the quality, flavor, and shelf-life of dairy products; methods to improve the safety and quality of milk and dairy products; development of dairy foods with probiotic, fermented, or other health-promoting properties; application of emerging technologies to understand and control microorganisms in dairy systems; and development of predictive, computational, or data-driven tools for dairy quality and safety assurance. The successful candidate is expected to develop collaborative research relationships with colleagues in Food Science and across Cornell in areas such as microbiology, molecular biology and genetics, veterinary medicine, animal science, engineering, and related disciplines.
Responsibilities This position has effort in research (50%) and extension (50%). A strong record or demonstrated potential for outstanding peer-reviewed scholarship, external funding, translation of knowledge, and engagement with stakeholders is expected. The successful candidate will advise and mentor graduate and undergraduate students and contribute to a vibrant culture of collaboration and inclusive excellence within the Department of Food Science and across Cornell.
Research (50%): The successful candidate will be expected to develop an internationally recognized and externally funded research program in dairy foods microbiology. The program should address fundamental and applied questions relevant to the microbiological safety, quality, and functionality of dairy foods and generate knowledge and tools that can be translated into practice across the dairy industry. The candidate is expected to mentor graduate students and other research personnel and to collaborate broadly with faculty, industry, government, and other stakeholders.
Extension (50%): The successful candidate will develop and deliver a nationally recognized extension program responsive to current and emerging needs of the dairy processing industry. Programming may include hands-on short courses and workshops for dairy industry professionals; workforce-development programs; online courses, certificates, and other digital educational resources; and technical assistance addressing microbiological issues associated with raw milk quality, dairy processing, product safety, spoilage, shelf-life, and microbial control. The incumbent will work closely with dairy processors and other stakeholders to identify emerging needs, translate research findings into practical guidance, and support implementation of science-based practices. The successful candidate will be expected to develop sustainable support for extension programming through participant fees, grants, industry partnerships, and other appropriate sources.
Service to the Department and University: The candidate will be expected to participate in faculty meetings, departmental and university committees, and professional and public service activities appropriate for a faculty member. The incumbent will also contribute to the broader dairy foods and food safety communities through professional leadership, stakeholder engagement, and collaborative activities.
Qualifications A Ph.D. in Food Science, Microbiology, Dairy Science, or a closely related field is required. The ideal candidate will demonstrate the potential to develop a nationally and internationally recognized program of innovative scholarship and extension in dairy foods microbiology. Candidates should demonstrate strong potential for interdisciplinary collaboration, external funding, graduate student mentorship, and effective engagement with dairy industry stakeholders.
Applications and Starting Date: The anticipated starting date is July 2027 or as negotiated. Qualified applicants should submit 1) a cover letter briefly summarizing background, qualifications, and interest in the position; 2) a curriculum vitae; 3) a research statement outlining experience, interests, and goals, 4) a teaching statement outlining experience, interests, and goals, 5) copies of four relevant publications; and 6) names and contact information for four references.
Materials should be submitted online to: https://academicjobsonline.org/ajo/jobs/32676 Applications received by November 15th, 2026, will be given full consideration. Applications will be accepted until the position is filled.
This is an in-person position. The successful candidate will be expected to live within commuting distance of Ithaca, NY. Relocation assistance may be provided.
Consistent with Cornell’s practice, appointment to academic positions requires candidates to disclose relevant information about their prior employment including whether they have been found to have violated institutional or employer policies related to or governing unlawful discrimination and harassment, academic and research misconduct, or financial misconduct.
We seek a colleague with an outstanding record demonstrating success and promise across all these areas, and who will be supported by and contribute to a vibrant culture of inclusive excellence at Cornell. Learn how CALS fosters an environment where faculty are supported, valued, and empowered to make meaningful contributions throughout their careers.
Inquiries may be directed to:
Search Chair: Abigail Snyder
Dept of Food Science
Cornell University, Ithaca, NY 14853
Email: abs276@cornell.edu
In compliance with New York's Pay Transparency Law, the annual base salary range for this assistant professor position is $90,000 - $135,000. This pay range represents base pay (for 9 months). Cornell University considers factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate’s work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, as well as market and organizational considerations when extending an offer.
Cornell University seeks to meet the needs of dual career couples, has a Dual Career program, and is a member of the Upstate New York Higher Education Recruitment Consortium to assist with dual career searches including positions available in higher education in the upstate New York area.
The new faculty member will join a collaborative, interdisciplinary community on the main campus in Ithaca, New York. Cornell University is an innovative Ivy League and Land-grant university and a great place to work. Our inclusive community of scholars, students, and staff impart an uncommon sense of larger purpose and contribute creative ideas to further the university's mission of teaching, discovery, and engagement.
Cornell’s regional and global presence includes state-wide Cornell Cooperative Extension programs and offices in all counties and boroughs, global partnerships with institutions and communities engaged in life-changing research and education, the medical college’s campuses on the Upper East Side of Manhattan and Doha, Qatar, and the Cornell Tech campus on Roosevelt Island in the heart of New York City.

jobs.description:
POSITION SPECIFICS
The Department of Sociology and Criminology at The Pennsylvania State University, in University Park, PA, USA, invites applications for a full-time tenure-track position, at the rank of Assistant Professor, to start in Fall 2027, with flexibility.
A Ph.D. in Sociology, or related field, is required by the appointment date.
Candidates for Assistant Professor must have demonstrated ability as a researcher, scholar, and teacher and have evidence of growth in scholarly achievement. Duties and responsibilities for assistant professor candidates include a combination of research, service, and teaching. Onsite teaching is an essential function of the job.
The successful candidate will have expertise in population-based approaches to aging, broadly defined. Their academic portfolio will also fit with the mission of the aging initiative being supported by the College of Liberal Arts and other units on campus, including the Social Science Research Institute (SSRI). The initiative includes a focus on federally funded aging research. Thus, candidates should be grant-active or show strong evidence of external funding potential.
Successful candidates will also strengthen the Department and College, and contribute to SSRI's mission, which is to foster novel, interdisciplinary collaborative research that addresses critical human and social problems.
Interested candidates must submit an online application at Penn State's Job Posting Board, and should upload the following application materials electronically: a letter of interest, CV or resume, and a list of three references with contact information. Inquiries may be directed to sociology@psu.edu. Review of applications will begin on October 15 and continue until the position is filled.
Visit our website at sociology.la.psu.edu for more information about the department. Visit the SSRI website for more information about the Institute.
BACKGROUND CHECKS/CLEARANCES
Employment with the University will require successful completion of background check(s) in accordance with University policies.
BENEFITS
Penn State provides a competitive benefits package for full-time employees designed to support both personal and professional wellbeing. In addition to comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, employees enjoy robust retirement plans. One of the standout benefits is the generous 75% tuition discount, available to employees as well as eligible spouses and children.
For more detailed information, please visit our < ahref="https://hr.psu.edu/current-employee/benefits">Benefits Page. (Note: For Postdoctoral benefits, please see our Postdoctoral Benefits page.)
CAMPUS SECURITY CRIME STATISTICS
Pursuant to the Jeanne Clery Disclosure of Campus Security Policy and Campus Crime Statistics Act and the Pennsylvania Act of 1988, Penn State publishes a combined Annual Security and Annual Fire Safety Report (ASR). The ASR includes crime statistics and institutional policies concerning campus security, such as those concerning alcohol and drug use, crime prevention, the reporting of crimes, sexual assault, and other matters. The ASR is available for review here.

Job Details

Holmes Hall
Position Title:
Open Rank, Professional Track Faculty, Finance
Position Type:
Full time
Location:
Holmes Hall

Faculty Exempt
Job Summary:
Job Duties:
The Freeman College of Management at Bucknell University invites
applicants for a Professional Track faculty position in finance,
with qualifications to teach undergraduate finance courses
beginning in Fall 2027. The successful candidate is expected to
successfully deliver a range of courses in finance as well as
having the opportunity to develop and offer new courses of interest
supporting the instructional needs in our major. The initial
appointment is for three years, with the possibility of
reappointment in subsequent years, contingent upon satisfactory
performance. The starting rank will be commensurate with
qualifications and experience.
Professional Track faculty members have a teaching load of six
courses per year with typical class sizes of around 25 students.
Additionally, candidates will be expected to advise students and
maintain faculty qualifications consistent with the AACSB
accreditation standards.
Although this position will not be eligible for tenure, Bucknell
values professional track colleagues as full members of the faculty
and provides extensive resources to support their growth. This
includes access to a robust Teaching & Learning Center and
funding for professional development and scholarly engagement.
Professional track faculty members are eligible to vote in
University and College faculty meetings and serve on faculty
committees.
Professional Track faculty members are reviewed every three years,
with the initial review occurring prior to the third year of the
appointment. Excellent teaching is the primary criterion for
renewal and promotion. This track includes three successive ranks.
Faculty members become eligible for promotion to the next rank
after six years of service at their current rank. Prior equivalent
service may be applied toward promotion.
The Freeman College, an AACSB-accredited unit, offers innovative
professional education within one of the nation's foremost liberal
arts universities. We believe that an education that combines
technical skills and deep intellectual exploration is the best
preparation for thoughtful and capable leaders who will have
significant impact on their profession, their community and
society. We seek faculty members capable of contributing to this
mission. The approximately 1000 students in the Freeman College of
Management may choose among five majors offered by highly
interdisciplinary departments that combine courses in the various
disciplines of management with offerings in the arts, humanities,
natural and social sciences, and engineering. For additional
information pertaining to our curriculum, go to https://www.bucknell.edu/management.
QUALIFICATIONS
Candidates must possess a graduate degree (or commensurate
professional experience) in a field appropriate for teaching
undergraduate finance courses.
Candidates must have either compiled a record of teaching
excellence or demonstrate potential for teaching excellence.
APPLICATION
Review of applications will begin no later than October 1, 2026,
and will continue until the position is filled. For additional
information, and to apply, please visit Bucknell's career site
(careers.bucknell.edu).
Applications will only be accepted online. We intend to conduct the
first round of interviews remotely. Complete files must
include:
A cover letter,
A current curriculum vitae,
A statement of teaching and advising philosophy,
Evidence of exceptional teaching or promise of excellence in
teaching.
*Please combine all items into a single pdf file before
submitting.
Candidates that progress through the interview process will be
asked to provide names and contact information for three
professional references, so that confidential letters of reference
may be obtained.
Please address any questions about the search to Prof. Karen
McGrath, Chair of the Search Committee, at
kms016@bucknell.edu.
ABOUT BUCKNELL
Bucknell University is a private, highly ranked, primarily
undergraduate, national liberal arts institution that also offers
strong professional programs in engineering, management, education,
and music. Bucknell University is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
Bucknell is committed to supporting the teacher-scholar model of
faculty development. The University sponsors a range of activities
to support the thriving of its faculty, including generous research
support and leave policies.
Bucknell is located in Lewisburg, Pennsylvania, on the banks of the
Susquehanna River. The Lewisburg area offers a combination of
outdoor recreation opportunities and small-town amenities. In
addition to the cultural and athletic events offered at the
University and in town, the region offers strong schools and
medical facilities, and an affordable cost of living. Bucknell is
about three hours from Philadelphia, New York, Baltimore, and
Washington, D.C.
This role is eligible for visa sponsorship in accordance with
University policy. At this time, the University is only able to
provide H-1B visa sponsorship for candidates currently residing in
the U.S. with a valid, transferable visa status (e.g. H-1B, F-1,
J-1). Bucknell is not currently in a position to initiate new H-1B
petitions for candidates residing abroad.
Benefits:
Eligible full- and part-time employees are compensated beyond base
salary through our total rewards package that includes (but is not
limited to):
Flexible scheduling options determined by role;
Medical, prescription drug, vision, dental, life, and long-term
disability insurance options
An outstanding 10% employer contribution to your retirement
plan (no contribution requirement for non-exempt positions)
Full-time and part-time members of the faculty and staff are
eligible for tuition remission for themselves. Additionally,
full-time members of the faculty and staff are eligible for tuition
remission for their spouse/spousal equivalent and are eligible for
various tuition programs for their children. Credit for full-time
benefits eligible employment at other institutions of higher
education will be applied to waiting periods.
A comprehensive employee wellness program including program
incentives
A myriad of other benefits, including parental leave, an
employee assistance program, fitness center membership, and the
power of your Bucknell ID card
To learn more about Bucknell's benefits, click here! (*Eligibility
criteria and waiting periods may apply.)
Inclusive Excellence:
Bucknell is committed to fostering an environment that embraces
diversity, equity and inclusion, and seeks candidates who will
contribute to a climate that supports the growth and development of
a diverse campus community. We endeavor to enhance our capacity to
value and capitalize on the cultural richness that diversity
brings. We encourage all individuals to apply and do not
discriminate in admissions, employment, educational programs and/or
activities on the basis of race, color, national or ethnic origin,
age, religion, disability, pregnancy, sex/gender, gender identity
and/or expression, sexual orientation, marital or family status,

E-Verify
Bucknell University participates with the United States Customs and

For additional information regarding Bucknell's E-Verify

Position Description
The Department of
Counseling, Leadership, Adult Education, and School Psychology
(CLAS) in the College of Education at Texas State
University, a Hispanic-Serving Institution (HSI) located in San
Marcos, Texas, invites applications for an Assistant
Professor of Educational and Community Leadership
beginning August 2027. This position involves teaching, research,
service, and leadership in our vibrant master's and doctoral
programs in Central Texas.
Position: This position involves teaching,
research, and service. Specific responsibilities include:
Teaching graduate courses in the Ph.D. and the master's degree
programs in Educational and Community Leadership, and the Principal
and Superintendent Certification Programs. Teaching and service
will be required across these programs in multiple locations,
including on the main campus in San Marcos, supporting the growing
expansion of our programs on the Round Rock Campus, and in
partnership cohort programs in surrounding school districts.
Developing and maintaining an active and productive research
agenda that results in peer-reviewed publications and national and
international visibility; commensurate with the university and
department expectations for tenure and/or promotion.
Seeking or having the potential to seek external funding to
support research and student development.
Contributing to service activities at the program, department,
college, and university level, and the broader educational
leadership profession.
Mentoring master's and doctoral students; the latter through
the dissertation process to timely degree completion.
For additional information about the Department of Counseling,
Leadership, Adult Education, and School Psychology please visit:
https://www.txst.edu/clas.html
Program: The Educational and Community Leadership
(EDCL) program prepares leaders in K–12 and community-based
contexts. The program emphasizes leadership, research-informed
practice, and quality educational experience.
Department: The CLAS Department serves
approximately 975 students seeking undergraduate, master's, and
doctoral degrees in Professional Counseling (COUN), Educational and
Community Leadership (EDCL), Adult, Professional, and Community
Education (APCE), School Psychology (SPSY), Student Affairs in
Higher Education (SAHE), and Integrated Studies (INTS). The CLAS
Department provides high quality undergraduate and graduate
education to promote significant transformational changes in
communities, schools, organizations, and institutions locally and
globally. Guided by expert faculty who are deeply engaged in
innovative research and dedicated to student success, CLAS students
grow into leaders and changemakers in schools, communities, and
organizations across Texas and beyond. The CLAS Department is proud
to be part of a public, Hispanic-Serving Institution that values
discovery and impact through research, teaching, and service.
University: Founded in 1899 as a small teaching
college, Texas State University is now home to over 40,000
students. The university holds a Carnegie classification of
Doctoral University-High Research Activity (R2) and is engaged in a
strategic plan to attain Doctoral University-Very High Research
Activity (R1) by 2027. Texas State University is located along the
beautiful San Marcos River. San Marcos is in the center of the
innovation corridor, 40 minutes south of downtown Austin and 60
minutes north of San Antonio and is rich in vibrant and eclectic
communities.

rank:
An earned doctorate in Educational Leadership, Educational
Administration, or closely related field.
Experience in educational leadership preparation and/or prior
leadership roles in K–12 settings (e.g., assistant principal,
principal, district administrator).
Record of, or demonstration of the potential for, sustained
research and publication in peer-reviewed journals and at the
national and/or international levels.
Record of, or demonstration of the potential for, securing
external funding for research.
Record of, or demonstration of the potential for, excellence in
graduate-level teaching, including experience teaching
doctoral-level courses.
Record of, or demonstration of the potential for, mentoring and
supervising doctoral students through to completion of their
dissertation and degree.
Record of, or demonstration of the potential for, service and
academic leadership at the program, department, college, and
professional levels.

rank:
Experience as a K–12 school or district leader at the level of
principal or higher.
Experience teaching courses in an Educational Leadership or
Educational Administration program.
Experience supervising and mentoring doctoral students through
dissertation completion.
Demonstrated success in building and sustaining district and

Job Title
Clinical Assistant Professor of Nursing-Hybrid position

Job Description
Texas A&M International University (TAMIU), a member of the
Texas A&M University System, welcomes applicants for a
Clinical Assistant Professor of Nursing-Hybrid position to
begin Fall 2026.
TAMIU is a Hispanic Serving Institution with over 8,000 students
located in Laredo, Texas, a vibrant and bicultural city with a
population of about 250,000. The university advances knowledge
through research and discovery, teaching and learning, community
engagement and public service, and with an intentional focus on
student success and research excellence. For more information,
please visit https://www.tamiu.edu/.
This is a non-tenure track, 12-month faculty appointment that
supports an online Master's of Science in Nursing program. Primary
duties will include teaching assigned didactic and/or immersive
nursing courses in the graduate and/or undergraduate programs (up
to 15 semester credit hours per semester); supervising and
evaluating students' progress in course work and clinical
experiences; implementing and evaluating courses as needed; serving
on and participating in college and university committees; advising
students throughout their program of studies, as appropriate; and
completing other duties as assigned by the program director or
department chair. Duties also include developing and evaluating
curriculum; developing and maintaining partnerships in and around
the community; engaging in other activities to serve the school and
the profession. Regular attendance on-campus is not required. The
curriculum combines online instruction with on-campus learning
activities, allowing faculty to live remotely from the Texas
A&M International University campus in Laredo, TX. However,
faculty in the program are required to travel to Laredo and be on
campus for designated periods each semester for immersive labs.
On-campus commitments typically range from five to six visits per
academic year, with the duration of each stay determined by program
needs. The candidate is expected to attend the Fall Faculty and
Administrative Staff Assembly and one commencement ceremony per
academic year. This position requires face-to-face interactions
through a regular schedule of attendance on campus and in the
workplace.
The Dr. F.M. Canseco School of Nursing is an accredited program by
the Accreditation Commission for Nursing Education (ACEN) and
approved by the Texas Board of Nursing (TBON). This non-tenure
track faculty position supports a hybrid Master's of Science in
Nursing program.
Required Qualifications
The successful candidate must hold a an earned doctorate in nursing
from an accredited university. ABDs will be considered but must
have earned a doctorate before appointment; must hold a master's
degree in nursing; a minimum of 5-years of clinical practice
experience as a registered nurse/ APRN; a minimum of 5-years
teaching experience in nursing education; a current unencumbered RN
license to practice nursing in the State of Texas; and must meet
and have all certification requirements for APRN for their
specialty. We strongly encourage candidates with experience in
collaborating with the community and healthcare partners, as well
as, experience and knowledge of online/distance/hybrid delivery
methods in higher education.
We offer competitive salaries and a benefits package including
health insurance, retirement benefits, and life insurance.
Additional pay is available for summer teaching. Financial support
for professional development opportunities, such as attending
academic conferences, is also provided. Moving expenses are covered
in whole or in part by the university.
Application Process
The completed employment application must include:
Letter of interest or cover letter that addresses
qualifications
Current curriculum vitae
Unofficial transcripts specifying conferred/ABD degree
Names and contact information of three current professional
references
Applications must be submitted online at https://www.tamiu.edu/admins/ohr/employment/.

process, you have only one opportunity to enter the requested
information, upload documents, and submit the application. You will
not be able to make changes or add additional documents once you
"Submit" the application materials. The software does not allow you
