jobs.description:
Job Details
Position Overview
This position is a full-time, academic-year, non-tenure-track
Assistant Teaching Professor position in the School of Business at
the University of Kansas. The position's primary responsibility is
teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in Finance and
Economics, with a particular emphasis on courses supporting the
Bicknell Certificate in Personal Finance, KU's CFP program within
the School of Business:
https://business.ku.edu/undergraduate-programs/degree-programs/bicknell-certificate-personal-finance
).
KU’s excellence is a result of the rich tapestry of experiences,
perspectives, and backgrounds of our faculty, staff, students, and
colleagues from across our nation and the globe. At KU, we invest
in continuous learning and growth by creating a climate where
people engage in respectful dialogue and debate and support each
other’s success. We foster a culture of care where each person is
seen, heard and valued. When people feel a true sense of belonging,
we believe they are better able to reach their full potential and
achieve remarkable things.
This position is subject to a
collective bargaining agreement between The University of
Kansas and United Academics. UAKU is the exclusive representative

The successful candidate must be eligible to work in the U.S. by
the effective date of the appointment. Any employment with the
University of Kansas is contingent upon satisfactory completion of

Job Description
80% Teaching
Teach undergraduate or graduate level courses on various topics in
personal and household finance, personal financial planning,
insurance, economics, finance and/or foundations of business.
Potential course assignments for this position include FIN 330
Introduction to Financial Planning and Retirement and FIN 430
Financial Planning Capstone within the Bicknell Certificate in
Personal Finance, although other course assignments are expected as
the program expands. Duties include, but are not limited to,
instruction in the area of finance, course preparation,
consultatio n, and assignment of course grades. Courses may be
taught in online or on-campus formats, including at the Lawrence
and/or Leavenworth campuses. The typical course load for this
appointment is eight courses per academic year. Course load and
teaching assignments will be determined by the F inance Area
Director to best meet the needs of the School of Business. All
faculty members are expected to abide by area, school, and
university policies and procedures.

Engage in service both within and outside the school and
university, including professional and scholarly engagement
activities that support instruction and student development.
Participate as an active member of the area and engage in
instruction-related activities beyond direct instruction. All
faculty members are expected to fulfill their share of service
duties needed to facilitate the efficient operation of the school.
May perform additional position-related activities as assigned by
the Dean or Area Director.
Required Qualifications
Possess a PhD in Finance or closely related discipline, OR an
MBA or other professional degree in a closely related discipline
plus a demonstrated record of scholarship and achievement, by the
start of the appointment.
Documented ability or high potential to successfully teach
across student populations, as demonstrated by prior experience in
teaching, training, leadership, or other relevant experience.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor - Aerospace Engineering
jobs.description:
Job Details
Position Overview
The Department of Aerospace Engineering at the University of
Kansas is seeking outstanding individuals for two full-time
tenure-track faculty positions at the rank of Assistant
Professor. Aerospace Engineering at the University of Kansas
has embraced a growth model which began with the undergraduate
program and is now focusing on research, discovery, and the
graduate program. Applications are welcome in any area of
collaboration with existing faculty, including but not limited to
AI/ML in aerospace applications, unmanned aircraft, advanced air
mobility systems, aerospace autonomy, flight test, remote sensing,
emerging aerospace propulsion, VLEO/reentry applications, and space
systems engineering. Current faculty are integrally engaged in
a broad array of transportation-related research, as well as
research supporting earth, energy, and the environment through
environmental remote sensing in the Center for Remote Sensing and
Integrated Systems (CReSIS). The Department of Aerospace
Engineering currently has 12 tenured/tenure-track faculty and three
instructional faculty, with programs leading to bachelor's,
master’s, and doctoral degrees. The Aerospace Engineering faculty
are currently engaged in numerous externally funded research
programs, with support from Federal (NASA, NSF, ONR, AFRL, ARL,
FAA), Industry (Lockheed, GE, Microsoft Research), and other
sources. The department encourages interdisciplinary research, and
the new hires are encouraged to collaborate with faculty in
Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical, Chemical, and Petroleum
Engineering, as well as other disciplines to advance research and
education, and create an impactful and sustained externally funded
research program.
The Assistant Professor position is subject to a
collective bargaining agreement between The University of
Kansas and United Academics. UAKU is the exclusive representative
for the bargaining unit, and it is the candidate’s right to be a
member or not be a member of a union without fear of personal or
professional repercussions.
Applications are sought from candidates with earned doctorates in
Aerospace Engineering or a closely related field in Engineering by
the time of appointment. Candidates should demonstrate a sustained
commitment to excellence in undergraduate and graduate teaching,
scholarly research, local and international service, and
departmental and student mentoring. The successful candidate must
be eligible to work in the U.S. by the effective date of
appointment. The successful candidate will be results-oriented,
have a record of superior scholarship demonstrated by: 1) a
promising vision for and experience in developing and maintaining
externally funded research, and 2) ability to teach high-quality
courses at both the undergraduate and graduate levels and mentor
and graduate M.S. and Ph.D. students. The department values impact
and engagement in pedagogy, in the curriculum, in outreach to
students, and in research.
The University of Kansas School of Engineering has embarked on a
strategic plan that leads to significant expansion while taking
explicit care to maintain and improve the high-quality student
programs for which the university is known. This is a multi-faceted
approach that drives growth in facilities, faculty, leadership,
research, and, most importantly, students, as it helps industry
partners find the new talent, designs, and techniques they need to
fuel economic growth and business success. Special consideration
will be given to applicants committed to excellence, who can
contribute to the University's innovative, collaborative, and
multidisciplinary initiatives to educate leaders, build healthy and
vibrant communities, and make discoveries that will change the
world.
Job Description
The University of Kansas is the state's flagship university, an R-1
institution and one of just 66 invited members of the prestigious
Association of American Universities (AAU). Our university
consistently earns high rankings for academics and recognition as a
premier research university (engaging in $275 million of externally
funded research annually). KU has 65 ranked graduate programs and
is ranked 24th in best value among public institutions in 2022. The
University values global engagement with more than 150 programs of
international study and cooperative research and offers more than
130 study abroad programs. Student enrollment for the
Lawrence-Edwards was 23,958 representing all 50 states and 112
countries.
KU is committed to upholding our core institutional values of
integrity; commitment to excellence and academic freedom;
disciplined inquiry in the search of knowledge; multicultural and
intellectual diversity; respect for the dignity and rights of the
individual; and inclusion, transparency, freedom of expression, and
communication ( https://provost.ku.edu/about
).
KU's excellence is a result of the rich tapestry of experiences,
perspectives, and backgrounds of our faculty, staff, students, and
colleagues from across our nation and the globe. At KU, we invest
in continuous learning and growth by creating a climate where
people engage in respectful dialogue and support each other's
success. We foster a culture of care where each person is seen,
heard and valued. When people feel a true sense of belonging, we
believe they are better able to reach their full potential and
achieve remarkable things.
Job Description
40% Teaching
Develop curriculum and teach undergraduate and graduate courses,
in-person and virtually in Aerospace Engineering and associated
disciplines. Participate in undergraduate and graduate student
academic advising. Mentor graduate students in research and serve
as the major advisor and chair of master’s and doctoral level
thesis committees.
40% Research/Scholarship
Develop and direct a sustainable research program that includes
directing students, establishing a strong externally funded
research program, and disseminating findings through peer-reviewed
manuscripts and/or issued patents. Collaborate with internal and
external research constituents.
20% Service
Participate in University, School, Departmental, and professional
service activities, including department and school service
committees, technical committees, industry boards, or other
programs related to the field. Foster a positive relationship with
industry and the community. Perform other duties as assigned by the
Department Chair.
Required Qualifications
Earned doctorate in Aerospace Engineering, or a closely related
field in Engineering, by the start date of appointment.
Demonstrated (or high potential for) teaching excellence in a
university setting including the ability to develop and teach
online courses.
Demonstrated (or high potential for) record of scholarship as
evidenced by publications, awards, presentations, books, and/or
patents.
Demonstrated (or high potential for) ability to develop an
externally funded research program, as evidenced by the record of
accomplishments and a well-defined and promising vision for
externally funded research.
This position requires a formal degree in the cited discipline
area(s) to ensure that candidates have the foundational knowledge
and skill set required to perform the duties of the position. The
level of degree is based on accreditation requirements,
institutional standards of academic and professional excellence,
alignment with peer institution benchmarks, and contributes to the
credibility and effectiveness of the role within the university
community.
Contact Information to Applicants
Emily Arnold (earnold@ku.edu) and Richard Hale (rhale@ku.edu)
Additional Candidate Instruction
Evaluation of required qualifications will be made through (a) your
letter of application describing your work and educational
experiences, including your commitment to cultivating a sense of
belonging for all students, staff and faculty in your work or
learning environments; (b) record of accomplishments and
productivity in research and teaching as addressed in the c.v.,
including research publications and conference presentations; c) a
statement addressing your vision for a sustainable program of
funded research; (d) a statement addressing your teaching
philosophy and approach to engaging teaching/advising practices,
pedagogical techniques and course materials; and (e) names and
contact information of three professional references.
Screening of applications will begin on November 20, 2026, and
continue until the position is filled. The target starting date is
August 18, 2027.
Complete applications will include:
Cover letter
Complete curriculum vitae
A vision statement for research interests and plans
A statement of teaching philosophy and plans
Contact information for three professional references

jobs.title: Tenure-Track Assistant Professor in Interior Architecture
jobs.description:
Job Details
Position Overview
The School of Architecture & Design at the University of Kansas
invites applications for a full- time tenure-track position of
Assistant Professor in the Interior Architecture program housed
within the Architecture Department. The position will begin in Fall
2027.
We seek candidates who demonstrate ability to teach a variety of
interior architecture studios and lecture/seminar courses in areas
of expertise including (but not limited to) interior material
technology and sustainability; history of architecture, interior
design and art history; and/or design research. The successful
candidate must be familiar with CIDA accreditation process and
professional standards, interested in teaching across the interior
architecture curriculum, able to engage in innovative and
cross-disciplinary teaching, actively participate in research
and/or creative scholarship, and are willing to contribute to
service commitments.
The mission of the Interior Architecture program is to educate
future professionals, focusing on innovative, equitable, holistic,
and meaningful interior environments that support the human
condition and improve the ecological health of the planet through
evidence-based design. The program seeks candidates who contribute
to this mission through innovative teaching, strong scholarship,
interdisciplinary collaboration, and engagement with the evolving
profession.
This position is subject to a collective bargaining agreement between The
University of Kansas and United Academics, United Academics of KU,
AAUP, or AFT. UAKU is the exclusive representative. As the State of
Kansas is a right to work state, you have the right to be a member
or not be a member of a union without fear of personal or
professional repercussions.
The successful candidate must be eligible to work in the United
States by the effective date of the appointment.
About the Interior Architecture Program and Architecture
Department
Launched in 2018, the Interior Architecture program offers a B.S.
in Interior Architecture degree, accredited by both CIDA (Council
for Interior Design Accreditation) and NASAD (National Association
of Schools of Art & Design). The dynamic body of faculty of the
Interior Architecture program reinforces the program goal of
human-centric design through their teaching and research, enabling
future professionals with a wholesome, well-rounded education.
Since its inception, the interior architecture student enrollment
has been growing steadily and graduates of B.S. in Interior
Architecture have been gainfully employed across the U.S. Upon
completion of the B.S. in Interior Architecture degree, graduates
also have the opportunity to apply for the M.Arch degree program
within the Architecture Department.
The Architecture Department faculty’s core purpose is to prepare
new practitioners in the design of the built environment. In
addition to the B.S. in Interior Architecture and M.Arch degrees,
the department also offers a BA in Architectural Studies program,
an MA in Architecture program, and a Ph.D. program. It has urban
design studios in Kansas City, as well as summer, semester, and
year‐long study abroad programs in approximately fifteen
international locations. Following the model set by our Health and
Wellness Design Institute and the Design Department’s Center for
Design Research, the Architecture Department is in the process of
establishing research centers around our recognized areas of
expertise: Design-Build, Sports and Entertainment, Interior
Architecture, Public Interest Design, Historic Preservation, and
Smart Cities. We believe in providing students with diverse
experiences and a comprehensive design education that will prepare
them for a rapidly changing profession and culture.
Job Description
About the University of Kansas
Founded in 1865, KU is a designated Carnegie comprehensive doctoral
research university and one of only 34 public members of the
prestigious Association of American Universities (AAU). The
university enrolls more than 28,000 students and offers students
and faculty opportunities to collaborate in its graduate programs
which include education, public health, medicine, law, and a number
of allied social science disciplines. Situated in the historic,
diverse, and culturally vibrant city of Lawrence, Kansas, 40
minutes from the Kansas City metropolitan area, the University of
Kansas’ Department of Architecture has a 108-year history of
educating Architects who have made significant contributions to the
State, region, and world.
KU’s excellence is a result of the rich tapestry of experiences,
perspectives, and backgrounds of our faculty, staff, students, and
colleagues from across our nation and the globe. At KU, we invest
in continuous learning and growth by creating a climate where
people engage in respectful dialogue and debate and support each
other’s success. We foster a culture of care where each person is
seen, heard and valued. When people feel a true sense of belonging,
we believe they are better able to reach their full potential and
achieve remarkable things.
Allocation of Effort:
Teaching (40% of total time)
Typical teaching expectation of faculty in the Architecture
Department is two 6-credit studios and one 3-credit lecture/seminar
course per academic year (a total of 15 credits per academic year).
The candidate will also meet department expectations in terms of
student advising, as needed.
Research (40% of total time)
Conduct scholarly research and/or creative professional work in
interior architecture and/or architecture. Disseminate research
results through peer-reviewed publications such as books,
monographs and/or articles in academic journals; peer-reviewed
presentations in conferences; exhibitions, and/or in other
appropriate scholarly venues.
Service (20% of total time)
Serve the program, department, university, and profession,
primarily through committees, boards, and related forms of
professional and institutional service.
Required Qualifications
Graduate/post-professional degree in interior design or
architecture (MID, MIArc, MIA, or equivalent professional Master’s
degree; MFA; M.Arch; Ph.D.* or D. Arch*).
Demonstrated record of research, creative work, and/or
professional experience in interior design/interior architecture
and/or architecture.
Contact Information to Applicants
Professor Nisha A. Fernando
Chair, Interior Architecture Search Committee
Nisha.Fernando@ku.edu
Additional Candidate Instruction
Applicants should submit the following items:
1) Letter of intent, including a statement outlining their area of
expertise, research and/or creative interests and
scholarly development and show how they will contribute to the
Interior Architecture program at the University of
Kansas;
2) Curriculum Vitae;
3) Names and contact information (email included) of three
references; and
4) A portfolio of academic/teaching (with student work as
applicable), research and/or creative work, professional
experience, and any other relevant work.
Please upload candidate package and indicate in the letter of
intent a URL to access the complete digital version of the
portfolio.
Review of applications begin on September 28, 2026 and will
remain open until position is filled.

jobs.title: Open Rank, Tenured/Tenure Track Professor in Social Work - 2 positions
jobs.description:
Job Details
Position Overview
The University of Kansas School of Social Welfare (KUSSW) invites
applications for two open-rank, tenure-track or tenured professor
positions beginning in Fall 2027. As part of a strategic investment
in strengthening the KUSSW’s quantitative and data-informed
research enterprise, we seek scholars with a strong, externally
fundable research agenda who use quantitative, computational, or
other data-informed methods to address pressing social challenges.
We are particularly interested in candidates whose scholarship
advances racial, social, economic, and environmental justice
through rigorous empirical research, including the analysis of
social systems, policy and program evaluation, and population-level
outcomes using large administrative or other complex data sets.
Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in Social Work or an M.S.W. with a
Ph.D. in a closely related field by the time of appointment (August
2027).
Successful candidates will contribute to the KUSSW’s nationally
recognized educational programs through excellence in teaching and
mentoring. We seek faculty whose scholarly expertise and teaching
interests align with macro social work practice, social policy,
community practice, program evaluation, and closely related areas.
Faculty teach across the School’s B.S.W., M.S.W., Ph.D., and D.S.W.
programs, which are offered through in-person, online, evening, and
weekend formats to serve students throughout Kansas and
beyond.
KUSSW is committed to fostering a collaborative and supportive
educational environment for students, faculty, and staff. We seek
colleagues whose research, teaching, and service reflect the values
and ethics of the social work profession and align with the
School’s Vision, Mission, and Guiding Principles.
This position is subject to a
collective bargaining agreement between The University of
Kansas and United Academics, United Academics of KU, AAUP, or AFT.
UAKU is the exclusive representative. As the State of Kansas is a
right to work state, you have the right to be a member or not be a
member of a union without fear of personal or professional
repercussions.
About The KUSSW
The KUSSW is situated in the beautiful, historic, and culturally
vibrant cities spanning Lawrence and the Kansas City metropolitan
area, with satellite partnerships across the state of Kansas.
Co-located in Lawrence with Haskell Indian Nations University, the
School of Social Welfare partners with Haskell in mutually
supporting the academic programs of each institution through
research, programs, and services. KUSSW and Haskell play a central
role in the life of the University of Kansas.
The main campus of the KU School of Social Welfare is in Lawrence
and offers BSW, MSW, and PhD degree programs. The KU Edwards Campus
is in Overland Park, a suburb of Kansas City, and offers BSW and
MSW courses. The MSW program is also offered at our partnership
site at Kansas State University - Salina. We also offer fully
online DSW and MSW Programs. We encourage you to consider joining
us in this growth as we continually strive to reinvent, innovate,
transform, and educate through quality education, research
advancement, and community engagement.
The successful candidate must be eligible to work in the U.S. by
the effective date of the appointment.
Job Description
About KU
The University of Kansas is a major comprehensive research and
teaching university that serves as a center for learning,
scholarship, and creative endeavor. The University of Kansas is the
only state university in Kansas to hold membership in the
prestigious Association of American Universities (AAU), a select
group of 62 public and private research universities that represent
excellence in graduate and professional education and the highest
achievements in research internationally. The University enrolls
more than 31,000 students, offers 5,000 courses, more than 400
degree and certificate programs and employs 2,800 faculty members,
many of them at the top of their fields. In KU’s dynamic,
cross-disciplinary research and learning environment, students
exchange ideas, discover new ways of processing the world, and
address society’s grand challenges.
KU’s excellence is a result of the rich tapestry of experiences,
perspectives, and backgrounds of our faculty, staff, students, and
colleagues from across our nation and the globe. At KU, we invest
in continuous learning and growth by creating a climate where
people engage in respectful dialogue and debate and support each
other’s success. We foster a culture of care where each person is
seen, heard, and valued. When people feel a true sense of
belonging, we believe they are better able to reach their full
potential and achieve remarkable things.

focused on advancing racial, social, economic, and/or environmental
justice; publish scholarly manuscripts; engage in scholarly and
community-based publications and presentations; impact the local,

A PhD in social work, OR or a Master of Social Work and a PhD

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor of Architecture
jobs.description:
Job Details
Position Overview
The School of Architecture & Design at the University of Kansas
invites applications for a tenure track or tenured position as
Assistant or Associate Professor of Architecture, with an emphasis
in Computational/Parametric Design and Advanced Manufacturing
Technologies .
The appointment is expected to begin in the spring semester of
2027.
Architects are increasingly expected to integrate advanced
computational design technologies, digital workflows, and research
into the design, coordination, fabrication, and performance of
buildings. This expertise spans the integration of building systems
and programs through computational and parametric design,
artificial intelligence, building performance analysis, advanced
digital fabrication, and industrialized construction
processes.
This position will play a central role in developing and
implementing coursework across the professional and graduate
curricula in these areas, fostering externally funded research in
computational design, digital fabrication, and emerging design
technologies, and coordinating professional and academic programs
that support certifications and advanced credentials in automated
design processes and digital practice.
The successful candidate should demonstrate expertise in one or
more of the following areas: Computational and parametric design,
advanced digital fabrication, industrialized construction, building
performance technologies, artificial intelligence integration in
architectural design, or related emerging digital technologies that
advance architectural practice and research.
The faculty is committed to excellence in applying its knowledge
and experience to educating the next generation of architects. The
Department seeks candidates who will contribute to this mission
through innovative teaching, impactful scholarship,
interdisciplinary collaboration, and engagement with the evolving
profession.
KU’s excellence is a result of the rich tapestry of experiences,
perspectives, and backgrounds of our faculty, staff, students, and
colleagues from across our nation and the globe. At KU, we invest
in continuous learning and growth by creating a climate where
people engage in respectful dialogue and debate and support each
other’s success. We foster a culture of care where each person is
seen, heard and valued. When people feel a true sense of belonging,
we believe they are better able to reach their full potential and
achieve remarkable things. The successful candidate must be
eligible to work in the U.S. by the effective date of the
appointment.
This position is subject to a collective bargaining agreement between The
University of Kansas and United Academics, United Academics of KU,
AAUP, or AFT. UAKU is the exclusive representative. As the State of
Kansas is a right to work state, you have the right to be a member
or not be a member of a union without fear of personal or
professional repercussions.
The successful candidate must be eligible to work in the United
States by the effective date of the appointment.
About the University
Founded in 1865, the University of Kansas is a designated Carnegie
comprehensive doctoral research university and one of the public
members of the prestigious Association of American Universities
(AAU). The University enrolls more than 30,000 students and offers
students and faculty opportunities to collaborate in its graduate
programs which include education, public health, medicine, law, the
humanities, and a number of allied social science disciplines.
Situated in the historic, diverse, and culturally vibrant city of
Lawrence, Kansas, 40 minutes from the Kansas City metropolitan
area, the University of Kansas’ Department of Architecture has a
109-year history of educating architects who have made significant
contributions to the state, region, and world.
Job Description
Allocation of Effort:
Teaching, 40 percent
The typical teaching expectation for Architecture faculty is two
6-credit upper-level architectural design studios and one 3-credit
lecture or seminar per year. The successful candidate will also
meet departmental expectations for student advising.
Research, 40 percent
Conduct research, creative work, and/or professional work focusses
on advanced manufacturing technologies, and related areas of
digital practice. Disseminate this work through peer-reviewed
publications, exhibitions, conferences, and/or other appropriate
scholarly and professional venues. Seek external funding to support
a focused research agenda.
Service, 20 percent
Serve the department, university, state, and profession, primarily
through committees, boards, and related forms of professional and
institutional service.
Required Qualifications
Required Qualifications for Both Assistant and Associate
Professor Candidates
Demonstrated record of research, creative work, and/or
professional work that demonstrates expertise in
computational/parametric design, advanced manufacturing processes
and related areas of digital practice.
Significant professional experience in architectural practice
plus a master’s degree in architecture, or a PhD in architecture
with an emphasis in computational/parametric design and advanced
manufacturing processes.
A professional degree in architecture, NAAB-accredited or
equivalent.
Required Qualifications for Associate Professor Candidates
Only
Established record of teaching consistent with the department’s
standards for promotion to the rank of Associate Professor of
Architecture.
Established record of research, creative work, and/or
professional work consistent with the department’s standards for
promotion to the rank of Associate Professor of Architecture.
Contact Information to Applicants
Marie-Alice L’Heureux
malheur@ku.edu
Additional Candidate Instruction
Applicants should submit the following items:
Letter of intent which includes a statement outlining their
area of expertise, research, creative, and/or professional
interests and shows how these will contribute to the degree
programs in the Architecture Department at the University of
Kansas;
Curriculum vitae;
Names and contact information (email included) of three
references; and
A portfolio that includes examples of professional, academic
(teaching and research), and any other relevant work. Please upload
candidate package and indicate in the letter of intent a URL to
access the complete digital version of the portfolio.
Application review will begin September 30th and will remain open
until the position is filled.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Position Overview
The University of Kansas School of Law invites applications for
both entry-level associate professor and lateral
tenure-track/tenured professor candidates for one position to begin
in the fall of 2027. Our primary curricular needs are in 1L and
core upper-level courses. We invite a plurality of scholarly
agendas, methodologies, and perspectives, ranging from traditional
doctrinal to empirical to critical-analytical to interdisciplinary
scholarship.
This position is subject to a
collective bargaining unit between The University of Kansas and
United Academics, that UAKU is the exclusive representative for the
bargaining unit, and that it is their right to be a member or not
be a member of a union without fear of personal or professional
repercussions.
KU Law ranks among the top 50 law schools in the nation and lands
at #24 among public law schools according to recent U.S. News &
World Report Rankings. Law faculty are active scholars,
researchers, and subject matter experts in their fields. KU ranks
#19 among public law schools for scholarly impact. Many professors
are authors of textbooks and casebooks used in classes at KU and in
law schools across the U.S. and overseas.
KU’s excellence is a result of the rich tapestry of experiences,
perspectives, and backgrounds of our faculty, staff, students, and
colleagues from across our nation and the globe. At KU, we invest
in continuous learning and growth by creating a climate where
people engage in respectful dialogue and debate and support each
other’s success. We foster a culture of care where each person is
seen, heard and valued. When people feel a true sense of belonging,
we believe they are better able to reach their full potential and
achieve remarkable things.
The University of Kansas is a Carnegie doctoral/research-extensive
university with a $2.7 billion endowment and a faculty of 3,571.
Current enrollment is 31,169 (22,544 undergraduate). Students come
from 116 nations and all 50 states; 26.6% of KU students are
members of minority groups. The 1,000-acre main campus is in
Lawrence, a community of 96,000 in hilly northeast Kansas that lies
about 35 miles west of Kansas City. Lawrence has a lively downtown
and a thriving arts and music scene, and its local government has
enacted ordinances supporting equality for all members of its
population. Lawrence also offers numerous sports and recreational
opportunities, local shops, and a wide range of good
restaurants.

Participate in professional service within the legal academy or
legal profession, such as committee work for local, regional,
national, or international professional associations like the
Association of American Law Schools, the American Bar Association,

jobs.title: Assistant Professor in the Department of English
jobs.description:
Job Details
Position Details : Randolph-Macon College invites
applications for a tenure-track position of Assistant Professor in
the Department of English to begin Fall 2027.
Institution Information: Randolph-Macon College is a
nationally recognized residential institution of about 1800
students located in Ashland, Virginia, just north of Richmond.
Founded in 1830, the college offers a broad range of academic
programs, including a graduate program in PA studies. The RMC
curriculum, grounded in a liberal arts core, fosters intellectual
growth and personal development, with a steadfast focus on helping
students find and pathways through college and to successful
outcomes. With a commitment to inclusivity and hands-on learning,
Randolph-Macon College provides an extraordinary educational
experience – enhanced by exceptional athletic and extracurricular
activities and supportive alumni – and prepares graduates for
success in their chosen fields and in their lives.
The English department gives students an understanding of human
nature, society, and history, while at the same time honing their
powers of expression. The major thus caters to a wide variety of
students, from those with a lifelong love of language and reading,
to those who write poetry and fiction, to those eager to understand
how language may be used to entertain, move, or persuade. English
majors find community in the Washington Literary Society,
contribute to our literary journal The Stylus, and
participate in unique internship opportunities. An RMC English
degree provides students with critical thinking and communication
skills that have repeatedly shown themselves valuable in an array
of professions as various as law, advertising, teaching, and
politics.
Major/Essential Functions : Randolph-Macon College faculty

jobs.title: Assistant Professor/Program Director – Medical Lab Technology
jobs.description:
Lead a respected Medical Laboratory Technology program while
preparing the next generation of laboratory professionals. As the
Assistant Professor/Program Director - MLT, you’ll provide
academic and program leadership for the Idaho Consortium for
Medical Laboratory Technology Education (ICMLTE), ensuring students
receive high-quality education and clinical experiences while the
program maintains its NAACLS accreditation.
You’ll oversee the day-to-day administration and coordination of
the program, including accreditation compliance, reports, site
visits, program evaluation, curriculum review, student learning
assessment, and program planning. You’ll build and maintain
relationships with clinical laboratories and healthcare
organizations, coordinate clinical affiliation agreements and
student onboarding requirements, and work with consortium
institutions and clinical partners to support strong learning
experiences. You’ll lead advisory and executive committee meetings,
contribute to budget planning, support faculty development,
coordinate adjunct faculty needs, and participate in student
recruitment and admissions activities. You’ll also teach assigned
Medical Laboratory Technology courses, provide academic advising
and laboratory supervision, and use a variety of instructional
methods and technologies.
We’re looking for a Medical Laboratory Science professional with
knowledge of education, program administration, and NAACLS
accreditation requirements. The ideal candidate can lead across
multiple institutions and build effective relationships with
faculty, students, clinical partners, and other stakeholders.
Strong communication, curriculum design and evaluation, training
and presentation skills, and proficiency with instructional
technology are essential. This role offers an opportunity to
combine clinical laboratory expertise, education, and program
leadership to make a lasting impact on students and the healthcare
workforce.
Enjoy
excellent benefits, including retirement
2 personal days per year
9 sick days per year
Tuition assistance

jobs.title: Associate Director, TCU Global Programs (Faculty-led & Summer Semester Programs)
jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Summary:
The Associate Director, reporting to the Director of TCU Global,
provides leadership and vision in the establishment of procedures
to effectively develop and deliver faculty-led and summer semester
programs. The Associate Director will support strategic planning
and innovative new programs in partnership with faculty, schools,
and colleges of TCU, and serve as the primary point of contact for
faculty in the TCU Global Office. The Associate Director will
oversee the management of all aspects of faculty-led and summer
semester programming and operations, and conduct program assessment
and evaluation supported by a Program Coordinator.
Duties & Essential Job Functions:
1. Leads development, coordination, and delivery of all
international faculty-led study abroad programs.
2. Manages all Summer Semester programs.
3. Oversees the proposal process for program development and site
visits. Works with faculty to assess potential programing
opportunities.
4. Manages the entire cycle of all faculty-led and summer semester
programs from advising, admission, arrival, to return.
5. Performs partner institution visits and site evaluations to
ensure the programs are providing quality experiences and
opportunities for TCU students for both existing and potential
partners. Provides on-site orientations to student participants.
Meets with receiving staff members at these institutions to ensure
the programs are running smoothly and there are no concerns.
Reviews processes and procedures associated with the university.
Performs wellness checks on study abroad students.
6. Designs strategies to increase the number and variety of
experiences offered. Conducts ongoing research of faculty-led
programs to expand and refine comprehensive program opportunities
to students and faculty.
7. Collaborates with administrative staff and faculty to supervise
quality and academic relevance of faculty-led programming
8. Creates and delivers comprehensive pre-departure and re-entry
orientations as necessary for students in faculty-led and summer
semester programs.
9. Creates reports by collecting and analyzing various data from
faculty-led programs. Makes recommendations to the Director and the
TCU Global Faculty Advisory Committee based on analysis of the
findings.
10. Designs and delivers high-quality, informative presentations
regarding current study abroad opportunities and how students can
access these programs. Works with faculty members to properly
disseminate information about available opportunities to interested
students. Develops and implements a strategic plan to ensure that
students are aware of the study abroad opportunities they have
available to them
11. Supervises the Program Coordinator (International Programs),
alongside the Associate Director of Semester Programs.
12. As a member of TCU Global Faculty Advisory Committee, supports
strategic planning and the creation and implementation of
innovative new programs in partnership with faculty, schools, and
colleges of TCU.
13. Serves as the primary point of contact for faculty in the TCU
Global Office.
14. Performs other related duties as assigned.
Required Education & Experience:
• Bachelor’s degree
• 4 years of administrative experience in programming or
international education in a university setting
Preferred Education & Experience:
• Master’s degree in a relevant field
• Experience responding to health, safety, and emergency situations
abroad.
Required Licensure/Certification/Specialized Training:
• None
Preferred Licensure, Certification, and/or Specialized
Training:
• None
Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:
Knowledge of study abroad policies and programs
• Skill in analytical analysis to translate data into informed
decisions
• Skill in clear communication, both oral and in writing, and
interpersonal skills.
• Skill in critical thinking demonstrated by the ability to analyze
information, evaluate results, and make decisions.
• Ability to manage multiple projects in an organized manner
• Ability to work with individuals from a variety of diverse
backgrounds
• Ability to assess student learning outcomes to preform program
evaluation
• Ability to manage a strategic priority such as increasing and
diversifying student participation in study abroad
• Ability to work well in a team and in partnership with others
both across TCU and abroad
• Ability to evaluate and make recommendations to improve
operations.
• Ability to collaborate with senior leadership, faculty, staff,
students, and international entities/organizations.
• Ability to learn and use various computer applications
• Ability to strategize, prioritize, and multi-task to meet goals
and deadlines
• Ability to independently travel domestically and
internationally.
TCU Core Competencies:
University Core Competencies definitions may be found on the Human
Resources website and in the staff performance management
system.
Physical Requirements (With or Without
Accommodations):
• Visual acuity to read information from computer screens, forms
and other printed materials and information.
• Able to speak (enunciate) clearly in conversation and general
communication.
• Hearing ability for verbal communication/conversation/responses
via telephone, telephone systems, and face-to-face
interactions.
• Manual dexterity for typing, writing, standing and reaching,
flexibility, body movement for bending, crouching, walking,
kneeling and prolonged sitting.
• Lifting and moving objects and equipment up to 10 lbs.
Work Environment:
• Work is indoors and sedentary and is subject to schedule changes
and/or variable work hours.
• There are no harmful environmental conditions present for this
job.
• This role is an on campus, in-person position with periodic
domestic and international travel.
• The noise level in this work environment is usually
moderate.
Employment Values Statement:
Texas Christian University values Integrity, Engagement, Community,
and Excellence in the workplace. TCU treats applicants and
employees with fairness and respect. TCU hires and promotes
individuals based on their qualifications and their commitment to
making a positive impact on our student-centered community. TCU is
an equal opportunity employer and follows all applicable employment
laws. TCU fairly considers all qualified individuals, ensuring we
are a workplace free from unlawful discrimination and
harassment.

jobs.title: Assistant Teaching Professor - APRN Core
jobs.description:
Job Details
Position Title:
Assistant Teaching Professor - APRN Core
Position Type:
Regular
About the Role:
The Assistant Teaching Professor is responsible for coordinating,
leading, and teaching courses in the MSN program.
The MSN Faculty upholds academic integrity, follows standards of
practice, and collaborates with the all MSN and SON faculty to
ensure curriculum alignment with CCNE Essentials and the national
standards applicable to the assigned track.
The role supports graduate preparation for national certification
eligibility in the APRN, NEL, or NED track, fosters program
effectiveness, and promotes a student-centered, high-quality
learning environment.
Organizational Relationship:
Workload assigned by the Associate Director/MSN Program
Director and SON Director
Evaluated annually by the Associate School Director and/or SON
Director and with input from peer faculty
Maintain regular, proactive communication with MSN Faculty and
Program Director regarding course operations, student concerns, and
any emerging issues, ensuring alignment with program expectations
and timely resolution.
Program Leadership:
Actively engage in SON, MSN program, course, and university
meetings, as designated by the SON Director and Associate
Director/MSN Program director to support shared governance and
program effectiveness.
Collaborate regularly with other MSN Faculty to address MSN
curriculum, course content, grading practices, student concerns,
and faculty or university-related matters. Escalate unresolved
issues to the MSN Program Director following appropriate
communication pathways.
Contribute to program success through participation in
activities related to student admission, progression, and
orientation, as well as curriculum review and enhancement for
students enrolled in or applying to the MSN program.
Ensure alignment with CCNE Standards, the national competencies
applicable to the assigned track (NONPF for APRN; AONL and NLN for
NEL and NED), and other professional standards as
appropriate.
Faculty Leadership:
Maintain an active presence and engagement throughout the MSN
program by monitoring responsiveness, grading practices, and
interactions with students.
Collaboratively review and discuss student assignments
receiving a grade of 80% or below to ensure timely academic support
and consistency in evaluation.
Plan, teach, manage, and evaluate lectures and course
activities while ensuring instructional excellence and innovation
in content delivery.
Review course materials, including readings, textbooks, and
learning resources, to ensure alignment with current evidence-based
practice, CCNE Standards, the national competencies applicable to
the assigned track (NONPF for APRN; AONL and NLN for NEL and NED),
and other professional standards as appropriate and communicate any
necessary updates to the applicable MSN Track Coordinator(s) to
maintain curricular relevance and accuracy.
Collaborates closely with the MSN Program Director/Associate
Director and MSN faculty to maintain the quality of courses and
overall program effectiveness while fostering an enriching learning
experience for students.
Other duties include:
Be accessible and available to students, supervisor, staff and
colleagues during NKU operation hours (8:00 am – 4:30 pm
EST).
Serve on SON and program committees as assigned and attend SON,
program, and other meetings in person or virtually; be an active
participate in SON, program, and university needs.
Education
Doctoral degree in Nursing or related field required. For APRN
track positions, an Advanced Practice Certification in a nurse
practitioner specialty (FNP, AGACNP, PMHNP). For NEL and NED track
positions, MSN in nursing with graduate preparation in nursing
leadership/administration or nursing education, respectively
Qualifications:
Minimum of two years of clinical nursing practice
required.
Must possess an active and unencumbered registered nursing (RN)
license in State of residence and, for APRN track positions, an
advanced practice license
For APRN track positions, at least five years of full-time,
past and current direct patient care as an APRN in the designated
specialty area.
For NEL and NED track positions, comparable full-time
professional experience in nursing leadership/administration or
nursing education, as applicable
Previous graduate- level teaching required
Previous online teaching experience required
Experience or expertise with course content
Pass pre-employment criminal background check as mandated by
state law
Professional Expectations:
Maintain active unencumbered RN licensure and, for APRN track
positions, APRN certification/licensure; NEL and NED faculty
maintain any certifications relevant to their track
Maintain current knowledge of professional discipline and
educational methodologies through continuing professional
development
For APRN track positions, maintain part-time clinical practice
as needed to maintain APRN certification/licensure; ensure clinical
practice (max release is one day weekly) does not interfere with
faculty duties
Maintain current knowledge of program policies, procedures, and
student progress
Adhere to faculty professional standards as delineated in the
NKU Faculty Handbook
Utilize nku.edu email for ALL course communications – students
are required to do the same
Teach and precept as needed to meet program needs
Required Training:
Completes ‘Best Practices for Online Teaching’ Canvas course as
assigned
Completes required Faculty Development courses annually
Complete Clinical systems training currently used in program
(i.e., Medatrax)
Please include:
RN license report (from NURSYS)
APRN Certificate (as appropriate)
CV
Teaching Philosophy
Cover letter
References
Work Environment & Physical Demands:

jobs.title: Assistant Teaching Professor and Clinical Coordinator, Cardiovascular Perfusion Program
jobs.description:
Job Details
Position Title:
Assistant Teaching Professor and Clinical Coordinator,
Cardiovascular Perfusion Program
Position Type:
Regular
About the Role:
Northern Kentucky University’s (NKU) School of Allied Health,
within the College of Health & Human Services, is seeking a
fulltime Clinical Coordinator and faculty member to teach in the
Master of Science in Cardiovascular Perfusion program.
NKU, a growing metropolitan university located 7 miles from
Cincinnati, is a university known to its faculty and students for
its commitment to student success. The clinical coordinator will
have teaching responsibilities and will oversee clinical aspects of
the program in collaboration with the program director, including
the development of relationships with clinical partners to provide
excellence in cardiovascular perfusion education
opportunities.
The ideal candidate for this position will be a perfusionist with a
strong science and research background with teaching experience
with the ability to teach across the perfusion curriculum, to
include anatomy and physiology, pathophysiology, pharmacology,
research methods and oversee research capstone projects.
This position will also require aspects of service and commitment
not only to the program, but also to the College of Health &
Human Services and the university by serving on various committees
when needed.
This is a 12-month non-tenure track renewable faculty position at
the rank of assistant teaching professor.
Primary Responsibilities
Teach face-to-face courses in the program, as assigned; a
limited number of courses may be online, but face-to-face teaching
is required
Engage in student recruitment, selection, guidance,
instruction, and evaluation.
Support the program director in accomplishing outcomes related
to planning, implementation, and evaluation of the program.
Assist the program director in course development.
Participate in the community advisory committee for the program
and various other service activities across multiple levels
(program, school, college, and university.
Help guide the program to ensure alignment with the
University’s strategic priorities of retention, graduation and
overall student success.
Communicate with current clinical sites and preceptors to
assist in coordinating clinical contracts.
Participate in various committee and service activities across
multiple levels, including program, school, college and
university.
Recruit and maintain clinical sites, coordinate clinical
contracts and obtain qualified preceptors at each clinical
facility. Establish and maintain working relationships with staff
within the clinical sites.
Minimum Education & Qualifications
Master’s degree (doctorate preferred) from an accredited
institution recognized by the US Secretary of Education at the time
the degree was conferred, in perfusion, and an education in related
sciences such as biology, anatomy and physiology, biochemistry,
pharmacology, exercise physiology, kinesiology.
Minimum of five (5) years of professional experience as a
perfusionist
Minimum of 3 years pedagogical teaching experience (or
instructional methodology) relevant to science courses within an
academic setting.
Highly developed interpersonal communication and organizational
skills.
Ability to create and maintain collegial relationships with
internal and external team members.
Commitment to the mission of NKU, College of Health and Human
Services, and Program.
Additional qualifications include:
Active engagement in professional organizations.
Any candidate who is offered this position will be required to
go through a pre-employment criminal background check as mandated
by state law.
NKU’s vision is that we will be nationally recognized for being
a student-ready, regionally engaged university that empowers
diverse learners for economic and social mobility. Our core values
place emphasis on our culture of excellence, creativity,
innovation, and collegiality. Your cover letter and/or teaching
statement should show, as a faculty member at NKU, how you will
contribute to our core values and our strategic framework,
especially in how you will contribute student success and
belonging.
Please include:
Teaching Philosophy
Cover letter
CV
References
Work Environment & Physical Demands:

jobs.description:
Job Details
Position Title:
Tenure Track- Assistant Professor Bachelor in Social Work
Program
Position Type:
Regular
About the Role:
The School of Social Work invites applications for a full-time,
tenure track Assistant Professor position. The faculty member in
this position will teach in both our BSW & MSW programs,
including in-person, hybrid, and online courses. We seek a
colleague who will contribute to a collegial and collaborative work
environment and maintain a presence on campus, with a strong
commitment to service and active engagement in scholarship.
Preference will be given to candidates with experience teaching
across the BSW and MSW curricula, including foundational and
applied research courses and practice-oriented courses.
Specific responsibilities include:
Faculty members are expected to engage in teaching, scholarship,
and service while demonstrating commitment to social work values
and competencies in alignment with the NASW Code of Ethics and CSWE
accreditation standards.
Develop and deliver engaging, student-centered courses across the
undergraduate and graduate curricula, including in-person, hybrid,
and online courses. Engage in service that contributes to the
University, the College of Health and Human Services, the School of
Social Work, the social work profession, and the larger community
(regional, national, and/or global). Contribute to the regular CSWE
reaffirmation cycles for the BSW and MSW programs. Actively engage
in scholarship activities, including peer-reviewed publications and
presentations at a national and/or international level.
Education/Qualifications:
Required qualifications:
MSW from a CSWE-accredited program. PhD in social work or a related
field (ABD considered with confirmed completion date). Experience
teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in online and in-person
formats.
Preferred qualifications:
Minimum of two years post-MSW practice experience. MSW-level
licensure (e.g. CSW, LCSW, LISW). Experience teaching foundational
and applied research courses. Experience teaching practice-oriented
courses. Experience conducting and disseminating scholarly
research. Experience with or demonstrated interest in community
engagement.
Please include:
Cover letter CV Names and contact information for 3 professional
references Teaching philosophy (2 page maximum) Writing sample
(e.g. published manuscript, book chapter, chapter from
dissertation) Copies of graduate transcripts (unofficial copies
accepted at this initial stage)

jobs.title: Assistant Professor, Master of Health Administration
jobs.description:
Job Details
Position Title:
Assistant Professor, Master of Health Administration
Position Type:
Regular
About the Role:
Northern Kentucky University’s School of Allied Health is seeking
applications for a full-time tenure-track faculty member to join
the online accelerated Master of Science in Health Administration
Program. The School of Allied Health, housed within the College of
Health and Human Services, is a multidisciplinary unit offering
both graduate and undergraduate clinical and non-clinical degree
programs. The successful candidate will bring their healthcare
management knowledge and experience into the online classroom, to
enrich the student experience and facilitate meaningful learning
opportunities. This position is a 9-month appointment reporting to
the Director of the School of Allied Health. Additional summer
teaching opportunities may be available.
Position Responsibilities:
Teaching: Courses taught may include healthcare systems
and environment, healthcare leadership, applied research methods,
healthcare quality and project management, and others as needed.
Capstone and internship field project management and coordination
may be additional responsibilities associated with this faculty
position. All program courses are taught online in accelerated
7-week sessions.
Scholarship: The successful candidate will develop and
maintain a record of research and scholarship, as required for
tenure.
Service: Active participation in service and committee
work across a variety of levels at the department, college, and
university levels is expected. Collaboration with the program
director to contribute to ongoing program and course review and
development is a key aspect of this role.
Required Education & Qualifications:
Earned doctoral degree in health administration/management, health
policy, public health or related discipline. Through education and
experience is able to teach the courses identified in the position
responsibilities. Evidence of at least 2 years effective teaching
in accelerated and online courses. Evidence of individual,
collaborative and/or multi-disciplinary research and scholarship
that contributes to the advancement their profession. At least 3
years of experience as a leader/administrator in the healthcare
industry.
Preferred Qualifications:
Demonstrated experience in online course review, online course
development, leading internship field projects and capstone
courses. Member of the American College of Healthcare Executives
(ACHE) Involvement with the Association of University Programs in
Health Administration (AUPHA) At least 5 years’ experience as an
administrator/executive leader in a healthcare organization
Research and scholarship focus in the field of healthcare
administration or area of study specific to those in the NKU MSHA
curriculum. Documented graduate level education and/or professional
experience in the fields of health policy and health care
management.
Please include:
Cover letter that addresses the applicant's qualifications
based on the position announcement
CV
Statement of Teaching Philosophy
Contact information for three professional references
Master of Science in Health Administration Mission
Statement:
The mission of the Master of Health Administration program at
Northern Kentucky University is to develop competent,
compassionate, and career‑ready healthcare leaders through
rigorous, student‑centered, competency‑based graduate education and
applied scholarship. Grounded in ethical practice and
evidence‑based management, the program prepares early- to
mid‑career professionals to lead healthcare organizations, improve
system performance, and positively impact the health and well‑being
of the communities they serve.

Samuel Merritt University graduates improve health outcomes and
reduce disparities for all members of our communities. We have

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of English
jobs.description:
The Department of English at the University of Maryland, College Park is hiring a tenure-track Assistant Professor of English with a specialization in Poetry to join a thriving creative writing program within a diverse and productive English department to begin in August 2027. Qualified candidates will have a strong reputation in the field of creative writing with a primary publication record in poetry, at least one full-length poetry book with a nationally recognized publisher, and an MFA in poetry or PhD (preferred) in English literature/creative writing with a focus in poetry.
The Department seeks a poet who also engages other media forms, genres, and/or secondary studies in literature or art, such as expertise or publications in indigenous studies, digital media, or creative nonfiction. Additional interests are also welcome, such as LGBTQIA+ and trans* literature, African American literature, multiethnic literatures, disability studies, and environmental humanities. An ideal candidate will be experienced in teaching creative writing workshops at the undergraduate/graduate levels, literature courses, and directing undergraduate honors projects or theses. Experience working on, running, or advising students on a literary journal, small press, or experimental or innovative publishing venture would be welcomed. Applicants should have demonstrated ability in working with a varied student body and documented mentorship. The poet’s tenure home will be in the Department of English and they will be a key member of the graduate and undergraduate creative writing programs.
Belonging, community, equity, and access drive the mission of the English Department, and we seek candidates whose creative work, teaching, and service have prepared them to contribute to and advance this mission. Within their applications, candidates are asked to summarize their leadership efforts and past or potential contributions to the collegiate community such as leadership in teaching, mentoring, research, or service towards building an equitable and varied scholarly environment and/or increasing access or participation of individuals from equity-deserving groups.
Best consideration date is October 15, 2026. Applications will be accepted and reviewed until the position is filled.
The University of Maryland is located in College Park, eight miles from the heart of Washington, DC, and served by the Washington Metro System, offering its faculty access to world-class library and archival facilities, an array of cultural institutions, and culturally and linguistically diverse communities. The MFA Program in Creative Writing is staffed by a stellar faculty, active on the national and international literary scene, with strong ties to the greater D.C. literary arts community. We are committed to belonging and community and run a vibrant program grounded in mentoring of young writers. MFA alumni are noted for their award-winning publications with independent and major presses, for continuing their graduate education at top-tier doctoral programs, and for starting their own nationally recognized journals and magazines.
UMD will not sponsor the successful candidate for work authorization in the United States now or in the future.

jobs.title: OPEN RANK: Construction Buyer or Senior Construction & Facilities Buyer
jobs.description:
University of Maryland, Baltimore (UMB) is seeking a talented
procurement professional to join the Department of Construction
& Facilities Procurement as either a Construction Buyer or
Senior Construction & Facilities Buyer. The level of the
position will be based on the selected candidate's qualifications
and relevant experience.
BENEFITS (Exempt Regular):
UMB offers a comprehensive benefits package that
prioritizes wellness, work/life balance, and professional
development, along with additional exciting perks
that employees can take advantage of. This position participates in
a retirement program (pension or optional retirement plan/ORP) that
must be selected and is effective on your date of hire. Exempt
regular staff receive a generous PAID leave package that includes
over 4 weeks of vacation accrued each year, 16 paid holidays, 3
personal leave days, unlimited accrual of sick time, and
comprehensive health insurance; professional learning and
development programs; tuition remission for employees and their
dependents at any University System of Maryland school; and
flexible work schedules and teleworking options (if applicable per
job).
UMB is a public university and constituent institution of the
University System of Maryland. All employees are expected to work
primarily physically within the State of Maryland.
PRIMARY DUTIES
For Construction Buyer :
- Perform procurement activities including all aspects of
transactions from initiation to award recommendation with a focus
on capital and non-capital construction procurements. Items
procured may be specialized in nature giving rise to unique
situations with complex specifications, limited market sources, and
close price bidding.
- Assist in preparing construction procurements for specific
building projects.
- Assist to resolve any differences on critical points and specific
contractual provisions.
- Drafts specifications and vendor qualification criteria for bids
and proposals upon researching the end user's needs to ensure
proper procurement, maximized competition, and proper equipment
form and function.
- Communicates on and settles any differences on critical points
and specific contractual provisions.
- Serves as liaison between campus and vendor community, supplying
end users with information on sources, discounts, pricing and
delivery provisions.
- Evaluate bid and proposal responses to contract awards and
debrief unsuccessful vendors.
- Researches market to determine if sole sources are justified and
to develop new sources for supplies and services.
- Performs other duties as assigned.
For Senior Construction & Facilities Buyer :
- Perform construction and facilities maintenance procurement
including all aspects of construction and facilities procurement
transactions from initiation to award recommendation. Procurement
may specialize in unique situations with complex specifications.
Procurements may include RFQ, IFB, Multistep Bid and RFPs.
- Work with project managers to draft specifications and vendor
qualification criteria for bids and proposals upon researching the
end user's needs to ensure proper procurement, maximized
competition, and proper form and function.
- Coordinate efforts to liaise between project managers and vendor
community, supplying end users with information on sources,
discounts, pricing and delivery provisions.
- Evaluate bid and proposal responses to contract awards and
debrief unsuccessful vendors.
- Maintain existing and develops new sources for construction and
contractor supplies and services.
- Prepare construction procurements for specific building
projects.
- Resolve any differences on critical points and specific
contractual provisions.
- Performs contract administration on all contracts awarded.
- Performs other duties as assigned.
Qualifications :
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
For Construction Buyer:
Education: Bachelor's degree. Substitution of equivalent
years of relevant experience in the field of construction,
construction procurement, maintenance, or maintenance procurement
may be made in place of Bachelor's Degree.
Experience: Two (2) years related construction, buying,
or procurement experience.
Supervisory Experience: N/A
Certification/Licensure: N/A
Other: Financial disclosure reporting required by State
of Maryland Ethics Committee.
Except for qualifications established by law, additional related
experience and formal education in which one has gained the
knowledge, skills, and abilities required for full performance of
the work of the job class may be substituted for the education or
experience requirement on a year-for-year basis with 30
undergraduate college credits being equivalent to one year of
related experience. In instances where specific education and/or
experience is required only directly related education and/or
experience may be substituted.
For Senior Construction & Facilities Buyer:
Education: Bachelor's degree. Substitution of equivalent
years of relevant experience in the field of construction,
construction procurement, maintenance, or maintenance procurement
may be made in place of Bachelor's Degree.
Experience: Three (3) years procurement, construction,
or project Management experience, including at least two (2) year
of construction procurement or maintenance procurement
experience
Supervisory Experience: N/A
Certification/Licensure: N/A
Other: Financial disclosure reporting required by State
of Maryland Ethics Committee.
Except for qualifications established by law, additional
related experience and formal education in which one has gained the
knowledge, skills, and abilities required for full performance of
the work of the job class may be substituted for the education or
experience requirement on a year-for-year basis with 30
undergraduate college credits being equivalent to one year of
related experience. In instances where specific education and/or
experience is required only directly related education and/or
experience may be substituted.
KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES
Knowledge of position requirements. Knowledge of all applicable
requirements, regulations, and laws. Skill in effective use of
applicable technology/systems. Ability to effectively communicate
both verbal and written thoughts, ideas, and facts. Ability to work
cooperatively with others and independently. Ability to
demonstrate, understand, apply, and adhere to the UMB Core Values
of Respect and Integrity, Well-being and Sustainability, Equity and
Justice, and Innovation and Discovery.
HIRING RANGE: $76,500 - $85,000 per year for Construction
Buyer / $83,000 - $98,000 per year for Senior Construction &
Facilities Buyer / Commensurate with education and experience
UMB is committed to cultivating a diverse and inclusive workforce
and is proud to be an equal employment opportunity employer. All
qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment
without regard to race, color, religion, age, ancestry or national
origin, sex, pregnancy or related conditions, sexual orientation,
gender identity or expression, genetic information, physical or
mental disability, marital status, protected veteran's status, or
any other legally protected classification.
