Commission on Higher Education. In addition, the Association to
Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB), The European
Foundation for Management Development (EFMD)'s EQUIS, and the
Association of MBAs (AMBA) accredit the School of Business; ABET
accredits its engineering programs; the Canadian Society for
Chemistry accredits the chemistry program; and the Master of Public
Administration and the Master of Public Policy programs of GAPP are
accredited by the Network of Schools of Public Policy, Affairs, and
administration (NASPAA). The AUC libraries contain the largest
English-language research collection in the region. They are an
active and integral part of the university's pursuit of excellence
in all academic programs. AUC is an English-medium
institution; eighty-five percent of the students are Egyptian. The
rest include students from nearly ninety countries, mainly from the
Middle East, Africa, and North America. Faculty salary and rank are
based on qualifications and professional experience. According to
AUC policies and procedures, all faculty are entitled to generous
benefits.
The roots of the Onsi Sawiris School of Business date back to
1947, when the first degree in economics was introduced in Egypt.
The school has been accredited by the Association to Advance
Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB) since 2006, the European
Foundation for Management Development (EFMD)'s EQUIS, and the
Association of MBAs (AMBA) since 2014, when it became among the 1%
triple-crown accredited business schools in the world. The school
is a member of the Global Alliance in Management Education (CEMS)
and the Global Network for Advanced Management (GNAM). In 2024, the
school was ranked by Eduniversal as the best in Africa for the 8th
consecutive year and 73rd globally in open enrolment in executive
education by the Financial Times. The school offers six
undergraduate degrees, including bachelor's degrees in economics,
accounting, marketing, finance, information and communication
technology management, and entrepreneurship. In addition, the
school offers six graduate degrees in economics, economic
development, finance, and international management, as well as an
MBA and an EMBA. The school is home to 8 research and outreach
centers, including the Access to Knowledge for Development Center,
the Center for Entrepreneurship and Innovation, the Venture Lab,
and the Al-Khazindar Business Research and Case Center. For more
information about the school: business.aucegypt.edu.
Job Description:
The American University in Cairo's Onsi Sawiris School of
Business invites nominations and applications for a faculty
position in the Heikal Department of Management at the
Assistant/Associate/Professor of Finance level for a fixed-term
four-year appointment, beginning in Fall 2027. The successful
applicant will be expected to contribute to teaching undergraduate
and graduate finance courses and thesis supervision in the Master
of Science in Finance. Possible fields of interest include, but are
not limited to, financial economics, business finance, corporate
finance, applied banking, Fintech, algorithmic trading, retail
banking, and portfolio theory.
The Heikal Department of Management seeks an exceptional
applicant whose research complements our strengths in the
department while transcending traditional research in finance. The
applicant is expected to develop a world-class research portfolio
and build a diverse research team in collaboration with business
and industry partners, focusing on addressing issues related to
emerging markets, with a particular emphasis on the Middle East and
Africa regions. Applicants will also be expected to engage in
academic and community development services consistent with
teaching and research, including ongoing activities in the
department, and undertake development projects. All faculty members
must be willing to teach introductory courses.
Requirements:
Applicants must hold a PhD in finance, economics, or a
business-related field from a reputable university, preferably
AACSB and/or EQUIS accredited. Applicants must demonstrate an
internationally recognized record of research excellence and
scholarly impact. Applicants must have a proven record of research
publications in the past five years in top-tier journals (A*/A
according to the ABDC ranking or Q1/Q2 according to Scopus
ranking). PhD candidates must demonstrate a strong research agenda
and a history of securing competitive research funding. Candidates
should demonstrate commitment to academic research, teaching, and
service.
Key Responsibilities:
Research & Scholarship
Leading a world-class research program in finance, banking,
fintech, financial economics, business finance, and their
implications on business.
Securing competitive external funding to sustain and expand
research initiatives.
Conducting impactful research.
Publishing in top-tier journals and presenting at leading
international conferences.
Teaching & Mentorship.
Developing innovative undergraduate and graduate curricula that
integrate emerging technologies and industry trends into the
finance discipline and their applications to business and the
economy.
Aligning degrees with changing market demands.
Delivering graduate and undergraduate courses in finance and
related disciplines.
Supervising and mentoring graduate students.
Mentoring faculty.
Institutional Leadership
Serving as a catalyst for interdisciplinary research across
departments, schools, and external partners.
Representing the school and university in national and
international forums, strengthening its global reputation, and
elevating the level of collaboration.
Community & Industry Engagement.
Building partnerships with industry, government, and civil
society to translate research into real-world impact.
Engaging in public discourse on finance, financial policies,
and their societal implications.
Supporting outreach programs that broaden participation in
finance education.
Collaborating with industry to implement applied research
projects.
Additional Information:
Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until
the position is filled. Only shortlisted candidates will be
contacted.
Application Instructions:
All applicants must submit the following documents online:
Cover letter outlining research, teaching, and leadership
vision.
Current Curriculum vitae.
Statements of research and teaching.
Sample of current research (up to three representative
publications).
Evidence of teaching effectiveness.
Completed AUC Personnel Information Form (PIF); and,
Three names of reference to busref@aucegypt.edu with the
subject line BUS/finc/2027.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor, School of Social Work
jobs.description:
Assistant Professor- Tenure System
Job # 1167599
Posting Snapshot:
The School of Social Work is seeking candidates for a nine-month Assistant Professor in the tenure system to join our team.
Reports to:
School of Social Work Director
Position Summary:
Michigan State University actively promotes a dynamic research and learning environment in which qualified individuals of differing perspectives and cultural backgrounds pursue academic goals with mutual respect and shared inquiry.
The School of Social Work is seeking candidates for an Assistant Professor position in the tenure stream. We seek candidates with a well-defined research agenda and the potential to make meaningful contributions to the field through creative, innovative, and rigorous scholarship. We encourage applications from candidates with research interests that build upon our four core areas of research expertise: health and aging; marginalized youth and families; sexual and gender minority health; and violence and violence prevention. We also welcome candidates with research interests that expand our School’s areas of expertise, including candidates whose research uses innovative research methods to address emerging issues in social work. Candidates should show promise for securing external research funding, producing high-quality scholarship, and contributing to our vibrant intellectual community. Position expectations include teaching across the social work curriculum, at both undergraduate and graduate levels, mentoring students, and participating in our school community. The successful candidate will have opportunities to collaborate with faculty across the university and participate in interdisciplinary research initiatives. Candidates who have experience promoting intellectual debates around a diversity of viewpoints and perspectives are especially encouraged to apply.
School Statement:
The MSU School of Social Work, within the College of Social Science, is dedicated to educating students for ethical, competent, responsive, and innovative social work practice, and to conducting and disseminating high quality research that improves the well-being of the most vulnerable in society. Our teaching, research, and outreach synergistically promote social justice, positive change, and solutions to the problems facing a broad cross section of individuals, families, groups, organizations, and communities. More than 650 students are enrolled in our CSWE- accredited BASW and MSW programs, and our PhD program.
Minimum Qualifications:
An earned doctorate in Social Work or a related field by the date of employment
A beginning record of scholarly productivity, evidenced by peer-reviewed publications, scholarly presentations, research funding activity, or other relevant scholarly contributions.
A clearly articulated research agenda with demonstrated potential to make meaningful contributions to social work knowledge.
Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively in writing and orally in scholarly, teaching, and professional settings.
Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively in research, teaching, or professional settings.
Commitment to engaged teaching, active learning, and student advancement, as evidenced by experience as instructor of record, teaching assistant, guest lecturer, or similar experience facilitating learning.
Preferred Qualifications:
MSW from an accredited School of Social Work
A record of success in acquiring extramural research funding
Teaching experience with undergraduate and graduate students across course delivery modalities (in-person, online synchronous, online asynchronous).
Candidates who have experience promoting intellectual debates around a diversity of viewpoints and perspectives are especially encouraged to apply.
This is a 9-month tenure-system position beginning September 2027. Salary for this position is negotiable and commensurate with qualifications and experiences. Michigan State University offers an excellent selection of benefits; please see www.hr.msu.edu for more information.
Required Application Documents:
Complete applications must include:
a cover letter detailing the reasons for applying for the position and how your research and/or background fits with the position description;
a curriculum vitae;
a 1-page research statement;
a 1-page teaching statement;
Names and contact information for three professional (3) references. The unit solicits reference letters in PageUp using the names/contact info the applicants provide. Note: applications cannot be reviewed until all three reference letters have been received.
Special Instructions
Applications must be submitted to the MSU Applicant Page at https://careers.msu.edu. Enter 1167599 in the search bar. We will begin reviewing applications Fall 2026 and will continue until position is filled. For questions, please contact Dr. Pilar Horner, phorner@msu.edu.

jobs.title: AS-28-04 Open ranks faculty positions in Political Science/International Affairs
jobs.description:
Job Details
School of Arts and Sciences
Department: Political Science and International Studies
Campus: Byblos
Expected Start Date: Fall 2027
Deadline for Applying: January 31, 2027
Position Summary
The Department of Political Science and International Studies (POLIS) at the School of Arts and Sciences, Lebanese American University, invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant/Associate in Political Science/International Relations.
The department seeks a highly qualified and motivated candidate who is committed to excellence in innovative teaching, impactful research, and dedicated academic advising. The ideal candidate will also actively contribute to institutional development and community engagement.
Responsibilities
Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in International Affairs and related areas on the Beirut and Byblos campuses.
Develop and deliver courses using innovative, evidence-based, and experiential approaches to teaching and learning.
Supervise senior study projects, MA theses, and other student research in international affairs and related fields.
Advise, mentor, and support undergraduate and graduate students in their academic and professional development.
Establish and maintain an active program of research and scholarly publication in international affairs and related areas.
Seek external research funding and develop collaborative research projects with colleagues within and beyond the University.
Contribute to curriculum development, program enhancement, assessment, and accreditation-related activities.
Contribute to the development of academic and professional partnerships with relevant local, regional, and international organizations.
Engage in service to the department, School, University, and the academic and professional communities.
Contribute to community engagement and initiatives related to conflict prevention, resolution, peacebuilding, diplomacy, negotiation, and mediation.
Participate in departmental and university committees and other academic activities as appropriate.
Perform additional academic and administrative responsibilities as assigned by the Department in response to departmental needs and priorities.
Qualifications
Minimum Qualifications
A PhD in Political Science/International Relations from a well-recognized university
Specialization in American, African, or Asian studies or a focus on International Organizations and diplomatic affairs.
Evidence of research and publication record
Evidence of teaching experience in research methods courses
Preferred Qualifications
Evidence of success in securing external funding for research
Specialization in quantitative research methods
The Department
The Department of Political and International Studies (POLIS) is dedicated to fostering the development of global leaders and citizens, advancing research to serve human progress, and upholding the values of human dignity, equity, good governance, and peace. Committed to interactive learning, interdisciplinary research, and collaborative partnerships, the department empowers students to engage with the world’s most pressing challenges while serving the broader community. It offers distinctive international cultural and educational experiences, with a strong focus on Middle East and North African studies through its BA in Political Science and International Affairs, MA in International Affairs, and Minors in Conflict Analysis and Resolution, Political Science and international affairs, and Legal Studies.
Courses are delivered in an interactive setting while being facilitated by distinguished faculty, holding PhDs from renowned American, Canadian, and European universities. Their expertise spans key areas such as Middle East and North African studies, security studies, Islamic studies, legal studies, international relations, conflict resolution, and governance. Through a dynamic blend of lectures, discussions, case studies, and experiential learning, students are encouraged to think critically and apply theoretical knowledge to real-world challenges. The department’s mission is to advance knowledge and equip students with the skills and insights necessary to lead with integrity and to serve both their communities and the global society.
The University
The Lebanese American University is an Equal Opportunity Employer operating in Lebanon under a charter from the Regents of the State University of New York. Information about the University can be found at http://www.lau.edu.lb.
Application Requirements
Prospective candidates should apply electronically by sending a letter of interest including a statement of teaching, research interests, as well as professional and creative projects, and an updated CV by email to: soas.careers@lau.edu.lb. The CV should include the names, e-mails and phone numbers of three references. The university reserves the right to contact additional references with notice given to the candidates at an appropriate time in the process.
Candidates must refer to position no. AS-28-04 in the subject line of the email.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Position Function:
The Department of Physical Therapy at Mississippi State University
Meridian invites applications for a full-time, 12-month,
tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant, Associate,
or Full Professor. Rank and salary will be commensurate with
qualifications and experience.
As a founding faculty member in the developing hybrid Doctor of
Physical Therapy (DPT) program, the successful candidate will
contribute to curriculum delivery, development, assessment, and
continuous improvement while supporting the program's mission,
vision, strategic priorities, and accreditation requirements. The
department is particularly seeking candidates with demonstrated
clinical and academic expertise in one or more of the following
areas: Cardiopulmonary Physical Therapy, Acute Care Physical
Therapy, Neurologic and Neuromuscular Rehabilitation, Pediatric
Physical Therapy. Candidates with board certification, advanced
clinical specialization, residency/fellowship training, or a strong
record of teaching and scholarship in these areas are especially
encouraged to apply.
The successful candidate will participate in teaching, student
mentoring, curriculum development, scholarship, service,
interprofessional education, and community engagement while helping
establish a contemporary, evidence-based DPT program that prepares
graduates for practice across broad healthcare settings. This
position aligns with the faculty expectations described in the
current MSU DPT faculty postings.
Salary Grade : UC
Please see Staff Compensation Structure or
Skilled Crafts and Service
Maintenance Compensation Schedule for salary ranges. For salary
grade UC, these positions are "Unclassified" and salary ranges are
determined by the hiring department.
Area of Specialization:
Physical Therapy
Essential Duties and Responsibilities:
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Teaching and Curriculum Development
• Teach didactic, laboratory, hybrid, and/or online courses within
the DPT curriculum.
• Develop instructional materials and learning activities that
promote clinical reasoning, evidence-based practice, professional
behaviors, and patient-centered care.
• Integrate contemporary frameworks, including the biopsychosocial
model, interprofessional practice, and the International
Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF),
throughout instruction.
• Participate in curriculum planning, assessment, and program
evaluation activities.
• Contribute expertise to the development of specialty coursework
and clinical integration experiences in cardiopulmonary, acute
care, neuromuscular, and/or pediatric practice.
• Assess student learning and provide timely formative and
summative feedback.
Scholarship
• Establish and maintain a scholarly agenda consistent with
university and accreditation expectations.
• Engage in research, scholarly dissemination, grant development,
quality improvement initiatives, or other scholarly
activities.
• Mentor students in scholarly projects and evidence-based practice
initiatives.
• Student Advising and Mentoring
• Serve as an academic advisor and mentor for DPT students.
• Support student professional development, leadership, and
lifelong learning.
• Foster a collaborative and student-centered learning
environment.
Service and Community Engagement
• Participate in departmental, college, and university
committees.
• Engage with professional organizations and community
partners.
• Assist with student recruitment, admissions activities, and
program outreach.
• Contribute to the development of healthcare partnerships and
clinical education relationships throughout Mississippi and the
surrounding region.
Minimum Qualifications:
Education
• Physical therapy degree from a CAPTE-accredited program.
• Doctoral preparation is required.
Licensure
• Current physical therapist license in Mississippi or eligibility
for Mississippi licensure within six months of employment.
Experience
• Demonstrated expertise in cardiopulmonary, acute care,
neuromuscular, pediatric physical therapy, or a combination of
these areas.
• Evidence of effective teaching, clinical instruction, student
mentorship, or professional education involvement.
Preferred Qualifications:
• Earned terminal academic doctorate (PhD, EdD, DSc, DrPH, or
related field).
• ABPTS board certification in Cardiovascular & Pulmonary,
Neurologic, Pediatric, Geriatric, or related specialty areas.
• Residency and/or fellowship training.
• Experience teaching in a DPT or other health professions
program.
• Experience with hybrid, online, and innovative instructional
methods.
• Active scholarly agenda with publications, presentations, or
funded projects.
• Interprofessional education and collaborative practice
experience.
• Experience developing simulation, acute care, cardiopulmonary,
pediatric, or neurologic laboratory activities.
• Preference given to candidates who reside within, or are willing
to relocate to, a reasonable commuting distance from Meridian,
MS.
Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:
• Strong commitment to excellence in teaching, scholarship, and
service.
• Knowledge of contemporary physical therapist education and CAPTE
accreditation standards.
• Ability to teach and mentor broad student populations.
• Effective interpersonal, communication, and collaboration
skills.
• Commitment to evidence-based practice and lifelong
learning.
• Ability to work collaboratively in a developing and innovative
DPT program.
Working Conditions and Physical Effort
Work is performed primarily in academic, laboratory, clinical, and
office environments associated with a health sciences educational
program. Faculty members may be required to travel periodically for
professional development, clinical partnership development, student
activities, or scholarly engagement.

Albany is a Carnegie-classified Research 1 institution driven
by academic excellence, pioneering research and scientific
discovery, and service to community. UAlbany's world-class faculty experts and approximately 17,500 students are
creating new knowledge in fields such as artificial intelligence,

Located in Albany, New York, New York State's capital, the

Adirondacks.

commence Fall 2027.

scholars with active and productive research agendas who display
potential to publish in leading accounting journals.
The position is targeted toward candidates with research and
teaching interests in one or more of the following areas:
accounting information systems, financial accounting, corporate
governance, and forensic accounting. Candidates should be willing
to teach courses at both the undergraduate and graduate
levels.
Key responsibilities of this position include:
Conducting innovative research and publishing in high-quality
peer-reviewed journals
Providing rigorous instruction in undergraduate and graduate
courses
Presenting scholarly research at academic conferences and
meetings
Contributing service to the department, the Massry School of
Business, the university, the local community, and the accounting
profession
All candidates must be sensitive to the needs of and possess an
interest in working in an academic community that is diverse with
regard to gender, race, ethnicity, religion, nationality, sexual
orientation or identity, disability status, and protected veteran
status.
The Massry School of Business at the University at Albany is a
dynamic, research-driven institution within a flagship public
research university. We are AACSB-accredited in both business
administration and accounting-a distinction held by fewer than 2%
of business schools worldwide. Our faculty are active scholars who
benefit from a collegial environment that values rigorous research,
interdisciplinary collaboration, and meaningful engagement with
industry and policy. The current accounting faculty have published
in journals that include The Accounting Review; Contemporary
Accounting Research; Auditing: A Journal of Practice & Theory;
Accounting, Organizations and Society; and Issues in Accounting
Education. Accounting researchers have access to Compustat and CRSP
through WRDS. The department supports faculty research by
purchasing other datasets as needed, and funding travel to
conferences. The Massry School houses cutting-edge research centers
including the Center for Institutional Investment Management
(CIIM), the Center for Advancement & Understanding of Social
Enterprises (CAUSE), and FACETS, a hub for analytics and systems
security research funded by agencies such as NSF, IARPA, and NIST.
These centers can provide faculty with valuable infrastructure and
access to industry and government partnerships.
Our 96,000 sq ft. state-of-the-art facilities include
technologically advanced classrooms and labs, a Bloomberg-equipped
trading room, and flexible collaborative spaces designed to foster
innovation and applied learning. With a strong commitment to
experiential education, the Massry School of Business actively
bridges research with practice, creating unique opportunities for
both scholarly impact and student mentorship. We are especially
proud of our inclusive and supportive academic culture, where
junior faculty are mentored, encouraged to pursue ambitious
research agendas, and supported in building lasting academic
careers. Located in New York's capital, the University at Albany
offers access to a diverse professional ecosystem, robust funding
opportunities, and a high quality of life.
Primary Responsibilities:
Research and professional scholarly activity (e.g., data
collection, data analysis, article writing, presentations at
professional meetings).
Material preparation, class development, and instruction at
undergraduate and graduate levels.
Service to department, school, and university
Functional and Supervisory Relationships:
Reports to Accounting & Law Department Chair; Dean of the
School of Business

Preferred candidates will have earned a Ph.D. and/or worked at

Licensed CPA

jobs.title: Assistant / Associate Professor of Astronomy
jobs.description:
Job Details
Position Description
Eastern University seeks a full-time, tenure-track astronomy
professor who will also serve as Director of the Bradstreet
Observatory and Julia Fowler Planetarium. This unique role combines
undergraduate teaching, active research, facility administration,
public outreach, and the integration of the Christian faith into
higher education.
Position Responsibilities
Teaching: Instruct introductory astronomy courses and
labs (e.g., The Solar System, Exploration of the Universe) and an
Honors Cosmology course. Must also be willing to teach math,
physics, or computer science based on departmental needs.
Facility Leadership: Direct academic and public
programming for the Observatory and Planetarium. Coordinate field
trips, public outreach, and astrophotography.
Administration: Supervise the Observatory/Planetarium
Administrator and the Researcher/Coordinator.
Undergraduate Research: Maintain an active research
program in astronomy/astrophysics that provides hands-on mentorship
and research opportunities for undergraduate students.
Christian Mission: Integrate a Christian worldview into
teaching, mentoring, and scholarship, adhering to the University's
Doctrinal Statement.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications
Ph.D. in Astronomy, Astrophysics, or a closely related
field.
Demonstrated effectiveness in teaching undergraduate students
(including non-science majors).
An active research program with the potential to involve
undergraduates.
Commitment to Eastern University’s Christian values and the
ability to integrate faith into teaching.
Willingness/ability to teach interdisciplinary courses (math,
physics, CS) as needed.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience in observational astronomy, astrophotography, or
astronomical instrumentation.
Background in Observatory administration or Planetarium
programming/education.
Experience with public outreach, astronomical data analysis,
and computational methods.
Application Materials Required
Curriculum Vitae (CV) and Cover Letter.
Statement of Teaching Philosophy.
Research Statement (must include plans for undergraduate
participation).
Statement describing the integration of Christian faith and
academic discipline.
Names and contact information for professional references.

jobs.title: Faculty Support Coordinator for School of Education
jobs.description:
Job Details
The Faculty Support Coordinator provides administrative support to
the Online Dean, Online Chairs, and online faculty members in
matters related to online education. This position communicates to
online faculty through weekly announcements, assists in course
assignments, and coordinates online adjunct faculty hires. This
position is located on campus in Lynchburg, VA.
Essential Functions and Responsibilities
1. Receives, manages, and enforces imperatives of the Online Dean
and Vice Provost.
2. Receives and reviews recommended online faculty teaching
assignments from Online Chairs and submits course assignments to
the Online Dean.
3. Supports online faculty by responding to all questions related
to online policies and procedures, technical issues, compensation,
teaching load, future scheduling of courses W-9, etc.
4. Collects and reviews all assessment and course evaluations from
Online Chairs and reports all online faculty assessment and course
evaluations to the Online Dean.
5. Oversees the faculty application and hiring process.
6. Works with Online Chairs in order to maintain and update faculty
communications.
7. Other duties as assigned.
Qualifications, Credentials, and Competencies
A bachelor's degree or 3-5 years' administrative experience,
proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and Canvas, and ability to
learn Sharepoint required. A master's degree, institutional
knowledge of Liberty, and experience using Sharepoint preferred.
Effective communication both verbally and in writing. Ability to
intuitively reason, analyze information and events, and apply
judgment in order to solve problems of both a routine and complex
nature. Excellent computer and organizational skills. Regularly
lift 10 or fewer pounds.

Full time
Location
Onsite

Compensation is determined based on factors such as qualifications,
experience, education, skills, and certifications, along with
University needs and external market conditions. Market benchmarks
may be used, as appropriate, in combination with internal equity to
ensure pay is fair and aligned with the broader compensation
structure.
The position may also be eligible for comprehensive
benefits , including health insurance, retirement plans, and
tuition assistance.

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor, History of Artificial Intelligence
jobs.description:
Job Details
The Department of History in the School of Humanities and Arts at
Rice University in Houston, Texas, seeks applicants for a
tenure-track assistant or associate professor in the history of
artificial intelligence, broadly conceived. A PhD or equivalent
degree in History or a closely related field is required by the
time of appointment. The area of geographical specialization is
open. The appointment will begin on July 1, 2027. We seek
applicants from any sub-field of history and welcome all historical
methodologies and approaches, such as social, cultural,
intellectual, political, economic, business histories, the history
of war, and the history of science, amongst others. The successful
candidate will be expected to teach and advise students at both the
graduate and undergraduate levels. Rice University has a
semester-based teaching schedule with a 2-2 teaching load. The
University expects faculty members to maintain an active program of
scholarly research and publication and to contribute service to the
Department, University, and profession.
This position will complement the Department of History’s strengths
and course offerings at the graduate and undergraduate levels. The
successful candidate will join a growing cluster of scholars of AI
across the university, reflecting Rice’s broad strategic investment
in becoming a global leader in Responsible AI. In particular, the
successful candidate will have opportunities for close intellectual
collaboration and shared programming with a concurrent hire in the
Department of Anthropology focused on the Social and Cultural
Dimensions of AI. The candidate will also build bridges between
History and interdisciplinary initiatives at Rice, including the
Ken Kennedy Institute, Data Sciences, the Medical Humanities
Program, the Science and Technology Studies Program, Environmental
Studies, and the Baker Institute for Public Policy.
Applicants will be evaluated based on the following criteria:
demonstrated excellence in historical research; clear evidence of
teaching effectiveness at the university level; and ability to
mentor and teach a diverse student body.
Review of applications will begin on November 15, 2026, and will
continue until the position is filled. Application materials must
be submitted online via Interfolio at
https://apply.interfolio.com/193599 and must include:
A letter of application summarizing research and teaching
qualifications
A current curriculum vitae
A research statement
Evidence of teaching effectiveness (such as course evaluations,
syllabi, or a teaching statement)
An article-length writing sample
Contact information for three professional references
For further information or questions, contact Dr. Caleb McDaniel , Department Chair.
General information about the Department of History can be found at
https://history.rice.edu .
Rice University is a private, comprehensive research university
located in the heart of Houston’s dynamic museum district and
adjacent to the Texas Medical Center. Rice University offers
undergraduate and graduate degrees across eight schools and has a
student body of over 4,800 undergraduates and a nearly equal number
of graduate students. The fourth largest and most diverse city in
the United States, Houston provides an opportunity for scholars to
collaborate with area universities, museums, and civic
organizations, and to engage with the broader metropolitan
community.
Rice University is an Equal Opportunity Employer with
commitment to diversity at all levels, and considers for employment
qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, age,
sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national or ethnic
origin, genetic information, disability or protected veteran
status.

jobs.title: Tenured and Tenure-Track Faculty in Environmental Health
jobs.description:
Job Details
Tenured and Tenure-Track Faculty in Environmental
Health
Rice University invites applications for multiple tenured and
tenure-track positions at the senior and junior levels in
Environmental Health, with preferred focus areas in environmental
and occupational epidemiology, environmental exposures and
sustainability, environmental risk assessment, toxicology,
infectious diseases, global environmental health, and climate
impacts on health, as well as the intersection of these areas with
environmental justice. The anticipated start date is July 1, 2027.
The ideal candidate(s) would bring an interdisciplinary approach,
leveraging quantitative training in biostatistics, epidemiological
modeling, spatial analytics (GIS), or AI/data science, with
experience analyzing clinical (e.g., electronic medical records),
registry (e.g., Texas Cancer Registry), or administrative (e.g.,
American Community Survey) health data.
Primary academic appointment will be in the Department of
Kinesiology, ranked #1 nationally by the popular Niche™ rankings
and home to Rice’s Public Health Sciences and Sports Medicine and
Exercise Physiology undergraduate degrees. These positions are part
of an initiative to support interdisciplinary environmental health
scholarship, including a new Climate + Health Excellence Center (
FORECAST ) funded by the Burroughs Wellcome
Fund. They will come with robust joint appointments in Departments
of BioSciences, Chemistry, and Earth, Environmental and Planetary
Sciences as most appropriate.
The successful candidate(s) will be expected to establish a
vibrant, externally funded research program, collaborate across
disciplines, and teach at the undergraduate and graduate levels. We
especially encourage applications from scientists addressing
climate impacts on human health and infectious disease, and
contributing to broad themes of sustainability or One Health
principles. Potential to connect to exercise science, the
department’s other major intellectual theme, will also be explored,
such as through interests in impacts of extreme heat, air quality,
and toxicants on human physiology and performance.
Candidates must have a PhD, DrPH, or equivalent degree in public
health science or a relevant field of natural science or
engineering and have completed the requirements for the degree by
July 1, 2027.
To apply, please submit the following materials online at https://apply.interfolio.com/193813
: (1) cover letter; (2) curriculum vitae; (3) research statement (3
pages max); (4) statement of teaching philosophy (3 pages max); and
(5) contact information for three references. The research
statement and statement of teaching philosophy may also include
plans for building a diverse and inclusive research group and
fostering equitable and inclusive classrooms. Applications that are
received by November 16, 2026, will receive full
consideration, but we will continue reviewing applications until
positions are filled. For additional information, please visit our
department website or contact the search
chairs, Dr. Cassandra Diep ( csdiep@rice.edu ) and Dr. Scott P.
Egan ( scott.p.egan@rice.edu)
.
Rice University is located in Houston, Texas, USA, and is a
private, coeducational, nonsectarian university that aspires to
path-breaking research, unsurpassed teaching, and contributions to
the betterment of our world. Rice fulfills this mission by
cultivating a diverse community of learning and discovery that
produces leaders across the spectrum of human endeavor. In our
candidate pools, we seek to attract greater representation
of women, scholars of color, people with disabilities, veterans,
and others who have historically been underrepresented in academia;
accelerate progress in building a faculty and staff varied in
background and thought; and maintain an environment that fosters
interaction and understanding within our community.
Rice University is an Equal Opportunity Employer with
commitment to diversity at all levels, and considers for employment
qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, age,
sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national or ethnic
origin, genetic information, disability or protected veteran
status.

jobs.description:
About Binghamton University:
Binghamton University is a premier public R1 research institution
in the State University of New York (SUNY) system that unites more
than 130 broadly interdisciplinary educational programs with some
of the most vibrant research in the nation. Our unique character -
shaped by our mission, outstanding academics, facilities, and
community life - promotes extraordinary student success, research,
and service; Binghamton University is where our students, faculty
and staff thrive.
Working at Binghamton University is more than about having a great
job - it is about having the opportunity to flourish in an
exciting, engaging environment. Our faculty and staff appreciate
Binghamton's collegial and inclusive culture and its commitment to
excellence, education, innovation, and civic engagement. Our
diverse campus community contributes to our success.
Binghamton merges rigorous academics, distinguished faculty who
value cutting-edge, and community-engaged research, teaching and
service, exceptional staff, and ultramodern facilities to engage
and challenge its 18,000+ students. Our high-achieving student body
represents diverse experiences from first-generation college-goers
to international students. Beyond their talent, these classmates
share a desire to shape the future through technology, insight,
intellectual exploration, and community service.
Job Description:
ABOUT THE DEPARTMENT:
The Art History Department has developed a distinctive profile
through a commitment to new theoretical perspectives and
cross-disciplinary approaches to the history of art, the built
environment, and the broader field of visual culture. We are
committed to the mutual enrichment of teaching and research, as
reflected in our distinctive undergraduate curriculum and our
prominence as an innovative and markedly international center for
graduate education.
ABOUT THE POSITION:
The Art History Department at Binghamton University invites
applications for a tenure-track position of Assistant Professor -
Asian Art, post-900 CE, beginning Fall 2027. A PhD in art history
or a related field by the start date of the appointment is
required. A promising record of research and experience teaching at
the undergraduate and graduate level is preferred.
This position seeks to build on and reinvigorate the department's
historical strength in the study of the art and culture of Asia,
including Islamic art and the art and architecture of East Asia.
Field and period of specialization post-900 CE are open. We
especially welcome applications from those sharing our commitment
to new theoretical perspectives and cross-disciplinary approaches
to the discipline. The successful candidate will develop a
curriculum that expands existing geographical and historical areas
of concentration in the department, work collaboratively with
colleagues in Art History as well as faculty in other departments
and programs, and participate actively in the intellectual life of
the university. The teaching and scholarship interests of the ideal
candidate will include transregional and interdisciplinary
approaches.
Binghamton University fosters a variety of interdisciplinary
programs, including the Center for Middle East and North African
Studies and the Asian and Asian American Studies Department, and
our new colleague will be encouraged to contribute to one or more
of these. Resources on campus to support professional and scholarly
development include the School of the Arts, which fosters
collaboration across its five departments (including Art History)
and the Binghamton University Art Museum.
Responsibilities include teaching courses at all undergraduate and
graduate levels. This position entails a 2-2 course load, with
typically one undergraduate lecture and one joint undergraduate /
graduate seminar offered per semester.
Requirements:
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:
PhD in art history or a related field by August 16, 2027
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
Teaching experience at the undergraduate or graduate level
Published research in a peer-reviewed publication

jobs.title: Tenure-Track Associate Professor/Assistant Professor
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for appointment as Tenure-Track
Associate Professor/Assistant Professor in the Department of
Microbiology, School of Clinical Medicine (Ref.: 537419), to
commence as soon as possible, on a three-year fixed-term contract,
with the possibility of renewal and with consideration for tenure
before the expiry of a second three-year fixed-term contract,
subject to satisfactory performance.
Applicants should possess a Ph.D. degree in Microbiology, Virology,
or related disciplines and demonstrate a strong track record in
virological research, in particular on the following areas: (1)
understanding virus-virus or virus-host interaction with structural
biology; (2) artificial intelligence or computational-guided
virological research; (3) immunity and immunopathology to viruses;
(4) multiple-omics investigations of virus-induced host response.
Those with less experience may be considered for appointment as
Assistant Professor.
The appointee is expected to manage on-going research projects on
emerging infectious diseases, consistently publish original
research articles in high-impact journals and obtain external
competitive grants. He/She will also participate in teaching and
contribute to the enhancement of medical and healthcare-related
courses.
Applicants who have responded to the previous advertisement (Ref.:
534742) need not re-apply.
A highly competitive salary commensurate with qualifications and
experience will be offered, in addition to annual leave and medical
benefits. At current rates, salaries tax does not exceed 15% of
gross income. The appointment will attract a contract-end gratuity
and University contribution to a retirement benefits scheme,
totalling up to 15% of basic salary. Housing benefits will also be
provided as applicable.
The University only accepts online application for the above post.
Applicants should apply online and upload an up-to-date C.V., and
contact information of 2 referees should be provided in the
application form. Review of applications will start as soon as
possible and continue until March 20, 2027, or until the
post is filled, whichever is earlier.

jobs.title: Tenure-Track Professor/Associate Professor/Assistant Professor in Chinese Language Education
jobs.description:
The University
Founded in 1911, the University of Hong Kong has attained its
pre-eminence as a research-led comprehensive university through
upholding the highest international standards of excellence in its
research pursuits, scholarship, teaching and learning, and service
to the community. The University is consistently ranked amongst the
world’s top universities: 11th in QS World University Rankings
2026, 1st in the QS Asia University Rankings 2026, 33rd in the
Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2026. In recent
years, the University was ranked multiple times as the most
international University in the world.
Home to ten disciplinary Faculties (Architecture, Arts, Business
and Economics, Dentistry, Education, Engineering, Law, Medicine,
Science, and Social Sciences), the University is committed to
fostering interdisciplinary exchange with an outlook for
transformative breakthroughs, innovations and global impact. There
are 42,330 undergraduate and postgraduate students from 97
countries, and more than 9,600 academic, academic-related and
administrative staff. The University has embarked on a number of
ambitious infrastructure and facilities projects required for
future expansion in the Northern Metropolis, Beijing, Shanghai and
Europe.
The Faculty of Education
HKU has been involved in teacher education since 1917, and the
Faculty of Education was established in 1984. The Faculty of
Education is forward-looking and world leading, ranking 5th
globally in Education (QS 2026). It has assumed an important role
in educational research and professional training as a major
provider of teacher education programmes and has contributed
significantly to education policy and development in Hong Kong with
its strong expertise in policy analysis and curriculum development.
The Faculty is also the first in Hong Kong to offer degree
programmes that train speech therapists and audiologists for the
local community. More information
about the Faculty can be found at https://web.edu.hku.hk/ .
The Position
We now invite applications for appointment as Tenure-Track
Professor/Associate Professor/Assistant Professor in Chinese
Language Education in the Faculty of Education.
Duties and Responsibilities
The appointee will teach Chinese Language pedagogy and assessment
courses offered in undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
He/She will also supervise research postgraduate students,
contribute actively to research and knowledge exchange, and assume
service/administrative responsibilities as appropriate. Candidate
appointed at the senior level will also lead collaborative and
interdisciplinary initiatives in research and knowledge exchange,
mentor and nurture the next generation of scholars and researchers,
and assume high-level service/administrative
responsibilities.
Essential Requirements
Applicants should possess (i) a Ph.D. degree in the broad area of
Chinese Studies, with specialization in Chinese Language and
Literature, Chinese Language Studies, Chinese Linguistics, Chinese
Language Education including assessment and pedagogy, or associated
areas such as Psycholinguistics or Bilingual Education; (ii) solid
teaching and research experience in Chinese Language Education;
(iii) a proven track record in, or strong potential for, sustained
high-quality research, scholarly publications and competitive
external funding; and (iv) ability or potential to demonstrate
academic leadership and strong commitment to the highest standard
of excellence. Experience related to primary school education would
be an advantage.
What We Offer
The appointment will be made on fixed-term full-time contract for 3
years initially, to commence on August 1, 2027 or as soon as
possible thereafter, with the possibility of renewal and
consideration for tenure before the expiry of the second three-year
fixed-term contract. Exceptionally outstanding candidates at
Professor/Associate Professor level may be considered for
appointment on tenure terms subject to approval.
A highly competitive salary commensurate with qualifications and
experience will be offered, together with contract-end gratuity and
University contribution to a retirement benefits scheme, totaling
up to 15% of basic salary. Other benefits include annual leave and
professional leave, medical benefits, and free access to on-campus
gyms and libraries. Housing benefits will be provided as
applicable.
How to Apply
The University only accepts online application for the above post.
Applicants should apply online at the University’s careers site (
https://jobs.hku.hk ) and upload
a cover letter indicating the earliest availability date, an
up-to-date C.V. with the contact information of three referees, one
sample of a representative research output, a research plan of not
more than 2 pages, and a teaching statement of not more than 2
pages. Review of applications will start on October 18, 2026
and continue until October 31, 2026, or until the post is
filled, whichever is earlier.
The University is an equal opportunities employer
and
is committed to equality, ethics, inclusivity, diversity and
transparency

Applications close: Oct 31, 2026 (HK Time)

Clinical Professor in Breast Surgery in the Department of Surgery,

jobs.title: Fractional Clinical Associate Professor/Clinical Assistant Professor in Implant Dentistry
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for appointment as Non-Tenure Track
Fractional Clinical Associate Professor/Clinical
Assistant Professor in Implant Dentistry of the
Faculty of Dentistry (Ref.: 537415), to commence as soon as
possible, on a two- to four-year fixed-term (50% fractional) basis,
with the possibility of renewal subject to satisfactory
performance.
The Faculty of Dentistry is the only dental school in Hong Kong,
China and the only one in China that uses English as the medium of
instruction. The high quality of the Faculty’s undergraduate and
postgraduate programmes, research excellence, knowledge exchange
(KE) and clinical/professional services have attained global
recognition, as evidenced by the Faculty’s global rankings among
the top three by the QS World University Rankings by Subject for
ten out of the past twelve years (2015-2026). The Faculty’s
strategic research themes include AI+ & Precision Dentistry,
Regenerative Dentistry, Global Oral Health, and Oral Ecosystem
& One Health. The Faculty also plays important roles in public
and professional education through its KE activities and Global
Education Hub for Oral Healthcare Professionals (GEHOHP),
translational research & innovation via its Global Hub for
Future Dentistry (GHFD) in collaboration with HKU
Techno-Entrepreneurship Core and Hong Kong Science & Technology
Parks Corporation, and enhancement of its global impacts through
proactive engagement, networking and partnership.
Applicants should demonstrate excellence in clinical care, research
and teaching in the field of Implant Dentistry on top of sound
knowledge and training in Periodontology. They are expected to work
collaboratively in a dynamic and diverse environment, develop a
competitive research portfolio, and contribute to the curricula
available at the undergraduate and postgraduate level. Ability to
partake undergraduate Periodontology teaching / education and
fluency in spoken and written English are essential.
For appointment as Clinical Associate Professor, applicants
should possess a Dental Bachelor's degree or equivalent, a clinical
specialist qualification or equivalent status in Implant Dentistry,
Prosthodontics or Periodontology, advanced training or clinical
experience in Implant Dentistry, and a Ph.D. degree or equivalent.
They should also have (i) proven ability for quality research, high
quality publications in international journals, and evidence of
local and regional recognition for scholarship and professional
expertise; (ii) demonstrated ability in undergraduate and
postgraduate education, clinical practice and research; (iii)
demonstrated clinical expertise; (iv) demonstrated participation in
Faculty and University affairs; and (v) demonstrated ability in KE
activities, and leadership in professional education programmes or
community engagement.
For appointment as Clinical Assistant Professor, applicants
should possess a Dental Bachelor’s degree or equivalent, a Master
of Dental Surgery degree or equivalent in Implant Dentistry,
Prosthodontics or Periodontology, and advanced training or clinical
experience in Implant Dentistry. They should also have (i) ability
in undergraduate and postgraduate clinical teaching and practice;
(ii) potential for and interest in research; (iii) proven ability
in clinical excellence; (iv) ability and willingness to participate
in Faculty affairs; and (v) active participation in KE
activities.
The appointee will engage in clinical and didactic teaching in
Implant Dentistry at both undergraduate and postgraduate levels,
supervise research projects, be expected to develop their own line
of research, and participate in the clinical and administrative
duties of the Faculty.
Information about the Faculty can be obtained at http://facdent.hku.hk/ . For general
enquiries, please contact Professor L.J. Jin, Dean of the Faculty
of Dentistry at ljjin@hku.hk .
For information about the post, please contact Professor W.K.
Leung, Chief, Division of Periodontology and Implant Dentistry, at
ewkleung@hku.hk .
A highly competitive salary commensurate with qualifications and
experience will be offered, in addition to annual leave and medical
benefits. At current rates, salaries tax does not exceed 15% of
gross income. The appointment will attract a contract-end gratuity
and University contribution to a retirement benefits scheme,
totalling up to 15% of basic salary. Housing benefits will also be
provided as applicable.
The successful candidate is required to obtain a valid registration
with the Dental Council of Hong Kong. (Note: Applicants who do not
hold a local dental license must fulfil the essential requirements
under the laws of a jurisdiction outside Hong Kong, China, to be
eligible for Limited Registration. For details, please refer to the
Dental Council of Hong Kong’s website at https://www.dchk.org.hk/en/registration/part_III.html
.)
The University only accepts online application for the above post.
Applicants should apply online at the University's careers site (
https://jobs.hku.hk ) and upload
a cover letter, an up-to-date C.V., a research statement and a

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of English (Creative Writing: Poetry)
jobs.description:
Job Details
Union College invites applications for the position of Assistant
Professor of English, beginning September 1, 2026. Review of
applications will begin on November 2, 2026 and continue until the
position is filled. Applications received by 11/2/2026 will receive
priority consideration.
Position description:
The Department of English at Union College invites applications for
a tenure-track position as Assistant Professor of English
specializing in Poetry. Candidates must have an M.F.A. or Ph.D. in
Creative Writing (Poetry) at the time of hire, experience in
teaching creative writing, and an established publication record,
such as a published book of poetry or the digital equivalent, or a
series of poems published in peer-reviewed journals.
Candidates will teach poetry workshops at all levels and literature
electives of their own design; contribute to the college's Complex
Questions general education curriculum; and develop a First-Year
Inquiry course in line with their own interests. Preference will be
given to candidates interested in organizing a departmental reading
series. The teaching load is two classes per 10-week trimester for
three trimesters per year (2-2-2).
We are especially interested in candidates who work in digital
poetics and/or digital studies more broadly, who incorporate
digital tools and platforms into their teaching and/or their poetry
publication, and who expand our digital course offerings, which may
include contributions that cross with Computer Science, or programs
in Digital Studies, Digital Media, and/or Science, Technology, and
Society. In particular, we seek candidates with demonstrated
interest and/or excellence in the creation, curation, and
maintenance of a peer-reviewed online journal, magazine, or other
digital resource for the publication and dissemination of
undergraduate creative writing. Finally, we encourage applications
from candidates who demonstrate through their teaching and service
a commitment to underrepresented perspectives, including those of
BIPOC and/or LGBTQIA+ writers. We welcome applications from
candidates whose teaching could support Union’s interdisciplinary programs in Africana Studies,
American Studies, Asian Studies, Climate Change Studies,
Environmental Studies, Film Studies, Gender, Sexuality &
Women’s Studies, Mental Health Care, Music Technology, Latin
American and Caribbean Studies, Law & Humanities, Religious
Studies, Russian & Eastern European Studies, and/or Public
Health.
About the English Department:
The newcomer to our faculty will enter a spirited collective of
academics, authors, and mentors. Within the Department of English
at Union College, we foster a cooperative and encouraging
environment dedicated to student achievement, offering a diverse
array of pedagogical perspectives that bridge conventional and
avant-garde explorations of letters and the craft of writing. We
teach a broad range of courses that include introductions to
various literary genres and those that confront the literary canon,
as well as intermediate- and upper-level courses that consider
traditional authors or time periods, in addition to thematic and/or
theoretical approaches that examine literature’s relationship to
global challenges and social justice. This curriculum includes
creative writing workshops in poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction,
screenwriting, and more. Our courses help support the
interdisciplinary programs listed above and others. In response to
growing student interest, the English department launched a
creative writing minor in Fall 2024, which continues to develop and
which this poetry position directly supports.
Application instructions:
Please submit all application materials as pdf files. Only
the materials listed below will be considered.
Application letter
Curriculum vitae
Writing sample (up to 15 pages)
Statement of teaching philosophy (1-2 pages), which includes
experiences, approaches, and classroom activities that increase
inclusivity and community for students of various backgrounds and
abilities.
Please send questions and other inquiries to Bunkong Tuon, Chair of
the Poetry Hiring Committee at tuonb@union.edu. Applicants
invited to the first round of interviews will receive a request for
the contact information for three professional references who can
speak to their abilities in creative work, teaching, and
departmental and institutional service.
Compensation
The annual salary range for this position is
$81,500-$83,500. Except for roles with a set rate of pay, the
wage/salary of the finalist selected for this role will be set
based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to
departmental budgets, qualifications, experience, education,
licenses, specialty, and training. The stated hiring rate/range
represents the College’s good faith and reasonable estimate of the
rate/range of possible compensation at the time of posting.
Location: Schenectady, NY
We offer exceptional benefits including:
Healthcare: Medical (PPO & HDHP), Dental, and Vision
Insurance (Flexible Spending and Dependent Care Accounts)
Free On-Campus Fitness Facility Access and Discounts for
On-Campus Wellness Programs
Pre and Post Tax participation in a 403(b) Retirement Plan
Salary Continuation Program in the event of Disability
Tuition Exchange
Background Checks: In accordance with our
background check policy , finalists for hire will undergo a
background check that includes education, employment, and criminal
convictions.
E-Verify Participation: Union College participates in
E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9
information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the
United States. Learn more about E-Verify and your
Right to Work (Derecho a Trabajar) .

jobs.title: Assistant Professor, Visual and Performing Arts
jobs.description:
Job Details
Fairfield University is a co-educational, comprehensive Jesuit
university with a 200-acre campus located along the scenic
shoreline community of Fairfield, CT. The University is comprised
of approximately 3,500 undergraduate and 1,200 graduate students
pursuing degrees within 5 schools: The College of Arts and
Sciences, The Charles F. Dolan School of Business, The School of
Engineering, The Marion Peckham Egan School of Nursing and Health
Studies, and School of Education and Human Development. As an
expression of our Jesuit, Catholic mission and identity, Fairfield
embraces a liberal humanistic approach to education, encouraging
critical thinking, cultivating free and open inquiry, and fostering
ethical and religious values.
Job Description:
The Department of Visual and Performing Arts at Fairfield
University seeks a full-time tenure-track faculty position in Film,
Television, and Media Arts Production at the rank of Assistant
Professor. We are looking for a practicing filmmaker, with a
background in directing, writing and/ or producing work in
narrative fiction, evidenced by a track record of public exhibition
(such as film festivals).
The successful applicant will teach hands-on, introductory courses
in filmmaking, short film screenwriting and editing, as well as
advanced courses in subjects that may include producing, feature
film/ television screenwriting, directing. The ability to engage
with Fairfield’s mission of fostering social justice and
responsibility is preferred. The teaching load is three
undergraduate courses each semester, with an active
research/creative agenda and university service required for
promotion and tenure. The appointment, pending final budget
approval, will have a starting date of September 1, 2027.
Requirements:
Applicants are expected to have completed a terminal degree (MFA,
preferred; PhD acceptable with relevant professional experience).
Applicants must have demonstrated excellence in undergraduate
teaching, with experience in screenwriting instruction emphasized,
and evidence of potential for academic career success.
Additional Information:
The Film, Television, and Media Arts (FTMA) program offers a major
and a minor and is one of six programs in the Department of Visual
and Performing Arts. FTMA students build skills in both critical
analysis and hands-on production while acquiring a solid foundation
in creating and reflecting on multimedia storytelling forms.
Benefiting from the personal attention of a faculty comprised of
scholars, artists, and industry professionals, students learn
practices and skills at the cutting edge of the field and are
mentored to understand the expressive power of media while
discovering their own creative voice.
All FTMA courses are based in Fairfield’s newly renovated Media
Center, featuring two studios, multiple post-production suites,
screening facilities, editing labs and a staffed equipment cage,
with industry-standard cinema gear ranging from RED cameras to Arri
LED lighting. Just a short train ride away from midtown Manhattan,
FTMA has strong links to the media industry in New York City, with
many faculty and alumni based there. After graduation, most FTMA
students acquire solid, entry-level jobs in a variety of media
fields or continue to develop their interest through graduate
studies.
Application Instructions:

15, 2026.

a letter of application that outlines your qualifications for
the position, includes a link to a portfolio containing examples of

a curriculum vitae
statement of teaching philosophy and experience
After passing through an initial screening process, applicants will
receive a request for graduate transcript, and recommendation
letters. Please email any additional documents and questions to
VPAsearch@fairfield.edu .

jobs.title: Assistant Teaching Professor, Modern Languages and Literatures
jobs.description:
Job Details
Fairfield University is a co-educational, comprehensive Jesuit
university with a 200-acre campus located along the scenic
shoreline community of Fairfield, CT. The University is comprised
of approximately 3,500 undergraduate and 1,200 graduate students
pursuing degrees within 5 schools: The College of Arts and
Sciences, The Charles F. Dolan School of Business, The School of
Engineering, The Marion Peckham Egan School of Nursing and Health
Studies, and School of Education and Human Development. As an
expression of our Jesuit, Catholic mission and identity, Fairfield
embraces a liberal humanistic approach to education, encouraging
critical thinking, cultivating free and open inquiry, and fostering
ethical and religious values.
Job Description:
The Department of Modern Languages and Literatures at Fairfield
University seeks applications for a non-tenure track Assistant
Teaching Professor of Spanish, with an emphasis in Latin American
studies and culture, to begin in the fall of 2027, pending final
budget approval. Teaching responsibilities include four classes per
semester (with a maximum of three preparations). The successful
candidate will be responsible for teaching courses at all levels of
our Spanish undergraduate curriculum, including elementary and
intermediate-level courses.
Candidates should have a demonstrated record of excellence in
teaching at the university level. Previous experience having
coordinated Spanish language programs at the undergraduate level
will be greatly valued. We seek candidates who will contribute to
the University's core curriculum priorities of writing across the
curriculum, social justice, and interdisciplinarity. The successful
candidate should expect to participate in department, college and
university-wide service, and may contribute to other
interdisciplinary programs in the Meditz College of Arts and
Sciences.
Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States
by the time of appointment. Please note that Fairfield University
will not provide visa sponsorship for this position.
The Department of Modern Languages and Literatures consists of 15
full-time faculty members, teaching a dynamic curriculum and
engaged in exciting faculty research representing a range of
fields, such as peninsular and Latin American literature and
cinema, cultural studies, linguistics, translation, or Spanish for
specific purposes.
Fairfield University is a Jesuit Catholic university, consistently
ranked as a top comprehensive university in New England, located in
the scenic shoreline community of Fairfield, CT, one hour from New
York City along Long Island Sound. Our five Colleges and
Professional Schools enroll approximately 5,300 undergraduate and
1,400 graduate students. The salary and the benefits for the
position are highly competitive.
Qualifications: PhD in Spanish required by time of
appointment.
To apply, please submit a CV, a cover letter, a teaching philosophy
statement, three recent course teaching evaluations, and three
letters of reference by November 1, 2026.
Please direct questions to Dr. Sergio Adrada-Rafael, Search
Committee Chair, at sadradarafael@fairfield.edu . If uploading more
than five documents, please send additional documents and letters
of reference to modernlanguage@fairfield.edu .

jobs.description:
Job Details
Applications must be submitted no later than 11:59 p.m. CT on the
day before the listed closing date.
Weekly Work Hours
30

Faculty Range F01
Salary Minimum
$63,600.00 Annually
FLSA
United States of America (Exempt)
Work Location
All positions are considered on-site roles.
After six months of employment, some positions may be eligible
to apply for a hybrid work arrangement based on job
responsibilities, operational needs, supervisor approval, and
Dallas College policy.
Academic (Faculty) positions require an on-campus presence,
even when teaching online courses, in accordance with state
law.
Position Type
Faculty
All positions are considered on-site roles. After six months of
employment, employees may have the opportunity to apply for a
hybrid work schedule. Academic positions (Faculty) require
on-campus presence, even if the role involves teaching online
classes, in accordance with state law.
Position Summary
Teaches students effectively in assigned dual credit classes and
maintains office hours for student consultation. Classes are in
person at assigned high school campuses.
Faculty in Dallas College are expected to perform the duties
enumerated in the formal Job Description; to fulfill their
responsibilities in accordance with the policies and procedures
established by the Dallas College Board of Trustees and outlined in
the Dallas College Board Policy Manual; and to comply with both
state and federal policy.
Required Knowledge, Skills & Abilities
The Dallas College System seeks faculty who strive for
excellence, are committed to continuous student learning, and
demonstrate passion and skill in effective teaching and learning
facilitation.
Such faculty are competent in their discipline and innovative in
their approach to learning, and they are committed to personal
growth and the on-going assessment and evaluation of their
teaching.
They demonstrate a commitment to the mission and philosophy of
the community college and to working effectively with diverse
populations.
They are committed to effective communication with others and
fostering an atmosphere of collegiality.
Finally, they demonstrate and promote high ethical standards and
academic honesty.
Physical Requirements
Normal physical job functions performed within a standard office
environment. Reasonable accommodations may be made to individuals
with physical challenges to perform the essential duties and
responsibilities.
Minimum Qualifications
Master’s degree or higher in the teaching discipline or Master’s
degree or higher with a concentration in the teaching discipline (a
minimum of 18 graduate semester hours in the teaching
discipline).
One year of demonstrated teaching experience required.
Official transcript will be required.
Bilingual or multilingual preferred.​
*** Will be subject to a criminal background check. Some
positions may be subject to a fingerprint check. ***
Key Responsibilities
Teaching and Learning
Teach students in assigned classes in accordance with course
descriptions and/or learning outcomes, the course syllabus, and
institutional policies and procedures
Provide students with a syllabus that includes required
institutional policies, course objectives, materials, and methods
of evaluation
Provide a workload schedule showing teaching and office
hours
Certify student attendance in classes by the established
deadlines
Maintain accurate and complete course records
Submit final grades by the established deadlines
Communicate with and provide feedback to students in a timely
fashion
Develop course curriculum and instructional materials
(individually or collaboratively)
Use knowledge of diverse communities and skill sets to diversify
teaching methods and delivery of content in instruction
Provide effective instruction to facilitate student learning in
all classes taught
Evaluate and assess student learning on a regular basis in all
classes taught
Participate in assessment activities at course, department,
college, and district levels to assist students in achieving
designated course objectives or learning outcomes
Use appropriate technologies to enhance classroom or online
instruction and to achieve established course objectives or
learning outcomes
Regularly evaluate teaching methods and use data to continually
improve instructional strategies
Institutional Service
Support the mission and goals of the college and the strategic
priorities of the Board
Serve on departmental, college, and/or district committees
Attend scheduled discipline, department, division, and college
meetings
Participate in the review of curricula and selection of
instructional materials within the discipline or department
Participate in required program reviews and the achievement of
departmental goals
Comply with all required college-level and program-level
accreditation standards
Discuss program, career, or transfer options and other college
services with students to support informed academic decisions
Attend required assembly/convocation and commencement/graduation
ceremonies
Perform other duties mutually agreed upon in consultation with
supervisor
Professional Development
Maintain knowledge and competence in the appropriate academic
discipline or workforce field
Maintain any required professional certification or licensure in
the appropriate academic or technical discipline, where
appropriate
Remain current with technological and pedagogical advances that
promote continuous improvement of student learning
Participate in a variety of professional development
activities
Participate in one's own performance review and evaluation
The intent of this job description is to provide a
representative summary of the major duties and responsibilities
performed by incumbents of this job and shall not be construed as a
declaration of the total of the specific duties and
responsibilities of any particular position. Incumbents may be
directed to perform job-related tasks other than those specifically
presented in this description. Position requires regular and
predictable attendance.
About Us
Since 1965, Dallas College, formerly Dallas County Community
College District, has served more than three (3) million students.
Comprising seven campuses located around the Dallas/Fort Worth
area, we are one of the largest community college systems in the
state of Texas. We strive to be a leader in the community college
space, placing students at the center of everything we do.
Dallas College is committed to cultivating an environment of
opportunity and belonging for all students and employees. We
recognize that the Dallas College workforce, and the diverse talent
that stems from it, is directly linked to our success. We are part
of an equal opportunity system that provides education and
employment opportunities without discrimination on the basis of any
protected attribute, including race, color, religion, national
origin, sex, disability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity
or gender expression, veteran status, pregnancy or any other basis
protected under applicable law. In accordance with applicable law,
Dallas College will make reasonable accommodations for applicants
and employees’ religious practices and beliefs, as well as any
mental health or physical disability needs.
