jobs.description:
Position Information
Position Title
Chemistry - Open Rank Organic Chemistry Faculty
Classification Title
Faculty Full Time (.75-1.0 FTE)
Benefits Eligibility
Benefits Eligibility
Department
Chemistry
Job Description
Tenure-Track Chemistry Position
The Hope College Chemistry Department invites applications for a
tenure-track position to begin in Fall 2027. We anticipate filling
at the Assistant Professor level, but candidates at all ranks are
encouraged to apply. Applicants must be able to teach lecture and
laboratory courses in Organic Chemistry. A Ph.D. in chemistry or a
closely related field is required; postdoctoral experience is
strongly preferred. The development of a strong, externally-funded,
experimental research program involving undergraduates is expected.
Start-up funds will be provided. Applications from persons with
diverse backgrounds and cultures, including women and persons of
color, are especially welcomed. Please submit application materials
to Dr. Jeffrey B. Johnson, Search Committee Chair, via www.hope.edu/employment/faculty
. A review of all completed applications will begin September
21.
About the Department of Chemistry
The Department of
Chemistry has long been one of the nation’s premier
undergraduate chemistry programs and is a national leader in
undergraduate research. The department of 16 faculty graduates 40
majors per year with BA and BS degrees in chemistry, biochemistry
& molecular biology, and neuroscience (accredited by the ACS
and ASBMB ). The hallmark of our program is undergraduate education
through excellent classroom teaching with appropriate modern
pedagogies integrated with authentic faculty scholarship that
engages undergraduate student collaborators. Student-faculty
collaborative research involves approximately 100 students per
year, including 60 who perform research in the department each
summer. From 2015-2025, members of the department have obtained
external funding of $18.8M, and have published over 90 papers
incorporating over 250 undergraduate student coauthors. Hope
students regularly receive national accolades such as NSF - GRFP,
Goldwater Scholar, and Fulbright fellowships. Based on NSF data,
293 Hope graduates have received PhDs in chemistry since 1958,
placing Hope in the top 1% US liberal arts and undergraduate
institutions. The Department has a broad range of modern instrumentation
for research and teaching , as well as endowed funds for
instrument maintenance and repair, faculty and student summer
support, and a well-funded competitive internal grants
program.
About the College and Community
Hope College is a strong co-educational, undergraduate,
residential, Christian liberal arts college with over 3200
students. It is a member of the Great Lakes Colleges Association
and is broadly accredited in programs ranging from Chemistry and
Engineering to Theater and Dance. Hope’s beautiful and
well-maintained campus is adjacent to award-winning downtown
Holland, Michigan, located near Lake Michigan. Holland’s population
of 35,000 has growing Hispanic/Latinx, African American, and Asian
populations in a general metropolitan area of over 100,000. Holland
is located 30 minutes from Grand Rapids, less than 90 minutes from
South Bend and Lansing, and approximately 2.5 hours from Detroit,
Ann Arbor, and Chicago. Since its founding in 1866, Hope College
has been affiliated with the Reformed Church in America and is
known for its ecumenical Christian atmosphere. Hope is recognized
as a national leader in undergraduate research and scholarship and
for providing professional preparation and life-changing
experiences in a friendly and welcoming community. The college
places a high priority on sustaining a supportive environment that
recognizes the importance of a diverse faculty and staff in order
to best prepare its students for successful careers in our
multicultural nation and global community.
Additional information about Holland and Hope College can be found
at hope.edu/jobs .
Application Details
Application materials include a cover letter, curriculum vitae,
description of research plans, statement of teaching philosophy and
competencies, unofficial transcripts, and the contact information
of three references. Successful applicants will demonstrate a
commitment to all aspects of Hope’s
mission as a liberal arts college. We are grounded in
robust ecumenical Christian
aspirations and daily strive for
inclusive excellence . In addition to the above
materials, we ask all candidates to describe in a separate mission
response how they will engage and support the holistic mission of
the College, including how their commitment to the Christian faith,
the liberal arts, and inclusive excellence shapes their approaches
and identities as teachers, scholars, and mentors.
Is this a visiting faculty position?
No
Rank
Open
Qualifications
Candidates must have a Ph.D. in chemistry or a related field;
postdoctoral experience is strongly preferred. Applicants must be
able to teach lectures and labs in Organic Chemistry. The
development of a strong, externally-funded, experimental research
program involving undergraduates is expected.
Physical Demands
This position requires remaining in a sitting or standing position
for frequent periods of time; uses office machinery such as a
computers, printers, copy machines; Occasionally involves moving
items over 10 pounds; frequently will move between different
offices/workspaces/buildings; and requires effective communication
abilities. In the case of temporary or permanent condition(s) that
require(s) accommodation(s), reasonable accommodation(s) may be
requested.

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor or Assistant/Associate Professor of Professional Practice -
jobs.description:
Job Details
Application Deadline:
Open Until filled
Position Details:
This full-time faculty position is on-campus and in-person.
The Harris College of Nursing & Health Sciences invites
applications for one 12-month faculty position as a Tenure-Track
Assistant/Associate Professor OR Assistant/Associate Professor of
Professional Practice (non-tenure) for the developing entry-level
Doctor of Occupational Therapy (OTD) Program at Texas Christian
University (TCU).
Tenure-Track Faculty Qualifications: Successful applicants will
have strong written and interpersonal communication skills, the
ability to maintain an active research/scholarship agenda
(including extramural funding) and teaching proficiency within
their area of expertise supporting the developing entry-level
Doctor of Occupational Therapy (OTD) Program at Texas Christian
University (TCU).
Professional Practice Track Faculty Qualifications: Successful
applicants will have strong written and interpersonal communication
skills and teaching proficiency within their area of expertise in
support of the developing entry-level Doctor of Occupational
Therapy (OTD) Program at Texas Christian University (TCU).
Other responsibilities include advising and mentoring graduate
students and contributing to university and community service in
alignment with institutional missions.
Applicants must be licensed or eligible for licensure as an
occupational therapist in the State of Texas and have earned a
Doctoral degree (OTD, PhD, EdD or equivalent) with three years
clinical experience preferred. Those with advanced clinical
credentialing/expertise (E.g., geriatrics, neuro-rehabilitation,
hand therapy, etc.) are especially encouraged to apply. Salary and
rank will be commensurate with the qualifications and experience of
the candidate. Review of applications will begin immediately and
continue until the position is filled. This position is slated to
begin June 1, 2027.
Applications not submitted online will not be considered. Questions
about the position can be directed via email (OTSearch@tcu.edu) to:
Leah Samantha Randolph, PhD, OTR, Search Chair - Assistant
Professor.
Department Details:
The Department of Occupational Therapy at Texas Christian
University is committed to preparing practice-scholars through a
collaborative, student-centered learning environment. Faculty work
closely together in a culture that values mentorship,
interprofessional engagement, and a strong scholarship agenda that
informs teaching, research and clinical practice. Through small,
single-cohort class structures, students and faculty develop
meaningful relationships that foster individualized support, active
collaboration, and a cohesive “family” culture within the
program.
Consistent with the core values of Texas Christian
University—Integrity, Engagement, Community, and Excellence—the
department emphasizes ethical leadership, active participation in
scholarship and service, and a deep commitment to student success.
Faculty are dedicated to advancing the profession through
innovative teaching, impactful research, and community partnerships
while cultivating graduates who are prepared to lead with
compassion, professionalism, and a commitment to excellence in
occupational therapy practice.
School/College Description:
The Harris College of Nursing & Health Sciences consists of
programs that prepare future health care and human services
professionals. The academic units within Harris College – Applied
Health Sciences, Communication Sciences & Disorders,
Occupational Therapy, Kinesiology, Nurse Anesthesia, Nursing, and
Social Work – are home to 1,900 students who are supported by
committed and talented faculty and staff. Harris College supports
the mission, vision, and values of TCU; we prepare global citizens
to think and practice as ethical leaders in health care and
educational settings.
Harris College offers 20 degree pathways in our health-related
disciplines. Students benefit from learning experiences in campus
laboratories and hospitals, clinics, schools, fitness facilities,
and community service agencies throughout the Dallas-Fort Worth
Area. On campus, the Miller Speech & Hearing Clinic provides
services for more than 300 families each year and serves as a
professional practice site for students majoring in speech
pathology and habilitation of the deaf. TCU Nursing and the School
of Nurse Anesthesia provide innovative learning experiences in
their state-of-the-art simulation centers.
The faculty and students at Harris College actively engage in
research for the purpose of improving health and well-being.
Undergraduate and graduate students have opportunities to form
mentoring relationships with internationally recognized faculty as
they conduct studies in such areas as pharmacogenetics,
carbohydrate metabolism, exercise physiology, health disparities,
heart disease, aging, Parkinson’s disease, caregiving, language
development in children with hearing loss, and forgiveness among
others. Our graduates are competent, compassionate, and in demand
in the workforce.
University & Fort Worth Description:
About TCU
Founded in 1873, Texas Christian University is a world-class,
private, Carnegie-classified national research university located
in Fort Worth, Texas. Inspired by its mission and core values of
integrity, engagement, community, and excellence, TCU consistently
ranks among the top universities and colleges in the United
States.
TCU’s campus — regularly ranked among the nation’s most beautiful —
spans 302 acres in a primarily residential area just minutes from
downtown.
The university comprises nine schools and colleges offering 117
areas of undergraduate study, 62 master’s level programs, and 37
areas of doctoral study. TCU is a leader across several
disciplines, including health care, business, energy, and the arts.
Total enrollment stands at 12,980, including 11,152 undergraduates
and 1,828 graduate students. Students are supported by over 2,200
faculty and staff, including more than 700 full-time faculty
members.
About Fort Worth
Fort Worth blends the approachable charm of a smaller city with the
amenities, cultural energy, and distinctive personality of a major
metro. As the nation’s 11th-largest city, with a rapidly growing
population of more than 1 million, Fort Worth and TCU share a
relationship that spans more than a century — one that continues to
deepen as many Horned Frogs choose to stay after graduation, drawn
by the region’s thriving job market. Part of the Dallas-Fort Worth
metropolitan area — the nation’s fourth-largest and a top tourism
destination — Fort Worth earned recognition from U.S. News &
World Report in 2025 as the No. 4 best big city to live in the
United States.
Fort Worth offers an impressive array of cultural, educational, and
entertainment opportunities, anchored by three world-class art
museums — the Kimbell Art Museum, the Modern Art Museum of Fort
Worth, and the Amon Carter Museum of American Art. The Bass
Performance Hall stands as one of the premier performance venues in
the country. Throughout the year, residents and visitors alike
enjoy concerts, film festivals, and other cultural events at
Sundance Square, Dickies Arena, Panther Island, and Near Southside
venues.
Required Application Materials & Application
Instructions:
To apply, submit Cover Letter, Curriculum Vitae, Teaching Statement
and contact information for three references online at
https://jobs.tcu.edu/en-us/listing/ (select "Harris College of
Nursing & Health Sciences" to locate the position
announcement). For tenure-track applicants, please include a
Research Statement with agenda. References will not be contacted
without prior notification of candidates. All questions regarding
the application process should be directed to Human Resources at
hrtalent@tcu.edu.
Employment Values Statement:
Texas Christian University values Integrity, Engagement, Community,
and Excellence in the workplace. TCU treats applicants and
employees with fairness and respect. TCU hires and promotes
individuals based on their qualifications and their commitment to
making a positive impact on our student-centered community. TCU is
an equal opportunity employer and follows all applicable employment
laws. TCU fairly considers all qualified individuals, ensuring we
are a workplace free from unlawful discrimination and
harassment.

jobs.title: Assistant, Associate or Full Professor in Mathematics
jobs.description:

Application Deadline:
November 1, 2026 (soft deadline)
Position Details:
This full-time faculty position is on-campus and in-person. The
Department of Mathematics at Texas Christian University (TCU)
invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor
position beginning in August 2027. Preference will be given to
candidates in areas of active research in the department, which
include Geometry, Topology, Operator Algebras, Number Theory,
Representation Theory of Lie Groups, and Statistics/Data Science.
Candidates must have a Ph.D. in Mathematics, Statistics, or a
closely related field by August 2027. Exceptional candidates may be
considered for appointment at a higher rank.
Department Details:
The Department of Mathematics is a small, collegial unit, currently
with 21 full-time faculty members. The department serves
approximately 125 majors in Math, Actuarial Science, and Data
Science and has a small graduate program offering Master’s and
Doctoral degrees in Mathematics. The university is located within
the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex, a vibrant metropolitan area of
about 8.5 million people.
School/College Description:
The Louise Dilworth Davis College of Science & Engineering
encompasses 9 departments (Biology, Chemistry & Biochemistry,
Computer Science, Engineering, Environmental and Geological
Sciences, Mathematics, Nutritional Sciences, Physics &
Astronomy, and Psychology) as well as the Ranch Management Program,
which offers both an undergraduate degree and a one-year
certificate program. Davis College is also home to the Pre-Health
Professions Institute, the Karyn Purvis Institute for Child
Development, the Institute of Behavioral Research, the Institute
for Environmental Studies, Monnig Meteorite Gallery, and the
Institute for Ranch Management. Davis College is the second largest
at TCU in terms of both undergraduate enrollment and number of
majors. It contains a disproportionate percentage of high-achieving
students, as evidenced by the fact that almost one-half of the
students in the Honors College have majors in The Louise Dilworth
Davis College of Science & Engineering. Research opportunities
abound for undergraduates, with 46 percent of majors engaging in a
substantive experience during which they work one-on-one with their
faculty mentor. Davis College also has five doctoral programs and
16 master’s programs, as well as two graduate certificate programs.
Davis College faculty are true teacher-scholars, for whom
instruction and research are viewed as complementary
activities.

by the region’s thriving job market. Part of the Dallas-Fort Worth
metropolitan area — the nation’s fourth-largest and a top tourism
destination — Fort Worth earned recognition from U.S. News &
World Report in 2025 as the No. 4 best big city to live in the
United States.
Fort Worth offers an impressive array of cultural, educational, and
entertainment opportunities, anchored by three world-class art
museums — the Kimbell Art Museum, the Modern Art Museum of Fort
Worth, and the Amon Carter Museum of American Art. The Bass
Performance Hall stands as one of the premier performance venues in
the country. Throughout the year, residents and visitors alike
enjoy concerts, film festivals, and other cultural events at
Sundance Square, Dickies Arena, Panther Island, and Near Southside
venues.
Required Application Materials & Application
Instructions:
Candidates should apply through MathJobs (http://www.mathjobs.org/)
and must also submit information through the TCU HR system. For the
application on MathJobs, please submit (a) an AMS cover sheet; (b)
a cover letter; (c) a complete vita, including a list of
publications; (d) a research plan; (e) a teaching statement
specifically addressing your teaching style, classroom techniques,
and assessment strategies; (f) copies of graduate transcripts; (g)
three or more confidential letters of recommendation, at least one
of which addresses the candidate’s teaching in detail; and (h) for
applicants who have not yet completed a Ph.D., undergraduate
transcripts. Candidates are strongly encouraged to describe in
their application materials how they might support the university

jobs.title: Assistant Professor in Operations and Analytics
jobs.description:
Georgetown University's McDonough School of Business invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position in Operations Management, within the Operations and Analytics (OPAN) Area. We seek to make an appointment at the Assistant Professor level. Pending budget approval, the appointment would begin at the start of Fall 2027. Candidates should hold a Ph.D. from a business-related discipline, or expect to defend their dissertation by August 2027. We are seeking candidates with high potential or demonstrated ability to publish distinguished operations management research in top-tier research outlets and teaching excellence in operations management and/or analytics.
ABOUT THE MCDONOUGH SCHOOL OF BUSINESS
Located in Washington, D.C., Georgetown University’s McDonough School of Business offers unparalleled access to the world’s business, policy and thought leaders as well as a collegial environment for professional development. The school, which attracts faculty and students from around the world, is committed to developing principled leaders capable of making complex business decisions in a global environment and who are dedicated to serving both business and society. The school’s undergraduate, MBA, Executive MBA, and specialized programs provide solid grounding in all the core management disciplines, with an emphasis on the global, ethical and political environment of business. The school’s programs are consistently highly ranked, and the OPAN Area is actively involved in all these programs. Additional information regarding Georgetown University is available at http://www.georgetown.edu and http://msb.georgetown.edu. The McDonough School of Business has an ongoing commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion as a fundamental aspect of the Georgetown community.
APPLICATION PROCEDURE
All applications should be submitted electronically by Interfolio. Interested applicants should provide a cover letter, a curriculum vitae, published and working papers, research and teaching statements, as well as the names and contact information for three references.
To ensure full consideration and to be considered for an interview at the 2026 INFORMS Annual Meeting in San Francisco (Nov 1-4), candidates should submit their applications (except for reference letters) by October 10, 2026. The application deadline (for submitting all application materials, including reference letters) is November 5, 2026, or until the position is filled.
The projected salary or hourly pay range for this position is $182,000 - $201,000, which represents the full range of anticipated compensation for this position. Compensation is determined by a number of factors including, but not limited to, the candidate’s individual qualifications, experience, education, skills, and certifications, as well as the University’s business needs and external factors.
Georgetown University is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer fully dedicated to achieving a diverse faculty and staff. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration for
employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity and expression, and sexual orientation), disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic
protected by law. If you are a qualified individual with a disability and need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application and hiring process, please click here for more information, or contact the Office of Institutional Diversity, Equity & Affirmative Action (IDEAA) at (202) 687-4798.

Job Details
Hiring Department
The Department of Learning, Teaching & Curriculum (LTC)
Job Description
The Department of Learning, Teaching & Curriculum (LTC) at the
University of Missouri seeks applicants for an assistant
(tenure-track) position in early childhood literacy education
(9-month appointment). The successful candidate will have a
doctorate in early childhood literacy education or early childhood
education with a literacy focus, a demonstrated potential for
excellence in scholarship, a commitment to conduct research, pursue
external funding that aligns with the University’s status as an AAU
member, and skills pertinent to research, teaching, service, and
collaboration.
A faculty member filling this position will maintain an active
program of research, teaching, and service that is consistent with
current College of Education and Human Development tenure-track
faculty. Of particular interest are scholars whose research is
based in early childhood (Birth- 3rd grade) and literacy education
and examines critical issues in early childhood literacy education
including early childhood literacy methods, standards, policies,
family, and community contexts in relation to literacy
education.
Maintain an active program of research and scholarship with the
potential for external funding
Teach courses related to early childhood literacy education
consistent with the program and departmental instructional needs
(e.g., early childhood literacy methods, assessment, or a
combination thereof)
Incorporate the current limitations and possibilities SoR
landscape in research and collaboration
Contribute primarily to ECE and Literacy Masters and
Undergraduate program through teaching, research, and service
Provide leadership and service to the program, department,
college, and university
Qualifications
An earned doctorate in early childhood education with a
literacy focus, early childhood literacy education, or a related
field
At least 3 years of experience teaching in early childhood
and/or early literacy classroom or teacher education settings
Applicants will be evaluated based upon the following
criteria:
Understanding of the current SoR landscape, including
imitations and possibilities for early language and literacy
teaching and learning
Knowledge of ECE and literacy policy, national/state
standards
Understanding of community and family systems supports early
childhood development
Record of (or demonstrated potential for) scholarly
productivity
Success as a collaborator on a scholarly or instructional
team
Ability to teach and support undergraduate and graduate
students of early childhood education and literacy
Ability to work and engage collegially with individuals from
early childhood, elementary, and literacy-focused settings as well
as with department, university, and community members
Knowledge of preservice teacher education for early childhood
literacy educators
Experience teaching at college level
Experience teaching in an online program
Experience in programmatic leadership
Grant experience and research collaboration
Anticipated Hiring Range
Salary: Competitive and commensurate with experience and
qualifications.
Application Materials
Apply on-line at http://hrs.missouri.edu/find-a-job/academic
. Upload a complete application including:
Letter of application describing qualifications for the
position and research agenda (including both publications and
recording of external funding);
Curriculum Vita (CV) that details scholarship, prior teaching
experiences, related work history, grants, advising, service, and
awards/honors. In addition, at the end of the CV, include a list of
names and contact information for three professional
references.
Search Committee Chairs: Dr. Amber Smith (
ansmith@missouri.edu ) and Dr. Angie Zapata ( zapatam@missouri.edu
)
Application Deadline
Review of applications will begin October 22, 2026, and continue
until filled.
Sponsorship Information
Employment visa sponsorship is not available for this
position.
Other Information
The College of Education and Human Development and LTC
The University of Missouri College of Education & Human
Development (CEHD) prepares and supports professionals in
education, information, lifespan, and intervention sciences that
improve the quality of life and economic development for the people
of Missouri, the nation and the world.
The College’s mission is fulfilled by taking a comprehensive,
collaborative approach across a wide range of disciplines and
professions, including educator preparation, leadership,
counseling, early childhood education, special education, higher
education, public policy, family and lifespan development,
information sciences and technology.
The CEHD serves more than 2,300 undergraduate and graduate students
across a broad portfolio of bachelor’s, master’s, specialist, and
doctoral programs. Nationally recognized for the strength and
breadth of its academic programs, the College ranks among the
nation’s top 30 graduate schools of education and among the top 20
public institutions, according to U.S. News & World
Report. Several of its programs also hold strong national
rankings, including special education, online education,
educational administration, and library and information studies.
The College has a substantial research and outreach footprint, with
nearly $47 million in annual research expenditures supporting work
that advances education, human development, and information
sciences, as well as outreach activities extending throughout
Missouri and beyond.
The Department of Learning, Teaching, and Curriculum includes more
than 30 faculty members from a range of emphasis areas, including

The mathematics education emphasis area has a proud tradition of

and leaders in public K–12 school districts.
Community Information
Columbia offers small-town friendliness with big city features and
a high quality of life for people of all ages and interests.
Founded on education and known as an ideal college town, its
location also makes it an attractive spot for businesses and
travelers. Located on Interstate 70 and U.S. Highway 63, Columbia
is right in the middle of the state and the nation. Just a couple
hours’ drive from St. Louis and Kansas City, Columbia is Boone

jobs.title: College of Osteopathic Medicine - Biomedical Science Faculty
jobs.description:
Job Details
Position Summary & Description
Position Summary & Description
The IUP College of Osteopathic Medicine (IUPCOM) invites applicants
for several inaugural full-time, tenure track and part-time
nontenure track Biomedical Sciences faculty teaching positions
beginning in the Fall of 2026. These roles offer a distinctive
opportunity to contribute to the College’s development by helping
to shape a forward-thinking and rurally-focused medical education
program grounded in interdisciplinary collaboration, community
engagement, and academic excellence with early clinical
experiences. Successful candidates will demonstrate a strong and
engaged commitment to medical education and play an integral role
in delivering an innovative, integrated, systems-based curriculum
that prioritizes active learning, clinical relevance, and
interprofessional collaboration. IUP is officially classified as an
R2 doctoral university institution and the College offers generous
start-up financial support, research laboratory space and
equipment, and other internal resources/support for scholarly
pursuits.
The faculty, working closely with the IUPCOM Dean's Office, will
provide support for the organization, development,
operationalization, and assessment of the clinically-oriented
biomedical science aspects of the four-year educational curricular
continuum.
Biomedical Sciences Faculty Sought
We are seeking multiple full-time, tenure track and part-time
nontenure track faculty members at the Instructor, Assistant,
Associate, or Full Professor level. Note: these roles are
curriculum development focused until students matriculate in the
fall of 2027, which will then transition into teaching-focus with
continued curriculum development. These positions include but not
limited to the following disciplines/roles:
Anatomy (gross anatomy and histology)
Develop curriculum and once students matriculate, deliver
lectures, lab instruction (cadaveric dissection, prosection, VR and
imaging-based anatomy); facilitate small-group, team-based, or
case-based learning sessions; direct or co-direct anatomy courses,
manage lab operations, cadaver procurement, and safety; integrate
clinical correlations and osteopathic principles (OMM relevance to
anatomy); develop practical exams and written assessments
Biochemistry & Molecular Biology
Develop curriculum and once students matriculate, teach
foundational biochemical pathways, molecular genetics, and
metabolism in systems-based curricula; align basic science content
with clinical relevance (e.g., disease mechanisms, diagnostics);
collaborate with pharmacology, pathology, and clinical faculty in
integrated blocks
Microbiology & Immunology
Develop curriculum and once students matriculate, teach
infectious diseases, host-pathogen interactions, and immune system
function; emphasize diagnostic reasoning, antimicrobial mechanisms,
and immunologic disorders; work with infectious disease faculty on
integrated teaching sessions
Pathology
Develop curriculum and once students matriculate, teach general
and systemic pathology, often as a bridge between the foundational
biomedical and clinical sciences; lead problem-based learning,
case-based discussions, and clinico-pathologic correlations; create
clinically oriented exam items reflecting disease mechanisms; work
closely with practicing pathologists or clinicians for applied
teaching
Pharmacology/Pharmacogenomics
Develop curriculum and once students matriculate, teach
mechanisms of action, pharmacokinetics/dynamics, and therapeutics;
link drug therapy to disease states in systems-based courses;
collaborate with physiology and pathology faculty toward knowledge
integration; develop active-learning modules (e.g., prescribing
simulations, case scenarios, etc.)
Physiology
Develop curriculum and once students matriculate, teach normal
function across organ systems (cardio, renal, respiratory, etc.);
connect physiology to pathophysiology, pharmacology, and clinical
medicine; lead integration experiences in small groups, case-based
sessions, and simulation exercises; sequence content to support
spiral/integrated curriculum models
Duties – These roles are curriculum development focused until
students matriculate in the fall of 2027, which will then
transition into teaching-focus with continued curriculum
development.
Collaborate in curriculum development, design, and upon student
matriculation, delivery of the biomedical sciences discipline of
the entirety of the curriculum with emphasis on clinically-oriented
vertical and horizontal integration across foundational and
systems-based courses
Contribute to the design and implementation of course and
system-level curricular objectives aligned with programmatic
outcomes
Develop curriculum and once students matriculate, teach and
facilitate in face-to-face classroom instruction, active learning
sessions, case-based discussions, and laboratory settings,
including anatomy and related biomedical sciences, as appropriate
to expertise
Contribute to clinically relevant biomedical science content in
clinical clerkship syllabi in Years 3-4, as appropriate
Participate in curriculum delivery, assessment, and continuous
quality improvement activities as part of the COM's ongoing
assessment program
Develop board-style questions aligned with COMLEX
competencies
Engage in scholarly activity, research, curricular innovation,
and professional service (University, community, state, national,
and international) consistent with expectations for tenure and
promotion, with an emphasis on osteopathic principles and
practice
Advise and mentor students regarding academic progress,
professional development, and career planning
Participate in faculty development activities and contribute to
the educational mission of the College
Demonstrate professionalism, ethical conduct, and collegiality
in all academic and institutional responsibilities
Perform other duties as assigned in support of the University,
biomedical sciences curriculum, and COM mission
Position Qualifications
Terminal degree (e.g., PhD, DO, MD, EdD, or PharmD) or
eligible, or master’s with teaching experience for all positions,
must have terminal degree (e.g., PhD, DO, MD, EdD, or PharmD) for
tenure-track roles and to be considered for rank of Assistant
Professor or higher.
Minimum (1) year academic experience as a faculty member at an
accredited US allopathic or osteopathic medical school, or other
clinical, graduate, or undergraduate program with proven experience
teaching biomedical sciences in an accredited health-sciences or
nursing program.
Essential Functions
Strong interpersonal and teamwork skills for working with
interdisciplinary faculty and engaging adult learners
effectively
Strong foundational and expert knowledge in area of biomedical
science specialization with ability to connect to clinical practice
and osteopathic principles
Demonstrated ability to mentor and motivate peers and
learners
Skills in delivering lectures, facilitating small groups
(TBL/PBL), and using active learning strategies in an integrated,
systems-based curriculum
Ability to develop course materials, align objectives with
competencies (e.g., COMLEX), and integrate content across
disciplines
Proficiency in writing high-quality exam questions (especially
board-style questions) and assessing student performance (written
exams, OSCEs, practicals)
Ability to engage in research or educational scholarship,
analyze data, and contribute to academic literature
Skill in advising, mentoring, and supporting diverse learners,
including professionalism and academic development
Demonstrated leadership and productivity in the areas of
medical education, clinical, or professional service
Good standing with all regulatory and governmental boards and
agencies

Develop curriculum and once students matriculate, instruct/lead

About the College
Spelman College seeks teacher/scholars dedicated to excellence in
teaching and to the continued enhancement of the academic
environment for students and colleagues. Founded in 1881, Spelman
College is a private four-year liberal arts college located in
Atlanta, GA. The oldest historically Black college for women in the
United States, Spelman is a member of the Atlanta University Center
Consortium and Atlanta Regional Consortium for Higher
Education.
Position Description
The Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry invites
applications for tenure-track positions at the rank of
Assistant Professor or Associate Professor to begin
August 2027 .
We seek outstanding teacher-scholars dedicated to excellence in the
chemical and biochemical sciences. The department is an American
Chemical Society ( ACS ) approved program, which has a strong,
proven reputation for educating and training women of African
descent to excel in STEM fields. The successful candidate will have
a doctorate in chemistry or a related area and be able to teach
courses at the undergraduate level in at least one or more of the
traditional sub-disciplinary areas of chemistry in Analytical,
Biochemistry, or Organic Chemistry. The teaching load is 3/3. The
position also requires contributing effectively to curriculum
development efforts, advising and mentoring students, providing
service to the department and college, and establishing a
competitive and highly productive undergraduate research program.
The research can be in one of the fields mentioned previously or an
interdisciplinary field involving the area such as bioanalytical
chemistry. Candidates with a demonstrated commitment to working
with women and underrepresented minority students through teaching,
mentoring, and research are especially encouraged to apply. All
courses are taught in-person.
Priority review for applications will begin on October
23, 2026 .
The application will close on November 2, 2026 .
This position is contingent upon the availability of sufficient
funding.
Qualifications
Ph.D. in Analytical Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, or Biochemistry
strongly preferred for these positions. We will also consider
interdisciplinary areas.

About the College
Spelman College seeks teacher/scholars dedicated to excellence in
teaching and to the continued enhancement of the academic
environment for students and colleagues. Founded in 1881, Spelman
College is a private four-year liberal arts college located in
Atlanta, GA. The oldest historically Black college for women in the
United States, Spelman is a member of the Atlanta University Center
Consortium and Atlanta Regional Consortium for Higher
Education.
The Spelman College Cosmetic Science Program is an
innovative, interdisciplinary academic program designed to prepare
students to be STEM experts in the cosmetics and personal care
industry. Launched in 2024, the program offers rigorous scientific
training focused on cosmetic ingredients, formulation, product
performance, and safety for textured hair and melanated skin
science. The curriculum draws upon expertise across natural
sciences, mathematics, and other disciplines to provide students
with a distinctive educational experience that connects fundamental
science with real-world applications.
The program is entering an important period of growth and
curricular expansion. The successful candidate will have the
opportunity to help shape the future direction of Cosmetic Science
at Spelman, providing intellectual leadership in developing
lectures, instructional laboratories, and research-based
experiences. We are particularly interested in candidates who can
translate their scientific expertise into a rigorous, laboratory-
and research-based curricula that respond to advances in cosmetic
science.
Position Description
The Spelman College Cosmetic Science Program seeks to invite
applicants for a tenure-track professorship starting Fall
2027.
Research Expectations
The successful candidate will establish an innovative, externally
fundable research program that advances the scientific
understanding of cosmetic ingredients, formulations, finished
products, and/or their interactions with biological systems. The
research program should provide meaningful opportunities for
undergraduate students to engage in discovery, develop technical
expertise, and contribute to scholarly outcomes.
We particularly welcome candidates whose research uses instrumental
and analytical approaches to investigate questions related to
product safety, performance, efficacy, formulation, hair and skin
science, ingredient characterization, or other areas relevant to
cosmetic and personal care science . Candidates whose
current research could expand into cosmetic science applications
are strongly encouraged to apply.
Teaching Expectations
The successful candidate will contribute to both the Chemistry
and Cosmetic Science curricula . Within Chemistry, teaching
responsibilities may include foundational and advanced courses and
laboratories. The candidate will also have the opportunity to shape
the expanding cosmetic science curriculum and related co-curricular
activities . While prior teaching experience in cosmetic
science is not required, candidates must demonstrate the capacity
to teach and develop innovative cosmetic science courses and
laboratory experiences.
The successful candidate will join a growing community of faculty,
students, and external partners committed to expanding Spelman’s
capacity in cosmetic science. In line with this, the position
offers a unique opportunity for a faculty member who is excited not
simply to teach within an established program, but to help build
and define its next phase of growth.
Qualifications
A Ph.D. in chemistry, chemical engineering, toxicology,
pharmacology, or a closely related field by the time of
appointment.
Strong training in chemistry and a record of research that
demonstrates the potential to develop an independent, externally
funded research program.
Expertise in experimental, analytical, or instrumental
approaches relevant to the characterization of chemicals,
materials, formulations, or biological systems.
The ability to teach undergraduate chemistry and the interest
and capacity to develop and teach courses in cosmetic science.
A commitment to undergraduate teaching, research mentorship,
and student development.

Job Details
Position Summary
( UGA ) invites applications for the position of Clinical
Assistant Professor in its Elementary Education program. We are
seeking an individual with expertise in PreK-5 teaching,
integrating theory and practice in teacher education programs, and
experience with the scholarship of teaching or engagement. This is
a nine-month academic contract, renewable appointment for the
2027-28 academic year that begins August 2027. In recognition of
the important role that clinical faculty play, starting salaries
for clinical faculty match those for tenure-track faculty, and the
University has a well-structured promotion system for individuals
in clinical track positions to advance to clinical associate
professor and clinical full professor ranks. Opportunities exist
for summer teaching appointments.
Special Instructions to Applicants
Applicants should submit:
A letter of application specifically responsive to the
position’s responsibilities and required qualifications as
described above
A curriculum vitae
Two writing samples
The names and contact information of three persons who could
provide letters of reference (transcripts and letters of reference
will be required only from selected finalists)
All material should be submitted electronically via uploading
pdf’s to this application.
Applications received by Sunday, October 25, 2026, will be
assured full consideration, but this position is open until filled.
Address questions to the search committee chair, Dr. Beth Tolley
btolley@uga.edu
.

About the University of Georgia
Chartered by the state of Georgia in 1785, the University of
Georgia is the birthplace of public higher education in America and
is the state’s flagship university (https://www.uga.edu/) . The
proof is in our more than 240 years of academic and professional
achievements and our continual commitment to higher education. UGA
is currently ranked among the top 20 public universities in U.S.
News & World Report. The University’s main campus is located in
Athens, approximately 65 miles northeast of Atlanta, with extended
campuses in Atlanta, Griffin, Gwinnett, and Tifton. UGA employs
approximately 3,100 faculty and more than 7,700 full-time staff.
The University’s enrollment exceeds 41,000 students including over
31,000 undergraduates and over 10,000 graduate and professional
students. Academic programs reside in 19 schools and colleges,
including our newly established School of Medicine.
About the College/Unit/Department
As the 4th largest public college of education in the country and
the 3rd largest college at UGA, the Mary Frances Early College of
Education ( MFE COE ) improves the lives of residents of Georgia
and beyond through our instruction, research, and service. The MFE
COE is a comprehensive college with disciplines focused on teacher
preparation, counseling and human development, communication
sciences, human movement sciences, career development, student
affairs, and educational administration and policy. We place
significant emphasis on graduate education with approximately 40%
of our students at the graduate level, making us the second largest
college at UGA with respect to graduate education.
ETAP has contributed to this stature locally, nationally, and
internationally. The department is characterized by critical,
forward-thinking research and innovative, dynamic teaching. ETAP is
committed to making equity, access, and belonging visible in its
courses, programs, policies, and practice. Our outreach and
research include a variety of multifaceted collaborations,
including those with local school districts and local
community-based informal education projects, as well as projects
that extend across the state of Georgia, the United States, and a
variety of international contexts. Information about the department
is available at
https://coe.uga.edu/directory/educational-theory-and-practice/.
The Elementary Education program at UGA, which includes Early
Childhood Education, has been ranked among the nation’s top 10
elementary education programs by U.S. News and World Report for
more than a decade. Our mission in the Elementary Education program
is to blend theory and practice grounded in our shared philosophy
of critical pedagogy. Upon program completion, we expect our
students to demonstrate teaching competencies related to habits of
reflexive practice, integrating scholarship and research, engaging
in professional collaboration, and appreciating and supporting
multiple backgrounds and perspectives. These elements of thought
and action are viewed as key to supporting critically informed and
equitable teacher decision-making. The Elementary Education program
is designed to offer theoretically and clinically rich experiences
in diverse environments. By the end of the program, teachers are
prepared to enact these commitments as leaders in their classrooms,
schools, and communities.
College/Unit/Department website
https://coe.uga.edu/directory/educational-theory-and-practice/.

jobs.title: Public Service Faculty - Strategic Management and Organizational Effectiveness Unit Manager
jobs.description:
Job Details
Position Summary
The Government Services and Research ( GSR ) Division of the Carl
Vinson Institute of Government provides applied research,
organizational consulting, strategic planning, and decision-support
services that help state and local governments strengthen
organizational effectiveness, improve operational performance, and
address complex public-sector challenges.
The Strategic Management and Organizational Effectiveness Unit
Manager provides strategic leadership for the Unit and is
responsible for the development, delivery, and continuous
enhancement of organizational consulting services that support
government clients throughout Georgia. The Unit Manager establishes
the strategic direction for the Unit’s consulting practice, leads
organizational assessments, strategic planning initiatives, process
improvement efforts, performance management projects, and other
management consulting engagements designed to improve
organizational effectiveness and public service delivery.
Responsibilities include supervising and developing public service
faculty and professional staff; managing client relationships,
contracts, and project portfolios; providing executive
consultation; conducting applied research; facilitating
executive-level planning and organizational development
initiatives; and building collaborative partnerships with state
agencies, local governments, University partners, and other
stakeholders. The Unit Manager identifies emerging client needs,
develops innovative service offerings, and contributes to the
continued success, innovation, and long-term effectiveness of the
Government Services and Research Division.
As a Public Service Faculty member, this position advances the
mission of the Carl Vinson Institute of Government by providing
objective, data-informed consultation, applied research, and
organizational expertise that strengthen government operations,
improve public sector performance, and enhance the capacity of
Georgia’s state and local governments to serve their
communities.
Position is located in our Atlanta Office: 18 Capitol Square SW,
Atlanta, GA 30334
Special Instructions to Applicants
Compensation will be determined by the qualifications and
experience of the successful applicant. Candidates will be
considered for the position until it is filled. Application
materials should include a cover letter, curriculum vita, a brief
writing sample from a technical report, and three references with
contact information. The finalists for the position will be
required to provide three letters of recommendation. All applicants
must apply through UGAJobs to be considered for the position.
Please note that successful applicants are responsible for ensuring
their eligibility to work in the United States (i.e., a citizen or
national of the United States, a lawful permanent resident, a
foreign national authorized to work in the United States without
need of employer sponsorship) on or before the effective date of
your appointment, and maintain eligibility without sponsorship
throughout your appointment.

About the University of Georgia
Chartered by the state of Georgia in 1785, the University of
Georgia is the birthplace of public higher education in America and
is the state’s flagship university (https://www.uga.edu/) . The
proof is in our more than 240 years of academic and professional
achievements and our continual commitment to higher education. UGA
is currently ranked among the top 20 public universities in U.S.
News & World Report. The University’s main campus is located in
Athens, approximately 65 miles northeast of Atlanta, with extended

approximately 3,100 faculty and more than 7,700 full-time staff.
The University’s enrollment exceeds 41,000 students including over

About the College/Unit/Department
The UGA Carl Vinson Institute of Government – Who We
Are
As a Public Service and Outreach unit at the
University of Georgia, the UGA Institute of Government contributes
directly to the university’s overarching public service mission of
improving people’s lives by helping to create jobs and prosperity,
developing leaders, and addressing critical issues. This public
service mission, and the Institute of Government’s role in its
success, is at the heart of UGA’s land-grant and sea-grant mission
to serve the State of Georgia and its residents.
We have a wide range of experts who inform, inspire, and innovate
every day so that governments, large and small, can be more
efficient and responsive to their citizens, address current and
emerging challenges, and serve the public with excellence. We are
uniquely positioned to provide impartial support to local
governments and state agencies and convene multi-disciplinary and
intragovernmental groups to plan for and address many of the
challenges faced by communities across Georgia.
Our areas of expertise and focus include workforce and economic
development; infrastructure and community resilience; government
operations and organizational effectiveness; measuring and
reporting on impact and outcomes; building skills, knowledge and
capacity of government leaders and teams; and maximizing technology
and data for governments and their leaders.
Whether it is through our award-winning PROPEL (Planning Rural
Opportunities for Prosperity and Economic Leadership) program for
rural communities, our CyberArch student program that helps Georgia
communities increase their cybersecurity, our efforts to build a
visionary plan for military and community partnerships to spur
economic prosperity and resilient infrastructure, our financial
management certificate program to build the capacity of public
officials, or hosting educational events about e-mobility

jobs.description:
Job Details
Position Title:
Two Tenure-Track Assistant Professor Positions in Information
Systems & Analytics
Position Type:
Regular
About the Role:
Assistant Professors in Information Systems and Analytics
The School of Computing and Analytics (SCA) at Northern Kentucky
University (NKU) invites applications for two full-time,
tenure-track Assistant Professor positions in Information Systems
and Analytics beginning August 2027. Salary and benefits are
competitive.
We are seeking candidates possessing teaching and/or research
expertise in one or more of the following areas: information
systems, security management, analytics and data-driven
decision-making, health informatics, health information systems,
health information management, or artificial intelligence in
healthcare.
The positions will contribute to the Information Systems &
Analytics (IS&A) programs: B.S. in Information Systems and
Business Informatics, M.S. in Information Systems, and M.S. in
Health Informatics. Learn more about the IS&A programs at
https://www.nku.edu/informatics/schools/sca/programs/isa/index.html
.
The SCA is part of the College of Informatics (COI)
(informatics.nku.edu) and is housed in Griffin Hall, a landmark
high-tech building. The School offers multiple degrees and is
organized into three program clusters: Computer Science &
Software Engineering (CS&SE), Cybersecurity & Information
Technology (CYS&IT), and Information Systems & Analytics
(IS&A). More information about the SCA is available at https://www.nku.edu/informatics/schools/sca/index.html
.
Teaching: Develop and teach both face-to-face and online
courses. The standard teaching load in the Information Systems
& Analytics program is three courses per semester for active
researchers. The candidate will be expected to teach at both the
undergraduate and graduate levels.
Research: Maintain an active research agenda in the field to
ensure ongoing qualification as a Scholarly Academic (SA) under
AACSB accreditation standards.
Service: Participate in service activities, including
serving on committees at the School, College, and University levels
and/or contributing to the professional community.
On-campus presence: This is not a remote position.
The successful candidates will be required to relocate to the
Northern Kentucky/Greater Cincinnati area.
Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in Information Systems or a closely
related field preferably from an AACSB-accredited program. ABD
candidates will be considered.
Documents should be submitted as part of the application process.
Must apply on the NKU Jobs website at: https://nku.wd108.myworkdayjobs.com/NKU_External
Please upload the following (all documents can be submitted in the
same documents box):
Cover letter
Curriculum vitae
Statement of teaching interests (required for all
applicants)
Statement of research interests (required for tenure-track
applicants)
List of three references with complete contact information
Priority will be given to applications received by November 1,
2026.
Applications will be accepted until the position is filled.
Questions concerning this position should be addressed to:
Mahathi Koutha, koutham1@nku.edu , 859-572-5240
All offers of employment are contingent upon a satisfactory
pre-employment criminal background check as mandated by state
law.
NKU’s vision is that we will be nationally recognized for being a
student-ready, regionally engaged university that empowers diverse
learners for economic and social mobility. Our core values place emphasis on our culture of
excellence, creativity, innovation, and collegiality. Your cover
letter and/or teaching statement should show, as a faculty member
at NKU, how you will contribute to our core values and our
strategic framework, especially in how you will contribute to
student success and belonging.

Welcome! We’re excited you’re considering an opportunity with

The West Virginia University Health System, the state’s largest
health system and largest private employer, comprises 18 hospitals
throughout the state and bordering states. In addition, it includes
five institutes, as well as providing management services for other
local hospitals through affiliate agreements.
Whether you are caring for our patients at one of the critical

West Virginia University School of Medicine and the Department of
Urology seek a Urologic Oncologist (ranks available: Assistant

jobs.title: Assistant / Associate / Professor and Director - Dental Hygiene - School of Dentistry
jobs.description:
Job Details
Unit: School of Dentistry
Department: General Practice
Duties & Responsibilities:
Virginia Commonwealth University (VCU) School of Dentistry is
seeking applicants for a full-time faculty position in the
Department of General Practice, Division of Dental Hygiene.
Academic rank, tenure eligibility, and salary commensurate with the
candidate’s qualifications and experience.
Mission or Goal of Unit:
The primary mission of the School of Dentistry is to educate
practitioners of Dentistry capable of meeting the general oral
health needs of the communities they serve. Integral parts of the
mission are research and other scholarly activity, patient care,
leadership in dental education and organized dentistry, and
collaboration and participation with other units within VCU and VCU
Health System. As the only dental hygiene program located within a
dental school in the Commonwealth of Virginia, our students have a
unique opportunity to work in integrated clinical settings
alongside DDS students as well as with faculty members from Dental
Hygiene, dentistry and specialty areas.
The Virginia Commonwealth University (VCU) School of Dentistry is
located in downtown Richmond, Virginia. With a 133-year history,
Virginia’s only dental school offers opportunities for selected,
qualified individuals to study dentistry and oral health through
its Doctor of Dental Surgery (D.D.S.) program, graduate specialty
training programs, and a dental hygiene program. The VCU School of
Dentistry is one of a small number of dental schools in the country
affiliated with an academic medical center, the only dental school
in the Commonwealth, and one of the oldest dental schools in the
United States, founded in 1893. It is one of six health sciences
academic programs on the Medical College of Virginia (MCV) Campus
of VCU.
Position Responsibilities:
The VCU School of Dentistry, Department of General Practice is
seeking a full-time Faculty to fill the position of Director for
the Dental Hygiene Program. The purpose of this position is to
inspire student success, provide strong academic leadership,
promote innovation and faculty achievement, and foster educational
inclusiveness. The Dental Hygiene Program Director is directly
responsible and accountable for ensuring the fulfillment of
educational goals and objectives, ensuring program compliance
through accreditation by the Committee on Dental Accreditation
(CODA). In addition, the Dental Hygiene Program director holds the
authority and responsibility for all administrative functions of
the program as well as supervision of program faculty and students
in a collaborative environment. The Dental Hygiene Program Director
serves as a liaison with the administration of the School of
Dentistry and reports directly to the Department Chair. The program
director is also responsible for didactic, preclinical and clinical
instruction of undergraduate and pre-doctoral students and
participates in student advising, committee assignments, and
scholarly activities. The Dental Hygiene Program Director serves as
the Chair of Dental Hygiene Admissions, facilitating recruitment
and retention of a diverse student body. Additional
responsibilities include providing continuing education offerings
to healthcare professionals. The Program Director will strive for
excellence in educating a diverse student population prepared to
promote optimum oral health in the community.
Core Responsibilities and Administrative Duties:
Coordinate program assessment activities on an annual
basis
Faculty supervision - Directs the coordination, and recruitment
of faculty including faculty schedules, teaching assignments and
evaluation
Curriculum - provides leadership for program curriculum
development, evaluation and revision to ensure student
success
Assess program mission and goals, ensuring alignment with
school and university strategic plans
Assessing, planning and operating program administration.
Initiate faculty development
Prepare faculty contracts
Chair the dental hygiene admissions committee-coordination,
evaluation and participation in determining admission criteria and
procedures as well as student promotion and retention
criteria
Maintain quality assurance to remain compliance with all
required agencies, including the Commission on Dental Accreditation
(CODA)
Maintain communication and work cooperatively with the
department chair and Dean of the school
Serve as representative on school and university
committees
Coordinate budgets and program instructional needs and supplies
with the department chair
Schedule and conduct program meetings
Serve as an academic advisor
Serve as course director and provide clinical instruction,
maintaining syllabi, grading and the electronic management
system
Serve as chair of the dental hygiene class committee and a
liaison to the Academic Progress Committee
Maintain program website and university bulletin
Required Qualifications:
Masters degree or higher in dental hygiene education or a
related field
Graduate of a program accredited by the Commission on Dental
Accreditation
Eligible for licensure in Virginia
Certification in local anesthesia and nitrous oxide/oxygen
sedation
Current CPR certification
Minimum of one year of clinical experience as a hygienist
Didactic teaching experience
Excellent interpersonal skills and communication skills
A demonstrated potential for leadership
Demonstrated ability to work in and foster an environment of
respect, professionalism, and civility with a population of
faculty, staff, and students from all backgrounds and experiences,
or a commitment to do so as a faculty member at VCU
For tenure-eligible positions at the Assistant Professor rank,
an established research agenda and a clear potential for external
funding, as well as potential for scholarship or creative
expression to complement and expand existing expertise in the
department
For tenure-eligible positions at the Associate Professor or
Professor ranks, a well-developed scholarly/research portfolio with
evidence of multi-disciplinary applications and external funding
appropriate to complement and expand existing expertise in the
department
Preferred Qualifications:
A minimum of three (3) years' experience in college level
teaching is preferred
Completion of a formalized leadership program is
preferred
Three recent letters of reference, or contact information for at
least three references, will be required for consideration.

Duties & Responsibilities:
The VCU School of Medicine communications team is seeking an

Additionally, this position will work with the rest of the SOM

faculty excellence and honors.
This position will also serve as the primary communicator for the
school’s Office of Research. A complex and extensive research
enterprise that partners across departments, schools and the VCU
Health System, SOM researchers received more than $316iverM in

with the school’s Office of Research to support and elevate the

research and interdisciplinary collaboration.
This role will serve as the day-to-day lead for strategic

programs across departments. This position will amplify school
research accomplishments while also creating and executing clear,

Partner with faculty and research leadership to advise on

jobs.title: Assistant Professor, Art & Design, Tenure Track
jobs.description:
The Burgum Arts & Sciences Endowed Chair, Assistant Professor of Emerging Technologies and Artificial Intelligence (New Media) in the Visual Arts. This is a tenure-track position.
The Department of Art & Design is seeking to hire a tenure-track Assistant Professor in any studio art with a specialization in Emerging Technologies and Artificial Intelligence (New Media) in the Visual Arts. In addition to salary and benefits, the Burgum Arts & Sciences Endowed Chair will receive professional development funding annually to support travel as well as equipment for teaching and creative activities/research. The successful candidate will be expected to teach undergraduate and graduate courses, produce creative activities/scholarship, and do service that contributes to the mission of the department, the college, and the university.
Purpose of Position: The Department of Art & Design at the University of North Dakota is seeking an Assistant Professor in any studio art with a specialization in Emerging Technologies and Artificial Intelligence (New Media) in the Visual Arts as the Burgum Arts & Sciences Endowed Chair. The department looks to hire a colleague who holds an MFA in any art form in the visual arts whose creative practices substantially utilize new technological media and/or AI to produce artistic objects and/or immersive environments. The ideal candidate may also engage in original scholarship and/or theory on issues related to the integration of emerging technologies in the artworld and analysis of its impacts within broader social and cultural contexts. This is a 9-month, tenure-track position supported by the Burgum Arts & Sciences Endowed Chair Endowment, contingent on availability of funding.
The Department of Art & Design is housed in the College of Arts & Sciences and currently offers an MFA in Visual Arts, BFAs in Visual Arts and Graphic Design, a BA in Visual Arts, and minors in Art History, Graphic Design, and Visual Arts. The department is the recipient of a generous annually recurring endowment from the Myers Foundations that supports a robust visiting artists program, curation of art exhibitions, and resources to enhance student teaching and learning among other activities.
Established in 1883, the University of North Dakota is the oldest research university in North Dakota. Founded with a strong liberal arts foundation, it is the state’s flagship university and is classified by the Carnegie Foundation as having very high research activity. UND offers degrees in more than 225 fields of study and enrolls nearly 16,000 students. It is the home of the state’s only School of Law and School of Medicine. The School of Medicine and Health Sciences has major initiatives in rural and public health, and Aerospace is home to one of the first and largest unmanned aerial vehicle programs in the world.
UND is located in Grand Forks, North Dakota, a vibrant college town of over 57,000 people located on the border of North Dakota and Minnesota. Short commutes, a great public-school system, high-quality medical facilities, low crime, ample parks and theaters, and a cost of living below that found in large American cities are some of Grand Forks’ advantages. Ranked as one of the top 5 Best Small College Towns, and America’s Best Hockey Town, Grand Forks offers stellar quality of life without the metropolitan hassles.
UND and the College of Arts & Sciences value diverse perspectives and seek applicants to help students succeed. The University of North Dakota is supportive of dual-career assistance both within the University and the local community. Please contact UND’s Recruiting Manager, Hannah Whalen (Hannah.Whalen@UND.edu), to explore dual-career opportunities.
Duties & Responsibilities
The successful applicant will receive a contract with an approximate distribution of 52% teaching (3/2), 38% research/creative activity, and 10% service. More specific duties and responsibilities for this position include:
Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in a studio art with an emphasis on the integration of emerging technologies and AI (new media)
Advise and mentor undergraduate and graduate students
Serve as a catalyst for attracting and supporting graduate students in the MFA in Visual Arts Program
Establish a solid and productive research program with emphasis in area of specialization, including seeking extramural funding to support individual and collaborative projects aligned with the UND LEADS Strategic Plan
Submit an annual report of creative/research, teaching, and public outreach activities supported by professional development funds provided by the Burgum Arts & Sciences Endowed Chair Endowment.
Required Competencies
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
The ability to teach, inspire, and mentor students
Effective interpersonal skills, including the ability to collaborate effectively with faculty, staff, and students
Time management and organizational skills
Competent in using technology and the ability to adopt new tools for both on-campus and online course delivery.
Minimum Requirements
MFA in Visual Arts (any studio art)
Successful completion of criminal history background check.
In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the US and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire.
Preferred Qualifications
Record of success as a practicing artist with established exhibition/creative activities significantly involving the utilization of emerging technologies and/or AI (new media)
Record of scholarship and/or theory on issues related to the integration of emerging technologies and AI in the artworld and broader social and cultural contexts
Teaching experience at the undergraduate and graduate levels in studio art
Experience developing and teaching courses on the utilization of emerging technologies and AI in the visual arts
Experience with teaching and course development for in-person and online environments, including asynchronous delivery methods
Experience mentoring undergraduate and graduate students and supervising BFA/MFA research/creative projects
Record of involvement in seeking extramural funding
To Apply
For full consideration, applications must be received by November 12, 2026, and include the following materials:
Curriculum Vitae
Cover Letter detailing your interest in the position and your qualifications highlighting the integration of emerging technologies and AI into your artistic practices, research, and teaching
Research/Creative Activities Portfolio: artist statement and 15-20 examples of current studio artwork
Teaching Portfolio: Statement of Teaching Philosophy, 2 sample syllabi (1 introductory level and 1 advanced or graduate level), sample assignments/course materials, student evaluations, and student work samples (no more than 15)
List of three (3) references with contact information
Unofficial transcripts. Please note that the selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts upon hire.
Position is open until filled.
Questions can be directed to the Department Chair, Lucian Stone at lucian.stone@und.edu.

jobs.description:
Job Description
Overview
AUBURN UNIVERSITY
DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN DEVELOPMENT AND FAMILY SCIENCE
ASSISTANT/ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR IN MARRIAGE AND FAMILY
THERAPY
POSITION AVAILABILITY: The Department of Human Development
and Family Science (HDFS) in the College of Human Sciences at
Auburn University invites applications for a nine-month,
tenure-track position at the assistant/associate level in
Marriage and Family Therapy (MFT), a fully COAMFTE
accredited, terminal Master’s degree program. The position will
begin August 2027.
THE DEPARTMENT: The Department includes 32 faculty members
(20 full-time, tenure-track and 12 non-tenure track focused on
teaching, research or outreach work), 285 undergraduates, and 55
graduate students and offers undergraduate, masters, and doctoral
degrees. It administers the Auburn University Marriage and Family
Therapy Center which houses the masters-level Marriage and Family
Therapy program; the Auburn University Early Learning Center; the
Harris Early Learning Center in Birmingham, AL; and the Family
Child Care Partnerships program. HDFS also administers
undergraduate and graduate certificate programs in Health Equity
Science as well as an Advanced Methods Certificate. The MFT program
is fully integrated within the broader HDFS department, and faculty
contribute to the department's teaching, research, and service
missions while bringing expertise in systemic clinical practice and
training. The MFT program is a full-time cohort model that accepts
6 students each year.
THE UNIVERSITY : Auburn University is a land-grant
institution with a student enrollment of over 28,000 undergraduate
students and 6,000 professional and graduate students. The
University provides instruction in approximately 70 academic
departments and maintains graduate research and public service
programs. The University is located in the city of Auburn in
east-central Alabama near several large metropolitan areas of
Alabama and Georgia. To learn more about Auburn University, visit
https://www.auburn.edu/academic/provost/facultyjobs/
. Auburn University is understanding of and sensitive to the family
needs of faculty, including dual-career couples.
Responsibilities
The successful candidate will contribute to the department through
excellence in research, teaching, clinical supervision, and
service. Responsibilities include maintaining a productive,
externally visible program of research; pursuing extramural funding
opportunities; teaching undergraduate and graduate courses within
the HDFS curriculum; providing supervision and training within the
MFT program; mentoring graduate students and chairing thesis and
dissertation committees; and participating in service activities
that support the university, profession, and community. The
department seeks candidates with a well-defined program of research
and welcomes candidates with research expertise in any area of HDFS
or MFT scholarship.
Qualifications
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: Candidates must possess a Ph.D. in
MFT or HDFS (if the latter, the applicant must have an MS in MFT)
at the time employment is scheduled to begin; AAMFT approved
supervisor status or supervisor candidate status; and MFT licensure
in Alabama or eligibility to obtain within 90 days of date of hire.
Experience or readiness to teach core MFT courses, supervising
clinical graduate students, and conducting research to advance the
fields of HDFS and/or MFT is necessary. The candidate must be
fluent in English, must possess excellent written and interpersonal
communication skills, and must meet eligibility requirements to
work in the United States at the time the appointment is scheduled
to begin and continue working legally for the proposed term of
employment. Candidates for appointment at the Associate Professor
rank must demonstrate an established record of scholarly
productivity and external funding.
APPLICATIONS: Please provide an application letter
addressing the position description, a research statement, a
teaching statement, a current CV, a transcript from the completed
PhD program, and 2-3 recent publications or other scholarly writing
samples. In addition, candidates must provide contact information
for three professional references who will be contacted for a
reference letter upon invitation for on-campus interviews. Review
of applications will begin November 30, 2026 and will continue
until the position is filled. Questions about the position should
be addressed to Dr. Mallory Lucier-Greer, Search Committee Chair,
at mluciergreer@auburn.edu .
Minimum Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
Contract Type
Continuing
Why Work at Auburn?
Ready to lead and shape the future of higher education? Apply
today! War Eagle!
Life-Changing Impact : Our work changes lives through
research, instruction, and outreach, making a lasting impact on our
students, our communities, and the world.
Culture of Excellence : We are committed to leveraging
our strengths, resources, collaboration, and innovation as a top
employer in higher education.
We’re Here for You : Auburn offers generous benefits,
educational opportunities, and a culture of support and work/life
balance.
Sweet Home Alabama : The Auburn/Opelika area offers
southern charm, vibrant downtown scenes, top-ranked schools, and
easy access to Atlanta, Birmingham, and the Gulf of Mexico
beaches.
A Place for Everyone : Auburn is committed to fostering
an environment where all faculty, staff, and students are welcomed,
valued, respected, and engaged.

It is our policy to provide equal employment and education
opportunities for all individuals without regard to race, color,
national origin, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender
identity, gender expression, pregnancy, age, disability, protected
veteran status, genetic information, or any other classification
protected by applicable law. Please visit the Office of Equal
Opportunity Compliance's website to learn more.
