jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Social & Digital Media in Journalism
jobs.institution: University of Arkansas-School of Journalism and Strategic Media
jobs.description:
The School of Journalism and Strategic Media (SJSM) in the Fulbright College of Arts and
Sciences at the University of Arkansas invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Social and
Digital Media in Journalism to start in August 2027. This is a standard nine-month faculty appointment.
SJSM seeks a scholar of Social and Digital Media with familiarity of the professional practice of social and digital
media in journalism. SJSM is particularly interested in candidates whose areas of focus expand into any of the
following: strategic communication, digital and platform cultures, media audiences and engagement, online
communities, influencers and creators, digital advertising and public relations, algorithms and platforms,
artificial intelligence and media, misinformation, or the social and cultural implications of digital media.
The successful candidate will maintain an active program of research and/or scholarly/creative activity and
contribute to the School's undergraduate and graduate curricula. Teaching responsibilities may include existing
courses in social and digital media as well as courses in the candidate's areas of expertise across the School's
journalism, multimedia, and advertising/public relations programs. The successful candidate will have
opportunities to develop new courses that complement and expand the School's curriculum in social and digital
media.
The position carries a 2-2 teaching load and includes requirements for research and service.
Faculty hired in this position will have an opportunity to be a part of Fulbright College’s multidisciplinary
Democracy as a Public Good cluster hire at the University of Arkansas. Through its Democracy as a Public Good
Initiative, the College will advance the University’s land-grant mission by expanding capacity to generate
knowledge that informs public understanding, contributes to policy and practice, and connects Arkansas to
national and international conversations about societal good. Building on existing campus expertise in issues
ranging from norms of democratic communication, free speech, media ethics and literacy, humanitarian
governance and civil society, risks that AI poses to democratic governance, immigration, and public law, new
faculty members participating in the cluster will advance their research agendas through mentoring and
opportunities for collaboration—both with other scholars and with communities in the state—that may result in
peer-reviewed publications, external funding, and new approaches to the pressing challenges that democracy
faces. The successful candidate for this position will have an opportunity to join a community of scholars
committed to confronting major issues, generating new knowledge, and providing research-based solutions that
investigate and strengthen democratic culture for people living in Arkansas and beyond.
This is an in-person position. Most university classes are offered face-to-face, and extensive in-person
engagement in such activities as office hours, student advising, and departmental, college, and university
committee meetings is essential to advancing student success and departmental effectiveness.

Classification Title:
CLIN AST/ASO PROF

Doctoral Level Licensed Psychologist (or license-eligible), Doctorate in Clinical and/or Counseling Psychology, with clinical experience working within an acute care hospital setting.
Job Description:
The University of Florida College of Medicine – Jacksonville, Department of Surgery, Division of Acute Care Surgery, seeks a full-time faculty position for a Surgical Psychologist at the non-tenure accruing level of Clinical Assistant or Associate Professor.
The position will include overall responsibility for the on-going, day-to-day operations of the psychological services/family management component of the trauma system, inclusive of crisis interventions, grief counseling, individual, family and group therapies, stress debriefings, psychological assessments and diagnoses, in-patient consultation/liaison services, and out-patient follow-up/referral as needed. Also provide on-going stress management consultation and debriefings as needed for surgical residents, medical students, nursing staff, and other allied health professionals.
Must have experience in program development and initiative and must be familiar working with a culturally diverse patient population that will include adults and children. Teaching responsibilities include co-direct supervision of the psychology post-doctoral fellow within the Division of Acute Care Surgery, and clinical teaching to medical residents, students, allied professionals and nursing staff on the psychological aspects of physical injury and other related topics specific to a collaborative care model, i.e. effective communication, capacity issues, stress management. Expected administrative responsibilities include membership on various committees at the hospital, local and University level. Also responsible for consistently obtaining and maintaining extra-mural funding for research activities, development and administration of research studies, scholarly presentations at the local, regional and national level, and publications in peer-reviewed journals.
About UF Health:
UF Health is the Southeast's premier academic health center and an integral part of the University of Florida. Our mission is to promote health through outstanding and high-quality patient care, innovative and rigorous education in the health professions and biomedical sciences, and research across the spectrum of basic, translational and clinical investigation. UF Health encompasses the Gainesville-based University of Florida colleges of Dentistry, Medicine, Nursing, Pharmacy, Public Health and Health Professions, and Veterinary Medicine; the UF Health Shands family of hospitals in Gainesville; UF Health Jacksonville medical center; UF Health North; an academic campus in Jacksonville that is home to the UF College of Medicine – Jacksonville and includes degree programs offered by the colleges of Nursing and Pharmacy; UF Health St. Johns in St. Augustine; UF Health Neighborhood Hospital in Ocala; and our campus in Central Florida, which includes UF Health Spanish Plaines Hospital and UF Health Leesburg Hospital. It also includes primary care and specialty practices throughout Central, North Central and northern Florida and Southeast Georgia. The UF Health network of hospitals and physician practices manages more than 3 million inpatient and outpatient visits each year, and serves patients from all 67 Florida counties, from across the nation and from dozens of countries around the world.
About College of Medicine – Jacksonville (COM-J):
The UF College of Medicine – Jacksonville is the largest of the three colleges at the Health Science Center Jacksonville. The college's 16 clinical science departments house more than 500 faculty members, 1,560 staff and 450 residents and fellows, as well as medical students from UF and around the country. We offer an incredible breadth of clinical training programs and proud to train many of best primary care providers and specialists throughout the region, the state and the country.
Research, discovery and innovation are critical aspects of our clinical campus and we have some of the country's leading researchers at our locations searching for and finding new treatments and clinical options.
The UF College of Medicine – Jacksonville faculty, administrators, residents, fellows, students and staff work as a team in pursuit of our common mission — to heal, to comfort, to educate and to discover through quality health care, elimination of health disparities, medical education, innovation and research.
To learn more about our college, leadership, mission, faculty resources, and the city of Jacksonville visit https://med.jax.ufl.edu/administrative-affairs/faculty-orientation-guide/.

Doctoral Level Licensed Psychologist (or license-eligible), Doctorate in Clinical and/or Counseling Psychology, with clinical experience working within an acute care hospital setting.
Preferred:
Clinical experience working within an acute care, hospital setting, as part of an interdisciplinary treatment team; experience in teaching within an academic medical setting; research experience; versed in clinical interventions with patients across the lifespan and also within a diverse patient population.

Job Details
IMPORTANT APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS:
Upload Resume or Curriculum Vitae for automatic
population of information to the application.

on your Resume/CV will be parsed and input into your Montclair
application.

containing information that the system parsed – the software is
intelligent, but you need to verify that the data is accurate.
In the “My Experience” section, you will find a
Resume/CV upload option where you can submit your cover letter and
all other supporting documents.
Note: If you have an expansive CV, we recommend that you
apply manually and only include the positions you have held in the
last ten (10) years . You will then be able to attach your
Resume/CV, as well as all other supporting documentation in the "My
Experience" section of your application.
Job Description
POSITION DESCRIPTION:
The Economics Department at Montclair State University seeking to
hire an Applied Empirical Economist with expertise in conducting
rigorous, data-driven research that informs public policy and
decision-making. This position offers the opportunity to conduct
high-impact research that contributes to evidence-based policies
aimed at improving economic opportunity, health outcomes, housing
affordability, and equitable access to emerging technologies.
The successful candidate is expected to investigate how artificial
intelligence (AI) and emerging technologies are transforming public
policy, with particular attention to their impact on areas such as
community development, health care, and affordable housing. The
candidate should demonstrate an interest in leveraging innovative
analytical tools and interdisciplinary approaches to address
complex policy challenges.
The successful candidate will be expected to establish a strong,
externally funded research program by securing competitive grants
and contracts from federal agencies, foundations, and other funding
organizations. They should demonstrate the potential to build
collaborative partnerships across disciplines and with community,
government, and industry stakeholders to advance impactful,
policy-relevant research.
Teaching: The standard annual teaching load for tenure-track
faculty is 12 teaching credit hours (TCH) a semester, with
additional TCH reassigned time (course release) available for
faculty with additional responsibilities such as mentoring doctoral
faculty or administering programs. Faculty are expected to center
student success and measurable learning outcomes through clear
course design, inclusive pedagogies, and the integration of
emerging disciplinary and pedagogical developments.
Responsibilities include classroom instruction, student mentoring
and advising, and developing and updating courses and curricula
aligned with student demands and institutional strategic
priorities.
Research, Scholarship, and Creative Activity: Faculty are
expected to be productive scholars or artists whose work embodies
formal inquiry or creative expression that expands, enhances, or
applies knowledge. Research results must be shared in significant
national and/or international scholarly or artistic venues
following rigorous review. The University supports these endeavors
through the Faculty Scholarship Program (FSP), which typically
provides research-active faculty with up to 6 TCH of reassigned
time per academic year to pursue their scholarly agenda.
Service: Faculty members are expected to perform valuable
service to the department, college/school, university, and
professional communities. This includes participating in shared
governance, academic program vitality, and sharing professional
expertise within and beyond the University. Service activities are
separate and distinct from the specific assignments for which
faculty members receive course release.
THE DEPARTMENT OF ECONOMICS:
The Department of Economics offers a BA in Economics, a minor in
Economics, and a concentration in Asset Management. Separately, the
department supports the MBA Program in teaching both required and
elective graduate level courses in economics. As the department has
a rich portfolio of programs, we seek candidates who can be
effective in teaching across all programs -- both introductory and
advanced courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels. The
candidate selected is expected to pursue scholarly research leading
to publications in high-quality, peer-reviewed journals and
conference proceedings and increase the visibility of the economics
department by developing relationships with external stakeholders.
In addition, the candidate is expected to serve on department,
school, and university-level committees, advise students, and
participate in curriculum review and development activities.
THE FELICIANO SCHOOL OF BUSINESS
The Feliciano School of Business is committed to transforming
today’s students into tomorrow’s business leaders through
innovative teaching, experiential learning, and strong industry
engagement. Accredited by AACSB International, the School offers
distinctive programs at both the undergraduate and graduate
programs, including the BS in Business Analytics, BS in Business
Administration (eight concentrations), BS in Accounting, BA in
Economics, BA in Hospitality, Sports, Events and Tourism, MBA, MS
in Accounting, MS in Business Analytics, MS in Digital Marketing
Analytics, and MS in Human Resource Analytics, as well as a range
of minors and undergraduate and graduate certificates. Among the
School’s strengths are its world-class faculty and staff, diverse
and driven student body, engaged alumni network, and strong
corporate and institutional partnerships. Both academic and
program-related activities are focused on student success and
experiential learning beyond the classroom. The Ellyn A. McColgan
Center for Student Services further supports students through
results-driven advising, career guidance, and access to
internships, co-ops, and mentorship opportunities that help prepare
them for success in today’s dynamic business environment. The
School is also home to the Feliciano Center for Entrepreneurship +
Innovation, a collaborative community that supports innovation and
entrepreneurship through mentorship, strategic guidance, and
opportunities that help students and entrepreneurs develop and grow
their ideas.
Nearly 120 full-time faculty members and 41 professional staff,
with terminal degrees and advanced training from leading
universities, bring a wealth of academic and industry expertise to
the School.
QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED:
● Earned doctorate or appropriate terminal degree.
● Record of achievement and potential for future success in
research, scholarship or creative activity.
● Demonstrated excellence in teaching all students.
● A record that demonstrates interest and commitment to
service.
PREFERRED
● Significant record of scholarly/creative work.
STARTING DATE August 27, 2027
REQUIRED MATERIALS
Cover letter, curriculum vitae, research and teaching
statements, and representative publications, which can be uploaded
during the application process.
Candidates who are shortlisted will be asked to supply 3
letters of recommendation separately.
APPLY BY: The position is open until filled, and application
review begins immediately.
Salary Range
$112,451.79-$124,505.29 Annually
The position may also be eligible for comprehensive benefits,
including health insurance, retirement plans, and tuition
assistance. For further details, please visit: https://www.montclair.edu/human-resources/benefits/
Montclair State University considers factors such as, but not
limited to, scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate’s
relevant work experience, education, skills, and internal equity,
when extending an offer.
Salary offers for internal employees who are part of a collective
bargaining unit (CBU) and are applying to a position that is within

provisions.

jobs.title: Tenure-Track Faculty Position In the Biomedical Engineering
jobs.description:
Tenure-Track Faculty Position in Biomedical Engineering
In the Department of Chemical & Biomedical Engineering
Florida A&M University–Florida State University College of Engineering
(Permanent Tenure-Track Position)
The Department of Chemical & Biomedical Engineering (CBE) at the Florida A&M University (FAMU)–Florida State University (FSU) College of Engineering invites applications from highly qualified individuals for a tenure track faculty position in biomedical engineering, in the city of Tallahassee, Florida. We are seeking faculty candidates for an assistant professor position; however, exceptional candidates at higher ranks will be considered.
CBE has a dynamic group of faculty members actively involved in research encompassing various areas of chemical engineering, materials science and engineering, and biomedical engineering. The department has seen major expansion in the graduate and undergraduate biomedical and chemical engineering education and research activities since the establishment of an undergraduate BME degree in 2019 through the hiring of 15 new faculty members and approximately doubling of the graduate and undergraduate enrollment. The expanding college of engineering has increased research expenditures by 195% over the last 5 years ($87.6M in FY2025) and is continuing to grow its faculty and campus. A new research facility (the Interdisciplinary Research and Commercialization Building) was completed in Spring of 2025, and an additional engineering building was recently funded by the state legislature. Our nationally recognized and award-winning faculty members have access to state-of-the-art laboratories for research in biomedical and chemical engineering and the two programs are closely integrated in research and education. In addition to present faculty at the FAMU-FSU College of Engineering and its associated research centers, successful candidates will have many opportunities to interact and collaborate at both universities (including the FSU College of Medicine, the National High Magnetic Field Laboratory, and the FAMU College of Pharmacy).
The FAMU-FSU College of Engineering is the nexus of two major public universities, each with a distinct mission but focused on world-class engineering education and research. Created by the Florida Legislature in 1982, the joint institution is the college of engineering for both Florida A&M and Florida State universities. This unique combination of focus, resources and mission from our parent institutions has created on our campus a truly innovative atmosphere that leverages the benefits of the traditional HBCU model with the innovations of an R1 public research university. The College fosters interdisciplinary research and collaboration across engineering, science, medicine, and other fields, while providing faculty, researchers, and students access to the complementary expertise and resources of both universities. All seven of the college’s eligible undergraduate degree programs are accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.
Candidates must possess an earned Ph.D. in biomedical engineering, chemical engineering, or a related discipline, and demonstrate documented potential for outstanding research. Although all applications will be reviewed, priority will be given to candidates that complement and build upon our research in polymeric biomaterials, regenerative medicine, and 3D bioprinting with a goal of aligning with the new FSU Health Initiative. Areas of particular interest include stem cell engineering, nanoparticle engineering, gene editing, immunomodulation, biomaterials, and biomedical imaging.
Successful candidates are expected to develop research programs that are internationally recognized with significant and sustained funding, incorporate interdisciplinary collaboration with researchers across campus, and demonstrate a strong commitment to excellence in education. Teaching undergraduate and graduate courses and supervising undergraduate, graduate, and post-doctoral researchers are expected.
If qualified and interested in the position, applicants should apply to Florida State University at https://hr.fsu.edu/facultyjobs, Job ID: 63474 with the following documents:
A cover letter
A full curriculum vitae
A 2 to 3-page research statement. This statement should clearly indicate how the proposed research efforts will connect to other efforts in the Department and universities.
A one-page teaching statement
No more than four selected publications for review
The names and contact information of four potential references

jobs.title: Assistant Professor & Associate Director, Center for Media Ethics & Literacy
jobs.institution: University of Arkansas-School of Journalism and Strategic Media
jobs.description:
: The School of Journalism and Strategic Media at the University of Arkansas invites
applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position. This hire will serve as the Associate Director of the
Center for Media Ethics and Literacy, reporting to the director. We are seeking a scholar whose research and
teaching align with our faculty cluster in Democracy, Ethics, and Immigration. The successful candidate will
combine scholarly excellence with a commitment to public engagement and pedagogical innovation within a
rapidly growing School of Journalism. This is a standard nine-month academic appointment.
Key Responsibilities
Research & Center Leadership:
- Center Administration: Serve as the Associate Director of the center, providing strategic leadership to
the College and the University.
- Scholarly Production: Produce high-impact scholarly research in the fields of media ethics, literacy and
theory, especially news literacy, civic engagement, and democratic practices.
- Public Engagement: Actively engage and educate the public and industry professionals on ethics and
literacy issues in the news cycle through the Center’s website, social media platforms, and other publicfacing initiatives.
- External Support: Pursue external research support (grants, fellowships, etc.) to advance the strategic
goals of the Center, the School, and the University.
Teaching & Mentoring:
- Instruction: Teach undergraduate and graduate students in the School of Journalism, utilizing innovative
media literacy pedagogy and practices to help students navigate the intersection of theoretical ethics
and real-world newsroom challenges, drawing upon professional experience in journalism and
reporting.
- Mentorship: Serve as a mentor and advisor to SJSM students.
- Committee Service: Serve on thesis and honors committees and participate in departmental, college,
and university governance as appropriate for a tenure-track faculty rank.
Faculty hired in this position will have an opportunity to be a part of Fulbright College’s multidisciplinary
Democracy as a Public Good cluster hire at the University of Arkansas. Through its Democracy as a Public Good
Initiative, the College will advance the University’s land-grant mission by expanding capacity to generate
knowledge that informs public understanding, contributes to policy and practice, and connects Arkansas to
national and international conversations about societal good. Building on existing campus expertise in issues
ranging from norms of democratic communication, free speech, media ethics and literacy, humanitarian
governance and civil society, risks that AI poses to democratic governance, immigration, and public law, new
faculty members participating in the cluster will advance their research agendas through mentoring and
opportunities for collaboration—both with other scholars and with communities in the state—that may result in
peer-reviewed publications, external funding, and new approaches to the pressing challenges that democracy
faces. The successful candidate for this position will have an opportunity to join a community of scholars
committed to confronting major issues, generating new knowledge, and providing research-based solutions that
investigate and strengthen democratic culture for people living in Arkansas and beyond.
This is an in-person position. Most university classes are offered face-to-face, and extensive in-person
engagement in such activities as office hours, student advising, and departmental, college, and university
committee meetings is essential to advancing student success and departmental effectiveness.
Regular, reliable, and non-disruptive attendance is an essential job duty, as is the ability to create and maintain
collegial, harmonious working relationships with others.
About the Department:
The School of Journalism and Strategic Media at the University of Arkansas is fully accredited by ACEJMC,
offering a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism with concentrations in Broadcast Journalism, Journalism, and
Multimedia Journalism, as well as a Bachelor of Arts in Advertising and Public Relations. The Media Law course is
required for students in both degree programs. SJSM also offers a Master of Arts in Journalism – in total serving
more than 950 undergrads and grads in AY25-26. For more information go to https://journalism.uark.edu/.
Duties will include:
 40% Teaching or Professional Performance
 40% Research/Scholarly and/or Creative Activities
 20% Academic Service Activities
Minimum Qualifications:
 Terminal degree in Journalism, Media Studies, Communication (or a closely related field) from an
accredited institution of higher education conferred by the date of initial appointment.
 A demonstrated record of exceptional teaching and mentoring at the graduate level and/or
undergraduate level, especially journalism-related courses.
 Evidence of, or a demonstrated potential for publishing high-quality, peer-reviewed research and a clear
vision for Center-led research initiatives.
 Demonstrated experience in journalism and reporting, combined with a strong working knowledge of
media-industry ethical standards and practices and evidence-based media literacy pedagogy.
Preferred Qualifications:
 Previous experience in the media industry or non-profit leadership roles.
 Experience in securing external funding and managing research budgets.
 A track record of public-facing communication (e.g., op-eds, public lectures, active media presence).
 Experience in mentoring undergraduate and graduate students in independent research.
Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs)
 Current knowledge in the field of media ethics, literacy and theory, especially news literacy, civic
engagement, and democratic practices.
 Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
 Ability to develop media ethics and literacy curriculum and research agendas.
APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS
Completed applications received by October 18, 2026, will be assured full consideration. Late applications will be
reviewed as necessary to fill the position.
For additional inquiries, please contact the search committee chair, Bobby Foster, at bjf001@uark.edu.
For a complete position announcement and information regarding how to apply, visit
https://uasys.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/en-US/UASYS/details/Assistant-Professor---Associate-Director--Centerfor-Media-Ethics-and-Literacy_R0091691-1?q=R0091691&locations=17a66cdad98201f7890cfb48ca00e249.
Applicants must submit:
 Curriculum vitae
 Cover letter/letter of application
 Teaching philosophy statement
 Research statement
 List of three professional references (name, title, email address, and phone number) willing to provide
letters of recommendation if requested during the application process. Letters of recommendation will
be requested only for candidates selected for interviews.
Review of applications will begin October 18, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled.
As an employer, the University of Arkansas offers a vibrant work environment and a workplace culture that
promotes a healthy work-life balance. The benefits package includes university contributions to health, dental,
life and disability insurance, tuition waivers for employees and their families, 12 official holidays, immediate
leave accrual, and a choice of retirement programs with university contributions ranging from 5 to 10% of
employee salary.
EMPLOYER INFORMATION
The University of Arkansas: Founded in 1871 as a land grant institution, the University of Arkansas is classified
by the Carnegie Foundation among the top two percent of universities in the nation with the highest level of
research activity. Ten colleges and schools serve more than 27,100 students with more than 200 academic
programs. University of Arkansas students earn nationally competitive awards at an impressive rate and
represent 50 states and more than 120 countries. The University of Arkansas is committed to providing an
educational and work environment in which thought, creativity, and growth are stimulated, and in which
individuals are free to realize their full potential.
Fulbright College: The Fulbright College of Arts and Sciences is a vital public good. We provide a
transformational education that prepares all students to lead and thrive in a complex world. Our research,
scholarship, and creative expression address society’s great challenges and push the boundaries of human
understanding. As the largest and most academically diverse unit on campus, with 3 schools, 16 departments,
and 43 academic programs and research centers, Fulbright College brings the world to Arkansas and Arkansas to
the world.
The Community: Fayetteville is home to the University of Arkansas campus and is known for its spectacular
views and ample green spaces. Fayetteville is considered one of the country’s finest college towns, and the
surrounding northwest Arkansas region is regularly ranked as one of the best places to live in the U.S. Some of
the nation’s best outdoor amenities and most spectacular hiking trails are within a short drive of campus.
For more information, visit: https://diversitynwa.com/
Culture in Northwest Arkansas
About Fayetteville
About University of Arkansas
The University of Arkansas is an equal opportunity institution. The University does not discriminate in its
education programs or activities (including in admission and employment) on the basis of any category or status
protected by law, including age, race, color, national origin, disability, religion, protected veteran status, military
service, genetic information, sex, sexual preference, or pregnancy. Federal law prohibits the University from
discriminating on these bases. Questions or concerns about the application of Title IX, which prohibits
discrimination on the basis of sex, may be sent to the University's Title IX Coordinator and to the U.S.
Department of Education Office for Civil Rights. Persons must have proof of legal authority to work in the United
States on the first day of employment. All application information is subject to public disclosure under the
Arkansas Freedom of Information Act.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor Adjoint
jobs.description:
Job Summary
The Adjoint Professor will support the research and educational
mission of BioServe Space Technologies and the Department of
Aerospace Engineering Sciences through technical advising, research
collaboration, student mentorship, and engagement with the broader
human spaceflight and commercial space communities. The position
will leverage extensive experience in spaceflight hardware
development, space life sciences, payload integration and
operations, and research aboard the International Space Station and
other spaceflight platforms.
CU is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all
applicable federal, state, and local laws governing
nondiscrimination in employment. We are committed to creating a
workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and
dignity, and we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to
apply, including protected veterans and individuals with
disabilities.
Who We Are
BioServe Space Technologies is a Center within the Ann and HJ Smead
Aerospace Engineering Sciences department at CU Boulder. Since its
inception in 1987, BioServe has designed, built, and flown hundreds
of microgravity life science research experiments and hardware on
over 75 spaceflight missions. BioServe has a full suite of
spaceflight-certified hardware available for use by its customers
and partners. Past partners include pharmaceutical and
biotechnology companies, Universities, NIH, NASA-funded and other
government agency researchers. BioServe is a full-service, turn-key
organization that enables its customers and partners to focus
solely on research while BioServe manages all other activities
required to successfully fly experiments in microgravity.
What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be
Provide technical and strategic guidance to BioServe Space
Technologies’ research and technology development programs.
Contribute to research proposals, publications, and future
research opportunities where appropriate and consistent with
applicable conflict-of-interest and outside-activity
requirements.
Advise and mentor undergraduate and graduate students involved
in spaceflight research and hardware development.
Support student education through guest lectures, project
reviews, and other teaching activities.
Participate in technical reviews and provide subject-matter
expertise in spaceflight hardware, payload development, space life
sciences, and mission implementation.
Help strengthen connections between CU Boulder, BioServe,
government agencies, academia, and the commercial human spaceflight
ecosystem.
Contribute to the development of future research opportunities
aboard commercial space stations and other emerging spaceflight
platforms.
What We Can Offer
This is a 0% time, zero compensation appointment.
Benefits
At the University of Colorado Boulder , we are
committed to supporting the holistic health and well-being of our
employees. Our comprehensive benefits package includes medical,
dental, and retirement plans; generous paid time off; tuition
assistance for you and your dependents; and an ECO Pass for local
transit. As one of Boulder County’s largest employers, CU Boulder
offers an inspiring academic community and access to world-class
outdoor recreation. In fact, CU Boulder has been named one of
Forbes' America's Best
Large Employers , ranking #4 among large employers in Colorado
and #28 among universities nationwide. Explore additional perks and
programs through the CU Advantage program.
Be Statements
Be empowered. Be game-changing. Be Boulder.
What We Require
Ph.D. in Aerospace Engineering, Bioastronautics.
Demonstrated 10 years plus experience developing, integrating,
and operating spaceflight hardware and scientific payloads within
BioServe Space Technologies.
Demonstrated 4 years plus experience leading spaceflight
research programs within BioServe Space Technologies as Principal
Investigator or technical/program lead.
Strong knowledge of human spaceflight, space life sciences, and
microgravity research.
Experience mentoring undergraduate and graduate students.
Demonstrated ability to collaborate across academia,
government, and the commercial space industry.
Special Instructions
To inquire about this role please do not apply here, instead email
your cv to Lauren Cole at lauren.cole@colorado.edu.
This announcement will remain active through September 22,
2026.
In compliance with the Colorado Job Application Fairness Act, in
any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying
information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school
attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting
or removing this information.
Posting Contact Information
Posting Contact Name: Boulder Campus Human Resources
Posting Contact Email: Recruiting@colorado.edu

jobs.title: Tenure-Track Faculty in Electrical, Computer and Energy Engineering
jobs.description:
Job Summary
The Department of Electrical, Computer and Energy Engineering
(ECEE) is hiring two tenure-track professors at the Assistant
Professor rank. We will consider candidates in all areas of
electrical and computer engineering. Potential research areas of
interest include communications, power, sensing, controls,
robotics, signals, computing hardware, and theory for quantum
technologies. We are particularly interested in candidates who
bridge disciplines, have synergistic interests with existing
faculty, or bring unique capabilities.
CU is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all
applicable federal, state, and local laws governing
nondiscrimination in employment. We are committed to creating a
workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and
dignity, and we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to
apply, including protected veterans and individuals with
disabilities.
Who We Are
The University of Colorado Boulder (CU Boulder) is one of
Colorado’s flagship public institutions and among the most
research-active public universities in the country. The College of
Engineering and Applied Science is the second largest school or
college on the CU Boulder campus and boasts top-tier rankings for
both its graduate and undergraduate engineering programs, earning
the 11th spot among public graduate programs and 17th nationwide
for undergraduate engineering. Multiple specialty areas are also
ranked within the top 20. Equally important, we are committed to
fostering a diverse and academically excellent community. Our
approximately 250 tenure-track, 120 instructional-track, and 30
research-track faculty serve more than 6,000 undergraduate
students, 1,300 master’s students, and 850 PhD students. Our
college's strategic vision has three core foci: (i) research and
innovation, (ii) education, and (iii) inclusion. We believe our
success depends on faculty who actively work to create an
environment where all students can thrive and who are committed to
the campus plan for creating and
sustaining supportive campus environments .
To learn more about the College of Engineering and Applied Science
please visit our website .
The ECEE Department includes 3 University Distinguished Professors,
8 endowed chairs, 40 tenure/tenure-track faculty, 8 teaching
faculty, and 4 research faculty. Faculty honors include 16 IEEE
Fellows, 4 members of the US National Academy of Engineering, a
National Science Foundation (NSF) Presidential Faculty Fellow, and
22 NSF CAREER Award recipients. The ECEE program consists of about
650 undergraduate and 450 graduate students and has averaged over
$16 million in annual research expenditures. The department
maintains close ties with local industry and national
institutes/labs such as NIST, NLR, and NOAA.
More information about the Electrical, Computer & Energy
Engineering Department is available on the
department website .
Information on the Electrical, Computer & Energy Engineering
Department's strategic vision can be found here .
What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be
Successful candidates will be expected to engage in
undergraduate and graduate teaching and mentoring; develop an
externally funded research program in their technical area;
contribute professional leadership and service to their unit, the
college, and their professional community; and cultivate and
contribute to the inclusive excellence of our academic
community.
The typical distribution of work for this role is 40% teaching,
40% scholarly and creative work (research), and 20% leadership and
service.
What You Should Know
The anticipated start date for this position is at the start of
the Fall 2027 semester; however, a later start date may be
negotiated.
What We Can Offer
The anticipated academic-year salary range for this position at
the Assistant Professor rank is $115,000-$145,000.
A relocation stipend may be available within CEAS
guidelines.
CU offers a competitive 401(a) retirement plan, with employees
contributing 5% of their annual eligible compensation and CU
contributing 10% of their eligible compensation. This plan is
standard for most faculty hires. For more information on CU's
retirement benefits, visit our website here .
In addition to a competitive salary, the University of Colorado
Boulder offers a wide variety of other benefits and perks. Links to
some of these are below. To forecast the value of your total
compensation, check out our total compensation
calculator . More information on some of our benefits and perks
is available here: gender-neutral paid
parental leave ; housing down-payment
assistance programs ; dual-career &
relocation resources ; and teaching , research , and
professional development
.
Benefits
At the University of Colorado Boulder , we are
committed to supporting the holistic health and well-being of our
employees. Our comprehensive benefits package includes medical,
dental, and retirement plans; generous paid time off; tuition
assistance for you and your dependents; and an ECO Pass for local
transit. As one of Boulder County’s largest employers, CU Boulder
offers an inspiring academic community and access to world-class
outdoor recreation. In fact, CU Boulder has been named one of
Forbes' America's Best
Large Employers , ranking #4 among large employers in Colorado
and #28 among universities nationwide. Explore additional perks and
programs through the CU Advantage program.
Be Statements
Be challenged. Be impactful. Be Boulder.
What We Require
Applicants must have earned a research doctorate in electrical
engineering, computer engineering or a related field, or have their
degree conferred before starting a tenure-track faculty
appointment.
Special Instructions
To apply, please submit the following materials as individual PDF
files:
Cover Letter: A one-page cover letter describing your
interest in the position and summarizing your personal academic
goals, as well as ways you may fit in the department.
Resume/CV: A current curriculum vitae.
A Statement of Research Philosophy: A statement of your
experience and plans for research and/or creative work that
contributes to the body of knowledge in your field and provides
broader benefits to education and society (2-3 pages).
A Statement of Teaching Philosophy: A statement of your
experience and plans for teaching and mentoring a diverse student
body (2-3 pages).
Leadership, Service and Community Contributions
Statement: In this statement, describe your leadership and
service experience, and demonstrated ability to contribute to a
supportive campus community. Please provide details on your track
record, calibrated to your career stage, that describe the specific
role you played in these efforts. These could include, but are not
limited to service on committees, outreach activities to broaden
engagement within engineering, or participation in advisory boards
or task forces contributing to policies or regulations. In
addition, describe your plans to contribute to our campus plan to
Create Supportive
Environments , and the College of Engineering and
Applied Science Strategic Vision (1-2 pages).
During the application process, you will be asked to provide the
names and contact information for at least three references to
submit a letter of recommendation to be considered along with your
application materials.
Applications will be accepted until the position is filled, however
for full consideration please apply by November 15, 2026
.
Note: Application materials will not be accepted via
email. Applications must be submitted through CU Boulder Jobs . Background checks will be conducted
for all final applicants.
In compliance with the Colorado Job Application Fairness Act, in
any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying
information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school
attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting
or removing this information.

Posting Contact Email: Recruiting@colorado.edu

jobs.title: Assistant Professor in Supply Chain Management & Operations
jobs.description:
Position Overview
School / Campus / College: University of Washington,
Bothell
Organization: Business
Title: Assistant Professor in Supply Chain Management &
Operations
Position Details
Position Description
The School of Business at the University of Washington invites
applications for a Tenure-Track Assistant Professor position in
Supply Chain Management and Operations, with an anticipated start
date of September 16, 2027. We seek applicants who demonstrate
commitment to excellence in research, teaching, and service in a
diverse and inclusive academic community. The successful candidate
will join our faculty on a full-time basis (100% FTE) for a 9-month
academic year, 3-year renewable appointment beginning September 16,
2027.
The successful candidate will be expected to maintain an active
research program and Scholarly Academic status as defined by AACSB;
publish in leading academic journals; teach a variety of
undergraduate and graduate courses in domains such as Operations
Management, Business Statistics, Supply Chain Management,
Information Systems, Business Analytics, and/or Artificial
Intelligence; and provide service to the School, the University,
and the community.
Applicants from research areas including Supply Chain Management,
Operations Management, Information Systems, Artificial
Intelligence, Business Analytics, Management Science, and related
fields are encouraged to apply. We especially welcome candidates
whose research connects supply chain and operations with AI,
machine learning, data-driven decision making, digital and
enterprise systems, resilience, sustainability, and
technology-enabled process innovation. Positive factors for
consideration include a doctorate from a highly regarded,
research-intensive U.S. institution or a comparably strong
international institution.
The School of Business
The UW Bothell School of Business is accredited by AACSB and is
deeply committed to the success of its faculty in research,
teaching, and service. We are well known for our undergraduate,
MBA, and MS Accounting programs, and enrollment has been growing at
a fast pace. Located 15 miles northeast of downtown Seattle, we
work closely with industry leaders, many of whom are headquartered
in the region, as well as smaller, innovative, and rapidly growing
companies in software, retail, medical equipment, biotechnology,
electronics, and aerospace sectors. Our students are drawn from and
work in companies such as Alaska Airlines, Amazon, Amgen, Boeing,
Costco, Expedia, Google, ICOS, Meta, Microsoft, Nintendo, Nvidia,
Phillips, PACCAR, REI, Starbucks, Symetra, T-Mobile, Tableau, and
Zillow, as well as in local, State, and Federal government.
The School’s Supply Chain and Operations faculty are active
scholars whose work has been published in leading journals
includingJournal of Operations Management, Production and
Operations Management, Manufacturing & Service Operations
Management, Operations Research, Decision Sciences, Journal of
Supply Chain Management, and IEEE Transactions in Engineering
Management, among others .
T he Supply Chain and Operations faculty cover courses in
Statistics, Introductory Operations and Project Management, a wide
range of Supply Chain Management courses, Information Systems, and
recently launched courses in Business Analytics and AI, across both
our undergraduate and graduate curriculum.
The School of Business is an undepartmentalized School and
encourages collegiality across the entire faculty. Faculty members
should expect to interact with colleagues from other business
disciplines. As part of UW tri-campus system, faculty members have
complete access to the computing and library resources of the
University of Washington.
University of Washington Bothell
Located in the heart of the Puget Sound region, the University of
Washington Bothell is one of the most dynamic public universities
in the state of Washington. UW Bothell is a student-centered campus
known for engaging students through classes, team projects, and
research in which students connect what they learn or create in the
classroom with the broader community. This is achieved through
close relationships with faculty members as teachers and mentors,
and staff dedicated to student success. The academic work of the
campus focuses on cross-disciplinary research, connected learning,
and community engagement, and prepares students for leadership in
the state of Washington and beyond.
The campus offers more than 55 undergraduate and graduate degree
programs in five schools. Current UW Bothell enrollment is over
6,000 students. More than 90% of undergraduates are from Washington
State, and approximately 40% are first-generation college
attendees. The priorities of the University’s current Strategic
Plan – “Expanding Access, Achieving Excellence”, are to enhance
community and campus engagement, and advance cross disciplinary
teaching and scholarship. In addition to award winning faculty and
staff, UW Bothell has been recognized for innovations in academic
programming and support services designed to help students graduate
on time and debt-free. It has also earned both recognition and
awards for its work in the area of environmental sustainability and
is just one of twelve institutions selected to join the launch
cohort of the Postsecondary Data for Action Network (PDAN), a new
national initiative co-led by the Institute for Higher Education
Policy (IHEP) and the Association for Institutional Research (AIR).
This selection places UW Bothell among a small group of colleges
and universities collectively committed to using data in smarter,
more student-centered ways.
Salary
The base salary range for this position will be $15,556 - $17,222
per month ($140,000 to $155,000 annually), commensurate with
experience and qualifications, or as mandated by a U.S. Department
of Labor prevailing wage determination.
Qualifications
Applicants for this position must have earned a doctorate (or
foreign equivalent) in Supply Chain Management, Operations
Management, Information Systems, Management Science, Operations
Research, Business Analytics, Industrial Engineering, or a related
field, by the date of appointment.
Instructions
Review of applications will begin upon receipt, and the position
will remain open until filled. Priority will be given to those
applications received by October 10, 2026. Applications will
only be accepted via Interfolio: https://apply.interfolio.com/193064
. Please direct general inquiries to BSsearch@uw.edu .
Applications should include the following materials:
Cover Letter: A cover letter of no more than 2 pages detailing
your interest in the position, relevant qualifications, and
experiences
Curriculum Vitae
Research Statement: A statement describing your research
interests and trajectory
Manuscripts: Copies of representative research papers
(published or unpublished)
Teaching Statement: A statement describing your teaching
philosophy, interests, and effectiveness
Teaching Portfolio: Evidence of teaching effectiveness and
excellence, including but not limited to complete sets of recent
teaching evaluations (three to five years, or all available years
if fewer than three years), teaching awards, special recognitions,
and other evidence of instructional achievement
References: Names and contact information for three references
who will be prepared to submit letters of recommendation upon
request
Applicants should articulate how their past experiences and/or
future plans in research, teaching, mentoring, and/or service
promote a sense of belonging and foster a welcoming and inclusive
environment.
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
Equal Opportunity
The University of Washington is committed to fostering an
inclusive, respectful and welcoming community for all. As an equal
opportunity employer, the University considers applicants for
employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, national
origin, citizenship, sex, pregnancy, age, marital status, sexual
orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information,
disability, or veteran status consistent with
UW Executive Order No. 81 .
Benefits Information
The University is committed to providing excellent benefits to our
faculty. For a summary of available benefits, please see UWHR benefits information .
Privacy Notice
Your application materials may be used for employment consideration
and shared in accordance with UW’s Privacy Policy.
Disability Services
The University of Washington is committed to providing access and
reasonable accommodation in its services, programs, activities,
education, and employment for individuals with disabilities. To
request disability accommodation in the application process,
contact the Disability Services Office at 206-543-6450 or
dso@uw.edu.

jobs.title: Assistant or Associate Professor in Accounting
jobs.description:
Position Overview
School / Campus / College: University of Washington,
Bothell
Organization: Business
Title: Assistant or Associate Professor in Accounting
Position Details
Position Description
The School of Business at the University of Washington Bothell
invites applications for a Tenure-Track faculty position at the
rank of Assistant or Associate Professor in Accounting, effective
September 16, 2027. We seek applicants who demonstrate commitment
to excellence in research, teaching, and service in a diverse and

Faculty in either position will teach both fundamental and advanced

Auditing, Advanced Tax, Forensic Accounting and fraud, Governmental

The School of Business
The UW Bothell School of Business is accredited by AACSB and is

MBA, and MS Accounting programs, and enrollment has been growing at
a fast pace. Located 15 miles northeast of downtown Seattle, we
work closely with industry leaders as well as smaller, innovative,
and rapidly growing companies in software, retail, medical
equipment, biotechnology, electronics, and aerospace sectors and
with a number of governmental agencies. Our students are drawn from
and work in companies such as Alaska Airlines, Amazon, Amgen,
Boeing, Costco, Expedia, Google, ICOS, Meta, Microsoft, Nintendo,

government.
We have a Beta Alpha Psi Chapter and an Accounting Club for
students who meet the academic requirements for admission to BAP
but whose schedule may not permit them to satisfy the service
requirements.

encourages collegiality across the entire faculty. The accounting
faculty members should expect to interact with colleagues from
other business disciplines. As part of UW tri-campus system,
faculty members have complete access to the computing and library
resources of the University of Washington, including commonly used
financial databases via WRDS.
University of Washington Bothell
Located in the heart of the Puget Sound region, the University of
Washington Bothell is one of the most dynamic public universities
in the state of Washington. UW Bothell is a student-centered campus
known for engaging students through classes, team projects, and
research in which students connect what they learn or create in the
classroom with the broader community. This is achieved through
close relationships with faculty members as teachers and mentors,
and staff dedicated to student success. The academic work of the
campus focuses on cross-disciplinary research, connected learning,
and community engagement, and prepares students for leadership in
the state of Washington and beyond.
The campus offers more than 55 undergraduate and graduate degree
programs in five schools. Current UW Bothell enrollment is over
6,000 students. More than 90% of undergraduates are from Washington
State, and approximately 40% are first-generation college
attendees. The priorities of the University’s current Strategic
Plan – “Expanding Access, Achieving Excellence”, are to enhance
community and campus engagement, and advance cross disciplinary
teaching and scholarship. In addition to award winning faculty and
staff, UW Bothell has been recognized for innovations in academic
programming and support services designed to help students graduate
on time and debt-free. It has also earned both recognition and
awards for its work in the area of environmental sustainability and
is just one of twelve institutions selected to join the launch
cohort of the Postsecondary Data for Action Network (PDAN), a new
national initiative co-led by the Institute for Higher Education
Policy (IHEP) and the Association for Institutional Research (AIR).
This selection places UW Bothell among a small group of colleges
and universities collectively committed to using data in smarter,
more student-centered ways.

$24,000 per month, commensurate with experience and qualifications,

foreign equivalent) in accounting (or a closely related
field).
The expectations for the research record are commensurate with

fields, as recognized by the academic profession. A record of one

beginning September 16, 2027. The Assistant Teaching Professor
position is not eligible for tenure.
The successful candidate will be expected to teach undergraduate
and graduate courses in Operations Management, Business Statistics,
Supply Chain Management, Business Analytics, and Artificial
Intelligence; develop and update courses and curricula that
integrate contemporary analytical methods, AI-enabled decision
tools, and experiential learning; advise and mentor students;
contribute to assessment and assurance-of-learning activities;
maintain an appropriate AACSB faculty qualification status; and
provide service to the School, the University, the profession, and
the community. Teaching faculty at the University of Washington
engage in teaching, scholarship, and service, and the successful
candidate will be encouraged to pursue pedagogical innovation,
applied scholarship, industry engagement, and leadership in
curriculum development.
Positive factors for consideration include a doctorate from a
highly regarded, research-intensive U.S. institution or a
comparably strong international institution; expertise spanning
Supply Chain Management, Information Systems, Artificial
Intelligence, and Operations; experience using contemporary
analytics and AI tools in instruction; evidence of teaching
effectiveness; and relevant industry or applied professional
experience.

The UW Bothell School of Business is accredited by AACSB and is
deeply committed to the success of its faculty in research,
teaching, and service. We are well known for our undergraduate,
MBA, and MS Accounting programs, and enrollment has been growing at
a fast pace. Located 15 miles northeast of downtown Seattle, we
work closely with industry leaders, many of whom are headquartered
in the region, as well as smaller, innovative, and rapidly growing
companies in software, retail, medical equipment, biotechnology,
electronics, and aerospace sectors. Our students are drawn from and

Phillips, PACCAR, REI, Starbucks, Symetra, T-Mobile, Tableau, and
Zillow, as well as in local, State, and Federal government.
The School’s Supply Chain and Operations faculty are active
scholars whose work has been published in leading journals
includingJournal of Operations Management, Production and
Operations Management, Manufacturing & Service Operations
Management, Operations Research, Decision Sciences, Journal of
Supply Chain Management, and IEEE Transactions in Engineering
Management,among others.
The Supply Chain and Operations faculty cover courses in
Statistics, Introductory Operations and Project Management, a wide
range of Supply Chain Management courses, Information Systems, and
recently launched courses in Business Analytics and AI, across both
our undergraduate and graduate curriculum.
The School of Business is an undepartmentalized School and
encourages collegiality across the entire faculty. Faculty members
should expect to interact with colleagues from other business
disciplines. As part of UW tri-campus system, faculty members have

University of Washington.

community and campus engagement, and advance cross disciplinary
teaching and scholarship. In addition to award winning faculty and
staff, UW Bothell has been recognized for innovations in academic
programming and support services designed to help students graduate
on time and debt-free. It has also earned both recognition and

is just one of twelve institutions selected to join the launch

This selection places UW Bothell among a small group of colleges
and universities collectively committed to using data in smarter,

The base salary range for this position will be $12,000 - $13,500
per month ($108,000 to $121,500 annually), commensurate with
experience and qualifications, or as mandated by a U.S. Department
of Labor prevailing wage determination.
Qualifications
Applicants for this position must have earned a doctorate (or
foreign equivalent) in Supply Chain Management, Operations
Management, Information Systems, Management Science, Operations
Research, Business Analytics, Industrial Engineering, Statistics,
or a closely related field, by the date of appointment.
Applicants must provide evidence of successful university-level
teaching or strong potential for teaching excellence and must be
able to teach across several of the following areas: Operations

The Boston College Theology Department invites applications for a senior scholar to serve as the inaugural holder of the Maureen and Craig Sullivan University Professorship. The holder of this new endowed chair will be a scholar who has demonstrated excellence in research and teaching in Catholic theology. Applicants should be established scholars in their field with a commitment to excellence in teaching at both the graduate and undergraduate levels. The appointment will be a tenured position at the rank of full Professor, and will begin in July 2027, with teaching duties beginning mid-August 2027.

Job Summary
The Angelo State University College of Arts and Humanities and
Department of Visual and Performing Arts invites applications from
qualified candidates to teach online and face-to-face courses in
Video Game Art and Animation. The Bachelor of Fine Arts in Video
Game Art and Animation is a new degree within the
Department of Visual and Performing Arts. The ideal candidate will
be able to help shape this degree for the next generation of video
game artists. Applications will be accepted continuously and
reviewed as instructional needs develop.
Ideal candidates will demonstrate strong abilities in art,
creativity, design, and technology, supported by professional or
academic experience in game design, technical art, real-time
production, and game development processes. They should be capable
of integrating visual arts with technology and teaching students
how visual design, 3D modeling and asset creation, animation,
lighting, materials, shaders, optimization, and interactive
features function together in professional game-production
settings.
They will also mentor students with backgrounds in graphic design,
digital art, and traditional fine arts. The goal is to help
students transfer their existing artistic knowledge into game
development and build industry-focused technical art portfolios
that demonstrate professional-level skills.
Essential Duties
Teaching:
Instruct undergraduate studio art courses ranging from foundation
drawing and design to courses involving Real-Time, Level Dressing,
VFX for games, 2D Animation, 3D Modeling and Sculpting, Lighting,
Rendering and Look Development. Other art courses as
assigned.
Research and Creative Works:
Maintain a significant, ongoing studio practice with a record of
professional accomplishments, such as solo and group exhibitions at
local, regional, national or international levels.
Professional Service:
Serve on departmental and university committees. Manage studio
facilities and assist in the coordination of the Video Game Art and
Animation program. Participate in student recruitment and
retention. Participate in departmental and Art Area meetings and
events. Maintain regular office hours. Work collaboratively and
productively with faculty colleagues to meet the needs of the
student body.
Curriculum Development:
Lead or collaborate on revisions of the curriculum, integrating
traditional skills with conceptual and interdisciplinary practices.
Create curriculum for new courses within the VGAA curriculum to
include both online and face-to-face modalities.
Mentorship:
Academic advising and mentoring BFA art
students.
Knowledge, Skills and Abilities
Proficiency in 2D and 3D digital art tools used in contemporary
game and animation production.
Proficiency in 3D asset creation and integration, procedural
production techniques, lighting, materials, shaders, rigging,
animation systems, artist-oriented scripting, AI-supported creative
workflows, XR optimization, and other commonly used tools and
processes associated with game development and real-time
production.
Ability to recruit, retain students in the Video Game Art and
Animation concentration.
Participate in departmental/Art Area meetings and events.
Maintain regular office hours.
Work collaboratively and productively with faculty colleagues
to meet the needs of students and the Art Program.
Minimum Qualifications
An MFA or PhD in game design, game programming, or a closely
related discipline, including fields such as computer science,
computer programming, or interactive design.
Preferred Qualifications
Professional experience within the game industry is highly
desirable.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor Adjoint
jobs.description:
Job Summary
The Adjoint Professor will support the research and educational
mission of BioServe Space Technologies and the Department of
Aerospace Engineering Sciences through technical advising, research
collaboration, student mentorship, and engagement with the broader
human spaceflight and commercial space communities. The position
will leverage extensive experience in spaceflight hardware
development, space life sciences, payload integration and
operations, and research aboard the International Space Station and
other spaceflight platforms.
CU is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all
applicable federal, state, and local laws governing
nondiscrimination in employment. We are committed to creating a
workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and
dignity, and we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to
apply, including protected veterans and individuals with
disabilities.
Who We Are
BioServe Space Technologies is a Center within the Ann and HJ Smead
Aerospace Engineering Sciences department at CU Boulder. Since its
inception in 1987, BioServe has designed, built, and flown hundreds
of microgravity life science research experiments and hardware on
over 75 spaceflight missions. BioServe has a full suite of
spaceflight-certified hardware available for use by its customers
and partners. Past partners include pharmaceutical and
biotechnology companies, Universities, NIH, NASA-funded and other
government agency researchers. BioServe is a full-service, turn-key
organization that enables its customers and partners to focus
solely on research while BioServe manages all other activities
required to successfully fly experiments in microgravity.
What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be
Provide technical and strategic guidance to BioServe Space
Technologies’ research and technology development programs.
Contribute to research proposals, publications, and future
research opportunities where appropriate and consistent with
applicable conflict-of-interest and outside-activity
requirements.
Advise and mentor undergraduate and graduate students involved
in spaceflight research and hardware development.
Support student education through guest lectures, project
reviews, and other teaching activities.
Participate in technical reviews and provide subject-matter
expertise in spaceflight hardware, payload development, space life
sciences, and mission implementation.
Help strengthen connections between CU Boulder, BioServe,
government agencies, academia, and the commercial human spaceflight
ecosystem.
Contribute to the development of future research opportunities
aboard commercial space stations and other emerging spaceflight
platforms.
What We Can Offer
This is a 0% time, zero compensation appointment.
Benefits
At the University of Colorado Boulder , we are
committed to supporting the holistic health and well-being of our
employees. Our comprehensive benefits package includes medical,
dental, and retirement plans; generous paid time off; tuition
assistance for you and your dependents; and an ECO Pass for local
transit. As one of Boulder County’s largest employers, CU Boulder
offers an inspiring academic community and access to world-class
outdoor recreation. In fact, CU Boulder has been named one of
Forbes' America's Best
Large Employers , ranking #4 among large employers in Colorado
and #28 among universities nationwide. Explore additional perks and
programs through the CU Advantage program.
Be Statements
Be empowered. Be game-changing. Be Boulder.
What We Require
Ph.D. in Aerospace Engineering, Bioastronautics.
Demonstrated 10 years plus experience developing, integrating,
and operating spaceflight hardware and scientific payloads within
BioServe Space Technologies.
Demonstrated 4 years plus experience leading spaceflight
research programs within BioServe Space Technologies as Principal
Investigator or technical/program lead.
Strong knowledge of human spaceflight, space life sciences, and
microgravity research.
Experience mentoring undergraduate and graduate students.
Demonstrated ability to collaborate across academia,
government, and the commercial space industry.
Special Instructions
To inquire about this role please do not apply here, instead email
your cv to Lauren Cole at lauren.cole@colorado.edu.
This announcement will remain active through September 22,
2026.

any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying
information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school
attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting

jobs.title: Tenure-Track Faculty in Electrical, Computer and Energy Engineering
jobs.description:
Job Summary
The Department of Electrical, Computer and Energy Engineering
(ECEE) is hiring two tenure-track professors at the Assistant
Professor rank. We will consider candidates in all areas of
electrical and computer engineering. Potential research areas of
interest include communications, power, sensing, controls,
robotics, signals, computing hardware, and theory for quantum
technologies. We are particularly interested in candidates who
bridge disciplines, have synergistic interests with existing
faculty, or bring unique capabilities.
CU is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all
applicable federal, state, and local laws governing
nondiscrimination in employment. We are committed to creating a
workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and
dignity, and we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to
apply, including protected veterans and individuals with
disabilities.
Who We Are
The University of Colorado Boulder (CU Boulder) is one of
Colorado’s flagship public institutions and among the most
research-active public universities in the country. The College of
Engineering and Applied Science is the second largest school or
college on the CU Boulder campus and boasts top-tier rankings for
both its graduate and undergraduate engineering programs, earning
the 11th spot among public graduate programs and 17th nationwide
for undergraduate engineering. Multiple specialty areas are also
ranked within the top 20. Equally important, we are committed to
fostering a diverse and academically excellent community. Our
approximately 250 tenure-track, 120 instructional-track, and 30
research-track faculty serve more than 6,000 undergraduate
students, 1,300 master’s students, and 850 PhD students. Our
college's strategic vision has three core foci: (i) research and
innovation, (ii) education, and (iii) inclusion. We believe our
success depends on faculty who actively work to create an
environment where all students can thrive and who are committed to
the campus plan for creating and
sustaining supportive campus environments .
To learn more about the College of Engineering and Applied Science
please visit our website .
The ECEE Department includes 3 University Distinguished Professors,
8 endowed chairs, 40 tenure/tenure-track faculty, 8 teaching
faculty, and 4 research faculty. Faculty honors include 16 IEEE
Fellows, 4 members of the US National Academy of Engineering, a
National Science Foundation (NSF) Presidential Faculty Fellow, and
22 NSF CAREER Award recipients. The ECEE program consists of about
650 undergraduate and 450 graduate students and has averaged over
$16 million in annual research expenditures. The department
maintains close ties with local industry and national
institutes/labs such as NIST, NLR, and NOAA.
More information about the Electrical, Computer & Energy
Engineering Department is available on the
department website .
Information on the Electrical, Computer & Energy Engineering
Department's strategic vision can be found here .
What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be
Successful candidates will be expected to engage in
undergraduate and graduate teaching and mentoring; develop an
externally funded research program in their technical area;
contribute professional leadership and service to their unit, the
college, and their professional community; and cultivate and
contribute to the inclusive excellence of our academic
community.
The typical distribution of work for this role is 40% teaching,
40% scholarly and creative work (research), and 20% leadership and
service.
What You Should Know
The anticipated start date for this position is at the start of
the Fall 2027 semester; however, a later start date may be
negotiated.
What We Can Offer
The anticipated academic-year salary range for this position at
the Assistant Professor rank is $115,000-$145,000.
A relocation stipend may be available within CEAS
guidelines.
CU offers a competitive 401(a) retirement plan, with employees
contributing 5% of their annual eligible compensation and CU
contributing 10% of their eligible compensation. This plan is
standard for most faculty hires. For more information on CU's
retirement benefits, visit our website here .
In addition to a competitive salary, the University of Colorado
Boulder offers a wide variety of other benefits and perks. Links to
some of these are below. To forecast the value of your total
compensation, check out our total compensation
calculator . More information on some of our benefits and perks
is available here: gender-neutral paid
parental leave ; housing down-payment
assistance programs ; dual-career &
relocation resources ; and teaching , research , and
professional development
.
Benefits
At the University of Colorado Boulder , we are
committed to supporting the holistic health and well-being of our
employees. Our comprehensive benefits package includes medical,
dental, and retirement plans; generous paid time off; tuition
assistance for you and your dependents; and an ECO Pass for local
transit. As one of Boulder County’s largest employers, CU Boulder
offers an inspiring academic community and access to world-class
outdoor recreation. In fact, CU Boulder has been named one of
Forbes' America's Best
Large Employers , ranking #4 among large employers in Colorado
and #28 among universities nationwide. Explore additional perks and
programs through the CU Advantage program.
Be Statements
Be challenged. Be impactful. Be Boulder.
What We Require
Applicants must have earned a research doctorate in electrical
engineering, computer engineering or a related field, or have their
degree conferred before starting a tenure-track faculty
appointment.
Special Instructions
To apply, please submit the following materials as individual PDF
files:
Cover Letter: A one-page cover letter describing your
interest in the position and summarizing your personal academic
goals, as well as ways you may fit in the department.
Resume/CV: A current curriculum vitae.
A Statement of Research Philosophy: A statement of your
experience and plans for research and/or creative work that
contributes to the body of knowledge in your field and provides
broader benefits to education and society (2-3 pages).
A Statement of Teaching Philosophy: A statement of your
experience and plans for teaching and mentoring a diverse student
body (2-3 pages).
Leadership, Service and Community Contributions
Statement: In this statement, describe your leadership and
service experience, and demonstrated ability to contribute to a
supportive campus community. Please provide details on your track
record, calibrated to your career stage, that describe the specific
role you played in these efforts. These could include, but are not
limited to service on committees, outreach activities to broaden
engagement within engineering, or participation in advisory boards
or task forces contributing to policies or regulations. In
addition, describe your plans to contribute to our campus plan to
Create Supportive
Environments , and the College of Engineering and
Applied Science Strategic Vision (1-2 pages).
During the application process, you will be asked to provide the
names and contact information for at least three references to
submit a letter of recommendation to be considered along with your
application materials.
Applications will be accepted until the position is filled, however
for full consideration please apply by November 15, 2026
.
Note: Application materials will not be accepted via
email. Applications must be submitted through CU Boulder Jobs . Background checks will be conducted
for all final applicants.

any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying
information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school
attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting
or removing this information.
