jobs.description:
University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus
Department: Anesthesiology
Job Title: Research Service Professional (Open Rank: Entry –
Intermediate)
Position #00853387 – Requisition #41164
Job Summary:
The Basak and Calero Laboratories in the Department of
Anesthesiology are interested in understanding the molecular
mechanisms that mediate brain injury and recovery after a cardiac
arrest. Our research uses translational animal models of cardiac
arrest with cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) across the lifespan
to study the role of various molecular pathways in mediating
neuronal cell death, synaptic loss, and cognitive
dysfunction.
We are currently seeking a Research Services Professional (RSP) to
perform small-animal surgeries and neurobehavioral testing in
support of these projects. The RSP will also be responsible for
tissue collections and histological analyses related to projects.
This position will work in a collaborative team environment and
will assist with lab maintenance responsibilities, including
regulatory compliance, maintenance of the mouse colony, and other
experiments as determined by the supervisors. Selected candidates
will have access to state-of-the-art equipment and resources to
conduct their research. The RSP is expected to attend weekly lab
meetings and departmental research seminars. The position offers an
excellent opportunity to gain insights into the pathophysiology of
brain injury in the setting of ischemia and support your
professional development in a collaborative research
environment.
Duties Performed (Entry Professional)
Perform rodent survival surgeries and post-operative
care.
Perform neurobehavioral testing to assess cognitive and motor
outcomes.
Manage animal colonies.
Maintain thorough and accurate lab records.
Collaborate with and support Principal Investigators (PI) and
other stakeholders with laboratory and research functions
Duties Performed (Intermediate Professional)
Lab Management responsibilities including lab ordering and
regulatory compliance.
Support training of other lab members and collaborators.
Train others on skills in which high proficiency has been
gained.
Learn and perform cardiac arrest and cardiopulmonary
resuscitation in rodents.
Monitor animals that have surgeries and provide support for
animal husbandry, as needed.
Learn and perform histology and immunohistochemistry brain
tissue from animals.
Work Location:
Onsite – this role is expected to work onsite and is located in
Aurora, CO.
Why Join Us:
The University of Colorado School of Medicine and the Department of
Anesthesiology is a world-class medical destination at the
forefront of transformative education, science, medicine, and
healthcare. The Department of Anesthesiology has several clinical
specialties and is a nationally recognized leader in anesthesiology
and peri-operative medical education. We are dedicated to
developing leaders in anesthesiology and perioperative medicine who
demonstrate clinical excellence, professionalism, and a commitment
to life-long learning. Our faculty have a resolve to create an
exciting academic environment that will build upon what is already
recognized as one of the finest residency programs in the country,
and by advancing education within our specialty, we continue to
improve the lives of learners and patients in a complex and
evolving world of medicine.

Job Details
The E. Craig Wall Sr. College of Business Administration at Coastal
Carolina University invites applications for a full-time
tenure-track position at the assistant/associate professor level in
the Department of Finance and Economics beginning Fall 2027. To be
considered, candidates should possess a Ph.D. in finance from an
AACSB -accredited program with a specialization supportive of one
or more of the finance degree tracks (wealth management, banking
and consumer finance, or corporate finance). The department also
offers a major and minor in commercial and investment real estate,
as well as a certificate in financial planning. We are also
launching a new M.S. Finance program in the fall of 2026.
Typically, the successful candidate will demonstrate interest
and/or experience in teaching in at least two of the department’s
areas of specialization—wealth management, banking and consumer
finance, corporate finance, or commercial and investment real
estate.
Applicants who are A.B.D. candidates with a clear plan for degree
completion by July 2027 may be considered (candidates who are ABD —
please ensure you document the timeline of defending your
dissertation in your application). A candidate with a completed
Ph.D. must have a recent and consistent record of publication in
quality refereed journals. The Department of Finance and Economics
also values candidates with industry experience and a commitment to
community engagement. Candidates holding professional
certifications (CFA, CFP, etc.) are preferred. The ideal candidate
would also have a track record of community engagement and
experiential learning that can create value for the department and
for student learning experiences.
The teaching load is three courses per academic semester, and may
include face-to-face, hybrid, and/or online deliveries. In addition
to teaching responsibilities, the successful candidate will be
expected to engage in research and scholarship, resulting in
high-quality publications. The Wall College of Business has a WRDS
platform with access to CRSP, Compustat, Bloomberg, and Datastream
to support quality scholarship and teaching. The position also
requires service activities, including contributing to the
assessment of student learning outcomes, and other service to the
department, college, university, community, and profession. It is
expected that the individual chosen for this position will possess

has increased significantly in recent years, with over 700 students
majoring in the discipline. The department also has minors in
economics, commercial and investment real estate, and actuarial
science and risk management along with a certificate in financial
planning (CFP Board Registered Program). Additional information
about the College and the University and its programs can be
obtained by accessing the university’s website ( http://www.coastal.edu ).

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Psychology
jobs.description:
Job Details
The Department of Psychology at Purdue University Fort Wayne invites applications for a tenure-track assistant professor position with a start date of August 16, 2027.
The position requires a Ph.D. in psychology with specialization in clinical or counseling psychology. ABD candidates will be considered with the expectation that a doctoral degree be awarded prior to start of employment. The successful candidate will teach undergraduate courses such as, but not limited to, Abnormal Psychology, Introductory Psychology, and additional courses in area of specialization. The position also requires developing a program of research leading to publication and some service to the university, community, and profession.
The Program
The Department of Psychology offers B.A. and B.S. degrees in psychology. We have 350 majors and 13 full-time faculty. The department is very collegial and an excellent place to work. We are committed to high quality teaching and research, and new faculty are well supported by the department, college, and university so they can maximize their achievements in these domains.
Purdue University Fort Wayne is a thriving regional campus of Purdue University. Fort Wayne is the second-largest metropolitan area in Indiana; a rapidly growing community located two hours from Indianapolis and three hours from Chicago. Fort Wayne was rated by Niche.com in 2022 as the #1 city for “Lowest Cost of Living” in the United States.
Application Process
Screening begins November 1, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled.
Applications should include: a cover letter describing your interest in and qualifications for the position; Curriculum Vitae; Teaching Philosophy Statement (1-2 pg.); Research Statement (1-2 pg.); and names and contact information of three (3) professional references and/or professional letters of recommendation. Candidates must also include evidence of Teaching and/or Research Effectiveness (e.g., course evaluations, copies of relevant publications, etc.). All candidates invited for a campus interview will be expected to do a 45 to 60-minute instructional student presentation as well as a 45-minute research presentation. Upload all application materials to
https://careers.purdue.edu/FW/go/FW-Faculty/7720100/
Department web address: https://www.pfw.edu/psychology/
Purdue Fort Wayne is an EEO/AA employer. This position is contingent on available funding and satisfactory background records check.

Georgia College & State University (GCSU) is the state's
designated public liberal arts university, where students learn the

with opportunities for a variety of transformational experiences
through its award-winning, high-impact practices. One of only three

undergraduate degrees in more than 40 majors, more than 30 graduate
programs, doctorates in education and nursing, professional
certificates, and continuing education programs.
As a member of the prestigious Council of Public Liberal Arts
Colleges (COPLAC), GCSU is committed to fostering a liberal arts
environment that values academic preeminence, interdisciplinary
inquiry and an inclusive learning community. GCSU enjoys a strong
reputation for academic excellence and nationally ranked programs
according to US News & World Report, The Princeton Review and
Colleges of Distinction - among other ranking sources.
Georgia College & State University takes great pride in
combining the educational experience of a private liberal arts
college with the affordability of a public university. Faculty and
staff are dedicated to student engagement and experiential learning
through high-impact practices such as internships, service- and
community-based learning, leadership development, study abroad

For more information, visit us online at gcsu.edu.

The Department of Biological and Environmental Sciences at Georgia
College & State University offers undergraduate majors in
Biology and Environmental Science, with concentrations available in
Marine Sciences and Biomedical Sciences. The department also offers
an M.S. program in Biology with both thesis and non-thesis options.
Our 29 full-time faculty members support approximately 395
undergraduate Biology majors, 112 Environmental Science majors, and
26 graduate students. To learn more about our programs, faculty,

Job Description Summary / TWC Summary
Tenure-track Assistant Professor position in the Department of
English specializing in American Literature, Media Studies, and
Popular Culture. Responsibilities include teaching specialized
undergraduate and graduate courses in 19th–21st century American
literature, print and digital media, popular culture, visual
culture, genre studies, and cultural theory across multiple
delivery modalities (face-to-face, online, evening, and/or weekend
formats); advising students; maintaining an active research agenda
focused on American literature, media history, popular culture,
television/digital media, public humanities, or fan studies;
developing interdisciplinary literature and media curriculum; and
contributing to departmental, college, and university service. The
successful candidate will demonstrate a strong commitment to
connecting literary and cultural studies with popular media
practices, preparing students for careers in publishing, media,
communications, education, cultural institutions, and creative
industries, and expanding opportunities for students to analyze,
preserve, and circulate culturally significant narratives across
print and digital platforms.
Essential Duties Summary
Develop and deliver specialized curriculum in American
literature, popular culture, print and digital media, television
analysis, genre fiction, visual rhetoric, and cultural
studies.
Teach upper-level and graduate courses in American Literary
History, Popular Culture Studies, Media Theory, Cultural Studies,
and related areas.
Develop courses that examine narrative across literature,
television, film, comics/graphic novels, podcasts, digital
platforms, fandoms, and emerging media.
Support departmental public humanities initiatives through
student-centered projects involving local literary archives, oral
histories, public exhibits, community storytelling, and digital
humanities.
Contribute expertise in American literary history and popular
media to initiatives documenting and preserving the cultural
histories of Houston’s historic communities and beyond.
Create opportunities for students to transform literary,
historical, and popular culture research into digital archives,
public exhibits, podcasts, essays, and other public-facing media
projects.
Build interdisciplinary pathways connecting English coursework
with Communication, Theater, History, African American Studies,
American Studies, Sociology, and Art History.
Develop partnerships with local cultural institutions,
libraries, publishers, archives, museums, media organizations, and
creative-industry partners to support experiential learning and
student career development.
Maintain an active research agenda and publishing trajectory
focused on American literature, popular culture, media studies,
digital humanities, public humanities, or cultural studies.
Support student success across undergraduate and graduate
literature, writing, media, and humanities courses.
Serve on departmental, college, and university committees.
Perform other job-related duties as assigned.

jobs.description:
Posting Details

Position Overview
Primary Purpose of Position
The College of Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences at North
Carolina Agricultural and Technical State University invites
applications for a nationally recognized and experienced thought
and/or practice leader to serve as the Henry E. Frye Endowed
Professor in the Department of History and Political Science. This
faculty member will contribute to the department’s teaching mission
by offering Political Science courses while advancing the public,
scholarly, and civic profile of the University through research,
engagement, and leadership in the field. The appointment is a
9-month, tenure-track position at the rank of Associate or Full
Professor, initially awarded as a one-year contract with the
possibility of renewal as a three-year appointment. The Henry E.
Frye Endowed Professor reports to the Chair of the Department of
History and Political Science and is expected to play a visible and
impactful role in shaping conversations around politics, policy,
and democratic practice at the local, state, and national
levels.
The primary purpose of the Henry E. Frye Endowed Professorship is
to recruit an accomplished and nationally recognized
scholar-practitioner whose distinguished record of professional
practice, scholarly research and/or creative activity, excellence
in teaching, and service reflects the highest standards of the
academy. The successful candidate will teach core Political Science
courses, including Electoral Politics, The Constitution, Civil
Liberties, and Statistics, while serving as a dynamic mentor to
students and junior faculty and advancing experiential and
service-learning opportunities. This position plays a critical role
in advancing the strategic priorities of the Department of History
and Political Science through contributions to program assessment,
fundraising, grant development, and service at the department,
college, and university levels. As the department expands its
academic offerings and civic reach, the Henry E. Frye Endowed
Professor will help shape innovative curricula, strengthen student
success, and elevate the department’s scholarly and public impact
within the College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences.
Primary Function of Organizational Unit
The Department of History and Political Science is housed within
the College of Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences. It offers a
Bachelor of Arts in Political Science and a Bachelor of Science in
History. The Department has over 110 majors.
The College of Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences houses the
Departments of Criminal Justice, English, History and Political
Science, Journalism and Mass Communication, Liberal Studies, and
Visual and Performing Arts. CAHSS is an academic unit that reports
to the Office of the Provost/Division of Academic Affairs and
enrolls more than 2,000 students and has more than 160 full-time
faculty members.
N.C. A&T is a public, land-grant, doctoral research institution
and has been the largest historically Black university in the
country for the past decade. With an enrollment of 15,275 students
in Fall 2026, the university offers 59 undergraduate degree
programs, 36 master’s programs, and 12 doctoral programs. It is
America’s top producer of Black graduates in Engineering and
Agricultural Science bachelor’s programs, as well as a top five
producer in numerous additional disciplines, including Liberal Arts
and Communications/Journalism. It also ranks no. 3 in master’s
degrees awarded to Black graduates in Engineering Technologies and
Related Fields, no. 4 in master’s degrees in Engineering, and no.
11 best business school for women in the nation.
Nationally recognized for its leadership and excellence in STEM
education and research, N.C. A&T is classified as “R2-High
Research Activity” in the Carnegie Classifications and is poised to
achieve “R1-Very High Research Activity” status. It also holds
Carnegie’s earned credential in Community Engagement and the
Association of Public and Land-Grant Universities ( APLU )
Innovation and Economic Prosperity designation. With an annual
economic impact of $2.4 billion, N.C. A&T plays a vital role as
a higher-education economic driver in North Carolina’s Piedmont
Triad region and across a state that is ranked No. 1 in the nation
for the second straight year as “best for business” by the CNBC
financial network.

A Ph.D. in a field related to Political Science, or a terminal
degree, with significant teaching/research/administrative
experience, preferably in a higher-education environment.
Candidates must have a distinguished record of scholarly and/or
professional work and accomplishments that reflect the integration
of learning, discovery, and engagement.

jobs.title: Associate Professor in Medieval European and/or Mediterranean History (400-1500)
jobs.description:
Job Details
Johns Hopkins, founded in 1876, is America's first research
university and home to nine world-class academic divisions working
together as one university.
Salary : $121,500 - $248,500
Johns Hopkins University: Zanvyl Krieger School of Arts and
Sciences: Department of History
Description
The Department of History at Johns Hopkins University invites
applications for a full-time position in Medieval European and/or
Mediterranean History (400-1500) at the rank of Associate Professor
(with tenure) or advanced Assistant (tenure-track) Professor to
begin July 1, 2027. The department seeks to hire a leading scholar
in the field with an ambitious research agenda and a significant
research profile, a demonstrable commitment to teaching at both the
undergraduate and graduate levels, and a willingness to engage in
conversations across history and the humanities. Scholars whose
work focuses on the history of Europe, the Mediterranean, North
Africa, and the Near East for any period from 400-1500 will be
considered, though preference will be given to those working across
geographical regions and whose temporal and methodological focus
complements strengths in the department. For current information
about the Department of History faculty, see: https://history.jhu.edu/people/
Qualifications
The successful applicant must hold a Ph.D. or equivalent
degree.

Applicants should submit an application to Interfolio . Application
materials should include: a cover letter, CV, research statement,
teaching statement, writing sample of no more than 40 pages, and
three letters of reference. Review of applications will begin on
October 15, 2026. For questions regarding this position, please
email Megan Zeller.

characteristics. The University is committed to providing qualified

performance and merit without regard to personal factors or
demographic characteristics that are irrelevant to the program
involved.

University and require special assistance or accommodation during

Business Services Office at jhurecruitment@jhu.edu . For

conditions related to pregnancy or childbirth), accessibility, or
religious reasons, please visit accessibility.jhu.edu .

for this position will be subject to a pre-employment background
check including education verification. When deciding whether a

EEO is the Law

Johns Hopkins University strongly encourages, but no longer
requires, at least one dose of the COVID-19 vaccine. This change

of vaccination status. We still require all faculty, staff, and
students to receive the seasonal
flu vaccine .

Job Description
Virginia Tech’s (VT) Fralin Biomedical Research Institute (FBRI) is
recruiting for an exceptional investigator in cancer research at
the level of Professor or Associate Professor.
The successful candidate will have a strong record of independently
funded basic or translational cancer research, along with
demonstrated commitment to faculty mentorship. This new position is
part of a major research initiative by VT and will be located at
the university’s health sciences and technology campus in Roanoke,
VA ( https://fbri.vtc.vt.edu/ ). Cancer
research faculty at the Roanoke campus have particular interest in
bioengineering, biomaterials, exosome biology, focused ultrasound,
radiation oncology, theranostics, tumor microenvironment, and

qualified candidates may additionally be considered for the role of

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Instruction in Chemistry
jobs.description:
NORTHWESTERN UNIVERSITY - The Department of Chemistry at Northwestern University is hiring an Assistant Professor of Instruction to serve as a member of our teaching track (non-tenure track) faculty. The successful candidate will be responsible for functions related to teaching, advising, scholarly activity, and contribution to the department's ACS-accredited undergraduate chemistry program; develop inquiry-based experiments and other approaches to improve student learning and persistence in laboratory courses and the corresponding lecture courses; develop or implement valid assessments of student learning in undergraduate chemistry courses. This position will also participate in teaching assistant training and mentoring, delivering laboratory lectures, conducting office hours, evaluating the academic progress of students, submitting course grades, and performing other administrative duties as required. Applicants must have completed a PhD in Chemistry, Chemical Education, or a related field, must have demonstrated excellence in teaching, experience in supervising/overseeing a laboratory, and have an interest in advancing and publishing educational innovations. This position is a full-time, benefits eligible, 9-month, continuing faculty position with an initial appointment of three years.
POSITION AVAILABLE: September 1, 2027. TO APPLY: Application materials (cover letter, CV, teaching philosophy and three letters of recommendation) should be submitted to the application link found at https://chemistry.northwestern.edu/about/open-positions.html by November 15, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. To ensure full consideration, completed applications should be received by this date. Questions regarding the position should be sent to Kre Britt at chemsearch@northwestern.edu.

The expected base pay range for this position is $80,000 - $95,000.
This base pay range is for a nine-month academic appointment, does not include summer salary, and is subject to negotiation.

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Teaching Professor
jobs.institution: Arizona State University, School of Civic and Economic Thought and Leadership
jobs.description: The School of Civic and Economic Thought and Leadership (SCETL) at Arizona State University invites applications for a full-time, in-person, benefits-eligible Assistant or Associate Teaching Professor position in our scholarly track of American constitutional thought with an anticipated start date in August 2027. This is a fixed-term, academic year (nine month) appointment with no tenure implications. Subsequent academic year renewals (Aug. 16 to May 15) are contingent upon performance, availability of resources, and the needs of the unit. Candidates’ primary teaching obligation would be SCETL’s signature course “Great Debates in American Constitutionalism and Politics.” This course heavily focuses on the American Founding and American constitutional institutions (e.g. federalism, the separation of powers) and we are proud to fulfill the Arizona Board of Regents requirement for a course in American Institutions to help understand and appreciate American constitutional principles. There will also be opportunity for additional relevant upper-division courses in American constitutionalism, American constitutional history, American civic thought, or civic thought more broadly. We would particularly welcome candidates who could supplement current department strengths by teaching courses on the American Founding, the First Amendment, the Second Amendment, Montesquieu, Religion and the American Civic Tradition, American Civil-Military Relations, the American Way or War (American military history), the Bible and Civic Thought, or the political thought of CS Lewis.

Parker University, the fourth-fastest growing college in Texas and the fastest-growing college in Dallas, is currently searching for a Full Time Faculty - Systems Pathology/Pharmacology/Toxicology to join our rapidly expanding team! Experience facilitating active learning, integrating basic science concepts with clinical application, and promoting critical thinking is expected. The ability to contribute across multiple Basic Sciences disciplines is preferred.

responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

WHAT YOU WILL NEED:
JOB SPECIFICATIONS:

WHY PARKER?
Founded in 1982 by Dr. James William Parker, Parker University has more than 1,800 students and 34 academic programs. Parker University proudly offers its famed Doctor of Chiropractic degree and Business and Technology and Health Sciences programs.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Clarinet
jobs.description:
The School of Music at Tennessee Tech University invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Clarinet, beginning August 1, 2027.
Tennessee Tech is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer.
Essential Functions: Responsibilities include teaching the clarinet studio and directing the clarinet choir. Supervise inventory and maintenance of the department’s clarinet equipment. Rehearse and perform as Principal Clarinet with the resident Bryan Symphony Orchestra and Cumberland Quintet (faculty woodwind ensemble). Administer all aspects of the Tennessee Tech clarinet program. Recruitment of students (especially clarinet majors). Other responsibilities, such as classroom instruction in core music courses may be assigned as determined by the candidate’s qualifications and departmental needs. Build and maintain professional relationships with public school music teachers and be an active participant in the School of Music.
Physical Demands: Those typical of an office/classroom environment.
Special Instructions to Applicants: To apply, please visit the full job description at https://jobs.tntech.edu and electronically upload a letter of application, curriculum vitae, teaching philosophy statement, and email contact information for three references who will be contacted via email to provide a reference letter, and copies of transcripts for all degrees (official transcripts of all degrees conferred and/or documentation of educational qualifications will be required upon hire). Written materials should demonstrate effective teaching experience in clarinet and other areas of specialty as appropriate to the candidate. In addition, candidates will submit at least 20 minutes’ worth of video or a combination of audio and video recordings of unedited clarinet performances from within the past 5 years, demonstrating multiple styles and settings. These recordings should be submitted as a Word file with direct links to the recordings from a file sharing platform such as YouTube, Vimeo, Dropbox, or something similar. Submission of materials is the applicant’s responsibility. Applications without all required materials are incomplete and will not be considered. Other benefits include medical and life insurance (shared cost with the university), retirement, optional 401k, and educational benefits.
Minimum qualifications: Earned Doctorate in Music required. (ABD may be considered, but degree must be conferred before job start date.) Evidence of excellence as a performer and teacher.
Preferred qualifications: Experience as a performer in solo, orchestral, and chamber or quintet settings. Experience teaching Woodwind Techniques course for music education majors. Experience as a teacher at the university level, in private instruction and/or in the public schools. Evidence of recruiting. Participation in regional, national, and international conferences.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor Tenure-Track Bioethics and Humanities
jobs.description:
Description
The Department of Bioethics and Humanities at the University of Washington School of Medicine invites applications for a Full-time (100% FTE) faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor Tenure-Track, with an anticipated start date of September 2027. We seek applicants who demonstrate commitment to excellence in research, teaching, and service in a diverse and inclusive academic community.
Assistant Professor Tenure Track appointments hold an initial 3-year renewable term that aligns with a 12-month service period (July 1-June 30). Faculty with 12-month service periods are paid for 11 months of service over a 12-month period (July-June), meaning the equivalent of one month is available for paid time off.
The base salary range for this position will be $6,456 - $10,000 per month, commensurate with experience and qualifications, or as mandated by a U.S. Department of Labor prevailing wage determination.
The successful candidate will be expected to:
Develop a research program of national and international importance in bioethics and humanities. The search’s primary emphasis will be the ethical, social, legal, policy, and/or humanistic dimensions of artificial intelligence (AI) and data-intensive technologies in science, medicine, biomedical research and health care; applications are also welcome from scholars working in other areas of biomedical innovation, including genomics, reproductive and cellular technologies, synthetic biology, and related emerging biotechnologies.
Lead high-quality independent scholarship and publish in peer-reviewed venues.
Pursue extramural research funding, including career-development, investigator-initiated, and/or collaborative awards, as appropriate to support a sustained program of research.
Contribute as a participant in the Department’s Science, Medicine, and Society Lab, a new initiative designed to advance interdisciplinary scholarship, collaborative grant development, teaching, and community-building around social, ethical, historical, legal, policy, and humanistic questions in science, medicine, and society.
Teach and mentor students and trainees across undergraduate, graduate, medical/professional, and other departmental educational programs as appropriate.
Perform service and administrative work that furthers the mission of the department, school, and/or university.
Collaborate effectively across disciplines, cultures, funding sources, and learning environments.
All University of Washington faculty are expected to engage in teaching, research, and service.
About the Department of Bioethics and Humanities
The Department of Bioethics and Humanities is an interdisciplinary department in the University of Washington School of Medicine, with a mission to advance rigorous scholarship, teaching, and public engagement on the ethical, social, historical, and humanistic dimensions of science, medicine, biomedical research and health care. Department faculty work across fields including education, genetics, health services, medical sociology, medicine, philosophy, public health, religious studies and related areas.
Our research and teaching address topics such as, community-based participatory research, clinical and research ethics, biotechnology, social justice and access to health care, global bioethics, medical error, and palliative and end-of-life care.
The Department is deeply connected to the wider UW ecosystem, with collaborative relationships across UW Medicine and the Schools of Law, Nursing, Pharmacy, Public Health, and Social Work, as well as the College of Arts and Sciences and Seattle Children’s. The successful candidate will join a department committed to interdisciplinary scholarship and to building new areas of strength at the intersection of science, medicine and society.
The Department offers an undergraduate minor, a master’s degree in bioethics, professional training programs, and ethics education in the UW School of Medicine.
Qualifications
Applicants for this position must meet the following minimum qualifications:
Terminal degree appropriate to their discipline (Ph.D., M.D., J.D. or foreign equivalent).
This position is not eligible for H-1B visa sponsorship.
Application Instructions
To ensure full consideration of your application, please submit all materials no later than November 30, 2026. Applications will only be accepted via Interfolio. The position will remain open until filled.
Applications should include the following materials:
A cover letter of no more than 2 pages detailing your interest in the position, relevant qualifications, and experiences
A curriculum vitae
2-page Research Statement: The statement should articulate a clear and compelling vision for your future research program and explain how your prior work establishes a foundation for pursuing that vision. Please also describe how your experiences and plans complement existing strengths across the department and UW, and how you would contribute to departmental research initiatives, including the Science, Medicine, and Society Lab, and to building scholarly community in the department and university.
A list of 3 referees, including names, affiliations, and full contact details. Referees should be prepared to provide letters of recommendation upon request.
Applicants should articulate how their past experiences and/or future plans in research, teaching, mentoring, patient care, and/or service promote a sense of belonging and foster a welcoming and inclusive environment.
Send queries about the position to Department Chair Dr. Amy Hinterberger at amyhint@uw.edu.

jobs.title: Forensic Psychology Assistant/Associate/Full Professor
jobs.institution: New College of Interdisciplinary Arts and Sciences
jobs.description:
The School of Interdisciplinary Forensics (SIF) in the New College of Interdisciplinary Arts and Sciences (New College) at Arizona State University (ASU) invites applications for a full-time, benefits-eligible tenured or tenure-eligible faculty position at the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor in forensic psychology/psychology and law. Salary and rank are based on qualifications at hire. The anticipated start date is August 2027.
The faculty member will be a core member of ASU’s Law and Behavioral Science group, an interdisciplinary collective of psychological scientists engaged in research that addresses current and emerging issues facing the legal system in its broadest sense. Information about our Law and Behavioral Science group—including faculty, research labs, academic programs, and events—can be found at https://lbs.asu.edu/.
Law and Behavioral Science faculty may participate in university-wide graduate programs. Thus, the successful candidate will join the faculty in SIF and have opportunities to collaborate with faculty across ASU, including colleagues in the School of Social and Behavioral Sciences, the Department of Psychology, and other behavioral science units. These collaborations will support the continued development of interdisciplinary academic programs and research initiatives in forensic psychology and psychology and law.
The area of specialization is open within psychological science applied to law or the legal system. We are, however, especially interested in candidates with expertise in clinical forensic psychology, correctional psychology, or police psychology. Within clinical forensic psychology, expertise in the assessment of people involved in the criminal legal system—including competency to stand trial, criminal responsibility, violence or recidivism risk, forensic neuropsychological assessment, and related forms of forensic clinical evaluation—is particularly desirable. Because this is a tenured or tenure-eligible faculty appointment, candidates with clinical or applied expertise must also demonstrate a strong program of empirical research, with a research record and agenda consistent with appointment to the tenure-track faculty of a research university.
About the School:
SIF bridges science, law, and justice, offering a unique approach to forensic education. The School has strengths in the psychological sciences (including social, clinical, and developmental psychology), the natural sciences (including anthropology, biology, chemistry, entomology, and genetics), and information technology (including cybersecurity and digital forensics). We integrate a wide array of disciplines, providing students with a comprehensive understanding of the role of science and technology in the legal system. With a focus on real-world applications and ethical considerations, SIF prepares students for careers that require scientific and technical expertise and a commitment to improving the administration of justice.
About the New College of Interdisciplinary Arts and Sciences:
At ASU’s New College of Interdisciplinary Arts and Sciences, we take pride in breaking down disciplinary barriers, cultivating an environment where innovative research flourishes. Our faculty are not just educators; they are trailblazers in their fields, consistently expanding the frontiers of knowledge. We invite you to join this dynamic community, where you will lead and engage in pioneering projects that redefine academic excellence.
Our interdisciplinary approach offers you unparalleled opportunities for personal and professional growth. By joining our faculty, you’re not just advancing your career; you’re shaping the future of education and research in meaningful ways. You’ll be empowered to innovate and address complex global challenges, all while preparing the next generation of leaders. We are committed to supporting and guiding you throughout your academic journey, ensuring that your contributions are impactful and transformative. For more information visit us at https://newcollege.asu.edu/.
New College is located on ASU’s West Valley campus, blending a liberal arts and science education with 21st-century workforce preparation and a learning hub for students of all ages and backgrounds supporting the rapid growth of its surrounding 14 communities. Integrating modern amenities with the natural beauty of outdoor spaces, the West Valley campus offers over 125 undergraduate and graduate degree programs across business, engineering, education, and the New College of Interdisciplinary Arts and Sciences.
About Arizona State University:
Arizona State University, ranked the No. 1 “Most Innovative School” in the nation by U.S. News & World Report for 11 years in succession, has forged the model for a New American University. Year after year, ASU ranks at or near the top of the list in areas that matter. ASU is a comprehensive public research institution, measured not by whom it excludes, but by whom it includes and how they succeed; advancing research and discovery of public value; and assuming fundamental responsibility for the economic, social, cultural and overall health of the communities it serves. ASU operates on the principles that learning is a personal and original journey for each student; that they thrive on experience and that the process of discovery cannot be bound by traditional academic disciplines. Through innovation and a commitment to accessibility, ASU has drawn pioneering researchers to its faculty even as it expands opportunities for qualified students, attracting some of the highest-quality students from all 50 states and more than 130 nations. To learn more about ASU, visit http://www.asu.edu.
All we do at ASU is guided and inspired by the ASU Charter, which reads:
ASU is a comprehensive public research university, measured not by whom it excludes, but by whom it includes and how they succeed; advancing research and discovery of public value; and assuming fundamental responsibility for the economic, social, cultural and overall health of the communities it serves.
Successful candidates will demonstrate throughout their materials how their research, teaching, and service will contribute to the fulfillment of this charter.
Essential Functions of the Position:
Establish and sustain a vigorous program of research.
Seek external research funding appropriate to the candidate’s research program.
Create and teach undergraduate and graduate courses in face-to-face, hybrid, and/or online formats.
Contribute to program curricula, program development, and, as appropriate, to university-wide efforts to train clinical behavioral scientists.
Develop research, educational, and professional collaborations with justice-system partners, as appropriate to the candidate’s expertise, such as courts (including the Arizona Supreme Court and Administrative Office of the Courts), law enforcement agencies, correctional systems, and behavioral health organizations.
Prepare course syllabi, lectures, learning exercises, exams, and other course materials, and grade assignments and assessments.
Develop, maintain, and update course materials as appropriate to the field and modality.
Maintain regular availability to students and support student success, including holding office hours weekly.
Mentor undergraduate and graduate students in research and professional development.
Contribute meaningful service to the School, College, University, profession, and community.
Engage in regular professional development and foster collegiality throughout the organization.
Attend faculty, unit, and committee meetings per unit expectations.
Required Qualifications:
A Ph.D., Psy.D., or other appropriate terminal degree in psychology or a closely related field by the time of appointment.
Demonstrated expertise in the application of behavioral science to law or the legal system.
For appointment at the rank of Associate or Full Professor, a record of teaching, research, and service that merits appointment at the corresponding rank with tenure at Arizona State University.
Desired Qualifications:
Significant experience in forensic clinical assessment or treatment, correctional psychology, police psychology, or related areas of forensic psychological practice.
A strong record of high-quality empirical, peer-reviewed scholarship in forensic psychology and/or psychology and law, with evidence of an active research agenda commensurate with career stage.
A successful record of seeking or securing external research funding commensurate with career stage.
Experience teaching and/or supervising students in forensic psychology, psychological assessment, or the intersection of behavioral science and law.
Evidence of successful course development and teaching effectiveness commensurate with the candidate’s rank, as demonstrated by student evaluations, syllabi, peer observations, annual performance evaluations, or similar materials.
Experience collaborating with justice-system partners such as law enforcement, courts, correctional systems, behavioral health organizations, or forensic hospitals.
Demonstrated commitment to working successfully with students from a wide variety of socio-economic and cultural backgrounds, including first-generation college students.
Demonstrated excellent English written and verbal communication skills.
For clinically oriented candidates, expertise in forensic psychological assessment or intervention in judicial, law enforcement, or correctional settings, including one or more of the following areas: competency to stand trial, criminal responsibility, violence or recidivism risk assessment, forensic neuropsychological assessment, fitness-for-duty evaluations, correctional counseling and rehabilitation, or related areas.
For clinically oriented candidates, current licensure in Arizona as a behavioral science clinician or eligibility for such licensure; board certification in an applicable forensic specialty, including ABPP, ABPN, ABCSW, NOFSW, the National Association of Forensic Counselors, or qualifications that would support pursuit of applicable certification.
Application Deadline:
The initial application deadline is October 21, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Standard Time. Applications will continue to be accepted on a rolling basis for a reserve pool. Applications in the reserve pool may then be reviewed in the order in which they were received until the position is filled. A background check and official transcripts are required prior to employment. For assistance with your application, or for position-related questions, contact Kristin Warriner at Kristin.Warriner@asu.edu.
Application Procedure:
Only electronic submissions via Interfolio will be reviewed. All required materials must be submitted at the time of initial application. Incomplete applications will not be considered. Please submit all application materials to https://apply.interfolio.com/193543.
Applications must contain:
A one- to two-page cover letter that addresses the required and desired qualifications and how your experience will complement existing expertise in the School of Interdisciplinary Forensics and advance the University Charter;
Curriculum vitae with contact information, including telephone number and e-mail address;
A two- to three-page research statement;
A one-page statement of teaching philosophy;
Evidence of teaching effectiveness, such as student evaluations, syllabi, peer observations, annual performance evaluations, etc.; and
Information for three professional references (including their positions, titles, e-mail addresses, and phone numbers); one reference must be from the applicant’s current employer.
Applicants advancing to stages beyond the initial review may be asked to provide additional materials, including evaluations of prior teaching.
ASU conducts pre-employment screening for all positions which includes a criminal background check, verification of work history, academic credentials, licenses, and certifications. Employment is contingent upon successful passing of the background check.
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
A background check is required for employment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other basis protected by law. (See https://www.asu.edu/aad/manuals/acd/acd401.html and https://www.asu.edu/titleIX/.)
In compliance with federal law, ASU prepares an annual report on campus security and fire safety programs and resources. (See ASU’s Annual Security and Fire Safety Report, which is available online at https://cfo.asu.edu/campuscrime.)

jobs.title: Assistant Tenure-Track Professor of Biology (specializing in Microbiology)
jobs.description:
Assistant Tenure-Track Professor of Biology (specializing in Microbiology)
Apply now Job no: 562254
Work type: Instructional Faculty – Tenured/Tenure-Track
Location: Chico
Categories: Unit 3 - CFA - California Faculty Association, Tenured/Tenure-Track, Full Time, Faculty - Natural Sciences
Equal Opportunity and Excellence in Education and Employment:
California State University (CSU), Chico is a comprehensive and residential public university, holding Hispanic-Serving Institution (HSI) designation. Chico State operates as part of the 22-campus CSU system, which educates the most ethnically, economically, and academically diverse student body in the nation. The University enrolls over 15,000 students, with over half identifying as first-generation college students.
Chico State is committed to recruiting outstanding candidates. The ideal candidate will embrace our values predicated on the primacy of student success and the elimination of equity gaps, have demonstrated experience working with diverse populations, and will contribute to policies, programs, and practices that support an inclusive, accessible, and equitable learning and working environment.
The Position: Assistant Tenure-Track Professor of Biology (specializing in Microbiology)
Position Starts: Fall 2027
College: of Natural Sciences
Department/School: Department of Biological Sciences
Salary: Salary commensurate with education and experience. (Anticipated hiring range: $78,000-$90,000 per year).
Initial Review Date: 10/19/2026; complete applications received after that date may be considered.
Minimum Qualifications:
The minimum education requirement for the appointment to this position is a PhD in Microbiology or a related field. Candidates nearing completion of the terminal degree may be considered; however, all requirements for conferral of the degree must be met no later than the start date of the position. Candidates should have a strong interest in undergraduate teaching excellence and enthusiasm for mentoring undergraduate and Master's level graduate students in research, a demonstrated ability or potential to establish externally funded research, and a record of publication.
Responsibilities:
This position carries responsibilities in the areas of teaching, scholarship, and service. Teaching assignments total 10-14 class hours per week including laboratories and lectures in topics such as applied microbiology (food, industrial, biotechnology, etc.), evolution, diversity, ecology, symbioses, and pathogenesis. The teaching opportunities for the General Microbiology position include a lower- and upper-division biology courses including, but not limited to, bacterial, archaeal, or protist microbiology. Candidates are encouraged to view a list of possible courses in the Chico State Biological Sciences course catalog. Scholarship duties include developing an externally-funded research program involving undergraduate and Master's level graduate students, supported by a startup package including research space, equipment and supply funding, and partial release time from teaching in the first two years of the appointment. Service opportunities include committee work and academic advising of majors in the BS degree in Microbiology and Biology and the BA in Biological Sciences program.
How to Apply:
Applicants must provide a current cover letter that includes a brief description of 1) your preparation to teach undergraduate majors level general microbiology with a focus on bacteria and microbial diversity with lecture (2 hrs/wk) and laboratory (6 hrs/wk), 2) a proposed research program at a comprehensive, regional, state university involving both undergraduate and Master’s level graduate students (including your area of research and teaching background, and how you have addressed, or plan to address teaching to diverse student groups), 3) a CV, and 4) contact information of three professional references. Additional information, including but not limited to, a research statement, teaching statement, official transcripts, and references, may be requested at a later time. All applicants must apply online; applications submitted via email or in-person to the department will not be considered.
The Department:
The Department of Biological Sciences includes 13 tenure track faculty, 12 part-time lecturer faculty, 25 master’s students, and 500 undergraduate biology majors with options in cell & molecular biology, organismal, evolutionary, and ecological biology, or plant biology, as well as 80 microbiology majors in general or medical microbiology. Department programs are enhanced by diverse laboratory and field facilities, a student computer lab, media preparation and stockrooms, and greenhouses. The Department has five active student clubs, including a Student Chapter of the American Society for Microbiology. Full information is available at www.csuchico.edu/academics/college/natural-sciences/departments/biological-sciences/. The College of Natural Sciences (https://www.csuchico.edu/academics/college/natural-sciences/) has further resources including biochemistry faculty with expertise in microbial proteomics and physiology.

the recognized leader in experience-driven lifelong learning. Our

designed to prepare students for purposeful lives and
careers.
The College of Science comprises six departments: Biology,
Chemistry and Chemical Biology, Marine and Environmental Sciences,
Mathematics, Physics, and Psychology. The Department of Chemistry
and Chemical Biology ("CCB") (https://cos.northeastern.edu/chemistry-chemical-biology/)
includes 38 tenured/tenure-track faculty, including joint
appointments, 30% of whom are women; 25 full-time teaching faculty;
two research faculty; and nine faculty with affiliated
appointments. CCB enrolls approximately 150 undergraduate majors;
30 M.S. and PlusOne (BS/MS) students; and 100 Ph.D. students. In
addition to degrees in Chemistry, a professional science Master's
degree in Biotechnology is also offered. The Department of Biology
(https://cos.northeastern.edu/biology/)
includes 25 tenured/tenure-track faculty, including joint
appointments; and 26 full-time teaching faculty. With its core
undergraduate degree programs in Biology and in Cell &
Molecular Biology, the department enrolls around one-quarter of all
undergraduate majors in the College of Science; it also co-manages
the Behavioral Neuroscience major with the Department of
Psychology. The graduate program in Biology currently has over 50
Ph.D. students in two primary concentrations (Cell & Molecular
Biology, and Molecular Microbiology), including 15 Industry Ph.D.
students who offer exciting partnership opportunities with pharma.
In addition to degrees in Biology, professional science Master's
degrees in Bioinformatics and in Cell and Gene Therapies are also
offered. The two departments co-manage the Biochemistry
major.
Experiential education is a hallmark of our programs, where
students gain experience at leading biotechnology companies based
in Boston's globally-dominant entrepreneurial space (Moderna,
Editas, Gingko Bioworks, for instance). Northeastern's integrative
education model is ranked #1 in Cooperative education programs (US
News and World Report: 2022) which leads directly to the remarkable
career placement rate of 96% for our students. The Massachusetts
campuses are physically located at the nexus of the largest
concentration of pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies in the
world.
Northeastern is home to the Coastal Sustainability Institute,
the Global Resilience
Institute, the Barnett Institute for Chemical and
Biological Analysis, the Center for Drug
Discovery, the Network Science Institute, the
Northeastern University Center for
Renewable Energy Technology, an NSF Frontier Center in Theoretical
Biological Physics, and the Center for Interdisciplinary Research on
Complex Systems, providing a rich multidisciplinary
intellectual environment.
About the Opportunity:
The College of Science at Northeastern University invites
applications for positions at the rank of tenure-track Assistant
Professor in Chemistry and Chemical Biology and/or Biology
beginning in academic year 2027-2028 or 2028-2029. Candidates who
are completing their PhD or at an early stage of their postdoctoral
training are encouraged to apply to these tenure-track faculty
appointments. Areas of interest in the current search include
Physical AI, Robotics & Autonomous Systems for Chemistry and
Biology, broadly interpreted. This spans intelligent infrastructure
and adaptive construction/manufacturing robotics using digital
twins and multi-agent controls; embodied and wearable AI systems
that bridge human-computer interaction and design; automated
self-driving laboratories that pair hardware instrumentation with
active-learning machine learning for experiment design to
accelerate chemistry, materials, and biomanufacturing
experimentation. Primary appointments will be in Boston at the
College of Science (Chemistry and Chemical Biology and/or Biology)
with possible other joint appointments across the College of
Engineering and Khoury College of Computer Sciences. Appointments
will have the opportunity to collaborate in cross-disciplinary
teams across the University and will complement existing
strengths.
Our tenure and promotion process values collaborative research and
teamwork. Hires will be mentored for success, with mentoring teams
and group guidance. In addition, a strong and effective faculty
development strategy is part of the Northeastern institutional
mission. The ADVANCE Office of Faculty Development office works in
conjunction with the Office of Research Development (ORD), the
Office of Belonging, the Center for Advancing Teaching and Learning
Through Research (CATLR), and University Decision Support (UDS) to
provide programs and trainings to further develop and support a
thriving faculty.
Responsibilities:
The potential hires are expected to develop vigorous research
programs cross cutting the fields of automated/self-driving labs
for chemistry and biology. Faculty members at Northeastern are
expected to develop independent research programs that attract
external funding; teach courses at the graduate and undergraduate
levels; mentor students and postdocs in their area of research; and
participate in service to the department, university, and
discipline. Qualified candidates must be prepared to work with
global student populations.
Qualifications:
Applicants must have a PhD in chemistry, biology, engineering or
related fields by the employment start date. We encourage
applicants from a wide range of backgrounds, including academia and
industry.
Applicants should have a strong record of scholarly accomplishment
that demonstrates the ability to build a strong research program.
Evidence of potential as a research scientist is expected, but
postdoctoral experience is not required for appointments at the
Assistant Professor level.
Candidates must be committed to excellence in undergraduate and
graduate teaching. They should embrace the Northeastern emphasis on
experiential education and the college philosophy that access to
science education and careers must be inclusive. Depending on the
research profile and expertise, a joint or affiliate appointment in
another department(s) within the University is possible.
Additional Information:
Interested candidates should apply here with a curriculum vita that
includes a list of publications, statements addressing the prompts
below, and names and contact information for at least three
professional references from whom letters of reference can be
solicited as needed.
Successful faculty at Northeastern will be dynamic and innovative
scholars with a record of research and teaching excellence and a
commitment to contributing to fostering belonging in the university
community. Thus, strong candidates for this faculty position will
have the expertise, knowledge, and skills to build their research,
pedagogy, and curriculum in ways that reflect and enhance this
commitment. Please indicate how your expertise, knowledge, and
skills have prepared you to contribute to this work with written
statements addressing the following prompts:
Research statement (no longer than 5 pages):
Please describe the focus of your research, including the questions
you have identified, the funding you have received to support the
work (if applicable), the results you have discovered, and the
products of these efforts. Highlight any cross-disciplinary
research efforts you have undertaken. Please also describe any
research you have undertaken with students and/or with the external
community. Finally, please outline the research directions you
foresee pursuing at Northeastern, any cross-disciplinary and
collaborative aspects, and the strategies you will take to address
each direction.
Teaching statement (1 page):
Please summarize your past instructional and mentorship
experiences, your pedagogical philosophy, your plans/goals for
teaching in the College of Science (including existing and proposed
courses), and your strategies for teaching and mentoring a diverse
cohort of undergraduate and graduate students.
Leadership statement (1 page):
Leadership Statement: Please summarize your experience in
leadership positions. Describe your leadership style, how you
intend to cultivate a culture that promotes a sense of belonging,
including fostering a free and open exchange of ideas and managing
different perspectives to help others strengthen their
practice.
Applications will be reviewed beginning on October 15, 2026, and
will continue until the position is filled. Questions may be
directed to the search committee chairs, Professor Sijia Dong,
s.dong@northeastern.edu and
Professor Win Chai y.chai@northeastern.edu.
Northeastern University is an equal opportunity employer. All
qualified applicants are encouraged to apply and will receive
consideration for employment without regard to race, religion,
color, national origin, age, sex, sexual orientation, disability
status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable
law.
Position Type
Academic
Additional Information
Northeastern University considers factors such as candidate work
experience, education and skills when extending an offer.
Northeastern has a comprehensive benefits package for benefit
eligible employees. This includes medical, vision, dental, paid
time off, tuition assistance, wellness & life, retirement- as
well as commuting & transportation. Visit https://hr.northeastern.edu/benefits/ for
more information.
All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply and will receive
consideration for employment without regard to race, religion,
color, national origin, age, sex, sexual orientation, disability
status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable
law.
Pay Range:
Assistant Professor: $105,000.00 - $125,000.00
With the pay range(s) shown above, the starting salary will depend
on several factors, which may include your education, experience,
location, knowledge and expertise, and skills as well as a pay
comparison to similarly-situated employees already in the role.
Salary ranges are reviewed regularly and are subject to
change.
To apply, visit https://northeastern.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/en-US/careers/job/Boston-MA-Main-Campus/Assistant-Professor--Chemistry-and-Chemical-Biology_R142430

jobs.title: Tenure-Track Assistant Professor in Political Philosophy
jobs.description:
Job Details
Tenure-Track Assistant Professor in Political
Philosophy
Description
The Department of Philosophy at the College of the Holy Cross
invites applications for a full-time tenure-track Assistant
Professor specializing in Political Philosophy to begin in August
2027. The ideal candidate will have an Area of Specialization in
Political Philosophy with an emphasis on the foundations of
democracy. Within this AOS, we plan to look for Areas of
Concentration in deliberative democracy, epistemological aspects of
democracy, philosophy of law, pluralism, and non-state democracy.
We expect such a candidate to meet needs at both the departmental
and institutional level by teaching courses in the above-mentioned
areas and perhaps by participating in interdisciplinary courses and
related activities and programs offered by the College. Successful
candidates will demonstrate excellence as both teachers and
scholars. As teachers, we seek candidates with a demonstrated
commitment to innovative, inclusive excellence in teaching.
As scholars, we seek candidates with an active, fruitful research
agenda who are cognizant of our obligations to the wider
community.
This position carries a 3-2 teaching load with a research leave
prior to tenure review of either a full year at 80% salary or a
semester at full salary, and generous sabbatical and fellowship
leaves for tenured faculty. To enable a smooth transition to Holy
Cross, new full-time tenure-track Assistant Professors receive
start-up funding to support their research and professional
development and have a one-course reduction in their first year of
teaching (i.e., 2-2). This position offers full benefits and a
starting salary of $102,500.
In alignment with the strategic plans for Holy Cross and the division of Academic Affairs, we view
academic excellence and inclusive excellence as inextricably
linked. Our faculty combine high-impact scholarship and outstanding
teaching with a deep commitment to inclusive excellence. They
generate new knowledge in their fields while utilizing
evidence-based teaching strategies and course designs to create
classroom environments where all students have a sense of
belonging, are valued, and can flourish to reach their full
potential. Academic freedom is a cornerstone of our intellectual
and moral community; the College is committed to supporting faculty
and students as they work to advance our educational mission and
serve the common good.
Qualifications
Candidates must demonstrate excellence in scholarship and
undergraduate teaching as well as a commitment to inclusive
pedagogies. A Ph.D. in Philosophy is required by the beginning of
the appointment.
Application Instructions
Please submit
A cover letter addressing the position requirements listed
above as well as the ways you might contribute to and further the
College's
mission as a Jesuit, undergraduate liberal arts college and its
core commitment
to creating a community where every individual feels empowered
to contribute their talents and perspectives.
A curriculum vitae.
Unofficial undergraduate and graduate transcripts.
A statement of your teaching philosophy and interests, with
particular emphasis on how you utilize evidence-based teaching
strategies to foster inclusive, high-belonging classroom
environments.
3 Confidential Letters of Recommendation
A Writing Sample (preferably published, but can be 'in process'
as well)
A Research statement that communicates the candidate's current
scholarly focus and future trajectory
The College of the Holy Cross uses Interfolio to collect all
faculty job applications. Please submit all materials to https://apply.interfolio.com/193949.
For full consideration, please apply by November 1. Initial
interviews via Zoom will take place in December 5-8, and campus
visits for finalists will take place in February 9-18. Questions
about this search may be directed to Professor Jeffrey Bernstein,
jbernste@holycross.edu.
The Provost's Office supports
the Association of American Universities' principles on
preventing sexual harassment in academia. Accordingly, all
finalists will be asked to attest that they are not currently under
investigation for sexual misconduct and that there are no
substantiated findings of sexual misconduct against them in any
previous position-or, if such findings exist, to provide a full
explanation. The candidate selected for an offer will also be asked
to provide written consent for the release of personnel information
from their prior employer.
For applicants who may require visa sponsorship: The College
supports new faculty in pursuing an appropriate visa or other
immigration status consistent with their qualifications and the
responsibilities of the position. Because several pathways may be
available, the College works with candidates who are offered
positions to determine the most appropriate option. Please note,
however, the College does not support H-1B visa petitions that are
subject to the payment of an additional $100,000 fee. The College,
where appropriate, will support H-1B petitions that are not subject
to the $100,000 fee.
To apply, visit https://apply.interfolio.com/193949
COLLEGE OF THE HOLY CROSS
College of the Holy Cross is a highly selective Catholic liberal
arts college in the Jesuit tradition. It enrolls about 3,200
students and is located in Worcester, Massachusetts - New England's
second-largest city.
The College seeks faculty members who demonstrate an enduring
commitment to academic excellence and inclusive excellence and who
embrace the educational benefits of a richly diverse community.
Holy Cross aspires to meet the needs of dual-career couples, in
part through its membership in the Higher Education Consortium of Central
Massachusetts and the New England Higher Education
Recruitment Consortium. To learn more about faculty life at the
College, applicants are encouraged to visit
Office of the Provost page.
EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYMENT STATEMENT
The College is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer and
complies with all Federal and Massachusetts laws concerning equal
opportunity.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor, History
jobs.description:
Job Details
Assistant Professor, History
R0011093
Tampa
If you are a current University of Tampa student, please search
for and apply to student jobs here via Workday. Job
applications for current students will not be considered if
submitted through the external career center.
Position Details
POSITION SUMMARY
The Department of History, Geography, and Legal Studies in the
College of Social Sciences, Mathematics and Education at the
University of Tampa invites applications for a tenure-track
position in United States and the World History Since 1945 at the
rank of Assistant Professor starting in August 2027. The Department
welcomes candidates from all specializations within this field, but
applications from candidates whose teaching and research includes
civil rights, human rights, or social movements are especially
desirable.
The successful candidate will be responsible for teaching three,
4-credit courses per semester, or six per year. Applicants are
expected to demonstrate a commitment to excellence in teaching and
to engaging students in learning beyond the classroom. Successful
candidates must have at least two years of full-time, in-person
teaching experience at the post-secondary level.
Applicants will have demonstrated scholarship in their area of
expertise. Other responsibilities include student advising, and
service to the department, college and University.
Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until
the position is filled. Salary is competitive and commensurate with
experience.
QUALIFICATIONS
The successful candidate must have a Ph.D. in History. (ABD will
not be considered.) Applicants must show evidence of outstanding
teaching and demonstrate the ability to teach a wide variety of
courses that engage History majors as well as general education
students. Finally, the candidate must show evidence of an active
research agenda, with the potential to involve undergraduate majors
in their work.
Required Attachments
All required documents listed below should be uploaded to the
attachment box at the bottom of the "My Experience" page of the
application before continuing through the application.
• Cover letter
• Curriculum vitae
• 250-word statement describing how you have successfully engaged
students in your classes
• 500-word statement of research agenda
• Recent course evaluations
• Graduate transcript (unofficial is acceptable for initial
review)
• Contact information for at least four professional
references
Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until
the position is filled.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
The University of Tampa is a medium-sized, comprehensive,
residentially based private institution of more than 11,000
undergraduate and graduate students. The University is ideally
situated on a beautiful 110-acre campus next to the Hillsborough
River, adjacent to Tampa's dynamic central business district, which
is a growing, vibrant, diverse metropolitan area. UTampa reflects
this vibrancy; with 30 consecutive years of enrollment growth
UTampa boasts 260 student organizations, a multicultural student
body from 50 states and more than 100 countries, and "Top Tier"
ranking in U.S. News and World Report.
The University delivers challenging and high-quality educational
experiences to a diverse group of learners. The University has a
strong core curriculum rooted in the liberal arts, an enduring
commitment to internationalization that has garnered the Senator
Paul Simon Award, and a practical, experiential approach to
learning. The University offers more than 200 areas of study,
including majors in our colleges of Arts and Letters, Business,
Natural and Health Sciences, and Social Sciences, Mathematics, and
Education, 18 master's programs, and 3 professional doctoral
programs.
The College of Social Sciences, Mathematics, and Education offers
rigorous, high-quality undergraduate curricula in Actuarial
Science, Computer Science, Criminology and Criminal Justice, Data
Science, Education, History, International Studies, Mathematics,
Political Science, Psychology, and Applied Sociology. Graduate
programs include a M.S. in Criminology and Criminal Justice, a
M.Ed. in Curriculum & Instruction, a M.Ed. in Educational
Leadership, and a M.S. in Instructional Design and Technology. Our
faculty are excellent teachers and scholars who engage their
students both in and out of the classroom. Our college continually
fosters relationships with governmental, not-for-profit, and
community organizations in the greater Tampa Bay region to provide
students with the opportunity to pursue an internship, volunteer,
or interact with professionals working in their chosen field. Each
department also offers study abroad courses that students can take
for credit toward their degree. For more information, see
https://www.ut.edu/academics/college-of-social-sciences-mathematics-and-education.
The faculty and administrators in CSSME, along with professional
staff across the University, will provide meaningful support for
your teaching and scholarship as elements of your personal and
career development. We encourage you to grow professionally, and we
support a healthy work-life integration to nurture that growth. The
vision of the College of Social Sciences, Mathematics, and
Education is "Empowering learners to make a difference." All
candidates are expected to contribute to the diversity of our
curriculum and community. We are searching for teacher-scholars who
will serve as mentors for our diverse student body, and who have a
demonstrated commitment to the academic success of all
students.
The University of Tampa is an equal opportunity employer dedicated
to excellence through diversity and does not discriminate based on
age, race, sex, disability, sexual orientation, national origin,
religion, marital status, gender identity, veteran status, or any
other non-job-related criteria. The University of Tampa recognizes
the importance of a multicultural community of students, faculty,
and staff who seek to advance our commitment to diversity. The
University invites applications from underrepresented groups and
those who have academic experiences with diverse populations.
Submission Guidelines
To receive full consideration for a faculty appointment with The
University of Tampa, please be sure to upload documents as required
for this position at time of application submission. Once your
application has been submitted, no changes may be made. Required
documents should be submitted in the attachment box at the bottom
of the "My Experience" page of the application before continuing
through the application. Note: A maximum of five (5)
documents may be attached to your application. If more than five
(5) documents are required, please combine the additional documents
into a single attachment so that you may continue through the
application process.
Background Check Requirements
Finalists may be required to submit to a criminal background
check.
To apply, visit https://utampa.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/en-US/Faculty/job/Tampa/Assistant-Professor--History_R0011093-1.

The Department of Management, Marketing, Logistics, and Business Analytics in UAA's College of Business and Public Policy is seeking an Assistant Professor of Business Analytics to teach and mentor students in Business and Data Analytics courses at both undergraduate and graduate levels. You will conduct research in these fields, covering topics such as machine learning, data mining, and predictive modeling, while also contributing to the university and community through service. This full-time, tenure-track role requires a Ph.D. in Business Analytics or Data Science and is a 9-month appointment beginning in August 2027.
UAA is a comprehensive public institution with a main campus in Anchorage, supported by community campuses and extension sites across Alaska. The College of Business and Public Policy is accredited by AACSB and offers BBA Degrees in Accounting, Economics, Finance, Management, Business and Data Analytics, and Marketing, along with MBA, MPA, and MPP Graduate programs, Associate degrees, and various Occupational Endorsement Certificates.
The Assistant Professor of Business Analytics is a full-time, 9-month, tenure-track position in the Management, Marketing, Logistics, and Business Analytics Department at the University of Alaska Anchorage. This role includes responsibilities in (1) teaching, (2) research, and (3) providing professional service to the university, the profession/discipline, and the community. The teaching load is three courses per semester, beginning in August 2027. The successful candidate will be expected to teach both undergraduate and graduate courses in subjects such as Business Analytics, Data Science, and AI.
A successful candidate should have expertise in teaching and research within Business Analytics, AI, and Data Science fields. The candidate should be capable of teaching advanced concepts and have a strong foundation in relevant technical skills, paired with effective teaching and communication abilities.
Minimum Qualifications:

A Ph.D. fields such as Computer Science, Mathematics, or Machine Learning will also be considered if applicant has completed relevant coursework and/or has relevant industry experience.
Candidates who are ABD may be considered if they provide evidence that degree completion will occur prior to the hire date.
