jobs.title: Tenure-Track Assistant Professor, Advertising Creative Strategy, Department Of Communication,
jobs.description:
Job Details
Tenure-Track Assistant Professor, Advertising Creative Strategy,
Department Of Communication, Advertising & Public
Relations
R0011094
Tampa
If you are a current University of Tampa student, please search
for and apply to student jobs here via Workday. Job
applications for current students will not be considered if
submitted through the external career center.
Position Details
The Department of Communication's Advertising and Public Relations
(ADPR) program, within the College of Arts & Letters, seeks a
full-time, tenure-track assistant professor to begin August 15,
2027, with a Ph.D. in Communication or a related terminal field
(terminal degree must be earned by August 15, 2027) to join a
thriving undergraduate program.
The candidate will teach courses related to Advertising Principles,
Campaigns, and Strategic and Creative Direction. Teaching load is 3
courses (12 credit hours) per semester over two 15-week semesters
per academic year.
The University of Tampa is a medium-sized, comprehensive,
residentially based private institution of more than 11,000
undergraduate and graduate students. The University is ideally
situated on a beautiful 110-acre campus next to the Hillsborough
River, adjacent to Tampa's dynamic central business district, which
is a growing, vibrant, diverse metropolitan area. UT reflects this
vibrancy; with 25 consecutive years of enrollment growth UT boasts
260 student organizations, a multicultural student body from 50
states and more than 100 countries, and "Top Tier" ranking in U.S.
News and World Report.
The successful candidate will demonstrate excellence in
undergraduate teaching, maintain an active record of scholarship,
participate in academic advising, and engage in service to the
department, college, university, and broader community. Candidates
with proven track records and experience in teaching creative
strategy and direction are preferred. We welcome innovative
pedagogies and creative research agendas and traditions of
scholarship.
Interested candidates should possess: a Ph.D. or other terminal
degree related to the field, by August 15, 2027; teaching
experience and professional experience are preferred.
The Department of Communication includes four vibrant majors and
participates in delivering two interdisciplinary M.A. programs.
Undergraduate programs include Advertising & Public Relations
(ADPR); Communication, Media &Culture (CMC); Journalism (JOU),
and Speech and Communication Studies (CSS). Graduate programs
include the M.A.in Professional Communication (MAPC) and M.A. in
Social and Emerging Media (MASEM).
The Advertising & Public Relations undergraduate program
fosters three concentrations: Advertising Creative, Public
Relations, and the General (combined) concentration. All three
concentrations prepare students for professional and academic
careers in strategic communication by featuring advanced digital
facilities, education in theory and practice, advanced
problem-solving, and exploration of communication ethics, as well
as critical perspectives on media and culture. Small class sizes at
The University of Tampa allow for mentorship connections with
students, as well as student engagement with local, national, and
international networks in media, advertising, and public
relations.
Responsibilities
The tenure-track faculty member in this position will support the

ways:

jobs.description:
Job Details
Two Tenure-Track Faculty Positions in Macroeconomics
Description
The Department of Economics and Accounting at the
College of the Holy Cross invites applications for two full-time
tenure-track positions, specializing in macroeconomics, to begin in
August 2027. The positions may be at either the Assistant Professor
or Associate Professor (without tenure) level. Strong preference
will be given to candidates with research and teaching interests in
macro development, economic growth, monetary economics,
international economics, or financial economics. The successful
candidate will be committed to developing effective and engaging
teaching practices in both elective courses related to their
research and core courses such as Quantitative Macroeconomics. The
successful candidate will also complement the curricular and
scholarly breadth of the department, is expected to establish and
maintain an active program of scholarly research in their
discipline or across disciplines, supervise student research, and
be engaged members of the department and College communities.
Each of these positions carries a 3-2 teaching load, and Holy Cross
offers generous sabbatical and fellowship leaves for tenured
faculty. To enable a smooth transition to Holy Cross, new full-time
tenure-track faculty receive start-up funding to support their
research and professional development and have a one-course
reduction in their first year of teaching (i.e., 2-2). Faculty who
enter Holy Cross as an assistant professor and who claim less than
three years of credit toward their tenure clock also have a
research leave prior to tenure review of either a full year at 80%
salary or a semester at full salary. This leave is not available to
faculty who enter as an untenured associate professor or who enter
as an assistant professor and claim three years of credit toward
their tenure clock.
Each of these positions offers full benefits. Starting salaries are
$123,000 for an assistant professor with no prior tenure-track
experience or one year of prior tenure-track experience at another
institution; $127,800-$131,400 for an assistant professor with two
or more years of prior tenure-track experience; and $134,400 -
$137,400 for faculty entering Holy Cross as untenured associate
professors. Salary within the applicable range will be based on
qualifications and experience.
In alignment with the strategic plans for Holy Cross and the division of Academic Affairs, we view
academic excellence and inclusive excellence as inextricably
linked. Our faculty combine high-impact scholarship and outstanding
teaching with a deep commitment to inclusive excellence. They
generate new knowledge in their fields while utilizing
evidence-based teaching strategies and course designs to create
classroom environments where all students have a sense of
belonging, are valued, and can flourish to reach their full
potential. Academic freedom is a cornerstone of our intellectual
and moral community; the College is committed to supporting faculty
and students as they work to advance our educational mission and
serve the common good.
Qualifications
Candidates must demonstrate excellence in scholarship and
undergraduate teaching as well as a commitment to inclusive
pedagogies. A Ph.D. is required by the beginning of the
appointment.

A cover letter addressing the position requirements listed
above as well as the ways you might contribute to and further the
College's
mission as a Jesuit, undergraduate liberal arts college and its
core commitment
to creating a community where every individual feels empowered
to contribute their talents and perspectives.

Your job market paper
Three confidential letters of recommendation
Unofficial graduate transcripts, and
A statement of your teaching philosophy and interests, with
particular emphasis on how you utilize evidence-based teaching
strategies to foster inclusive, high-belonging classroom
environments.

faculty job applications. Please submit all materials to https://apply.interfolio.com/193937.

early January, and campus visits for finalists will take place in

directed to Professor Justin Svec (jsvec@holycross.edu).

jobs.title: LITERACY EDUCATION - ASSISTANT PROFESSOR (TENURE-TRACK)
jobs.institution: University of Vermont College of Education and Social Services
jobs.description:
The College of Education and Social Services (CESS) at the University of Vermont invites nominations and applications for a full-time, nine-month, tenure-track position in the Department of Education beginning Fall 2027, at the rank of Assistant Professor with research and teaching that emphasize foundational literacy or literacy development in early ages/grades. Applicants should be motivated by the opportunity to contribute to the CESS mission to "create a more humane and just society.”
The successful candidate will demonstrate expertise in foundational literacy through publications, teaching, and service. We are particularly interested in those with training in quantitative methods and experience with grant-writing and oversight of externally funded projects.
The University
Established in 1791, the University of Vermont is classified as a prestigious Carnegie R1 institution and consistently ranked as one of the top public universities in the United States. UVM is distinctive for its small New-England liberal arts college feel. UVM’s tradition of equity and social justice extends not only to faculty, staff, and students, but also is reflected in a commitment to environmentally sound and sustainable practices. Notable innovations include complex data mapping and analysis, material innovation, social and rural health and mental health, and health and medical sciences.
The College
The Mission of The College of Education and Social Services is to educate and prepare outstanding professionals in education, human services, and social work; engage in scholarship of high quality; and provide exemplary professional service to Vermont, the nation, and the world. We do this to contribute to a more humane and just society, free from oppression, that maximizes human potential and the quality of life for all individuals, families and communities.
The Department
The Department of Education is home to educator and leadership preparation programs at the UG, Masters, EdD and PhD levels, with graduate programs ranked # 69 by USNWR. The programs are nationally accredited, award recognized, and known for high-impact instructional practices with a community-engagement focus. Faculty are nationally and internationally recognized in their fields as evidenced by disciplinary awards, Fullbright and Spencer awards, and comparative faculty metrics placing us in the top tiers of publications and interdisciplinary scholarly works.
The Community
Burlington, Vermont, is ranked by Indeed as the #3 best city to work in the United States and CNN ranks Burlington as #6 as “America’s Best Towns to Visit in 2026.” Burlington and UVM share a panoramic setting on the shores of Lake Champlain, between the Green Mountains of Vermont and the Adirondack Mountains of New York State. We are a walkable and bikeable community with University sponsored ride sharing and public transportation. The Burlington International Airport is served by Delta, American, United and other major carriers. We have a rich cultural, civic, and arts community as well as a wide range of outdoor activities year-round. Vermont’s size and history support an environment of access and opportunities for collaborative agency partnerships throughout the state and region.
Responsibilities:
The successful candidate will assume a range of responsibilities that include:
Consistent and cohesive program of research
Excellence in teaching and advising
Collegial service contributions
Required Qualifications:
Doctoral degree in a relevant discipline
Record of publication commensurate with rank
Relevant experience with external grant funding
Teaching excellence in higher education
Strong collegial, communication, and collaborative teamwork skills
Preferred Qualifications:
Foundational literacy expertise relevant for educator preparation programs
Collaborative skills and experience with state department policies and literacy-related change initiatives related to literacy
Content area expertise in literacy interventions across universal instruction and tier 2 and 3 interventions
Experience and commitment that will help elevate UVM’s position as a leader in literacy in the state and beyond
The University of Vermont is a welcoming, educationally purposeful community committed to creating an inclusive environment that embraces intellectual diversity and global perspectives. We seek to prepare students to be accountable leaders who will bring to their work a grasp of complexity, effective problem-solving and communication skills, and an enduring commitment to learning and ethical conduct. Members of the University of Vermont community embrace and advance the values of Our Common Ground: Respect, Integrity, Innovation, Openness, Justice, and Responsibility. The successful candidate will demonstrate a strong commitment to UVM’s mission and advancing Our Common Ground values through their teaching, service, research, scholarship, or creative arts.
Salary Range (9 Mo): Assistant Professor: $79,000-$82,000
Final offers include a start-up package for research, with salary determinations based upon experience and qualifications.
Application Process
Review of applications will begin October 15, 2026, and continue until the position is filled. For more detailed information about us, visit our web pages Department of Education; the College of Education and Social Services; and the University of Vermont..
Anticipated starting date is August 23, 2027. Please apply online at www.uvmjobs.com. Include 1) a cover letter specifically addressing how your qualifications meet position requirements; 2) a current curriculum vitae; 3) a separate 1 page statement on how you, as a faculty member in the department, would enhance the impact of Our Common Ground Values at UVM; and 4) the names and email addresses of three references who can be contacted for letters of support before a candidate is advanced to on-campus interviews in the search process. For all applicants, employment is subject to a successful background check. For more information about the position, please contact the Search Committee Chair, Lori Meyer, at lori.meyer@uvm.edu.
The University of Vermont is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other category legally protected by federal or state law.

jobs.title: Tenured Associate Professor in Sociology
jobs.description:
The Department of Sociology at Vanderbilt University invites applications for a tenured Associate Professor in Sociology with research specialization in computing and society to begin fall semester 2027. The successful candidate will study the societal drivers and effects of computing as a social and material force, applying sociological theories and methods to questions of AI, machine learning, quantum computing, and/or social media. They will use rigorous and theoretically driven qualitative and/or quantitative methods, and their work will have strong potential for external funding. An ideal candidate will be prepared to respond to growing student demand, both undergraduate and graduate students, to learn about how social factors are built into computing systems and how computing systems organize social life. Additionally, we seek a faculty member who will complement our department’s existing strengths in sociological study of demography, health, social psychology, and/or work. This position will also support the new Arts & Science Core curriculum, with the opportunity to teach in the first-year Core or develop an Exploratory Core course.
Qualifications
Qualifications: Vanderbilt expects excellence in research and teaching. A Ph.D. in sociology is required.
Application Instructions
Please submit via Interfolio [https://apply.interfolio.com/193367] the following
1) a letter describing research and teaching interests and professional experience
2) curriculum vitae.
Shortlisted candidates will be invited to submit three letters of reference and evidence of teaching effectiveness, including course evaluations.
Applications will be reviewed starting October 15, 2026 and continue until the position is filled. Please contact Holly McCammon (holly.j.mccammon@vanderbilt.edu), Department Chair, with any questions.
EEO Statement
Vanderbilt University shall abide by the requirements of 41 CFR §§ 60-1.4(a), 60-300.5(a) and 60-741.5(a). These regulations prohibit discrimination against qualified individuals based on their status as protected veterans or individuals with disabilities and prohibit discrimination against all individuals based on their race, color, religion, sex, or national origin. Moreover, these regulations require that covered prime contractors and subcontractors provide equal employment opportunity without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, protected veteran status or disability.

The University
One of the largest universities in the country, California State
University, Northridge (CSUN) is an urban, comprehensive university
that delivers award-winning undergraduate and graduate programs to
over 36,000 students annually and counts over 425,000 alumni who
fuel the region's economy. Since its founding in 1958, CSUN has
made a significant and long-term impact on California, generating
nearly $1.9 billion in economic impact and more than 12,000 jobs
each year. California State University, Northridge is a designated
Minority Serving and Hispanic Serving Institution (MSI/HSI) and a
California Black Serving Institution (BSI), nationally and
statewide recognized for advancing opportunity and promoting the
success of Hispanic, Black, African American, and other
historically underserved students. In 2025, Washington Monthly
named the university the No. 1 master's university in the nation
for contributions to the public good and ranked CSUN No. 2 Best
Bang for the Buck in the West and No. 3 Best Colleges for Your
Tuition and Tax Dollars. Also in 2025, the university earned a
4.5-star rating in Money's Best Colleges, ranked No. 3 for
diversity among public universities and No. 8 in the nation for
social mobility in The Wall Street Journal/College Pulse. In
addition, CSUN placed No. 9 on the California Mobility Index for
advancing economic and social mobility from the College Futures
Foundation.
About the Position of Associate Vice President for Faculty
Affairs
The Associate Vice President for Faculty Affairs (AVP FA) serves as
the University's academic personnel officer for faculty (Unit 3)
and academic student employees (Unit 11). Reporting to the Provost
and Vice President for Academic Affairs, the AVP FA provides
strategic leadership and administrative oversight for all faculty
lifecycle matters, including recruitment, appointment, evaluation,
retention, tenure, promotion, compensation, leaves, retirement, and
faculty professional success. The AVP FA ensures compliance with
collective bargaining agreements, CSU policies, and applicable
state and federal regulations while advancing equity, diversity,
inclusion, and belonging in all academic personnel processes.
As a member of the Academic Affairs leadership team, the AVP FA
advises the Provost, deans, and department chairs on complex
faculty personnel and labor relations matters. The AVP FA
interprets and implements collective bargaining agreements,
oversees grievance and disciplinary processes, conducts or
supervises investigations as appropriate, and represents the
University in labor management and arbitration proceedings. The
position works closely with Human Resources, Equity and Compliance,
and shared governance bodies to ensure fair, consistent, and
legally sound personnel practices. This role requires sound
judgment, collaborative leadership, and the ability to balance
institutional priorities with faculty interests in a dynamic higher
education environment.
As a leader, the AVP will have the opportunity to thrive in a
community in which our leaders share common traits as identified in
our Leadership Principles https://www.csun.edu/leadership-principles.

institution

complex policies and procedures

inclusion, belonging, and accessibility in higher education
Demonstrated ability to handle sensitive and confidential
matters with sound judgment, integrity, and professionalism
Excellent written, oral, and interpersonal communication
skills, including collaborating with campus partners, building
trust, and facilitating shared governance

including recruitment, evaluation, retention, tenure, and
promotion
Demonstrated experience interpreting and implementing
collective bargaining agreements in a unionized higher education
environment
Demonstrated experience administering or advising on grievance,
disciplinary, or conflict resolution processes
Demonstrated experience collaborating with human resources,
equity/compliance offices, or legal counsel on personnel
matters
Demonstrated experience supporting equity-focused initiatives
in faculty hiring, evaluation, and retention
Demonstrated experience mentoring faculty and supporting
department chair leadership development
Demonstrated experience supervising professional staff and
managing administrative budgets while upholding staff welfare
through dignity- and respect-centered supervision
Demonstrated experience representing an institution in
systemwide committees or external relations
Demonstrated experience leading organizational change, process
improvement, or modernization of administrative systems

The department of Communication Studies at California State

Professor.
The successful candidate will teach undergraduate and graduate
courses in the department. The ideal candidate will remain active

debate and forensics pedagogy, and maintain a scholarly agenda that
results in publication or equivalent contributions.

Description
The Department of Statistics and Data Science (SDS) at The
University of Texas at Austin invites applications for
professional-track faculty positions at the rank of Assistant,
Associate, or Full Professor of Instruction. SDS is the newest and
fastest growing department in the College of Natural Sciences and
is dedicated to delivering high-quality, innovative education in
statistics and data science across the university. Our programs
include an undergraduate major and minor in Statistics and Data
Science, an M.S. and Ph.D. in Statistics, an undergraduate
certificate in Applied Statistical Modeling, and an online M.S. in
Data Science offered in collaboration with the Department of
Computer Science. SDS is internationally recognized for excellence
in statistical methodology and theory, applied statistics, data
science, biostatistics, and machine learning.
The department currently has 25 tenured/tenure-track and 10
professional-track faculty members. While professional-track
faculty are not eligible for tenure, we hire with the intent that
all new faculty will build lasting careers as part of our
community. The department is committed to investing in the
professional growth of all of our faculty.
Austin, the capital of Texas, is a center for high-technology
industry, including companies such as 3M, Amazon, AMD, Apple,
Applied Materials, AT&T, Dell, Google, IBM, National
Instruments, and Samsung. Much of Austin's lifestyle is driven by
outdoor activities, media, and music.
More information about the department is here.
Qualifications
Candidates must hold a doctoral degree in statistics, computer
science, biostatistics, data science, or a related discipline by
August 2027. We especially welcome applicants with teaching
experience or professional practice as a statistician,
biostatistician, or data scientist; these experiences are valued
but not required.
Application Instructions
Applicants should submit a cover letter, a CV, and a teaching
statement. As part of the application process, candidates will be
asked to provide the names and email addresses of two individuals
who are willing to provide letters of support via Interfolio. A
link to a professional website may be provided on the candidate's
CV.
Applications for the Assistant/Associate/Full Professor of
Instruction positions will be reviewed on an ongoing basis, but
priority will be given to applications received on or before
November 30, 2026.
The department is committed to respecting the confidentiality of
the search process.
A background check will be conducted on applicants selected for the
positions.
Questions about the search process should be directed to Professor
Jay Bartroff, SDS Professional-Track Faculty Search Committee Chair
and SDS Associate Chair. Please send inquiries to
statjobs@austin.utexas.edu instead of emailing the search committee
chair directly.
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

opportunity/affirmative action employer, complies with all

affirmative action. The University is committed to a policy of
equal opportunity for all persons and does not discriminate on the
basis of race, color, national origin, age, marital status, sex,
sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, disability,
religion, or veteran status in employment, educational programs and
activities, and admissions.

California State University, Long Beach (CSULB) is a Hispanic Serving Institution
(HSI) and an Asian American and Native American Pacific
Islander-Serving Institution (AANAPISI). CSULB earned the
prestigious Seal of Excelencia in 2023, joining a distinctive group
of colleges and universities who have been recognized for its

the Black Excellence Collegium, dedicated to promoting Black
excellence and advancing Black Student Success, and El Concilio for
Latinx Success at the Beach, whose mission is to build capacity and
promote inclusive servingness across initiatives and efforts for
the benefit of all students. The President's Equity and Change
Commission is dedicated to achieving inclusive excellence in our
community and culture and throughout the university. CSULB's Beach 2030 University Action
Plans prioritize engaging all students; expanding access to higher
education; promoting intellectual achievement; building community;
and cultivating resilience.
College of the
Arts
Department of Dance
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:
Professional preparation demonstrated through at least one of
the following:
MFA or PhD in Dance, Performance Studies, or a related field,
with a Dance-based creative/research profile (Transcript or
official notification of completion of the master's or doctoral
degree by August 1, 2027, if applicable).
MA in Dance or a related field with professional performance
and/or choreographic experience in Latinx/e and/or Afro-Latinx/e
dance forms
Professional performance and/or choreographic experience in
Latinx/e and/or Afro-Latinx/e dance forms at a regional, national,
and/or international level
Demonstrated ability to teach one or more Latinx/e and/or
Afro-Latinx/e dance forms
Qualification(s) to teach one or more of the following
technical praxis courses: modern/contemporary, jazz, African,
street dance, and/or ballet
Demonstrated commitment to working successfully with a diverse
student population, including low socioeconomic and
first-generation students
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
Sustained professional experience in commercial, concert dance,
and/or culturally embedded contexts with national or international
impact
Demonstrated college teaching experience
Demonstrated ability to teach traditional, contemporary,
commercial, and/or diasporic dance forms with a focus on Latinx/e
and/or Afro-Latinx/e social, political, cultural, and aesthetic
practices
Demonstrated ability to teach and mentor college students from
a Latinx/e and/or Afro-Latinx/e culturally relevant and culturally
sustaining perspective in one or more of the following: technical
praxis courses, dancemaking and/or improvisation, dance studies,
dance pedagogy, dance conditioning and/or Pilates, and/or dance
technologies (such as screen dance)
Demonstrated evidence of a body of choreographic work in
Latinx/e and/or Afro-Latinx/e traditional, contemporary, and/or
diasporic dance forms
Fluency in Spanish and English
Experience successfully working with populations
demographically and/or socioeconomically similar to the CSULB
student body
Experience mentoring or supporting students using inclusive and
culturally relevant teaching strategies in a diverse classroom
DUTIES:
Teach undergraduate and/or graduate courses in Latinx/e and/or
Afro-Latinx/e dance forms and other areas of
praxis/theory/production according to expertise. (Mode of
instruction may include in-person, hybrid, online, and/or any
combination thereof.) Technical praxis courses currently offered
include modern/contemporary, jazz, African, street dance, and
ballet
May be assigned to teach other department courses appropriate
to training and expertise, including general education courses
Assist with development of curriculum in area(s) of
expertise

expertise
Choreograph for department concerts. Direct department concerts
and/or events
Participate in student recruitment and mentor graduate
candidates and undergraduate dance majors or minors, including
engaging in thesis supervision and providing guidance to students
interested in further study or career opportunities in
performance/choreography and/or pedagogy
Responsible for producing creative/scholarly work commensurate
with the requirements for tenure and expected to contribute to the
development and vitality of the department, college, and
university, through service and continued engagement in the
field
Participate in service to the department, college, university,
and field/community
CSULB seeks to recruit faculty who enthusiastically support the
University's strong commitment to the academic success of all of
our students, including students with disabilities, students who
are first generation to college, veterans, students with diverse
socio-economic backgrounds, and students of diverse sexual
orientations and gender expressions. CSULB seeks to recruit and
retain a diverse workforce as a reflection of our commitment to
serve the People of California, to maintain the excellence of the
University, and to offer our students a rich variety of expertise,
perspectives, and ways of knowing and learning.
ABOUT THE DEPARTMENT OF DANCE:
CSULB is the state's largest and most comprehensive publicly funded
school for the arts, with approximately 40,000 graduate and
undergraduate students. CSULB Dance is housed within the College of
the Arts (COTA), which includes five additional departments in art,
design, film, music, and theater, as well as the Carolyn Campagna
Kleefeld Contemporary Art Museum, and the Carpenter Performing Arts
Center (CPAC). Enrollments in the department are representative of
our state's demographics. Many of our majors transfer from
California's extensive high-quality community college system.
Our department takes a holistic, student-centered approach to
education that integrates dance-making and physical training with
coursework in dance history, ethnography, dance science, somatics,
pedagogy, design, production, and an array of immersive and
challenging creative and research opportunities. Through these
experiences, our faculty seeks to equip each of our graduates with
the skills, knowledge, and confidence to engage in the dynamic
field of dance, and its related studies, and to contribute to its
vitality as artists, scholars, educators, and advocates.
The Department of Dance offers the following degree pathways: MA,
MFA, BA, BS, BFA, and a dance minor. Additionally, the Department
offers a teaching credential in Dance through the College of
Education. Recent and ongoing revisions to the undergraduate
curriculum work to dismantle the hierarchy of Western dance forms
and acknowledge the artistic and cultural contributions and
relevance of diasporic dance forms to our communities and the
profession. Significant changes include the elevation of Street
dance to an area of concentration within the BA/BFA, and the

Latinx/e and/or Afro-Latinx/e dance forms."

Applied Geospatial Analysis, Assistant Professor

Tenure Track Faculty Position
Assistant Professor of Applied Geospatial

Department of Plant Sciences
Don B. Huntley College of Agriculture
Salary Range: $81,572 - $85,572
California State Polytechnic University, Pomona invites
applications for a tenure track faculty position in the Plant
Science Department. Cal Poly Pomona is one of three polytechnic
universities in the 22-campus
California State University system and among 12 such
institutions nationwide. Since its founding in 1938, Cal Poly
Pomona students participate in an integrative experiential learning
education that is inclusive, relevant, and values diverse
perspectives and experiences. With a variety of degree programs in
the arts, humanities, sciences, engineering, and professional
disciplines, the university is well known for its learn- by-doing
approach and
Teacher Scholar Model.
The university is noted for its scenic and historic 1,400-acre
campus, which was once the winter ranch of cereal magnate W.K.
Kellogg. We acknowledge that Cal Poly Pomona resides on the
territorial and homelands of the Tongva and Tataavium people who
are the traditional land caretakers of Tovaangar. The university's
nearly 30,000 students are taught and mentored by the campus's more
than 1,400 faculty as part of 54 baccalaureate and 29 master's
degree programs, 11 credential and certificate programs, and a
doctorate in educational leadership.
Highly regarded among its peer institutions, Cal Poly Pomona is No.
2 in the U.S. News and World Report rankings of top public regional
universities in the west and was named the No. 28 best value
college in the nation by Money Magazine. Cal Poly Pomona, a
Hispanic-Serving Institution and an Asian American and Native
American Pacific Islander-Serving Institution, stands as a national
leader in promoting social mobility, and was
placed among the 25 top institutions in the country in awarding
bachelor's degrees to minoritized students by Diverse Issues in
Higher Education. In 2022, the campus launched the Black Thriving Initiative recognizing
that Cal Poly Pomona's future as a university is linked to the
success of its Black community. More information about our
Principles of Community can be found here.
The Cal Poly Pomona campus is located less than 30 miles east of
downtown Los Angeles at the intersection of Los Angeles, Orange,
Riverside and San Bernardino counties. It is within an hour's drive
of beaches, mountains and deserts. For additional information about
the university, please visit www.cpp.edu, and for more about faculty
life, please see YourLife@CPP.
Student Population. Cal Poly Pomona is the number one polytechnic
university in the nation for student diversity and economic
mobility. Our caring and inclusive campus community is committed to
helping anyone who dreams of success achieve it. In Fall 2024, Cal
Poly Pomona served more than 25,000 students and close to 2,000
graduate students, mostly residents of California. Over half of Cal
Poly Pomona students are first-generation college students, 70%
receive financial aid, and 42% are low-income students. The
university enrolls 57% of historically underrepresented students.
Our diverse student body identifies as 54% Hispanic/Latinx, 21%
Asian, 13% White, 4% two or more races, 3% unknown, 2% African
American/Black, 2% International, less than 1% Native Hawaiian or
Pacific Islander, and less than 1% Native American. Forty-five
percent of students enroll in our STEM majors, and our top five
enrolled programs across the university include mechanical
engineering, computer science, civil engineering, psychology, as
well as finance, real estate, and law.
Don B. Huntley College of Agriculture: The Don B.
Huntley College of Agriculture prepares students to address
challenges facing agriculture, food systems, natural resources, and
communities through Cal Poly Pomona's signature learn-by-doing
educational approach. The College provides students with
opportunities to integrate scientific knowledge, emerging
technologies, and practical experience through classroom,
laboratory, field, and community-based learning. Its location in
Southern California provides a distinctive setting for studying
agriculture across urban, peri-urban, and production systems and
for developing partnerships with agricultural industries, agencies,
communities, and other stakeholders.
Plant Science Department: The Plant Science
Department is a close-knit learning community that provides
students with hands-on, experiential education on plant growth and
production, soil health, pest management, environmental
stewardship, and technology-supported, data-driven agriculture. The
curriculum emphasizes practical problem solving, critical thinking,
communication, and the integration of scientific and technological
approaches to address challenges facing modern agricultural
systems.
Experiential learning is central to the Department's teaching and
research mission. Faculty and students have access to diverse
on-campus agricultural and research environments including the
125-acre Spadra
Farm, the student-led
Microfarm, AGRIscapes Center,
the CPP Apiary,
the Lyle Center
for Sustainability and Regenerative Studies, the Center
for Turfgrass, Irrigation, and Landscape Technology,
vertical growing facilities, and many other agricultural
landscapes across campus. These resources provide opportunities to
connect field observations and sampling, laboratory measurements,
geospatial technologies, and agricultural management
decisions.
Position description:
The Department of Plant Science invites applications for a
tenure-track Assistant Professor of Applied Geospatial
Analysis.
The successful candidate will teach existing undergraduate courses
in their area of expertise and develop new courses and curriculum
in GIS, spatial analysis, geospatial technologies, and/or related
applied geoscience methods relevant to agricultural and
environmental systems. Consistent with Cal Poly Pomona's
learn-by-doing philosophy, the faculty member will incorporate
hands-on laboratory, field, and data-driven experiences that
connect environmental data collection, spatial analysis,
interpretation, and visualization to real-world challenges in urban
and agricultural landscapes. The teaching assignment is 2-3 courses
per semester for the candidate's first two years. In subsequent
years, the teaching assignment will be 3-4 courses per semester,
with course-reduction opportunities for research, service, and
teaching initiatives.
The successful candidate will establish an active scholarship
focused on agricultural and environmental systems using geospatial
and applied geoscience approaches. The faculty member will
disseminate scholarly work through peer-reviewed publications
and/or professional presentations and pursue funding to support
their research program. Opportunities exist for interdisciplinary
collaboration with faculty in the Department of Plant Science in
areas such as precision agriculture, entomology, pest management,
plant breeding, plant pathology, ethnobotany, soil science,
environmental toxicology, urban agriculture, and related
disciplines, as well as with faculty and programs across the
university. Consistent with Cal Poly Pomona's Teacher-Scholar
Model, the successful candidate will mentor students in research
activities, field investigations, and applied projects, integrating
scholarship with the department's emphasis on experiential and
applied learning.
The successful candidate will participate in internal service to
the department, college, and university, as well as external
service to professional organizations or the broader community.
Internal service includes participating in departmental planning
activities and serving on academic senate, hiring, or curriculum
development committees. External service may include developing
collaborative relationships with industry, government agencies,
nonprofit organizations, and community partners.
The above activities will contribute to the candidate's
responsibilities in teaching, scholarship, and service and will be
evaluated in accordance with departmental and university
expectations for retention, tenure, and promotion.
We encourage applications at various stages of their academic
careers, such as advanced "all-but-dissertated" candidates,
postdoctoral fellows, junior faculty on both tenure and non-tenure
tracks, teaching faculty, scholars in contingent roles, those in
research and teaching positions outside of traditional academia, as
well as independent scholars, to submit their applications.
Candidates must hold a Ph.D. by the start of employment.
Minimum requirements include:
A Ph.D. in geography, environmental science, environmental
studies, soil science, plant biology, agronomy, forestry,
entomology, agricultural engineering, or other related field from
an accredited institution. Degree must be conferred by the start
date of the position.
Demonstrated expertise in geographic information systems (GIS),
spatial analysis, remote sensing, geospatial data science, or
related geospatial methods.
Demonstrated ability to work effectively with students, staff,
and faculty from diverse ethnic, cultural, and socioeconomic
backgrounds.
Preferred/Desired Qualifications:
Preference will be given to candidates who demonstrate one or more
of the following:
Expertise applying geospatial technologies to agriculture,
urban agroecosystems, environmental monitoring, environmental
justice, or natural resource management.
Experience with remote sensing, drone-based data collection,
spatial modeling, geospatial data science, or geospatial artificial
intelligence (GeoAI).
Experience with industry-relevant software and platforms, such
as ArcGIS, QGIS, Python, R Statistics, Google Earth Engine, ENVI,
or others.
Experience teaching GIS, spatial analysis, remote sensing,
data-driven agriculture, or related subjects, with an emphasis on
high-impact techniques such as hands-on, experiential, or
field-based teaching.
Experience mentoring students in research or applied
projects.
Evidence of potential to obtain funding for research
activities.
Experience collaborating across disciplines or with industry,
government agencies, community organizations, growers, or other
stakeholders.
Experience communicating spatial information through maps,
visualization, or other approaches that support agricultural or
environmental decision-making.
Application
A completed application will consist of a:
Cover letter in which you describe your interest in the
position, relevant experience, and how you meet the minimum and
preferred qualifications;
Curriculum vitae;
Teaching Philosophy statement (2-page max) that addresses Cal
Poly Pomona's commitment to excellence in education and includes
examples of practices used to support student learning and
success;
Research Statement (2-page max);
The names and contact information for at least three
individuals who can serve as references during the final stages of
interview
Finalists for the position will:
be required to provide official transcripts for highest degree
before the on-campus interview;
be required to provide three letters of reference dated within
the last two years;
Final candidates being interviewed are expected to make a
presentation of creative work and a teaching demonstration to
faculty and interact with students.
Please direct inquiries to mlaiken@cpp.edu.

Position Details:
The Opportunity:
The School of Mechanical and Materials Engineering (MME) in the Voiland College of Engineering and Architecture (VCEA) at Washington State University invites applications for a full-time, 9-month, tenure-track position at the Assistant Professor rank in Pullman, WA. MME seeks to strengthen its capabilities in robotics and autonomous systems, with an emphasis on intelligent robotic systems designed to operate in complex, unstructured, and dynamic environments.
The search is intentionally broad across robotics and autonomy. Relevant application domains include, but are not limited to, agriculture, advanced manufacturing, environmental monitoring, nuclear systems, underwater and marine robotics, infrastructure inspection, construction, disaster response, and other real-world and mission-critical applications.
Candidates whose work can complement and create new collaborations with MME's existing strengths in advanced manufacturing, materials, energy, nuclear engineering, and related areas are particularly encouraged. It is anticipated the successful candidate will begin their appointment on August 16, 2027.
Job Duties:
The successful candidate is expected to establish an internationally recognized, externally funded research program that advances the autonomy, intelligence, robustness, and reliability of next-generation robotic systems. The candidate will collaborate with current faculty to build interdisciplinary teams and contribute to excellence in teaching, mentoring, and service.
We seek candidates with a strong foundation in robotics and autonomous systems. Areas of expertise may include, but are not limited to, robot perception, sensing, navigation and localization, planning and control, manipulation, robot learning, embodied AI, human-robot interaction, multi-robot systems, mechatronics, robotic system integration, and autonomous decision-making for physical robotic systems operating in real-world environments.
Candidates who integrate artificial intelligence and machine learning with physical robotic systems are particularly encouraged to apply. Research that connects robotics with the School's existing strengths-including advanced manufacturing and materials-is welcomed, but the candidate's primary scholarly identity should be in robotics and autonomous systems. The successful candidate should be capable of developing and teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in robotics and related areas, including mechatronics, system dynamics, control systems, introduction to robotics, robot dynamics, and other courses aligned with the department's educational mission and the candidate's expertise. The typical workload for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position within MME is 40% research, 40% teaching, and 20% service.
Additional Information:
This is a full-time (100% FTE), 9-month, tenure-track faculty position. This position is not eligible for overtime.
Screening date: First consideration will be provided to applications submitted before November 1, 2026. Review of applications will remain ongoing until the posting close date of January 31, 2027.
9-month Academic Salary: $100,000 - $115,000 USD | Commensurate with experience and qualifications
In accordance with RCW 49.58.110, the above salary reflects the full salary range for this position. Individual placement within the range is based on the candidate's current experience, education, skills, and abilities related to the position, or as mandated by a U.S. Department of Labor prevailing wage determination.
Benefits: WSU offers a comprehensive benefits package which includes paid sick leave; paid holidays; medical, dental, life and disability insurance package for employees and dependents; retirement; deferred compensation, optional supplemental retirement accounts. For additional information, please review the detailed Summary of Benefits offered by WSU for Faculty and Total Compensation.
Required Qualifications:
Ph.D. degree in Mechanical Engineering, Robotics Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field by the date of hire.
Demonstrate a strong commitment to building a world-class research program at WSU through publication of peer-reviewed research in leading journals and conferences, with potential to secure external research funding.
Proven or potential for successful teaching and instruction.
Demonstrated record of or potential for commitment to equitable and inclusive educational experiences and service in alignment with WSU's land grant mission.
Preferred Qualifications:
Demonstrated record of accomplishments and potential to become an outstanding scholar and educator in robotics and autonomous systems.
Excellent communication skills and the ability to teach undergraduate and graduate courses in robotics and related areas, such as mechatronics, dynamics, controls, and robot dynamics.
Demonstrated record or potential to become a national and international leader in robotics and autonomous systems, particularly in the development of intelligent robotic systems for real-world, unstructured, and dynamic environments.
Strong commitment to building a robust, externally funded research program and fostering interdisciplinary collaborations, including opportunities to connect robotics with MME strengths in advanced manufacturing, materials, energy, nuclear engineering, and related areas.

Washington State University, a land-grant, multiple-campus Research 1 institution. This position will serve on the Pullman campus, which has an enrollment of around 20,000 students and is located in Southeastern Washington on the homelands of the Nimíipuu (Nez Perce) Tribe and Palus people. Located 80 miles south of metropolitan Spokane, Pullman is also a quick drive away from the scenic Idaho panhandle and Moscow Mountain. The rolling hills of the Palouse offer a wide range of activities and a true four-season climate. The area provides ample opportunity to enjoy the cultural and academic hub of both Washington State University and the University of Idaho, in the neighboring town of Moscow, Idaho. With a population of 34,000, Pullman is a quintessential college town-ranked #1 in the "Best Cities to Live in Washington" by the Washington State Chamber of Commerce 2019 report; and recognized by Bloomberg Businessweek as the "Best Place to Raise Kids" in Washington state. Department of Psychology
Cal Poly Humboldt is a Hispanic-Serving Institution
(HSI) that strives to foster an equitable and inclusive community
that supports our students of diverse backgrounds. Cal Poly
Humboldt is committed to achieving the goals of equal opportunity
and endeavors to employ faculty of the highest quality committed
promoting excellence for all students.
DESCRIPTION:
Cal Poly Humboldt and the Department of Psychology invite
applicants for a full-time, academic year, tenure-track faculty
position in any field of psychology (e.g., Behavioral, Clinical,
Cognitive, Developmental, Neuroscience, Quantitative,
Social).
DEPARTMENT:
The Cal Poly Humboldt Psychology department is dedicated to
providing undergraduate and graduate students with the skills to
scientifically and critically evaluate psychological processes. Our
courses address the impact of culture and context on human
functioning, fostering an appreciation for differences through
research and applied experiences. We value and respect diversity as
a strength and in this regard, seek to attract and retain the best
possible students, staff, and faculty. We prepare our students to
apply their knowledge and skills from psychology to create a
socially just and an equitable society.
The Department of Psychology offers a B.A. degree, a minor program,
course options for general education requirements and electives,
service courses for other majors, and three graduate options
leading to the M.A. degree in School Psychology, Counseling
Psychology (MFT), and Academic Research in Psychology. Faculty with
specializations in each area contribute to all programs and options
in the department.
For more information about the department, please visit: https://psychology.humboldt.edu/
PROFESSIONAL DUTIES:
Candidates should be committed to teaching excellence and to
building a strong research record. Instructional assignments may
include: undergraduate and graduate courses (e.g. Introduction to
Psychology, Introductory and Advanced Psychological Statistics,
Introductory and Advanced Research Methods in Psychology,
Psychology of Critical Thinking, etc.). Candidates may have the
opportunity to teach other courses in their area of specialization.
Instructional assignments will be consistent with the programmatic
needs of the department and students.
The primary professional responsibilities of instructional faculty
members are: teaching, research, scholarship, creative activity,
and service to the University, profession and to the community.
These responsibilities include: advising students, participation in
campus and system-wide communities, maintaining office hours,
working collaboratively and productively with colleagues, and
participation in traditional academic functions. Probationary
faculty are typically provided ongoing mentorship to be a
successful member of the faculty. During the first two years of the
probationary period, teaching responsibilities will be reduced by
approximately one course each semester. The reduced teaching load
supports the establishment of research, scholarship and/or creative
activities required for retention, tenure, and promotion.
Cal Poly Humboldt also continues to build unique and innovative
learning opportunities for students, bridging multiple disciplines
across the spectrum. Cal Poly Humboldt is a leader in "learning
communities" that build relationships between students, faculty,
staff, administrators, and the community. These communities
incorporate environmental and social responsibility.
RANK, SALARY AND BENEFITS:
We seek to fill this position at the Assistant Professor rank;
however, rank and salary are dependent on the appointee's
qualifications and experience. The Assistant Professor
Classification annual salary range for this position is $74,652 -
$158,688; the anticipated starting annual salary is $80,000 -
$84,000.
Cal Poly Humboldt provides an excellent benefits package for
faculty. Information about benefits plans can be found at:
https://www.calstate.edu/csu-system/careers/benefits/Documents/employee-benefits-summary.pdf
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:
An earned PhD, PsyD or equivalent in Psychology or a closely
related field from an accredited college or university is required
at the time of appointment. If ABD, degree requirements must be
completed by date of appointment. Candidates specializing in
Clinical/Counseling, or School Psychology must hold or be eligible
for appropriate California professional licensure at the time of
appointment. Candidates specializing in Behavior Analysis (BCBA or
BCBA-D) must hold or be eligible for the professional certification
required to perform the anticipated duties of the position at the
time of appointment.
The successful candidate must demonstrate the following:
Record of training or experience in the field of psychology, or
closely related field;
Excellence in, or clear potential for, university-level
teaching and creating a student-centered learning environment;
Evidence of, or clear potential for, conducting and publishing
original research on psychology, or closely related field in
peer-reviewed journals;
Expertise in theoretical frameworks related to psychology or
area of expertise;
Willingness to work collaboratively and productively with
colleagues;
Demonstrated experience working effectively with diverse
student and/or research populations;
Demonstrated knowledge and familiarity addressing issues of
concern facing students from diverse backgrounds in higher
education; and
Record of, or potential for, involving students in research and
scholarly activity.
Preferred qualifications for this position include:
Potential for effective teaching in a broad range of Psychology
courses using a variety of instructional methodologies;
Demonstrated program of research;
Commitment to participating in professional development
opportunities that build effectiveness in teaching, areas of
inclusion, intercultural communication, and advancing
diversity;
Commitment to academic advising and student mentorship;
Potential to supervise master's theses or projects; and
Commitment to contribute to departmental, institutional,
professional, and/or community service.
Working in the state of California is a condition of employment
for this position. Pursuant to the California State University
(CSU) Out-of-State Employment Policy (effective January 1, 2022),
hiring employees to perform CSU-related work outside of the state
of California is prohibited. The employee must be able to accept
on-campus instruction, as assigned, and come to campus when needed.
The CSU also prohibits hiring and retaining employees working
permanently from a business location outside of the United
States.
At the time of appointment, the successful candidate, if not a U.S.

on the University policy on support for non-immigrant probationary
faculty visa acquisition, please visit the Faculty Immigration

https://www.humboldt.edu/academic-personnel-services/faculty-immigration-resources

DIVERSITY STATEMENT:
As an institution, Cal Poly Humboldt is committed to eliminating
the equity gap in all student populations with dynamic,
student-centered practices and policies that fully engage the
campus community. The ideal candidate will share Cal Poly
Humboldt's commitment to helping its racially and socioeconomically
diverse students succeed in their degree and career
objectives.
We value the ability to serve students from a broad range of
cultural heritages, socioeconomic backgrounds, genders, ability,
and orientations. Therefore, we prioritize applicants who
demonstrate they understand the benefits diversity brings to a
professional educational community. The successful candidate will
be an equity-minded individual committed to collaborating with
faculty, classified staff, administration, and students who are
also committed to closing equity gaps.
Cal Poly Humboldt sits on the traditional homelands of the Wiyot
people in what is currently called Arcata, CA. The Wiyot people
call the area Goudi'ni (over in the woods). The Cal Poly Humboldt
campus in Northern California is in close proximity to several
thriving Native American tribes and communities. Cal Poly Humboldt
currently has the largest percentage of Native American students in
the CSU system and has over 30 Native American faculty and staff
many from local area California Indian tribes. Cal Poly Humboldt is
home to a number of leading Native American programs including the
Indian Tribal Education and Personnel Program (ITEPP) and the
Indian Natural Resource, Science and Engineering Program (INRSEP).
There are also many opportunities at Cal Poly Humboldt to conduct
research, teaching and community work on Native American history
and cultures in Special Collections at the Cal Poly Humboldt
library. The Humboldt Room in the Library has fantastic resources
for tribally focused archive materials from the region. Cal Poly
Humboldt strives to build a supportive and inclusive Native
community and engages with Native communities through various
initiatives and opportunities like the annual California Indian Big
Time and Indigenous People's Week and a chance to network with
other faculty and staff as part of the Cal Poly Humboldt Council of
American Indian Faculty and Staff. For more information, please
visit: www.humboldt.edu/nasp

October 18, 2026, applications received after
screening has begun will be considered at the discretion of the
university. Early response is encouraged.
See more photos at Cal Poly
Humboldt's Flickr page.
It is the responsibility of the applicant to provide complete
and accurate employment information. Evidence of required

All CSU employees are obligated to respond to and report

At Cal Poly Humboldt, bold hearts and open minds shape the
future.
Cal Poly Humboldt is part of the 23-campus California State
University system. The University has a comprehensive arts and
sciences curriculum, which is recognized nationally for its high
academic quality. Founded in 1913, Cal Poly Humboldt began as a
small college for teachers. Today Humboldt has grown into a
comprehensive university with rigorous science and liberal arts
programs. Designated a polytechnic in 2022, Cal Poly Humboldt
provides hands-on, impactful educational opportunities that lead to
meaningful, measurable outcomes for the individual, for the state,
and the world. Cal Poly Humboldt is proud to have nearly 6,000
students of all backgrounds spread across 61 majors, 13 graduate
programs, and 4 credential programs - all of whom contribute
passion and creativity within their fields and set the stage for a
future grounded in equity and sustainability. Hands-on learning,
inspired teaching, groundbreaking research, and thought-provoking
creative activity happen daily at Humboldt. Finding a better future
is a task for the bold, open, down-to-earth, and visionary. Cal
Poly Humboldt strives to cultivate these qualities in leaders,
innovators, and scholars in every field.
Cal Poly Humboldt's main campus is located in Arcata, California,
in the northwestern part of the state along the coast, situated
among redwood trees in an area that offers unmatched scenic beauty,
moderate climate and opportunities for outdoor activities. The
surrounding Humboldt County locale has a population of around
130,000. The community offers an excellent range of businesses,
services and cultural activities/performances. The local schools
are ranked in the top performance percentiles, both nationally and
in the state. Additional information about Cal Poly Humboldt can be
found at: http://www.humboldt.edu

allegations of misconduct.

campus community. The ideal candidate will share Cal Poly
Humboldt's commitment to helping its racially and socioeconomically
diverse students succeed in their degree and career
objectives.
We value the ability to serve students from a broad range of
cultural heritages, socioeconomic backgrounds, genders, ability,
and orientations. Therefore, we prioritize applicants who
demonstrate they understand the benefits diversity brings to a
professional educational community. The successful candidate will
be an equity-minded individual committed to collaborating with
faculty, classified staff, administration, and students who are
also committed to closing equity gaps.
Cal Poly Humboldt sits on the traditional homelands of the Wiyot
people in what is currently called Arcata, CA. The Wiyot people
call the area Goudi'ni (over in the woods). The Cal Poly Humboldt
campus in Northern California is in close proximity to several
thriving Native American tribes and communities. Cal Poly Humboldt
currently has the largest percentage of Native American students in
the CSU system and has over 30 Native American faculty and staff
many from local area California Indian tribes. Cal Poly Humboldt is
home to a number of leading Native American programs including the
Indian Tribal Education and Personnel Program (ITEPP) and the
Indian Natural Resource, Science and Engineering Program (INRSEP).
There are also many opportunities at Cal Poly Humboldt to conduct
research, teaching and community work on Native American history
and cultures in Special Collections at the Cal Poly Humboldt
library. The Humboldt Room in the Library has fantastic resources
for tribally focused archive materials from the region. Cal Poly
Humboldt strives to build a supportive and inclusive Native
community and engages with Native communities through various
initiatives and opportunities like the annual California Indian Big
Time and Indigenous People's Week and a chance to network with
other faculty and staff as part of the Cal Poly Humboldt Council of
American Indian Faculty and Staff. For more information, please
visit: www.humboldt.edu/nasp

At Cal Poly Humboldt, bold hearts and open minds shape the
future.
Cal Poly Humboldt is part of the 23-campus California State
University system. The University has a comprehensive arts and
sciences curriculum, which is recognized nationally for its high
academic quality. Founded in 1913, Cal Poly Humboldt began as a
small college for teachers. Today Humboldt has grown into a
comprehensive university with rigorous science and liberal arts
programs. Designated a polytechnic in 2022, Cal Poly Humboldt
provides hands-on, impactful educational opportunities that lead to
meaningful, measurable outcomes for the individual, for the state,
and the world. Cal Poly Humboldt is proud to have nearly 6,000
students of all backgrounds spread across 61 majors, 13 graduate
programs, and 4 credential programs - all of whom contribute
passion and creativity within their fields and set the stage for a
future grounded in equity and sustainability. Hands-on learning,
inspired teaching, groundbreaking research, and thought-provoking
creative activity happen daily at Humboldt. Finding a better future
is a task for the bold, open, down-to-earth, and visionary. Cal
Poly Humboldt strives to cultivate these qualities in leaders,
innovators, and scholars in every field.
Cal Poly Humboldt's main campus is located in Arcata, California,
in the northwestern part of the state along the coast, situated
among redwood trees in an area that offers unmatched scenic beauty,

jobs.title: Assistant or Associate Professor of Nuclear Engineering, Fall 2027
jobs.description:
The Department of Nuclear Engineering at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (UTK) invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the Assistant or Associate Professor level. The department will pursue tenure consideration for qualified candidates. The anticipated start date is August 2027.
Duties include teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in nuclear engineering-related subjects, developing and sustaining an externally funded research program, advising graduate students, publishing scholarly work, and providing service to the department, college, university, and professional community.
The UT Department of Nuclear Engineering is the largest Nuclear Engineering PhD program in the United States, with a diverse research portfolio and close collaborations with Idaho National Laboratory (INL), Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL), the Y-12 National Security Complex, and more than 150 nuclear-related companies within 50 miles of the campus. The department is housed in the state-of-the-art Zeanah Engineering Complex, home to more than 20 nuclear engineering laboratories and computational resources. The department is committed to cultivating work/life balance and a family-friendly environment for faculty, staff, and students.
The Tickle College of Engineering (TCE), comprised of nine departments that house 213 tenure-track and 80+ non-tenure-track faculty, is in the midst of unprecedented growth under Chancellor Donde Plowman and Dean Matthew Mench, having added 30+ new faculty over the past 4 years and set records in research expenditures ($113.9M in FY25J, enrollment (4,800 undergraduate and 1,500 graduate students), and increased ranking (now 28th among public universities) in the US News and World Report list of top engineering colleges. Key partnerships with Oak Ridge National Laboratory and Consolidated Nuclear Security (Y-12) and growth are supported by new facilities including the Zeanah Engineering Complex and the Innovation South building.
Knoxville is a vibrant city with a beautiful, walkable downtown, active neighborhoods, a lively nightlife with numerous theaters and museums, a rich live music scene, and eclectic dining. Nestled in the foothills of the Great Smoky Mountains and surrounded by lakes and the Tennessee River, Knoxville offers outstanding access to outdoor recreation and is within 200 miles of four major metropolitan areas.
Qualifications
We seek candidates whose research and teaching interests strengthen and broaden the department's capabilities in one or more of the following areas: reliability and maintainability of nuclear systems and components; data analytics, artificial intelligence, digital twin technologies, and cyber security for nuclear applications; nuclear instrumentation and control; radiation instrumentation; robust decision-making, empirical/data-driven modeling, and process & equipment monitoring; thermal-fluid sciences and experimental reactor thermal-hydraulics. Candidates whose work bridges experimentation, computational modeling, sensing, and thermal­fluid or reactor systems analysis in support of reliable, sustainable nuclear power are especially encouraged to apply. Ideally, successful candidates will be able to contribute across more than one of these areas. Preference will be given to applicants with demonstrated (or clearly emerging, for more junior candidates) research success that complements existing departmental strengths and who have a vision for developing collaborative, sustainably funded research programs. Candidates must also show strong commitment to high-quality undergraduate and graduate teaching.
Candidates for assistant professor must have a demonstrated potential to develop a nationally recognized, externally funded research program. Candidates for associate professor must lead a nationally recognized externally funded research program and demonstrate the potential to develop an international recognized research program.
Applicants must hold a doctorate in Nuclear Engineering or a closely related field by the effective date of appointment.

The Social Work Department at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee

Intelligence and Data Science Cluster Hire Initiative. UWM Academic
Affairs, with generous support from the Northwestern Mutual Data
Science Institute (NMDSI), is making a strategic investment in this

resources.
The new faculty will have a record of securing external funding
along with experience in academic settings that is commensurate
with a rank of Advanced Assistant Professor (with ability to join
UWM as tenured associate) or higher. Applicants are expected to
have expertise both in a critical social work-related area of
research (e.g., applied gerontology, health disparities, poverty
policy, child welfare, community practice, criminal justice, etc.)

engagement, and develop AI and Data Science talent to support
Milwaukee's growth as a technology and innovation hub. Candidates

as Fellows with UWM's Connected Systems, which houses the Microsoft
AI Co-Innovation Lab

Community Engagement & Professions: Helen Bader School of
Social Welfare and the School of Information Studies.

Produce scholarship in an important area of social work

Advance interdisciplinary AI and Data Science research at

Collaborate with NMDSI to address real-world challenges.
Innovate and expand AI and Data Science educational

Department:
The Helen Bader School of Social Welfare is comprised of the

UWM is recognized by the Carnegie Foundation as both a Research 1

economic growth. As one of the few Carnegie R1 Research

Position Summary
The
Department of Chemistry at the University at Buffalo, The State
University of New York, invites applications for a SUNY Empire
Innovation Program faculty position in sustainable materials
chemistry, as broadly defined, at the level of Associate or
Full Professor. Candidates with research interests in
experimental chemistry – involving materials synthesis,
characterization, measurement, and/or the development of analytical
tools and methods – that advances sustainable technologies, energy
conversion and storage, and a cleaner environment, are especially
encouraged to apply. Research programs that integrate the
development of functional materials with innovative approaches for
their chemical, electrochemical, or spectroscopic characterization
are particularly welcome.
This position is supported by SUNY's Empire Innovation Program
that funds the expansion of research excellence in strategic areas
through the recruitment of top faculty that are recognized leaders
of their fields.
The successful candidate will be expected to
Develop and sustain a nationally and internationally
recognized, externally funded research program;
Contribute to excellence in undergraduate and graduate
education;
Mentor students and researchers from diverse backgrounds;
Provide leadership and service to the Department, University,
and broader scientific community.
Application materials must be submitted via UB Jobs at https://www.ubjobs.buffalo.edu/postings/64368.
Applications received by December 1, 2026 will be
given priority consideration. The search will continue until the
position is filled.
About the Department
The Department of Chemistry offers a highly collaborative and
research-intensive environment spanning the traditional areas of
analytical, inorganic, organic, and physical chemistry, as well as
interdisciplinary research at the interfaces of chemistry with
materials science, engineering, biology, medicine, and physics. The
Department is committed to excellence in research and education and
to fostering an inclusive environment for students, faculty, and
staff. Faculty benefit from extensive opportunities for
interdisciplinary collaboration across the University at Buffalo,
including the College of Arts and Sciences; the Schools of
Engineering and Applied Sciences, Dental Medicine, Medicine and
Biomedical Sciences, and Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences; the
RENEW Institute; and the Center for Computational Research, as well
as with regional research partners including Roswell Park
Comprehensive Cancer Center and the Hauptman-Woodward Medical

Details
The Department of History at the University of Utah seeks a
tenure-line Assistant Professor in the modern history of China with
a preference for East Asian, transnational, or global Chinese
histories. The position is part of a new International and Area
Studies initiative within the College of Humanities. Competitive
applicants will have a demonstrated commitment to research and
research-informed teaching at all levels of the undergraduate and
graduate curriculum. The teaching load is two courses per semester.
Teaching responsibilities include undergraduate and graduate
courses in the applicant's areas of expertise, contributing on a
rotating basis to the teaching of both halves of our two-course
Asian history survey (before and after 1500), and an additional
service course. History faculty have opportunities to participate
in the University's interdisciplinary initiatives in Asian and
International Studies, Environmental Humanities, the Medical
Humanities, Games, and Digital Humanities, among other programs.
The PhD is preferred but ABD candidates are encouraged to apply.

Applicants should submit a cover letter, CV, writing sample,
statement of teaching philosophy and practice, and teaching
evaluations if available. Applicants will also provide the names
and email addresses of three references, whom our system will
automatically contact for letters of recommendation.

jobs.title: Faculty Positions in Mathematics | College of Arts & Sciences
jobs.description:
Faculty Positions in Mathematics | College of Arts & Sciences
Post date: September 22, 2026
Application deadline: December 15, 2026
The Department of Mathematics and Statistics at American University of Sharjah (AUS) is accepting applications for a full-time, regular faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor, commencing in August 2027. In exceptional cases, appointment at a higher rank may be considered. We welcome applications from outstanding candidates in all areas of mathematics; preference will be given to candidates specializing in algebra or applied mathematics. For full consideration, applications must be received by December 15, 2026. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Apply at https://acg-apps1.aus.edu/cas/empapp/apply.php?p=MTH-27-01.
JOB QUALIFICATIONS: All candidates must hold a PhD in Mathematics or Applied Mathematics. Applicants should demonstrate a solid and active research record, with evidence of quality publications and clear potential for sustained contributions to the field. Successful candidates will be expected to establish and maintain an active research program, supervise master’s and PhD students, secure research grants, and engage in international collaborations. Evidence of excellence in teaching across all curriculum levels and strong communication skills in English are required. Preference will be given to candidates with experience in North American-style education.
APPLICATION PROCEDURE: A complete application consists of two PDF files. The first file contains a cover letter, a research statement, and a teaching statement. The second file contains the candidate's curriculum vitae and contact details for three references. Shortlisted candidates will be asked to contact their references to have their letters of recommendation sent directly to the search committee. These reference letters must address research, teaching, and overall potential, with at least one of these letters specifically addressing the applicant's teaching experience.
ABOUT THE DEPARTMENT: The Department of Mathematics and Statistics at AUS offers diverse programs, including a PhD in Mathematics, a Master of Science in Mathematics, a Bachelor of Science in Mathematics, a Bachelor of Science in Data Science, and minors in applied and computational mathematics, actuarial mathematics, and data science. Our student body spans a wide range of nationalities and enjoys a diverse and inclusive environment. The department currently consists of 27 full-time faculty members who are actively engaged in original research across different areas of mathematics and statistics. For more information, you can learn more about the department at www.aus.edu/cas/department-of-mathematics-and-statistics.
ABOUT THE UNIVERSITY: American University of Sharjah (AUS) invites applications from accomplished scholars committed to excellence in teaching, learning and research within an American-style, globally recognized institution. Successful candidates will be offered a salary commensurate with experience, along with free housing, paid utilities and other attractive benefits.
As a comprehensive, independent, non-profit, coeducational university, AUS is consistently ranked among the top 10 universities in the Arab region and among the top 17 percent of ranked universities in the world (QS, 2027). The university fosters a diverse community of over 6,000 students from more than 100 nations, with English as the language of instruction and the workplace.
Located in Sharjah's University City, AUS is directly adjacent to the Sharjah Research, Technology and Innovation Park, providing faculty with significant opportunities to engage in interdisciplinary research and contribute directly to the UAE’s rapidly expanding innovation ecosystem. The campus is set in a vibrant and cosmopolitan area, offering abundant opportunities for travel, entertainment and cultural experiences, with Sharjah International Airport minutes away and Dubai International Airport only 30 minutes from campus. A number of schools aligned with various international curricula are located nearby.
AUS is licensed and its programs are accredited by the Commission for Academic Accreditation of the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research of the United Arab Emirates. AUS has been accredited in the United States of America by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education (1007 North Orange Street, 4th Floor, MB #166, Wilmington, DE 19801 USA) since June 2004.
For more information, please visit www.aus.edu.
